body.text: oṃ namo ratnatrayāya
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels.

body.text: p.1.1/.evaṃ mayā śrutam/ ekasin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma/ jetavane +anāthapiṇḍadasya^ārāme/
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

body.text: p.1.2/.atha^āyuṣmān ānandaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātra^cīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ mahā^nagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/ atha^āyuṣmān ānandaḥ śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛta^bhakta^kṛtyo yenānyatamam udapānaṃ tena^upasaṃkrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robes, entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having wandered through <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms and finished his meal, approached a certain well.

body.text: p.1.3/.tena khalu samayena tasminn udapāne prakṛtir nāma mātaṅga^dārikā udakam uddharate sma/ atha^āyuṣmān ānandaḥ prakṛtiṃ mātaṅga^dārikām etad avocat/ dehi me bhagini pānīyaṃ pāsyāmi/
body.translated_text: At that time, at that well, a <s>Mātaṅga</s> (outcast) girl named <s>Prakṛti</s> was drawing water. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl thus: 'Give me water, sister, I will drink.'

body.text: p.1.4/.evaṃ kite prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikāyuṣmantam ānandam idam avocat/ mātaṅga^dārikāham asmi bhadantānanda/ na^ahaṃ te bhagini kulaṃ vā jātiṃ vā pṛcchāmi/ api tu sacette parityaktaṃ pānīyaṃ dehi pāsyāmi/
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl said to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'I am a <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.' [He replied:] 'I do not ask you, sister, about your family or your birth. But if you have water to spare, give it to me, I will drink.'

body.text: p.1.5/.atha prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikāyuṣmantam ānandāya pānīyam adāt/ atha^āyuṣmān ānandaḥ pānīyaṃ pītvā prakrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl gave water to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having drunk the water, departed.

body.text: p.1.6/.atha prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikāyuṣmanta ānandsya śarīre mukhe svare sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca nimittam udgṛhītvā yoniśo manasikāreṇāviṣṭā saṃrāgacittam utpādayati (1) sma/ āryo me ānandaḥ svāmī ayād iti/ mātā ca me mahā^vidyādharī sā śakṣyaty āryam ānandam ānayitum/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, having carefully observed the auspicious signs on the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>'s body, face, and voice, being seized by thorough mental attention, generated a mind of passionate attachment, thinking: 'The noble <s>Ānanda</s> shall be my husband! And my mother is a great <s>vidyādharī</s> (sorceress) — she will be able to bring the noble <s>Ānanda</s> to me.'

body.text: p.2.1/.atha prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā pānīyaghaṭam ādāya yena caṇḍāla^gṛhaṃ tena^upasaṃkramya pānīya^ghaṭam ekānte nikṣipya svāṃ jananīm idam avocat/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, taking her water-pot, approached the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (outcast) house, set down the water-pot in one place, and said to her mother:

body.text: p.2.2/.yat khalv evam amba jānīyā ānando nāma śramaṇo mahāśramaṇa^gautamasya śrāvaka upasthāyakas tam ahaṃ svāminam icchāmi/ śakṣyasi tam amba ānayitum/
body.translated_text: 'Know this, mother: there is a monk named <s>Ānanda</s>, a disciple and attendant of the great ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. I desire him as my husband. Can you bring him, mother?'

body.text: p.2.3/.sā tām avocat/ śaktā +ahaṃ putri ānandam ānayituṃ/ sthāpayitvā yo mṛtaḥ syād yo vā vīta^rāgaḥ/ api ca rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ śramaṇa^gautamam atīva sevate bhajate paryupāsate/ yadi jānīyāt so +ayaṃ caṇḍāla^kulasyānarthāya pratipadyeta/ śramaṇaś ca gautamo vīta^rāgaḥ śrūyate/ vīta^rāgasya [mantrāḥ] punaḥ sarva^mantrān abhibhavanti/
body.translated_text: She said to her: 'I am able, daughter, to bring <s>Ānanda</s> — except one who is dead or one who is free from passion. But King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> greatly serves, worships, and attends upon the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. If he were to learn of it, he would act to the detriment of the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> family. And the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is heard to be free from passion. The mantras of one free from passion overcome all [other] mantras.'

body.text: p.2.4/.evam uktā prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā mātaram idam avocat/ sa ced amba śramaṇo gautamā vīta^rāgastasya^antikāc chramaṇam ānandaṃ na pratilapsye jīvitaṃ parityajeyaṃ sa cet pratilipsye jīvāmi/
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl said to her mother: 'If, mother, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is free from passion and I cannot obtain the monk <s>Ānanda</s> from him, I shall give up my life. But if I do obtain him, I shall live.'

body.text: p.2.5/.mā te putri jīvitaṃ parityajasi ānayāmi śramaṇam ānandam/
body.translated_text: 'Do not give up your life, daughter. I shall bring the monk <s>Ānanda</s>.'

body.text: p.2.6/.atha prakṛter mātaṅga^dārikāyā mātā madhye gṛhāṅganasya gomayenopalepanaṃ kṛtvā vedīm ālipya darbhān saṃstīrya^agniṃ prajvālya^aṣṭaśatam arka^puṣpāṇāṃ gṛhītvā mantrān āvartayamānā ekaikam arka^puṣpaṃ parijapya agnau pratikṣipati sma/ tatra^iyaṃ vidyā bhavatiḥ
body.translated_text: Then the mother of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, in the middle of the courtyard, smeared the ground with cow-dung, plastered an altar, spread <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass), kindled a fire, and taking eight hundred <s>arka</s> (calotropis) flowers, while reciting mantras, she consecrated each <s>arka</s> flower and cast it into the fire. There this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) was recited:

body.text: p.3.1/.amale vimale kuṅkume sumane/ yena baddhā +asi vidyut/ icchayā devo varṣati vidyotati gajeti vismayaṃ mahā^rājasya samabhivardhāyituṃ devebhyo manuṣyebhyo gandharvebhyoḥ śikhi^grahā devā viśikhi^gra(@)hā devā ānandasya^āgamanāya saṃgamanāya kramaṇāya grahaṇāya juhomi svāhā/
body.translated_text: '<s>Amale</s>, <s>Vimale</s>, <s>Kuṅkume</s>, <s>Sumane</s>! By whom lightning has been bound — by whose will the god rains, flashes, and thunders — to increase the wonder of the great king, from the gods, from humans, from <s>Gandharvas</s>; O <s>Śikhigraha</s> gods, O <s>Viśikhigraha</s> gods — for the coming, the meeting, the approach, and the seizing of <s>Ānanda</s>, I offer oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!'

body.text: p.3.2/.atha^āyuṣmata ānandasya cittam ākṣiptaṃ/ sa vihārān niṣkramya yena caṇḍāla^gṛhaṃ tena^upasaṃkrāmati sma/
body.translated_text: Then the mind of the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was overpowered. He went out from the monastery and began approaching the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> house.

body.text: p.3.3/.adrākṣīc caṇḍālī āyuṣmantam ānandaṃ dūrād eva^āgacchantaṃ/ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prakṛtiṃ duhitaram idam avocat/ ayam asau putri śramaṇa ānanda āgacchati śayanaṃ prajñapaya/
body.translated_text: The <s>Caṇḍālī</s> (outcast woman) saw the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> coming from afar. Having seen him, she said to her daughter <s>Prakṛti</s>: 'There, daughter, the monk <s>Ānanda</s> is coming. Prepare a bed.'

body.text: p.3.4/.atha prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā hṛṣṭa^tuṣṭā pramudita^manā āyuṣmata ānandasya śayyāṃ prajñapayati sma/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, overjoyed, delighted, and elated in mind, prepared a bed for the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.

body.text: p.3.5/.atha^āyuṣmān ānando yena caṇḍāla^gṛhaṃ tena^upasaṃkrāntaḥ/ upasaṃkramya vedīm upaniśrityā +asthāt/ ekānta^sthitaḥ sa punar āyuṣmān ānandaḥ prārodīd/ aśrūṇi pravartayamāna evam āha/ vyasana^prāpto +aham asmi na ca me bhagavān samanvāharati/
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> house. Having approached, he stood near the altar. Standing alone, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> then wept. Shedding tears, he spoke thus: 'I have fallen into calamity, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> does not look after me.'

body.text: p.3.6/.atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandaṃ samanvāharati sma/ samanvāhṛtya saṃbuddha^mantraiś caṇḍāla^mantrān pratihanti sma/ tatra^iyaṃ vidyāḥ/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> looked after the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Having looked after him, he countered the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> mantras with the mantras of the Fully Enlightened One. There this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) was recited:

body.text: p.3.7./.sthitir acyutiḥ sunītiḥ/ svasti sarva^prāṇibhyaḥ/
body.translated_text: 'Stability, firmness, good conduct! May there be well-being for all living creatures!'

body.text: p.4.1ab/.saraḥ prasannaṃ nirdoṣaṃ praśāntaṃ sarvato +abhayaṃ/
body.translated_text: 'The lake is clear, faultless, tranquil, free from fear in every direction,

body.text: p.4.1cd/.ītayo yatra śāmyanti bhayāni calitāni ca/
body.translated_text: where calamities are pacified and fears are dispelled.

body.text: p.4.2ab/.tad vai devā namsyanti sarva^siddhāś ca yoginaḥ/
body.translated_text: That indeed the gods honor, and all accomplished <s>yogins</s>.

body.text: p.4.2cd/.etena satya^vākyena svastyā^ānandāya bhikṣave//
body.translated_text: By this truthful utterance, may there be well-being for <s>Ānanda</s> the monk.'

body.text: p.4.3/.atha^āyuṣmān ānandaḥ pratihata^caṇḍāla^mantraś caṇḍāla^gṛhān niṣkramya yena svako vihāras tena^upasaṃkramitum ārabdhaḥ/
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, whose <s>Caṇḍāla</s> mantras had been countered, went out from the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> house and began to approach his own monastery.

body.text:
p.4.4/.adrākṣīt prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā/ ānandam āyuṣmantaṃ pratigacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ svāṃ jananīm idam avocat/ ayam asau mātaḥ śramaṇa ānandaḥ pratigacchati/ tām āha mātā/ niyataṃ putri śramaṇena gautamena samanvāhṛto bhaviṣyati/ tena mama mantrāḥ pratihatā bhaviṣyanti/ prakṛtir āha/ kiṃ punar amba balavattarāḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya mantrā na^asmākaṃ/
tām āha mātā/ balavattarāḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya mantrā na^asmākaṃ/ ye putri mantāḥ sarva^lokasya prabhavanti tān mantrān śramaṇo gautama ākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ pratihanti/ na punar lokaḥ prabhavati śramaṇasya gautamasya mantrān pratihantuṃ/ evaṃ balavattarāḥ avamaṇasya gautamasya mantrāḥ/
body.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl saw the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> going back. Having seen him, she said to her mother: 'There, mother, the monk <s>Ānanda</s> is going back.' Her mother said to her: 'Surely, daughter, he has been looked after by the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. Therefore my mantras must have been countered.' <s>Prakṛti</s> said: 'But mother, are the mantras of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> more powerful than ours?' Her mother said to her: 'The mantras of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> are more powerful than ours. The mantras that prevail over the entire world — the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, if he wishes, counters those mantras. But the world is not able to counter the mantras of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. So much more powerful are the mantras of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>.'

body.text: p.4.5/.atha^āyuṣmān ānando yena bhagavāṃs tena^upasaṃkrāntaḥ/ upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā^ekānte +asthāt/
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and stood to one side.

body.text:
p.4.6/.ekānta^sthitam āyuṣmantam ānandaṃ bhagavān idam avocat/ udgṛhṇa tvam ānanda imāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīvidyāṃ dhāraya vācaya paryavāpnuhi/ ātmano hitāya sukhāya bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnām upāsakānām upasikānāṃ hitāya sukhāya/ iyam ānanda ṣaḍkṣarīvidyā ṣaḍbhiḥ samyak saṃbuddhair bhāṣitā caturbhiś ca mahā^rājaiḥ śakreṇa devānām indreṇa brahmaṇā ca sahāpatinā/ mayā ca^etarhi
śākyamuninā samyak^saṃbuddhena bhāṣitā/ tvam apy etarhy ānanda tāṃ dhāraya vācaya paryavāpnuhi/ yad uta tad yathā:
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, who was standing to one side: 'Learn, <s>Ānanda</s>, this <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Vidyā</s> (Six-Syllable Spell), retain it, recite it, and master it — for your own benefit and happiness, and for the benefit and happiness of monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers. This <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Vidyā</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, has been spoken by six Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas, by the four Great Kings, by <s>Śakra</s> the Lord of the Gods, and by <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s>. And it has now been spoken by me, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. You too now, <s>Ānanda</s>, retain it, recite it, and master it. That is as follows:

body.text: p.5.1/.aṇḍare pāṇḍare kāraṇḍe keyūre +arci^haste khara^grīve bandhu^mati cīra^mati dharavidha cilimile viloḍaya viṣāṇi loke/ viṣa cala cala/ gola^mati gaṇḍavile cilimile sa^atinimne yathā saṃvibhakta^gola^mati gaṇḍa^vilāyai svāhā/
body.translated_text: '<s>Aṇḍare</s>, <s>Pāṇḍare</s>, <s>Kāraṇḍe</s>, <s>Keyūre</s>, <s>Arcihaste</s>, <s>Kharagrīve</s>, <s>Bandhumati</s>, <s>Cīramati</s>, <s>Dharavidha</s>, <s>Cilimile</s> — shake off the poisons in the world! Poison, move away, move away! <s>Golamati</s>, <s>Gaṇḍavile</s>, <s>Cilimile</s>, <s>Saatinimne</s> — as has been distributed to <s>Golamati Gaṇḍavilā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!'

body.text: p.5.2/.yaḥ kaś cid ānanda^ṣaḍakṣaryā vidyayā paritrāṇaṃ svastyayanaṃ kuryāt sa yadi vadha^arho bhavet daṇḍena mucyate/ daṇḍa^arhaḥ prahāreṇa prahāra^arhaḥ paribhāṣaṇayā paribhāṣaṇa^arho romaharṣaṇena romaharṣaṇa^arhaḥ punar eva mucyate/
body.translated_text: Whoever should perform protection and benediction with <s>Ānanda</s>'s <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Vidyā</s> — if he were deserving of death, he would be freed with [only] a beating; if deserving of a beating, with a blow; if deserving of a blow, with a scolding; if deserving of a scolding, with a mere bristling of hair; if deserving of a bristling of hair, he would be entirely freed.

body.text: p.5.3/.na^aham ānanda taṃ samanupaśyāmi sa^deva^loke samāra^loke sabrahma^loke saśramaṇa^brāhmaṇikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ sa^deva^mānuṣikāyāṃ sa^asurāyāṃ yas tv anayā ṣaḍakṣayaṃ vidyayā rakṣāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ rakṣā^sūtre bāhau baddhe svastyayane kṛte +abhibhavituṃ śakroti varjayitvā paurāṇaṃ karma^vipākam/
body.translated_text: 'I do not see, <s>Ānanda</s>, in this world with its gods, with its <s>Māra</s>, with its <s>Brahmā</s>, among the generation of ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans, including the <s>Asuras</s> — anyone who is able to overpower one for whom protection has been performed with this <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Vidyā</s>, for whom a protection cord has been tied on the arm, for whom a benediction has been performed — except through the ripening of previous <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: p.6.1/.atha prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā tasyā eva rātryā atyayāt śiraḥ^snātā +anāhata dūṣya^prāvṛtā muktā^mālya^ābharaṇā yena śrāvasto nagarī tena^upasaṃkramya nagara^dvāre kapāṭa^mūle niśrityā +asthāt/ āyuṣmantam ānandam āgamayamānā/ niyatam anena mārgeṇa^ānando bhikṣurāgam iṣyati^iti/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, after the passing of that night, having bathed her head, wrapped in a fresh garment, adorned with garlands and ornaments of pearls, approached the city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> and stood leaning against the base of the city gate, waiting for the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, [thinking]: 'Surely <s>Ānanda</s> the monk will come by this road.'

body.text:
p.6.2/.atha^āyuṣmān ānandaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātra^cīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/ dadarśa prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārika^āyuṣmantam ānandaṃ/ dūrata eva dṛṣṭvā ca punar āyuṣmantam ānandaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā gacchantam anugacchati tiṣṭhantam anutiṣṭhati/ yad yad eva kulaṃ piṇḍāya praviśati tasya tasyaiva dvāre tūṣṇībhūtā tiṣṭhati āyuṣmantam
ānandam āmantrayamāṇā/
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robes, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl saw the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Having seen the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> from afar, she followed closely behind him — when he walked, she walked after him; when he stopped, she stopped. Whatever household he entered for alms, she stood silently at its door, calling out to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.

body.text:
p.6.3./.dadarśāyuṣmānānandaḥ prakṛtiṃ mātaṅga^dārikāṃ/ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar jehrīymāṇarūpo +apragalbhāyamānarūpo duḥkhī durmanāḥ śīghraṃ śīghraṃ śrāvastyā vinirgamya yena jetavanaṃ tanopasaṃkrāntaḥ/ upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvekānte +asthād/ ekānta^sthita āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat/ iyaṃ me bhagavan
prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā gacchantam anugacchati, tiṣṭhantam anutiṣṭhati/ yad yad eva kulaṃ piṇḍāya praviśāmi tasya tasyaiva dvāre tūṣṇībhūtā tiṣṭhati/ trāhi me bhagavan trāhi me sugata/
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> saw <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl following closely behind him. Having seen her, feeling ashamed and embarrassed, distressed and disheartened, he quickly left <s>Śrāvastī</s> and approached <s>Jetavana</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, Blessed One, follows closely behind me — when I walk, she walks after me; when I stop, she stops. Whatever household I enter for alms, she stands silently at its door. Protect me, Blessed One! Protect me, <s>Sugata</s>!'

body.text:
p.6.4/.evam ukte bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam idam avocat/ mā bher mā bher iti/ atha bhagavān prakṛtiṃ mātaṅga^dārikām idam avocat/ hiṃ te prakṛte mātaṅga^dārike ānandena bhikṣuṇā/ prakṛtir āha/ svāminaṃ bhadantam ānandam icchāmi/ bhagavān āha/ (7) anujñātāsi prakṛte mātāpitṛbhyām ānandāya/ anujñātāsmi bhagavann anujñātāsmi sugata/ bhagavān āha/ tena hi
sammukhaṃ mamānujñāpayya tvam/
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Do not fear, do not fear.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl: 'What do you want with the monk <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Prakṛti Mātaṅga</s> girl?' <s>Prakṛti</s> said: 'I desire the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> as my husband.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Have you been given permission by your parents for [marriage with] <s>Ānanda</s>?' 'I have been permitted, Blessed One; I have been permitted, <s>Sugata</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Then obtain permission directly in my presence.'

body.text: p.7.1/.atha prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato +antikāt prakrāntā/ yena svakau mātāpitarau tena^upasaṃkrāntā/ upasaṃkramya mātāpitroḥ pādān śirasā vanditvā^ekānte +asthād/ ekānta^sthitā svakau mātā pitarāv idam avocat/ sammukhaṃ me +amba tāta śramaṇasya gautamasyānandāyotsṛjatam/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowed her head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. She approached her own parents. Having approached, she bowed her head at the feet of her parents and stood to one side. Standing to one side, she said to her parents: 'In the presence of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, mother and father, release me to <s>Ānanda</s>.'

body.text: p.7.2/.atha prakṛter mātaṅga^dārikāyā mātāpitarau prakṛtim ādāya yana bhagavāms tena^upasaṃkrāntau/ uapsaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā^ekānte nyaṣīdatāṃ/ atha prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā banditvā ekānte +asthād/ ekānta^sthitā bhagavantam etad avocat/ imau tau bhagavan mātāpitarāv āgatau/
body.translated_text: Then the parents of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl, taking <s>Prakṛti</s> along, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). Having approached, they venerated the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with their heads and sat down to one side. Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl, having venerated the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with her head, stood to one side. Standing to one side, she addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: "<s>Bhagavān</s>, these are my parents who have come."

body.text: p.7.3/.atha bhagavān prakṛter mātaṅga^dārikāyā mātāpitarāv idam avoct/ anujñātā yuvābhyāṃ prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikānandāyeti/ tāv āhutuḥ/ anujñātā bhagavann anujñātā sugata/ tena hi yūyaṃ prakṛtim apahāya gacchata svagṛham/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the parents of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl thus: "Is <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl permitted by you two to go to <s>Ānanda</s>?" They said: "She is permitted, <s>Bhagavān</s>, she is permitted, <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)." "Then you may leave <s>Prakṛti</s> and go to your own home."

body.text: p.7.4/.atha prakṛter mātaṅga^dārikāyā mātāpitarau bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato +antikāt prakrāntau/
body.translated_text: Then the parents of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl, having venerated the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with their heads and having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, departed from the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
p.7.5/.atha prakṛter mātaṅga^dārikāyā mātāpitarāv aciraprakrāntau viditvā bhagavān prakṛtiṃ mātaṅga^dārikām idm avocat/ arthikāsi prakṛte ānandena bhikṣuṇā/ prakṛtir āha/ arthikāsmi bhagavann arthikāsmi sugata/ tena hi prakṛte ya ānandasya veśaḥ sa tvayā dhārayitavyaḥ/ sā āha/ dhārayāmi bhagavan dhārayāmi sugata/ pravrājayatu māṃ sugata pravrājayatu māṃ
bhagavān/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that the parents of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl had recently departed, addressed <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl thus: "<s>Prakṛti</s>, do you desire the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) <s>Ānanda</s>?" <s>Prakṛti</s> said: "I desire him, <s>Bhagavān</s>, I desire him, <s>Sugata</s>." "Then, <s>Prakṛti</s>, you must wear the garb that <s>Ānanda</s> wears." She said: "I will wear it, <s>Bhagavān</s>, I will wear it, <s>Sugata</s>. Let the <s>Sugata</s> ordain me! Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> ordain me!"

body.text: p.8.1/.atha bhagavān prakṛtiṃ mātaṅga^dārikām idam avocat/ ehi tvaṃ bhikṣuṇi cara brahma^caryam/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl thus: "Come, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun), practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>)."

body.text:
p.8.2/.evam ukte prakṛtir mātaṅga^dārikā bhagavatā muṇḍā kāṣāya^prāvṛtā/ atha bhagavān prakṛtiṃ mātaṅga^dārikām ehi bhikṣuṇīvādena pravrājayitvā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati sma, samādāpayati sma, samuttejayati sma, saṃpraharṣayati sma/ yeyaṃ kathā dīrgha^rātraṃ saṃsārasamāpannānāṃ pratikūlā śravaṇīyā/tad yathā/ dānakathā śīlakathā svargakathā kāmeṣv
ādīnavaṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ bhayaṃ saṃkleśavyavadānaṃ bodhipakṣāṃs tān dharmān bhagvān prakṛtyai bhikṣuṇyai saṃprakāśayati sma/
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl, by the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, became shaven-headed and clothed in saffron robes. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having ordained <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> girl with the formula 'Come, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>,' instructed her with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, inspiring her, uplifting her, and gladdening her. This discourse, which should be heard by those who have been immersed in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) for a long time and which runs counter (to worldly ways) — namely: a discourse on generosity, a discourse on morality, a discourse on heaven, the danger in sensual desires, the escape, the fear, the defilement and purification, and the factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) — these <s>dharmas</s> the <s>Bhagavān</s> elucidated for the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>.

body.text: p.8.3/.atha prakṛtir bhikṣuṇī bhagavatā dharmyaya kathayā saṃdarśitā samādāpitā samuttejitā saṃpraharṣitā hṛṣṭa^cittā kalyāṇacittā muditacittā vinīvaraṇacittā ṛjucittā +akhilacittā bhavyā dharma^deśitam ājñātum/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>, having been instructed, inspired, uplifted, and gladdened by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, became joyful in mind, virtuous in mind, delighted in mind, with mind free from hindrances, with mind upright, with mind unobstructed — fit to understand the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: p.9.1/.yadā ca bhagavān jñātaḥ prakṛtiṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ hṛṣṭa^cittāṃ kalyāṇacittāṃ muditacittāṃ vinivaraṇacittāṃ bhavyāṃ pratibalāṃ sāmutkarpikīṃ dharma^deśanām ājñātuṃ tadā yeyaṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhānāṃ caturārya^satyaprativedhikī sāmutkarṣikī dharma^deśanā, yad uta duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodho mārgaḥ, tāṃ bhagavān prakṛter bhikṣuṇyā vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati sma/
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> knew that the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s> was joyful in mind, virtuous in mind, delighted in mind, with mind free from hindrances, fit, capable, and ready to understand the exalted teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> — then that exalted teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, which penetrates the <s>Catvāry Āryasatyāni</s> (Four Noble Truths), namely: <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>samudaya</s> (origination), <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), and <s>mārga</s> (the path) — that the <s>Bhagavān</s> elucidated in detail for the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>.

body.text: p.9.2/.atha prakṛtibhikṣuṇī tasminn evāsane niṣaṇṇā caturārya^satyānyabhijñātāsit/ duḥkhaṃ sumudayaṃ nirodhaṃ mārgaṃ// tad yathā vastām apagatakālakaṃ rajanopagataṃ raṅga^udake prakṣiptaṃ samyag eva raṅgaṃ pratigṛhṇīyād evam eva prakṛtir bhikṣuṇī tasminnevāsane niṣaṇṇā caturārya^satyāni abhisamayati sma, tad yathā duḥkhaṃ sumudayaṃ nirodhaṃ mārgam/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>, seated on that very seat, realized the <s>Catvāry Āryasatyāni</s> (Four Noble Truths) — namely, <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>samudaya</s> (origination), <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), and <s>mārga</s> (the path). Just as a cloth, free from stains, having been brought to the dye, when cast into the dye-water would take the color perfectly — even so the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>, seated on that very seat, directly realized the <s>Catvāry Āryasatyāni</s> (Four Noble Truths): <s>duḥkha</s>, <s>samudaya</s>, <s>nirodha</s>, and <s>mārga</s>.

body.text: p.9.3/.atha prakṛtir bhikṣuṇī kṛṣṭa^dharmā prāpta^dharmā vidita^dharmā akopya^dharmā paryavasita^dharma^adhigata^artha^lābha^saṃvṛttā tīrṇa^kāṅkṣā^vicikitsā vigata^kathaṃkathā vaiśāradya^prāptā +apara^pratyayā +ananyaneyā śāstuḥ śāsane +anudharma^cāriṇī ājāneyamānā dharmeṣu bhagavataḥ pādayoḥ śirasā nipatya bhagavantam idam avocat/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>, having plowed the <s>Dharma</s>, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, having understood the <s>Dharma</s>, having reached the <s>Dharma</s> that is unshakable, having arrived at the accomplishment of the <s>Dharma</s> and the attainment of its meaning, having crossed beyond doubt and uncertainty, free from perplexity, having attained confidence, not depending on another, not led by another, practicing in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> in the teaching of the Master, and acknowledging (her attainment) in the <s>dharmas</s>, fell at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with her head and addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus:

body.text:
p.9.4/.atyayo me bhagavann atyayo me sugata/ yathā bālā yathā mūḍhā yathā +avyaktā yathā +akuśalā duṣprajña^jātīyā yāham ānandaṃ bhikṣuṃ svāmi^vādena samudācarṣaṃ/ sa^ahaṃ bhadantātyayamatyayataḥ paśyāmi/ atyayam atyayato dṛṣṭvā deśayāmi/ atyayam atyayata āviṣkaromi/ āyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpadye/ atas tasyā mama bhagavann atyayam atyayato jānātu pratigṛhṇātu
anukampām upādāya/ bhagavān āha/ āyatyāṃ saṃvarāya sthitvā tvaṃ prakṛte +atyayam atyayato +adhyāgamaḥ/ yathā bālā yathā mūḍhā yathā +avyaktā yathā +akuśalā duṣprajña^jātīya tvam ānandaṃ bhikṣuṃ svāmi^vādena (10) amudācarasi^iti/ yataś ca tvaṃ prakṛte +atyayaṃ jānāsi atyayaṃ paśyasi āyatyāṃ ca saṃvaram āpadyase, aham api te +atyayam atyayato gṛhṇāmi/ vṛddhir
eva te prakṛte pratikāṅkṣatavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na hāniḥ/
body.translated_text: "A transgression has been committed by me, <s>Bhagavān</s>! A transgression, <s>Sugata</s>! Foolish as I was, deluded, ignorant, unskilled, and of poor wisdom, I addressed the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ānanda</s> with the language of a husband. I, venerable sir, see my transgression as a transgression. Having seen it as a transgression, I confess it. I make my transgression manifest. For the future, I undertake restraint. Therefore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, let the <s>Bhagavān</s> know my transgression as a transgression, accept it, and show compassion." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Having resolved upon restraint for the future, you, <s>Prakṛti</s>, have acknowledged your transgression as a transgression — that, foolish, deluded, ignorant, unskilled, and of poor wisdom, you addressed the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ānanda</s> with the language of a husband. Since you, <s>Prakṛti</s>, know the transgression, see the transgression, and undertake restraint for the future, I too accept your transgression as a transgression. Growth alone, <s>Prakṛti</s>, is to be expected for you in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, not decline."

body.text:
p.10.1/.atha prakṛtir bhikṣuṇī bhagavatā^abhinanditā anuśiṣṭā ekāvyapakṛṣṭā +apramattā ātāpinī smṛtim atī saṃprajānā prahitāni viviktāni viharati sma/ yad arthaṃ kula^duhitaraḥ keśān avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā^āgārād anāgārikāṃ pravrajanti tadanuttara^brahmacarya^paryavasānaṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñaya sākṣāt kṛtya^upasaṃpadya
pravedayate sma/ kṣīṇā me jātir uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ na^aparamasmād bhavaṃ prajānāmi^iti/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>, having been commended and instructed by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, mindful, fully aware, with efforts exerted, in seclusion — for the very purpose for which daughters of good families, having cut their hair and donned saffron robes, go forth with perfect faith from the household life to homelessness — that unsurpassed consummation of the holy life, she herself, in this very life, directly knew, realized, and attained it, and she declared: "Birth is exhausted for me, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, I know no further existence beyond this."

body.text: p.10.2/.aśrauṣuḥ śrāvasteyakā brāhmaṇa^gṛhapatayo bhagavatā kila canḍāla^dārikā pravrājiteti/ śrutvā ca punar avadhyāyanti/ kathaṃ hi nāma caṇḍāla^dārikā bhikṣūṇāṃ samyakcaryāṃ cariṣyati/ bhikṣuṇīnām upāsakānām upāsikānāṃ samyak^caryāṃ cariṣyati/ kathaṃ hi nāma caṇḍāla^dārikā brahma^kṣatriya^gṛhapati^mahā^śāla^kuleṣu pravekṣyati/
body.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śrāvastī</s> heard: "The <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is said, has ordained an outcaste (<s>caṇḍāla</s>) girl!" Having heard this, they murmured disapprovingly: "How can an outcaste girl practice the proper conduct among <s>bhikṣus</s>? How can she practice proper conduct among <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, among male and female lay followers? How can an outcaste girl enter the households of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, householders, and great families?"

body.text: p.11.1/.aśrauṣīd rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavatā caṇḍāla^dārikā pravrājiteti/ śrutvā ca punar avadhyāyāti/ kathaṃ hi nāma caṇḍāla^dārikā bhikṣūṇāṃ samyak^caryāṃ cariṣyati/ bhikṣuṇīnām upāsakānām upāsikānāṃ samyak^caryāṃ cariṣyati/ kathaṃ brāhmaṇa^kṣatriya^gṛhapati^mahā^śāla^kuleṣu pravekṣyati/
body.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> heard: "The <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is said, has ordained an outcaste girl!" Having heard this, he too murmured disapprovingly: "How can an outcaste girl practice the proper conduct among <s>bhikṣus</s>? How can she practice proper conduct among <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, among male and female lay followers? How can she enter the households of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, householders, and great families?"

body.text:
p.11.2/.vimṛṣya ca bhadaraṃ yānaṃ yojayitvā bhadraṃ yānam abhiruhya saṃbahulaiś ca śrāvasteyair brāhmaṇa^gṛhapatibhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ śrāvastyā niryāti sma/ yena jetavanam anāthapiṇḍadasya^ārāmas tena^upasaṃkrāntaḥ/ tasya khalu yāvatī yānasya bhūmis tāvad yānena gatvā sa yānād avatīrya pattikāya^parivṛtaḥ pattikāya^puraskṛtaḥ padbhyām eva^ārāmaṃ prāvikṣat/
praviśya yena bhagavāṃs tena^upasaṃkrāntaḥ/ upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/ te +api saṃbahulāḥ śrāvasteyakā brāhmaṇa^kṣatirya^gṛhapatayo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā^ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/ apy aikatyā bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃrañjanīṃ saṃmodinīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya^ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/ apy aikasyā bhagavataḥ purataḥ
svakasvakāni mātā^paitṛkāṇi nāma^gotrāṇi anuśrāvya^ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/ apy aikatya yena bhagavāṃs tena^añjaliṃ praṇamya^ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/ apy aikatyās tūṣṇīṃ bhūtā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
body.translated_text: Having reflected, he had a fine carriage yoked, and mounting the fine carriage, surrounded and preceded by a great number of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, he set out from <s>Śrāvastī</s> toward the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Having gone by carriage as far as the ground was passable for the carriage, he descended from the carriage and, surrounded and preceded by a retinue on foot, entered the park on foot. Having entered, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he venerated the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with his head and sat down to one side. Those many <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and householders of <s>Śrāvastī</s> also, having venerated the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with their heads, sat down to one side. And some, having exchanged with the <s>Bhagavān</s> face-to-face various pleasing and delightful conversations, sat down to one side. And some, having announced their own maternal and paternal names and clan-names before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, sat down to one side. And some, having saluted the <s>Bhagavān</s> with joined palms, sat down to one side. And some sat down to one side in silence.

body.text: p.11.3/.atha bhagavān rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalam ārabhya teṣāṃ ca saṃbahulānāṃ śrāvasteyakānāṃ brāhmaṇa^kṣatriya^gṛhapatīnāṃ cetasā cittam ājñāya prakṛter bhikṣuṇyāḥ pūrvanivāsam ārabhya bhikṣūnām antrayate sma/ icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavas tathā^āgatasya sammukhaṃ prakṛter bhikṣuṇyāḥ pūrva^nivāsam ārabhya dharma^kathāṃ śrotum/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having comprehended with his mind the thoughts of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> and of those many <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and householders of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, beginning from the former lives of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>, addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: "Do you wish, <s>bhikṣus</s>, to hear a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> face-to-face from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, beginning from the former lives of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>?"

body.text:
p.11.4/.bhikṣavo bhagavantam āhuḥ / etasya bhagavan kāla etasya sugata samayo yad bhagavān prakṛter bhikṣuṇyāḥ pūrva^nivāsam ārabhya dharma^kathāṃ kathāyet/ yad bhagavataḥ (12) śrutvā bhikṣavo dhārayiṣyanti/ bhagavān āha/ tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye/ evaṃ sādhu bhagavann iti te bhikṣavo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣuḥ/ bhagavāṃs
tān idam avocat/
body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "This is the time, <s>Bhagavān</s>! This is the occasion, <s>Sugata</s>, for the <s>Bhagavān</s> to tell a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> beginning from the former lives of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Prakṛti</s>. Having heard from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>bhikṣus</s> will retain it." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Then listen, <s>bhikṣus</s>, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak." "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>!" — those <s>bhikṣus</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said to them thus:

body.text:
p.12.1/.bhūta^pūrvaṃ bhikṣavo +atīte +adhvani gaṅgā^taṭe +atimukta^kadalī^pāṭalaka^āmalakī vana^gahana^pradeśe tatra triśaṅkur nāma mātaṅga^rājaḥ prativasati sma/ saṃbahulaiś ca mātaṅga^sahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ/ sa punar bhikṣavas triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rajaḥ pūrva^janma^adhītān vedān samanusmarati sma sa^aṅga^upāṅgān sarahasyān sanighaṇṭa^kaiṭabhān sa^akṣara^prabhedān
itihāsa^pañca^mānanyāni ca śāstrāṇi/ padako vaiyākaraṇo lokāyata^yajña^mantre mahā^puruṣa^lakṣaṇe niṣṇāto niṣkāṅkṣo bhāṣyaṃ ca yathārdharmaṃ veda^vrata^padāny anuśrutaṃ ca bhāṣate sma/
body.translated_text: "Once upon a time, <s>bhikṣus</s>, in a past age, on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in a forest region dense with <s>atimukta</s>, banana, <s>pāṭalaka</s>, and <s>āmalakī</s> trees, there dwelt a <s>Māṭaṅga</s> king named <s>Triśaṅku</s>, together with many thousands of <s>Māṭaṅgas</s>. Now, <s>bhikṣus</s>, this <s>Māṭaṅga</s> king <s>Triśaṅku</s> used to recollect the <s>Vedas</s> that he had studied in a previous birth — with their <s>aṅgas</s> (limbs) and <s>upāṅgas</s> (sub-limbs), with their secrets, with their glossaries and indices, with their phonetic analyses, together with the <s>itihāsas</s> (histories) and the five sciences. He was a reciter, a grammarian, proficient in the <s>Lokāyata</s> and sacrificial <s>mantras</s>, accomplished and free from doubt in the marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), and he spoke the commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) according to the true <s>Dharma</s>, the precepts of the <s>Vedic</s> observances, and the traditions.

body.text: p.12.2/.tasya triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rājasya śārdūakarṇo nāma kumāro +abhūd utpannaḥ/ rūpataś ca kulataś ca śīlataś ca guṇataś ca sarva^guṇaiś ca^upeto +abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paramayā śubha^varṇa^puṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ/
body.translated_text: To this <s>Māṭaṅga</s> king <s>Triśaṅku</s>, a son was born named Prince <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> — endowed with form, lineage, character, virtue, and all qualities, handsome, pleasing to behold, inspiring confidence, graced with the highest excellence of beautiful complexion.

body.text: p.12.3/.atha triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rājaḥ/śārdūlakarṇaṃ kumāraṃ pūrva^janmādhītān vedān adhyāpayati sma/ yad uta sa^aṅga^upāṅgān sarahasyān sanighaṇṭa^kaiṭabhān sa^akṣara^prabhedān itihāsa^pañca^mānanyāni ca śāstrāṇi bhāṣyaṃ ca yathā^dharmaṃ veda^vrata^padāni/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> king <s>Triśaṅku</s> taught Prince <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> the <s>Vedas</s> that he had studied in a previous birth — with their <s>aṅgas</s> and <s>upāṅgas</s>, with their secrets, with their glossaries and indices, with their phonetic analyses, together with the <s>itihāsas</s> and the five sciences, the commentary according to the true <s>Dharma</s>, and the precepts of the <s>Vedic</s> observances.

body.text:
p.12.4/.atha triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya^etad abhavat/ ayaṃ mama putraḥ śārdūlakarṇo nāma kumāraḥ/ upeto rūpataś ca kulataś ca śīlataś ca guṇataś ca/ sarva^guṇa^upeto +abhirūpo (13) darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paramayā ca varṇa^puṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ/ cīrṇa^vrato +adhīta^mantro veda^pāragaḥ/ samayo +ayaṃ yan ny aham asya niveśana^dharmaṃ kariṣye/ tat kuto ny
avaṃ śārdūlakarṇasya putrasya śīlavatīṃ guṇavatīṃ rūpavatīṃ pratirūpāṃ prajāvatīṃ labheyam iti/checked
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Māṭaṅga</s> king <s>Triśaṅku</s> thought thus: "This son of mine, Prince <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>, is endowed with form, lineage, character, and virtue. Possessing all qualities, he is handsome, pleasing to behold, inspiring confidence, graced with the highest excellence of complexion. He has completed his vows, studied the <s>mantras</s>, and reached the far shore of the <s>Vedas</s>. It is now time for me to arrange his marriage. Where then might I find for my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> a girl who is virtuous, possessed of good qualities, beautiful, suitable, and capable of bearing children?"

body.text: p.13.1/.tasmin khalu samaye puṣkarasārī nāma brāhmaṇa utkūṭaṃ nāma droṇa^mukhaṃ paribhuṅkte sma/ samapta^utsadaṃ sa^tṛṇa^kāṣṭha^udakaṃ dhānya^sahagataṃ rājñā +agnidattena brahma^deyaṃ dattam/
body.translated_text: At that time, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> was enjoying a <s>droṇamukha</s> (district) called <s>Utkūṭa</s>. It had been given as a <s>brahmadeya</s> (Brahmanical grant) by King <s>Agnidatta</s>, complete with its outlying areas, together with grass, wood, and water, and accompanied by grain.

body.text:
p.13.2/.puṣkarasārī punar brāhmaṇa upetaḥ mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaḥ saṃśuddho gṛhiṇyāmanākṣipto jātivādena gotra^vādena yāvad āsaptamamātāmahapitāmahaṃ/ yugapad upādhyāyo +adhyāpako mantra^dharas trayāṇāṃ vedānāṃ pāragaḥ sa^aṅga^upāṅgānāṃ sarahasyānāṃ sanighaṇṭa^kaiṭabhānāṃ sa^akṣara^prabhedānām itihāsa^pañca^mānāṃ sadṛśa^vyākartā padako vaiyākaraṇaḥ/
lokāyata^yajña^mantra^mahā^puruṣa^lakṣaṇeṣu pāragaḥ/ sphītam utkūṭaṃ nāma droṇa^mukhaṃ paribhuṅkte/
body.translated_text: <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, was well-born on both his mother's and father's side, of pure descent, unchallenged by his wife with respect to birth or lineage up to the seventh generation on both maternal and paternal sides. He was simultaneously a teacher, an instructor, a keeper of mantras, accomplished in the three <s>Vedas</s> together with their <s>aṅgas</s> (limbs) and <s>upāṅgas</s> (sub-limbs), with their secret teachings, with the <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> [glossaries], with the analysis of syllables, with the <s>Itihāsas</s> as the fifth; he was an able expounder, a <s>padaka</s> (expert in word analysis), and a grammarian. He was accomplished in <s>Lokāyata</s> (worldly philosophy), sacrificial mantras, and the marks of a great person. He enjoyed the prosperous <s>droṇamukha</s> called <s>Utkūṭa</s>.

body.text: p.13.3/.puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya prakṛtir nāma māṇavikā duhitā bhūtā/ upetā rūpataś ca kulataś ca śīlataś ca guṇataś ca/ sarva^guṇa^upetā +abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā paramayā varṇa^puṣkalatayā samanvāgatā śīlavatī guṇavatī/
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> had a daughter, a young woman named <s>Prakṛti</s>. She was endowed with beauty, family, virtue, and good qualities — possessed of all qualities, lovely, beautiful, pleasing, endowed with the highest excellence of complexion, virtuous, and full of good qualities.

body.text: p.13.4/.atha triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya^etad abhavat/ asty uttara^pūrveṇa^utkūṭo nāma droṇa^mukhaḥ, tatra puṣkarasāro nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati/ upeto mātṛtaḥ pitṛto (14) yāvat tatraivedike pravacane vistareṇa/ sa ca^utkūṭaṃ droṇa^mukhaṃ paribhṅkte/ sasapta^utsadaṃ satṛṇa^kāṣṭha^udakaṃ dhānya^bhogaiḥ sahagataṃ rājñā +agnidattena brahma^deyaṃ dattam/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, thought thus: 'To the northeast there is a <s>droṇamukha</s> called <s>Utkūṭa</s>; there dwells a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, well-born on both his mother's and father's side' — and so on in detail as in the Vedic teaching. 'And he enjoys the <s>droṇamukha</s> <s>Utkūṭa</s>, complete with its seven outlying areas, together with grass, wood, and water, accompanied by grain revenues, given as a <s>brahmadeya</s> by King <s>Agnidatta</s>.'

body.text: p.14.1/.tasya puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya prakṛtir nāma māṇavikā duhitā upetā rūpataś ca kulataś ca śīlataś ca sarva^guṇa^upetā +abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā paramayā varṇa^puṣkalatayā samanvāgatā/ śīlavatī guṇavatī putrasya me śārdūlakarṇasya pratirūpā patnī bhaviṣyatiti/
body.translated_text: 'This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> has a daughter, a young woman named <s>Prakṛti</s>, endowed with beauty, family, virtue — possessed of all qualities, lovely, beautiful, pleasing, endowed with the highest excellence of complexion, virtuous, full of good qualities. She would be a fitting wife for my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>.'

body.text: p.14.2/.atra triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rāja etam evārthaṃ bahulaṃ rātrau cintayitvā vitarkya tasyā eva rātryā atyayāt pratyūṣa^kāla^samaye sarva^śvetaṃ vaḍavā ratham abhiruhya mahatā śvapākagaṇenāmātyagaṇena parivṛtaś caṇḍāla^kula^nagarān niṣkramya^uttarena prāgacchadyenotkūṭaṃ droṇa^mukham/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, having pondered this very matter extensively during the night and deliberated, at the passing of that very night, at the time of dawn, mounted an all-white chariot drawn by mares, and surrounded by a great assembly of <s>Śvapākas</s> (outcaste attendants) and a retinue of ministers, he departed from the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> capital city and proceeded northward toward the <s>droṇamukha</s> <s>Utkūṭa</s>.

body.text: p.14.3/.atha triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rāja utkūṭasya^uttarapūrveṇa sumanaskaṃ nāma^udyānaṃ nānā^vṛkṣa^saṃcchannaṃ nānā^vṛkṣa^kusumitaṃ nānā^dvijanikūjitaṃ nandanam iva devānāṃ tad upasaṃkrāntaḥ/ upasaṃkramya brāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇam āgamayamāno +asthāt/ brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī māṇavakān mantrān vācayitum ihāgamiṣyati^iti/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, went to a garden called <s>Sumanaska</s>, to the northeast of <s>Utkūṭa</s>, covered with various trees, blossoming with various flowers, resounding with the songs of various birds, like <s>Nandana</s>, the garden of the gods. Having arrived there, he waited for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> [thinking]: 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> will come here to make the young men recite mantras.'

body.text: p.14.4/.atha brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī tasyā eva rātryā atyayāt sarva^śvetaṃ vaḍavāratham abhiruhya śiṣyagaṇaprivṛtaḥ pañca^mātrair māṇavaka^śateḥ puraskṛta utkūṭān niryti sma, brāhmaṇakān mantrān vācayitum/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, at the passing of that very night, mounted an all-white chariot drawn by mares, and surrounded by his group of disciples, preceded by some five hundred young students, set forth from <s>Utkūṭa</s> to make the Brahmanical students recite mantras.

body.text:
p.15.1/.adrākṣīt triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rājo brāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇaṃ sūryam iva^udayantaṃ tejasā jvalantam iva hutavahaṃ yajñam iva brāhmaṇa^parivṛtaṃ śakram iva deva^gaṇaparivṛtaṃ haimavantam ivauṣadhibhiḥ samudram iva ratnaiś candram iva nakṣatrair vaiśravaṇam iva yakṣa^gaṇair brahmāṇam iva deva^rṣigaṇaiḥ parivṛtaṃ śobhamānaṃ/ dūrata evāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā
cainaṃ pratyudgamya yathā^dharmaṃ kṛtvedam avocat/
body.translated_text: <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, saw the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> — like the sun rising, blazing with splendor like fire, surrounded by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> like a sacrifice, surrounded by his company of gods like <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), like the <s>Himavān</s> (Himālaya) with its herbs, like the ocean with its jewels, like the moon with its constellations, like <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) surrounded by hosts of <s>Yakṣas</s>, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by hosts of divine sages, resplendent. Having seen him approaching from a distance, he went out to meet him and, having paid due respects, said this:

body.text: p.15.2/.ahaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin svāgatam āyāhi/ kāryaṃ ca te vakṣyāmi tac chrūyatāṃ/ evam ukte brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī triśaṅkumātaṅga^rājam idam avocat/
body.translated_text: 'Sir <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, welcome! Come! I shall tell you my business — please hear it.' Thus addressed, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> said this to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king:

body.text: p.15.3/.na hi bhos triśaṅko śakyaṃ brāhmaṇena saha bhoḥ kāraṃ kartuṃ/
body.translated_text: 'Sir <s>Triśaṅku</s>, it is not possible for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> to use the address "sir" [with you].'

body.text:
p.15.4/.ahaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin śaknomi bhoḥ kāraṃ kartuṃ/ yacchakyaṃ me kartuṃ bhavati naiva tacchakyaṃ te kartuṃ/ api tu catvāro bhoḥ puṣkarasārin puruṣasya kāryasamārambhāḥ pūrva^samārabdhā bhavanti/ yad uta ātmārthaṃ vā parārthaṃ vātmīyārthaṃ (16) vā sarva^bhūta^saṃgrahārthaṃ vā/ idaṃ ca^atra mahattaraṃ kāryaṃ yat te vyākhyāsyāmi tac chrūyatāṃ/ putrāya
me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaram utsṛja bhāryā^arthāya/ yāvantaṃ kula^śulkaṃ manyase tāvantaṃ dāsyāmi/
body.translated_text: 'Sir <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I am able to use the address "sir." What I can do, you cannot do. But listen, sir <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, there are four kinds of undertakings that a man begins: namely, for one's own sake, for another's sake, for the sake of one's own people, or for the welfare of all beings. And here is a greater matter which I shall explain to you — please hear it. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as a wife. Whatever you consider the appropriate bride-price, that much I shall give.'

body.text: p.16.1/.idaṃ ca khalu punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya bhṛśaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī abhiṣaktaḥ kupitaś caṇḍībhūto +anāttamanāḥ kopaṃ ca kveṣaṃ ca mrakṣyaṃ ca tatpratyayāt saṃjanayitvā lalāṭe triśikhāṃ bhṛkuṭiṃ kṛtvā kaṇṭhaṃ dhamayitvā +akṣiṇī parivartya nakula^piṅgalāṃ dṛṣṭim utpādya triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅga^rājam idam avocat/
body.translated_text: Upon hearing this speech of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> was greatly offended, angered, become furious, displeased; and having generated anger, rage, and wrath in response to that, having knitted his brows into a triple-peaked frown on his forehead, having puffed up his throat, having rolled his eyes and produced a glare tawny like a mongoose's, he said this to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king:

body.text: p.16.2/.dhig grāmyaviṣaya/ caṇḍāla/ nedaṃ śvapākavacanaṃ yuktaṃ/ yastvaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ veda^pāragaṃ hīnaś caṇḍāla^yonijo bhūtvā icchasy avamardituṃ/ bho durmate/
body.translated_text: 'Shame on you, rustic sensualist! <s>Caṇḍāla</s>! This speech of a <s>Śvapāka</s> (dog-cooker) is not proper — you who, being a lowly one born of <s>Caṇḍāla</s> birth, wish to trample upon a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has mastered the <s>Vedas</s>! You wicked-minded one!'

body.text: p.16.3ab/.prakṛtiṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi; ātmānaṃ ca^abhimanyase/
body.translated_text: You do not know your own nature, and you think too highly of yourself;

body.text: p.16.3cd/.bāla^agre sarṣapaṃ mā bho sthāpaya(mā)kleśam āgamaḥ/
body.translated_text: do not place a mustard seed on the tip of a needle, sir — let trouble not come!

body.text: p.16.4ab/.mā prārthayā +aprārthanīyāṃ vāyuṃ pāśena bandhaya/
body.translated_text: Do not seek what should not be sought — [it is like trying to] bind the wind with a noose!

body.text: p.17.1ab/. na hi cāmī^karaṃ mūḍha bhaved bhasma kadācana/
body.translated_text: For gold, O fool, can never become ashes;

body.text: p.17.1cd/.prakāśe bāndhakāre kiṃ viśeṣo nopalabhyate//
body.translated_text: between light and darkness, is not a difference perceived?

body.text: p.17.2ab/.caṇḍāla^yonijas tvaṃ hi dvijātiḥ punar apy ahaṃ/
body.translated_text: You are born of <s>Caṇḍāla</s> birth, while I am a twice-born;

body.text: p.17.2cd/.hīnaḥ śreṣṭhena sambandhaṃ mūḍha prāthayase kathaṃ//
body.translated_text: how, O fool, do you, a low one, seek alliance with a superior?

body.text: p.17.3ab/.caṇḍāla^yonibhūtas tvam aham asmi dvijātijaḥ/
body.translated_text: You are born of <s>Caṇḍāla</s> birth; I am born of the twice-born;

body.text: p.17.3cd/.na hi śreṣṭhaḥ prahīnena sambandhaṃ kartum icchati//
body.translated_text: a superior does not wish to form an alliance with an inferior.

body.text: p.17.4ab/.śreṣṭhāḥ śreṣṭhair hi sambandhaṃ kurvantīha dvijātayaḥ/
body.translated_text: The superior twice-born form alliances with the superior —

body.text: p.17.4cd/.vidyayā ye tu sampannāḥ saṃśuddhaś caraṇena ca//
body.translated_text: those who are accomplished in learning and purified in conduct,

body.text: p.17.5ab/.jātyā caivān abhikṣiptā mantraiḥ paramatāṃ gatāḥ/
body.translated_text: unchallenged in birth, who have attained the highest state through mantras,

body.text: p.17.5cd/.adhyāpakā mantra^dharās triṣu vedeṣu pāragāḥ//
body.translated_text: who are teachers, keepers of mantras, accomplished in the three <s>Vedas</s>,

body.text: p.17.6ab/.nighaṇṭakaiṭabhān vedān brāhmaṇa ye hy adhīyate/
body.translated_text: who study the <s>Vedas</s> with the <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> glossaries —

body.text: p.17.6cd/.tais tādṛśair hi sambandhaṃ kurvantīha dvijātayaḥ//
body.translated_text: with such ones do the twice-born form alliances here.

body.text: p.17.7ab/.na hi śreṣṭho hi hīnena sambandhaṃ kartum icchati/
body.translated_text: A superior does not wish to form an alliance with an inferior;

body.text: p.17.7cd/.prārthayase +aprārthanīyāṃ vāyuṃ pāśena bandhituṃ//
body.translated_text: you seek what should not be sought — [it is like trying to] bind the wind with a noose.

body.text: p.17.8ab/.yad asmābhiś ca sambandham iha tvaṃ kartum icchasi/
body.translated_text: That you wish to form an alliance with us here —

body.text: p.17.8cd/.jugupsitaḥ sarva^loke kṛpaṇaḥpuruṣādhamaḥ/
body.translated_text: you are despised in all the world, wretched, the lowest of men!

body.text: p.17.8ef/.gaccha tvaṃ vṛṣala kṣipraṃ kim asmān avamanyase//
body.translated_text: Go away quickly, you <s>Vṛṣala</s> (low-caste one)! Why do you disrespect us?

body.text: p.18.1ab/.caṇḍālāḥ saha caṇḍālaiḥ pukkaśāḥ saha pukkaśaiḥ/
body.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍālas</s> [marry] with <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, <s>Pukkaśas</s> with <s>Pukkaśas</s> —

body.text: p.18.1cd/.kurvantīhaiva sambandhaṃ jātibhir jātir eva ca//
body.translated_text: they form alliances here, caste with caste indeed.

body.text: p.18.2ab/.brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyaiḥ saha/
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s> with <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,

body.text: p.18.2cd/.sārdhaṃ vaiśyās tathā vaiśyaiḥ śūdrāḥ śūdrais tathā saha//
body.translated_text: <s>Vaiśyas</s> with <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> with <s>Śūdras</s> —

body.text: p.18.3ab/.sadṛśāḥ sadṛśaiḥ sārdham āvahanti parasparaṃ/
body.translated_text: equals marry among themselves, mutually;

body.text: p.18.3cd/.na hi kurvanti caṇḍālāḥ sambandhaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha//
body.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍālas</s> do not form alliances with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: p.18.4ab/.sarva^jātivihīno +asi sarva^varṇa^jugupsitaḥ/
body.translated_text: You are devoid of all caste, despised by all classes —

body.text: p.18.4cd/.kathaṃ hīnaś ca śreṣṭhena sambandhaṃ kartum icchasi//
body.translated_text: how do you, a low one, wish to form an alliance with a superior?'

body.text: p.18.5/.idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇasya puṣkarasāriṇas triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rāja idam avocat/
body.translated_text: Having heard this further speech of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, said this:

body.text: p.18.6ab/.yathā bhasmani sauvarṇe viśeṣa; upalabhyate/
body.translated_text: 'Just as a difference is perceived between ashes and gold,

body.text: p.18.6cd/.brāhmaṇe vānya^jātau vā na viśeṣo +asti vai tathā//
body.translated_text: such a difference does not exist between a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and one of another caste.

body.text: p.18.7ab/.yathā prakāśatamasor viśeṣa; upalabhyate/
body.translated_text: Just as a difference is perceived between light and darkness,

body.text: p.18.7cd/.brāhmaṇe vānya^jātau vā na viśeṣo +asti vai tathā//
body.translated_text: such a difference does not exist between a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and one of another caste.

body.text: p.18.8ab/.na hi brāhmaṇa; ākāśān maruto vā samutthitaḥ/
body.translated_text: For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> did not arise from the sky or from the wind,

body.text: p.18.8cd/.bhitvā vā pṛthivīṃ jāto jāta^vedā yathāraṇeḥ//
body.translated_text: nor was he born by splitting the earth, as fire is born from the fire-stick.

body.text: p.18.9ab/.brāhmaṇā yonito jātāś caṇḍālā; api yonitaḥ/
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are born from the womb, and <s>Caṇḍālas</s> too from the womb —

body.text: p.18.9cd/.śreṣṭhatve vṛṣalatve ca kiṃ vā paśyasi kāraṇaṃ//
body.translated_text: what reason do you see for superiority or inferiority?

body.text: p.18.10ab/.brāhmaṇo +api mṛtotsṛṣṭo jugupsyo +aśucir ucyate/
body.translated_text: Even a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, when dead and abandoned, is called impure and loathsome;

body.text: p.18.10cd/.varṇās tathā^eva vā^apy anye kā nu tatra viśeṣatā//
body.translated_text: so too are all the other classes — what distinction is there then?

body.text: p.19.1ab/.yat kiñ cit pāpakaṃ karma kilviṣaṃ kalir eva ca/
body.translated_text: Whatever sinful deed, whatever transgression and strife there is

body.text: p.19.1cd/.sattvānām upaghātāya brāhmaṇais tat prakāśitaṃ//
body.translated_text: for the harm of beings — that was devised by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: p.19.2ab/.iti karmāṇi ca^etāni prakāśitāni brāhmaṇaiḥ/
body.translated_text: These rituals were devised by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

body.text: p.19.2cd/.karmabhir dāruṇaiś ca^api ``puṇyo +ahaṃ'' brūvate dvijāḥ//
body.translated_text: and even with cruel rites, the twice-born say "I am pure."

body.text: p.19.3ab/.māṃsaṃ khāditukāmais tu brāhmaṇair upakalpitaṃ/
body.translated_text: By <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who wished to eat meat, it was devised

body.text: p.19.3cd/.mantrair hi prokṣitāḥ santaḥ svargaṃ gacchanty ajaiḍakāḥ//
body.translated_text: that goats and sheep, when consecrated with mantras, go to heaven.

body.text: p.19.4ab/.yady eṣa mārgaḥ svartāya kasmān na brāhmaṇā hy amī/
body.translated_text: If this is the path to heaven, why do not these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>

body.text: p.19.4cd/.ātmānam athavā bandhūn mantraiḥ saṃprokṣayanti vai//
body.translated_text: consecrate themselves or their kinsmen with mantras?

body.text: p.19.5ab/.mātaraṃ pitaraṃ ca^eva bhrātaraṃ bhaginīṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: Their mother, father, brother, sister,

body.text: p.19.5cd/.putraṃ duhitaraṃ bhāryāṃ dvijā na prokṣayanty amī//
body.translated_text: son, daughter, wife — these twice-born do not consecrate [for sacrifice].

body.text: p.19.6ab/.mitraṃ jñātiṃ sakhīṃ vā^api ye vā viṣayavāsinaḥ/
body.translated_text: A friend, a relative, a companion, or even those dwelling in the realm —

body.text: p.19.6cd/.prokṣitās te +api vā mantraiḥ sarve yāsyanti sadgatiṃ//
body.translated_text: if consecrated with mantras, they too would all go to a good destination.

body.text: p.19.7ab/.sarve yajñaiḥ samāhutā gamiṣyanti satāṃ gatiṃ/
body.translated_text: All, having been offered in sacrifices, would go to the abode of the righteous —

body.text: p.19.7cd/.paśubhiḥ kiṃ nu bho yaṣṭair ātmānaṃ kiṃ na yakṣyase//
body.translated_text: what then is the point of sacrificial animals? Why will you not sacrifice yourself?

body.text: p.19.8ab/.na prokṣaṇair na mantraiś ca svargaṃ gacchanty ajaiḍakāḥ/
body.translated_text: Not by consecrations nor by mantras do goats and sheep go to heaven;

body.text: p.19.8cd/.na hy eṣa mārgaḥ svargāya mithyāprokṣaṇam ucyate//
body.translated_text: this is not the path to heaven — the consecration is called false.

body.text: p.19.9ab/.brāhmaṇair audracittais tu paryāyo hy eṣa cintitaḥ/
body.translated_text: By <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of cruel mind, this system was devised;

body.text: p.19.9cd/.māṃsaṃ khāditukāmais tu prokṣaṇaṃ kalpitaṃ paśoḥ//
body.translated_text: by those who wished to eat meat, the consecration of animals was contrived.

body.text: p.19.10ab/.anyac ca^ahaṃ pravakṣyāmi brāhmaṇair yat prakalpitaṃ/
body.translated_text: And I shall speak of something else that was devised by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>:

body.text: p.19.10cd/.pātakā hi samākhyātā brāhmaṇeṣu catur^vidhāḥ//
body.translated_text: four kinds of mortal sins are declared among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: p.20.1ab/.suvarṇa^cauryaṃ madyaṃ ca guru^dārā^abhimardanaṃ/
body.translated_text: Stealing gold, drinking liquor, violating the teacher's wife,

body.text: p.20.1cd/.brahmāghnatā ca catvāraḥ pātakā brāhmaṇeṣv amī//
body.translated_text: and killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — these are the four mortal sins among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: p.20.2ab/.suvarṇa^haraṇaṃ varjyaṃ steyam anyanna vidyate/
body.translated_text: Stealing gold is forbidden, but other theft is not [considered wrong];

body.text: p.20.2cd/.suvarṇaṃ yo hared vipraḥ sa tena +abrāhmaṇo bhavet//
body.translated_text: a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who steals gold — by that he ceases to be a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text:
p.20.3ab/.surāpānaṃ na pātavyam anyapānaṃ yatheṣṭataḥ/
p.20.3cd/.surāṃ tu yaḥ pived vipraḥ sa tena^abrāhmaṇo bhavet//
body.translated_text: Liquor should not be drunk, but other drink is permitted at will; a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who drinks liquor — by that he ceases to be a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text: p.20.4ab/.guru^dārā na gantavyā; anyadārā yatheṣṭataḥ/
body.translated_text: The teacher's wife should not be approached, but other women at will;

body.text: p.20.4cd/.guru^dārāṃ tu yo gacchet sa tena^abrāhmaṇo bhavet//
body.translated_text: a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who approaches the teacher's wife — by that he ceases to be a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text: p.20.5ab/.na hanyād brāhmaṇaṃ hy ekaṃ hanyād anyān anekaśaḥ/
body.translated_text: One should not kill a single <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, but may kill others in multitudes;

body.text: p.20.5cd/.hayātta brāhmaṇaṃ yo vai sa tena^abrāhmaṇo bhavet//
body.translated_text: he who kills a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — by that he ceases to be a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text: p.20.6ab/.ity ete pātakā hy uktā brāhmaṇeṣu catur^vidhāḥ/
body.translated_text: Thus these four kinds of transgressions against <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> have been declared;

body.text: p.20.6cd/.bhavanty abrāhmaṇā yena tato +anye +apātakāḥ smṛtāḥ//
body.translated_text: by which one becomes a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — others are considered lesser offenses.

body.text: p.20.7ab/.kṛtvā caturṇam ekaikaṃ bhaved abrāhmaṇas tu saḥ/
body.translated_text: Having committed any one of these four, one becomes a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

body.text: p.20.7cd/.labhate na ca sāmīcīṃ brāhmaṇāṇāṃ samāgame/
body.translated_text: and does not receive the proper reception in an assembly of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;

body.text: p.20.7ef/.āsanaṃ ca^udakaṃ ca^eva vyutthānaṃ sa na ca^arhati//
body.translated_text: neither a seat, nor water, nor the honor of others rising — he is not worthy of these.

body.text: p.20.8ab/.tasya niḥsaranaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ patitasya tu/
body.translated_text: But a means of restoration for one who has fallen has been seen by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>:

body.text: p.20.8cd/.vrataṃ vai sa samādāya punar brāhmaṇatāṃ vrajet//
body.translated_text: having undertaken a vow, he may regain the status of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text: p.20.9ab/.asau dvādaśa^varṣāṇi dhārayitvā kharājinaṃ/
body.translated_text: He should wear the hide of a donkey for twelve years,

body.text: p.20.9cd/.khāṭvāṅgam ucchritaṃ kṛtvā mṛtaśīrṣe ca bhojanaṃ//
body.translated_text: carrying a raised skull-staff (<s>khaṭvāṅga</s>) and eating from a skull;

body.text: p.21.1ab/.etad vrataṃ samādāya niścayena nirantaraṃ/
body.translated_text: having undertaken this vow resolutely and without interruption,

body.text: p.21.1cd/.pūrṇe dvādaśame varṣe punar brāhmaṇatāṃ vrajet//
body.translated_text: at the completion of the twelfth year, he may regain the status of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text: p.21.2ab/.iti niḥsaraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇais tu tapasvibhiḥ/
body.translated_text: Thus the means of restoration has been seen by the ascetic <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

body.text: p.21.2cd/.kumārgagāmibhir mūḍhair aniḥsaraṇadarśibhiḥ//
body.translated_text: but the deluded who follow wrong paths see no such means of restoration.

body.text:
p.21.3/ tad idaṃ brāhmaṇa te bravīmi, saṃjñāmātrakam idaṃ lokasya yad idam ucyate brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra ity vā/ sarvam idam ekam eveti vijñaya putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ māṇavikāmanuprayaccha bhāryā^arthāya/ yāvantaṃ kula^śulkaṃ manyase tāvantam anupradāsyāmi/ idaṃ ca khalu punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya
brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī abhiṣaktaḥ kupitaś caṇḍībhūto +anāttamanāḥ kopaṃ ca dveṣaṃ ca catpratyayaṃ janayitvā lalāṭe triśikhāṃ bhṛkuṭiṃ kṛtvā kaṇṭhaṃ (22) dhamayitvā +akṣiṇī parivartya nakula^piṅgalāṃ dūṣṭim utpādya triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅga^rājam idam avocat/
body.translated_text: Now I say this to you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: it is merely a conventional designation of the world when one speaks of '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,' or '<s>Kṣatriya</s>,' or '<s>Vaiśya</s>,' or '<s>Śūdra</s>.' Knowing that all this is one and the same, give the maiden, your daughter by nature, to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as his wife. Whatever you consider the appropriate bride-price, I shall give that much. Upon hearing this renewed speech of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, king of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, feeling insulted, became angry, fierce, and displeased; and having generated wrath, hatred, and resentment, furrowing his brow into three-pointed wrinkles on his forehead, puffing out his throat, rolling his eyes and casting a fierce mongoose-tawny glance, he spoke thus to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, king of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>:

body.text: p.22.1ab/.asamīkṣyaitattvayā hi kṛtā saṃjñeyam īdṛśī/
body.translated_text: Without proper examination, this kind of declaration has been made by you:

body.text: p.22.1cd/.ekaiva jātir loke +asmin sāmānyā na pṛthag^vidhā//
body.translated_text: 'There is only one birth-class in this world, common to all, not of different kinds.'

body.text: p.22.2ab/.kathaṃ śvapāka^jātīyo brāhmaṇaṃ veda^pāragaṃ/
body.translated_text: How can one born of the <s>Śvapāka</s> (dog-cooker) caste dare to challenge a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has mastered the <s>Vedas</s>?

body.text: p.22.2cd/.nihīnayonijo bhūtvā vimarditum iha^icchasi//
body.translated_text: Being born from a low womb, you wish to trample upon him here!

body.text:
p.22.3/.rājānaḥ khalu vṛṣala prati[vi]bhāgajñā bhavanti/ tad yathā deśa^dharme vā nagara^dharme vā grāma^dharme vā nigamadhama vā śulka^dharme vā āvāha^dharme vā vivāha^dharme vā pūrva^karmasu vā/ catvāra ime vṛṣala varṇāḥ/ yad uta brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdra iti/ teṣāṃ vivāha^dharmeṣu catasro bhāryā brāhmaṇasya bhavanti/ tad yathā brāhmaṇī kṣatriyā
vaiśyā śūdrī ceti/ tisraḥ kṣatriyasya bhāryā bhavanti/ kṣatriyā vaiśyā śūdrī ceti/ vaiśyasya dve bhārye bhavataḥ/ vaiśyā śūdrī ceti/ śūdrasya av ekā bhāryā bhavati śūdrī eva/ evaṃ brāhmaṇasya vṛṣala catvāraḥ putrā bhavanti/tad yathā brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdraś ceti/ kṣatriyasya trayaḥ putrāḥ, kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdra iti/ vaiśyasya dvau putrau, vaiśyaḥ
śūdra iti/ śūdrasya tv eka eva putro bhavati yad uta śūdra eva/
body.translated_text: Kings, O <s>Vṛṣala</s> (low-born), are knowledgeable about distinctions — namely in matters of regional law, city law, village law, market-town law, customs-duty law, the law of taking a bride, the law of giving in marriage, and in prior deeds. There are four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), O <s>Vṛṣala</s> — namely <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>. In matters of marriage law, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has four wives — namely a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, a <s>Kṣatriyā</s>, a <s>Vaiśyā</s>, and a <s>Śūdrī</s>. A <s>Kṣatriya</s> has three wives — a <s>Kṣatriyā</s>, a <s>Vaiśyā</s>, and a <s>Śūdrī</s>. A <s>Vaiśya</s> has two wives — a <s>Vaiśyā</s> and a <s>Śūdrī</s>. A <s>Śūdra</s> has only one wife — a <s>Śūdrī</s> alone. Thus, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, O <s>Vṛṣala</s>, has four sons — namely a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a <s>Vaiśya</s>, and a <s>Śūdra</s>. A <s>Kṣatriya</s> has three sons — a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a <s>Vaiśya</s>, and a <s>Śūdra</s>. A <s>Vaiśya</s> has two sons — a <s>Vaiśya</s> and a <s>Śūdra</s>. A <s>Śūdra</s>, however, has only one son — a <s>Śūdra</s> alone.

body.text: p.22.4/.te brāhmaṇāḥ punar vṛṣala brahmaṇaḥ putrāḥ/ aurasā mukhato jātāḥ/ urasto bāhutaḥ kṣatriyāḥ/ nābhito vaiśyāḥ/ padbhyāṃ śūdrāḥ/
body.translated_text: Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, O <s>Vṛṣala</s>, are the sons of <s>Brahmā</s> — born legitimately from his mouth. The <s>Kṣatriyas</s> from his chest and arms; the <s>Vaiśyas</s> from his navel; the <s>Śūdras</s> from his feet.

body.text: p.22.5/.brahmaṇā^ayaṃ khalu vṛṣala lokaḥ sarva^bhūtāni nirmitāni/
body.translated_text: By <s>Brahmā</s>, O <s>Vṛṣala</s>, this world and all beings were created.

body.text: p.23.1ab/.tasya jyeṣṭhā vayaṃ putrāḥ kṣatriyās tad anantaraṃ/
body.translated_text: We are his eldest sons; the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> come next after us;

body.text: p.23.1cd/.vaiśyāstritīyakā varṇāḥ śūdranāmnā caturthakaḥ// iti//
body.translated_text: the <s>Vaiśyas</s> are the third class, and the fourth is named <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text: p.23.2/.sa tvaṃ vṛṣala caturthe +api varṇe na saṃdṛśyase/ ahaṃ ca^agre varṇe śreṣṭhe varṇe parame varṇe pravare varṇe/ paramārthaṃ ca saṃyogamākāṅkṣasi praṇaśya tvaṃ vṛṣala kṣipraṃ / mā ca^asmākam avamaṃsthāḥ/
body.translated_text: You, O <s>Vṛṣala</s>, are not even counted among the fourth <s>varṇa</s>. And I belong to the foremost class, the highest class, the supreme class, the most excellent class. Yet you desire a union with us! Perish quickly, O <s>Vṛṣala</s>! And do not hold us in contempt!

body.text: p.23.3/.idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇasya puṣkarasāriṇas triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rāja idam avocat/ idam atra brāhmaṇa śṛṇu yad bravīmi/ brahmaṇā^ayaṃ lokaḥ, sarva^bhūtāni nirmitāni/
body.translated_text: Upon hearing this renewed speech of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, king of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>, spoke thus: Hear what I say here, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. By <s>Brahmā</s> this world and all beings were created.

body.text: p.23.4ab/.tasya jyeṣṭhā vayaṃ putrāḥ kṣatriyās tad anantaraṃ/
body.translated_text: We are his eldest sons; the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> come next after us;

body.text: p.23.4cd/.vaiśyās trṛtīyakā varṇāḥ śūdranāmnā caturthakaḥ//iti//
body.translated_text: the <s>Vaiśyas</s> are the third class, and the fourth is named <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text: p.23.5ab/.sapāda^jaṅghāḥ sanakhāḥ samāṃsāḥ sapārśvapṛṣṭhāś ca narā bhavanti/
body.translated_text: With feet and legs, with nails, with flesh, with sides and backs — human beings are all the same;

body.text: p.23.5cd/.ekāṃśato nāsti yato viśeṣo varṇāś ca catvāra ito na santi//
body.translated_text: since from no single aspect is there a distinction, the four classes do not exist.

body.text: p.23.6ab/.atho viśeṣaḥ pravatosti kaścit tad brūhi yac ca^anumataṃ yathā te/
body.translated_text: If there is indeed some distinguishing excellence, then state what is accepted by you as such;

body.text: p.23.6cd/.atho viśeṣaḥ pravaro hi nāsti varṇāś ca catvāra ito na santi//
body.translated_text: but if there is no such distinguishing excellence, then the four classes do not exist.

body.text: p.24.1ab/. yathā hi dāurukā bālāḥ krīḍamānā mahā^pathe/
body.translated_text: Just as children playing on the highway

body.text: p.24.1cd/.pāṃśupuñjāni saṃpiṇḍya svayaṃ nāmāni kurvate//
body.translated_text: shape heaps of dust and give them names of their own —

body.text: p.24.2ab/.idaṃ kṣīram idaṃ dadhi; idaṃ māṃsam idaṃ ghṛtaṃ/
body.translated_text: 'This is milk, this is curd, this is meat, this is ghee' —

body.text: p.24.2cd/.na ca bālasya vacanāt pāṃśavo +annaṃ bhavanti hi//
body.translated_text: yet by the words of children, dust does not become food;

body.text: p.24.3ab/.varṇās tathāiva catvāro yathā brāhmaṇa bhāṣase/
body.translated_text: so too the four classes that you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, speak of

body.text: p.24.3cd/.pāṃśupuñjābhidhānena yogo [yaḥ ko] py eṣa na vidyate//
body.translated_text: have no more real connection than the naming of heaps of dust.

body.text: p.24.4ab/.na keśena na karṇābhyāṃ na śīrṣaṇa na cakṣuṣā/
body.translated_text: Neither by hair, nor by ears, nor by head, nor by eyes,

body.text: p.24.4cd/.na mukhena na nāsayā na grīvaya na bāhunā//
body.translated_text: nor by mouth, nor by nose, nor by neck, nor by arms,

body.text: p.24.5ab/.norasāpyatha pārśvābhyāṃ na pṛṣṭhena^udareṇa ca/
body.translated_text: nor by chest, nor by sides, nor by back, nor by belly,

body.text: p.24.5cd/.norubhyām atha jañṅhābhyāṃ pāṇipāda^nakhena ca//
body.translated_text: nor by thighs, nor by calves, nor by hands, feet, or nails,

body.text: p.24.6ab/.na svareṇa na varṇena na sarvāṃśair na maithunaiḥ/
body.translated_text: nor by voice, nor by complexion, nor by any limbs, nor by sexual union —

body.text: p.24.6cd/.nānāviśeṣaḥ sarveṣu manuṣyeṣu hi vidyate//
body.translated_text: no distinguishing difference whatsoever is found among all human beings.

body.text: p.24.7ab/.yathā hi jātiṣv anyāsu liṅgaṃ yoniḥ pṛthak pṛthak/
body.translated_text: Just as among other animal species, the distinguishing marks and origins are separate and distinct,

body.text: p.24.7cd/.sāmānyaṃ kāraṇaṃ tatra kiṃ vā jātiṣu manyase//
body.translated_text: the commonality is the basis there — so what do you consider the basis among the classes?

body.text: p.24.8ab/.saśīrṣakāś ca^atha narāsthi^yuktāḥ sacarmakāḥ sendriyasodarāś ca/
body.translated_text: Having heads, joined with bones, having skin, possessing sense organs and bellies —

body.text: p.24.8cd/.ekāṃśato nāsti yato viśeṣo varṇā na yuktāś caturo +abhidhātuṃ//
body.translated_text: since from no single aspect is there a distinction, it is not proper to speak of four classes.

body.text: p.24.9ab/.athāsti kaścit pravaro viśeṣas tad brūhi yaccānumataṃ yathā te/
body.translated_text: If there is indeed some distinguishing excellence, then state what is accepted by you as such;

body.text: p.24.9cd/.atho viśeṣaḥ pravaro +atra nāsti varṇā na yuktāś caturobhidhātuṃ//
body.translated_text: but if there is no such distinguishing excellence, it is not proper to speak of four classes.

body.text: p.25.1ab/.doṣo hy ayaṃ ca^atra bhaved ayukto yad yat tvayā ca^abhihitaṃ nidāne/
body.translated_text: There would be an improper fault in what you have said regarding the origin of things;

body.text: p.25.1cd/.śrutvā tu mattaḥ pratipadya saumya yac ca^atra manye śṛṇucodyamānaṃ//
body.translated_text: but having heard from me and considered, O gentle one, hear what I think regarding this matter.

body.text: p.25.2ab/.yac ca^atra yuktaṃ viṣamaṃ samaṃ vā tāt te pravakṣyāmi niyujyamānaḥ/
body.translated_text: Whatever is proper here, whether unequal or equal, that I shall declare to you when called upon;

body.text: p.25.2cd/.doṣo hi yaś ca^api bhaved ayukto vakṣyāmi te hy uttarata^uttaraṃ ca/
body.translated_text: and whatever fault would be improper, I shall state to you further and further.

body.text: p.25.3ef/.śrutvā tu mattaḥ pratipadya saumya karma^adhipatyaprabhavā manuṣyāḥ//
body.translated_text: Having heard from me and considered, O gentle one — human beings arise from the supremacy of their actions.

body.text: p.25.4/.anumānam api te brāhmaṇa yadi pramāṇaṃ, tatra yad bravīṣi brahmā eka iti tasmāt prajā api eka^jātyā eva/ vayam apy eka^jātyā bhavāmaḥ/ yac ca vravīṣi brahmaṇā^ayaṃ lokaḥ sarva^bhūtāni ca nirmitāni^iti/ sa cette brāhmaṇa idaṃ pramāṇaṃ, tad idaṃ te brāhmaṇa ayuktaṃ yad bravīṣi catvāro varṇā brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā śūdrāś ceti/
body.translated_text: If inference is also a valid means of knowledge for you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, then — regarding what you say, that <s>Brahmā</s> is one — from that it follows that all creatures are of one birth-class. We too are of one birth-class. And you say that by <s>Brahmā</s> this world and all beings were created. If this, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is your authority, then it is inconsistent of you to say that there are four <s>varṇas</s>: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>.

body.text: p.25.4/.api tu brāhmaṇa mithyā mama vaco bhavet yadi brāhmaṇa saṃvādena munuṣyajāter nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ yad uta śīrṣato vā mukhato vā karṇato vā nāsikāto vā (26) bhrūto vā rūpato vā saṃsthānato vā varṇato vā ''kārato vā yonito vā ''hārato vā sambhāvato vā nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, my words would be false only if by mutual agreement some differentiation of the human species could be discerned — whether by head, or by face, or by ears, or by nose, or by eyebrows, or by appearance, or by bodily form, or by complexion, or by shape, or by origin, or by diet, or by mode of birth — if some differentiation could be discerned.

body.text: p.26.1/.tad yathā^api bhoḥ puṣkarasārin gavāś ca gardabho ṣṭramṛgapakṣyajaiḍakā^nāmaṇḍajajarāyujasaṃsvedajaupapādukānāṃnānā^karanaṃ prajñāyate/ yad uta pādato +api mukhatopi varṇato +api saṃsthānato +api āhārato +api yonisambhavato +api nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate naca^evaṃ teṣāṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ tat tasmāt sarvam idam ekam iti/
body.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, among cows, donkeys, camels, deer, birds, goats, those born from eggs, those born from wombs, those born from moisture, and those born spontaneously — differentiation is discerned, namely by feet, by face, by complexion, by bodily form, by diet, and by mode of birth — yet no such differentiation is discerned among the four <s>varṇas</s>. Therefore, all this is one.

body.text: p.26.2/.api ca/ brāhmaṇāmīṣāṃ phalguvṛkṣāṇāmāmrātakajambukharjūrapanasadālāvanatindukamṛdvīkabīja^pūrakakapitthākṣoḍanārikelatiniśakarañja^ādīnāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ yad uta mūlataś ca skandhataś ca tvagbhāgataś ca sārataś ca patrataś ca puṣpataś ca phalataś ca nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ na ca^evaṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among these fruit-bearing trees — <s>āmrātaka</s>, <s>jambu</s>, date-palm, jackfruit, <s>dālāvana</s>, <s>tinduka</s>, grape-vine, citron, wood-apple, walnut, coconut, <s>tiniśa</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and others — differentiation is discerned: by root, by trunk, by bark, by heartwood, by leaf, by flower, and by fruit — yet no such differentiation is discerned among the four <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text: p.26.3/.tad yathā brāhmaṇāmīṣāṃ sthalajānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ sāratamālanaktamālakarṇikārassaptaparṇaśirīṣakovidārasyandanacandanaśiṃśapairaṇḍakhadira^ādīnāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/
body.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among these dry-land trees — <s>sāratamāla</s>, <s>naktamāla</s>, <s>karṇikāra</s>, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>kovidāra</s>, <s>syandana</s>, <s>candana</s>, <s>śiṃśapa</s>, <s>eraṇḍa</s>, <s>khadira</s>, and others — differentiation is discerned.

body.text: p.26.4/.yad uta mūlataś ca skandhataś ca tvagbhāgataś ca gulmataś ca sārataś ca patrataś ca puṣpataś ca phalataś ca viśeṣa upalabhyate/ na ca^evaṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/
body.translated_text: Namely, by root, by trunk, by bark, by bush, by heartwood, by leaf, by flower, and by fruit — a distinction is perceived. But no such differentiation is discerned among the four <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text: p.26.5/.tad yathā bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn amīṣāṃ kṣīravṛkṣāṇām udumbaraplakṣāśvatthanyagrodhavalgukety evam ādīnāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ yad uta mūlataś ca skandhataś ca tvag bhāgataś ca sārataś ca patrataś ca puṣpataś ca phalataś ca nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ na tv eva caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/
body.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, among these milky trees — <s>udumbara</s>, <s>plakṣa</s>, <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>nyagrodha</s>, <s>valguka</s>, and the like — differentiation is discerned: by root, by trunk, by bark, by heartwood, by leaf, by flower, and by fruit; yet no such differentiation is discerned among the four <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text:
p.26.6/.tad yathā puṣkarasārinn amīṣām api phalabaiṣajyavṛkṣāṇām āmalakīharītakīvibhītakī pharasaka^ādīnām anyāsām api vividhānām oṣadhīnāṃ grāma^jānāṃ pārvatīyānāṃ tṛṇa^vanaspatīnāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ yad uta mūlataś ca skandhataś ca (27) gulmataś ca sārataś ca patrataś ca puṣpataś ca phalataś ca nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ na tv eva caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ
nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/
