body.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, among these medicinal fruit-trees — <s>āmalakī</s>, <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītakī</s>, <s>pharasaka</s>, and other various herbs, village-grown and mountain-grown, grasses and forest trees — differentiation is discerned: by root, by trunk, by bush, by heartwood, by leaf, by flower, and by fruit; yet no such differentiation is discerned among the four <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text: p.27.1/.tad yathā sthalajānāṃ puṣpa^vṛkṣāṇām atimuktaka^campaka^pāṭalānāṃ sumanā vārṣikādhanaṣkārika^ādīnāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ yad uto rūpato +api varṇato +api gandhato +api saṃsthānato +api nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ na tv eva caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/
body.translated_text: Just as among dry-land flowering trees — <s>atimukta</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s>, jasmine, <s>vārṣikā</s>, <s>dhanaṣkārikā</s>, and others — differentiation is discerned: by form, by color, by fragrance, and by shape; yet no such differentiation is discerned among the four <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text:
p.27.2/.tad yathā brāhmaṇām īṣām api jalajānāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ padma^utpala^saugandhika^mṛdu^gandhika^ādīnāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ yad uta rūpataś ca gandhataś ca saṃsthānataś ca vaṇataś ca nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ natveva varṇānāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate/ tad yathā puṣkarasārin amī brāhmaṇā iti kṣatriyā iti vaiśyā iti śūdrā iti/ tasmād ekam eva^idaṃ sarvam
iti/
body.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among these aquatic flowers — lotus, blue lotus, <s>saugandhika</s>, <s>mṛdugandhika</s>, and others — differentiation is discerned: by form, by fragrance, by shape, and by color; yet no such differentiation is discerned among the <s>varṇas</s>. Therefore, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> — these are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, these are <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, these are <s>Vaiśyas</s>, these are <s>Śūdras</s> — hence all this is one and the same.

body.text: p.27.3ab/.apy anyat te pravakṣyāmi brāhmaṇaiḥ kalpitaṃ yath|ā/
body.translated_text: I shall tell you yet another thing, as conceived by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>:

body.text: p.27.3cd/.śiraḥ satāraṃ gaganam ākāśam udaraṃ tathā//
body.translated_text: The head is the sky with its stars; the abdomen is space;

body.text: p.27.4ab/.parvatāś ca^apy ubhāv ūrū pādau ca dharaṇī^talaṃ/
body.translated_text: the two thighs are the mountains; and the feet are the surface of the earth;

body.text: p.27.4cd/.sūryācandramasau netre roma tṛṇa^vanaspatī//
body.translated_text: the sun and moon are the eyes; the grass, plants, and trees are the body-hair;

body.text: p.27.5ab/.aśrūṇy avocad varṣā +asya nadyaḥ prasrāvam eva ca/
body.translated_text: his tears, they said, are the rain; the rivers are his urine;

body.text: p.27.5cd/.sāgarāś ca^apy amedhyaṃ vai; evaṃ brahmā prajāpatiḥ//
body.translated_text: and the oceans are his excrement — thus is <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Prajāpati</s>.

body.text: p.28.1/.parīkṣasva tvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sva^lakṣaṇaṃ/ yasmād brahmaṇo brāhmaṇā utpannās tasmāt kṣatriyā api vaiśyā api śūdrā apy utpannāḥ/
body.translated_text: Examine for yourself the characteristics of <s>Brahman</s>. Since <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are born from <s>Brahman</s>, so too are <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> born from him.

body.text: p.28.2ab/.evaṃ prasūtir yadi tatvataḥ syāt tato hi syād varṇa^kṛto viśeṣaḥ/
body.translated_text: If birth were truly thus, then there would be a distinction based on <s>varṇa</s> (class).

body.text: p.28.2cd/.yadi brāhmaṇā brahma^lokaṃ vrajeyus trayaś ca varṇā na vrajeyuḥ svargaṃ/
body.translated_text: If <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were to go to <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of Brahman) and the three other <s>varṇas</s> were not to go to heaven,

body.text: p.28.2ef/.evaṃ bhaved varṇa^kṛto viśeṣo na cenna catvāro bhavanti varṇāḥ//
body.translated_text: then there would be a distinction based on <s>varṇa</s>; but if not, then these four <s>varṇas</s> do not exist.

body.text: p.28.3ab/.yasmād dhi varṇaś caturtha evaṃ prayāti svargaṃ svakṛtena karmaṇā/
body.translated_text: Since the fourth <s>varṇa</s> too goes to heaven by the merit of his own actions,

body.text: p.28.3cd/.yatas tapaś ca^ārṣam iha praśastaṃ tasmād dvijāter na viśeṣaṇaṃ syād//
body.translated_text: and since the austerity of the sages is praised here, therefore there is no special distinction for the twice-born.

body.text: p.28.4ab/.yadi brāhmaṇaḥ syād ihaika eva dvijihvaś catuḥ^śravaṇas tathā^eva/
body.translated_text: If a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> alone were unique here — having two tongues, four ears,

body.text: p.28.4cd/.catur^viṣāṇo bahupād dviśīrṣa evaṃ kṛte varṇa^kṛto viśeṣaḥ//
body.translated_text: four horns, many feet, and two heads — then there would be a distinction based on <s>varṇa</s>.

body.text: p.29.1ab/.rāgaiś ca nāma paraghātanaṃ ca evaṃ prakāraṃ ca viheṭhanaṃ ca/
body.translated_text: Passions, murder of others, and affliction of this kind,

body.text: p.29.1cd/.sattvasya vai karmaṇo dhvaṃsanaṃ ca etāny akalyāṇakṛtāni vipraiḥ//
body.translated_text: and the destruction of beings' merit by action — these unwholesome deeds are done by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text:
p.29.2ab/.yuddhaṃ vivādṃ kalahāny abhīkṣṇaṃ goprokṣaṇaṃ cintitaṃ brāhmaṇair hi/
p.29.2cd/.atharvaṇaḥ karmaṇā trāsanaṃ ca etāni mantrāṇi kṛtāni vipraiḥ//
body.translated_text: War, disputes, and quarrels incessantly, the sprinkling of cattle — these are devised by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; and terrifying others through the rites of the <s>Atharvaveda</s> — these <s>mantras</s> are composed by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: p.29.3ab/.pāpecchatā bahu^jana^vañcanaṃ ca śāṭhyaṃ ca dhaurtyaṃ ca tathā^eva kalpaṃ/
body.translated_text: Desire for evil, cheating of many people, deceit and knavery, and contrivances —

body.text: p.29.3cd/.evaṃ pareṣām ahitaṃ vicintya kadā ca te svargam ito vrajeyuḥ//
body.translated_text: having thus conceived harm to others, when will they ever go to heaven from here?

body.text: p.29.4ab/.ye brāhmaṇā ugratapā vinītā vratena śīlena sadā hy upetāḥ/
body.translated_text: Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are of fierce austerity, disciplined, always endowed with vows and good conduct,

body.text: p.29.4cd/.ahiṃsakā ye dama saṃyame ratās te brāhmaṇā brahma^puraṃ vrajanti//
body.translated_text: non-violent, delighting in self-control and restraint — those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> go to the city of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: p.29.5ab/.saha^asthi^māṃsaḥ sanakhaḥ sacarmā duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ mūtra^purīṣam ekaṃ/
body.translated_text: Having the same bones and flesh, the same nails and skin, the same suffering and pleasure, the same urine and excrement,

body.text: p.29.5cd/.pañca^indriyair nāsti yato viśeṣas tasmān na vai varṇa^catuṣka eṣaḥ//
body.translated_text: since there is no distinction in the five sense organs, therefore this fourfold <s>varṇa</s> system does not truly exist.

body.text: p.29.6/.tad yathā nāma brāhmaṇa kasya^cit puruṣasya catvāraḥ putrā bhaveyuḥ/ sa teṣāṃ nāmāni kuryān nandaka iti vā jīvaka iti vā aśoka iti vā śatāyur iti vā / iṣṭāś ca (30) punar bho etasya puruṣasya putrā bhaveyuḥ/ tatra yo nandakaḥ sa nandet/ yo jīvakaḥ sa īvet/ yo +aśokaḥ sa na śocet/ yaḥ śatāyuḥ sa varṣaśataṃ jīvet/
body.translated_text: Suppose, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a certain man has four sons. He gives them names: <s>Nandaka</s>, or <s>Jīvaka</s>, or <s>Aśoka</s>, or <s>Śatāyus</s>. And suppose these sons of that man are beloved. Would the one named <s>Nandaka</s> therefore rejoice? Would the one named <s>Jīvaka</s> therefore live? Would the one named <s>Aśoka</s> therefore not grieve? Would <s>Śatāyus</s> therefore live a hundred years?

body.text: p.30.1/.nāmataḥ punar brāhmaṇa teṣāṃ nānā^karaṇaṃ prajñāyate na jātitaḥ/ tatkasya hetoḥ/ iha khalu punar brāhmaṇa pitṛtaḥ putro jāyte/ tasmāc ca tatredaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ bhavati:
body.translated_text: O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the differentiation among them is known through names, not through birth. For what reason? For here, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a son is born from his father. And therefore this explanation applies:

body.text: p.30.2ab/.mātā bhastrā pituḥ putro yena jātaḥ sa eva saḥ/
body.translated_text: The mother is a bellows; the son is of the father — the one from whom he is born, he is that very one.

body.text: p.30.2cd/.yady evaṃ bho vijānāsi na te (putrā) parabhūtāḥ kvacit//
body.translated_text: If you understand this, your sons will never be inferior to anyone.

body.text: p.30.3/.parīkṣasva brāhmaṇa saṃyageva ko +atra brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūtra iti/
body.translated_text: Examine properly, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: who here is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, who a <s>Vaiśya</s>, who a <s>Śūdra</s>?

body.text: p.30.4ab/.sarve kāṇāś ca kubjāś ca sarve +apasmāriṇopi vā/
body.translated_text: All are blind, all are hunchbacked, all may be epileptic,

body.text: p.30.4cd/.kilāsinaḥ kuṣṭhinaś ca gaurāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ pṛthak pṛthak//
body.translated_text: some have white spots, some have leprosy, some are fair, some are dark — each differently.

body.text: p.30.5/.pratiṣṭhitāḥ samamajjānakhatvacapārśva^udaravaktrāḥ prajā hi tāḥ svakarmaṇā/ evaṃ gate brāhmaṇa naiva bhavati viśeṣaḥ/ ko jāti^kṛto viśeṣaḥ/
body.translated_text: People have the same marrow, nails, skin, sides, abdomen, and face — distinguished only by their own actions. This being so, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, there is no distinction at all. What distinction is there based on birth?

body.text: p.30.6/.yasmān na jāter viśeṣaṇo +asti tasmān na vai varṇa^catuṣka eva/
body.translated_text: Since there is no distinction based on birth, therefore this fourfold <s>varṇa</s> system does not truly exist.

body.text: p.31.1/.tasmāt te brāhmaṇa bravīmi saṃjñāmātram idaṃ lokasya yad idaṃ brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā caṇḍāla iti vā/ ekam idaṃ sarvam idam ekaṃ/ putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaram utsṛja bhāryā^arthāya yāvantaṃ kula^śulkaṃ manyase tāvantam anupradāsyāmi/
body.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I tell you: this is merely a convention of the world — that one is called <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or <s>Vaiśya</s>, or <s>Śūdra</s>, or <s>Caṇḍāla</s>. All this is one; all this is the same. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as his wife — whatever bride-price you consider appropriate, I shall pay.

body.text:
p.31.2/.idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārīdam avocat/ kiṃ punarbhavatā ṛgvedo +adhītaḥ, yajurvedo +adhītaḥ, sāmavedo +adhītaḥ, atharvavedo +adhītaḥ, āyurvedo +adhītaḥ kalpādhyāyo pi/ adhyātmam api mṛgacakraṃ vā nakṣatra^gaṇo vā tithi^kramagaṇo vā tvayādhītaḥ/ karma^cakraṃ vā tvayādhigataṃ/ athavā +aṅgavidyā vā vastravidyā
vā śivāvidyā śakunividyā vā tvayādhītā/ athavā rāhucairtaṃ vā śukra^caritaṃ vā grahacaritaṃ vā tvayādhītaṃ/ athavā lokāyateṃ bhavatā bhāṣyapravacanaṃ vā pakṣādhyāyo vā nyāyo vā tvayādhītaḥ/
body.translated_text: Having heard this speech of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> said this: 'But have you studied the <s>Ṛgveda</s>? Have you studied the <s>Yajurveda</s>? Have you studied the <s>Sāmaveda</s>? Have you studied the <s>Atharvaveda</s>? Have you studied the <s>Āyurveda</s> and the chapter on ritual procedure? Have you studied the science of the self, the circle of animals, the constellation groups, or the sequence of lunar days? Have you mastered the circle of actions? Or have you studied the science of bodily signs, the science of garments, the science of <s>Śiva</s>, or the science of bird omens? Or have you studied the movements of <s>Rāhu</s>, the movements of <s>Śukra</s>, or the movements of the planets? Or have you studied the <s>Lokāyata</s> (materialism), or commentary and exposition, or the chapter on dialectics, or logic?'

body.text:
p.32.1/.evam ukte triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rāhaḥ puṣkarasāriṇaṃ brāhmaṇam etad avocat/ etac ca mayā brāhmaṇādhītaṃ bhūyaś ca^uttaraṃ / yad api te brāhmaṇa evaṃ syād aham asmi mantreṣu pāraṃ prāpta iti/ tatra te brāhmaṇa saha dharmeṇānumānaṃ pravakṣyāmi/ na khalv evaṃ brāhmaṇa prāthamakalpikānāṃ sattvānām etad abhavat/ yad uta brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya
iti vā śūdra iti vā/ ekam idaṃ sarvam idam ekaṃ/
body.translated_text: When thus addressed, <s>Triśaṅku</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king said this to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>: 'I have studied all this, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and more besides. Even if you think, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, that you have reached the far shore of the <s>mantras</s> — I shall explain to you the reasoning in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>. Indeed, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the beings of the first age did not have such distinctions as <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or <s>Vaiśya</s>, or <s>Śūdra</s>. All this is one; all this is the same.'

body.text:
p.32.2/.atha brāhmaṇa sattvānāmasadṛśānāṃ ca^ubhayathā sadṛśānāṃ tato +anye sattvāḥ śālikṣetrāṇi kelāyanti gopāyanti vāpayanti vā/ te +amī kṣatriyā iti saṃjñā udapādi/ athātra brāhmaṇa tad anyatamānāṃ sattānām etad abhavat/ parigraho rogaḥ parigraho gaṇḍaḥ parigrahaḥ śalyaḥ/ yannu vayaṃ svaparigraham apahāyāraṇyāyatanaṃ gatvā
tṛṇa^kāṣṭhaśākhāparṇapalāśakānupasaṃhṛtya tṛṇa^kuṭikāṃ vā parṇakuṭikāṃ vā kṛtvā praviśya dhyāyena iti/
body.translated_text: Then, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among beings both dissimilar and similar in both respects, certain beings cultivated, protected, and sowed rice fields. For them, the designation <s>Kṣatriya</s> arose. Then, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, certain other beings thought: 'Possession is a disease; possession is a boil; possession is a thorn. Let us abandon our possessions, go to a forest hermitage, gather grass, wood, branches, leaves, and foliage, build a grass hut or a leaf hut, enter it, and meditate.'

body.text: p.32.3/.atha te sattvās taṃ svakaṃ parigraham apahāyāraṇyāyatanaṃ gatvā tṛṇa^kāṣṭhaśākhāpatraparṇapalāśakais tṛṇa^kuṭiṃ vā parṇakuṭikāṃ vā kṛtvā tatra^eva praviśya dhyāyanti sma/ te tatra sāyam āsanahetoḥ prāntavāṭikāṃ prātaraśanahetoś ca grāmaṃ piṇḍāya praviśanti sma/
body.translated_text: Then those beings, having abandoned their possessions, went to a forest hermitage, built a grass hut or a leaf hut from grass, wood, branches, leaves, and foliage, entered it, and meditated. They would enter a nearby garden in the evening for their evening meal, and in the morning they would enter the village for alms.

body.text: p.32.4/.atha teṣāṃ grāma^vāsināṃ sattvānām etad abhavat/ duṣkarakārakā vata bhoḥ sattvā ye svakaṃ parigraham utṛjya grāma^nigamajana^padebhyo bahir nirgatās teṣāṃ bahirmanaskā brāhyaṇā iti saṃjñā udapādi/ te ca punar grāma^vāsinaḥ sattvās tān atīva satkurvanti sma/ teṣāṃ ca dātavyaṃ manyante sma/
body.translated_text: Then the village-dwelling beings thought: 'Remarkable indeed are those beings who, having abandoned their possessions, have gone forth from villages, towns, and districts.' For those whose minds were turned outward, the designation <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> arose. And those village-dwelling beings honored them greatly and considered them worthy of gifts.

body.text: p.33.1/.atha teṣām eva sattvānām anyatame sattvās tāni dhyānāny asaṃbhāvayanto grāmeṣv avatīrya mantra^padān svādhyāyanti sma/ tāṃs te grāma^nivāsina āhuḥ --- na levalam ime sattvā ime +adhyāpakāḥ, teṣām adhyāpakā iti loke saṃjñā udapādi/
body.translated_text: Then certain other beings among them, unable to sustain those meditations, descended into the villages and recited <s>mantra</s> verses and studied texts. The village-dwellers said of them: 'These beings are not mere beings — they are teachers.' Thus the designation 'teachers' (<s>adhyāpaka</s>) arose in the world.

body.text: p.33.2/.ayaṃ hetur ayaṃ pratyayo brāhmaṇānāṃ loke prādurbhāvāya/ athānyatame sattvā viveka^kāla^pratisaṃyuktān karma^antān vividhān artha^pratisaṃyuktān kurvanti sma/ teṣāṃ vaiśyā iti saṃjñā udapādi/
body.translated_text: This is the cause, this is the condition for the appearance of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in the world. Then certain other beings engaged in various commercial activities connected with gain and suited to the proper time. For them, the designation <s>Vaiśya</s> arose.

body.text: p.33.3/.athānyatame sattvāḥ kṣudreṇa karmaṇā jīvikāṃ kalpayanti sma/ teṣāṃ śūdrā iti saṃjñā udapādi/
body.translated_text: Then certain other beings made their livelihood through menial work. For them, the designation <s>Śūdra</s> arose.

body.text: p.33.4/.bhūta^pūrvaṃ brāhamṇa anyatamaḥ sattvo vadhūm ādāya ratham āruhyānyatam asminn araṇyapradeśe gataḥ/ tatra ca ratho bhagnaḥ/ tasmān mātaṅgama [mā tvaṃ gamaḥ] iti saṃjñā udapādi/
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a certain being took a bride, mounted a chariot, and went to a certain forest region. There his chariot broke. From this, the designation <s>Mātaṅga</s> ('Don't go!') arose.

body.text: p.33.5/.kṣetraṃ karṣanti ye teṣāṃ karṣakā iti saṃjñā prvṛttā/ bhāṣyeṇa ca parṣadaṃ rañjayati dharmeṇa śīlabratasamācāreṇa samyak, tasya rājā iti saṃjñā +abhūt/
body.translated_text: Those who plough fields — for them, the designation 'ploughmen' (<s>karṣaka</s>) arose. And one who delights an assembly through eloquence, through <s>Dharma</s>, through the proper conduct of moral vows — for him, the designation 'king' (<s>rājā</s>) arose.

body.text: p.33.6/.tato +anye sattvā vāṇijyayā jīvikāṃ kalpayanti teṣāṃ vaṇija iti saṃjñā (34) udapādi/ tataś ca^anye sattvāḥ pravrajanti sma/ pravrajitvā parān jayanti kleśān jayanti^iti teṣāṃ pravrajitā iti loke saṃjñā udapādi/
body.translated_text: Then certain other beings made their livelihood through trade — for them, the designation 'merchant' (<s>vaṇij</s>) arose. And certain other beings went forth into homelessness; having gone forth, they conquered others and conquered afflictions — for them, the designation 'renunciant' (<s>pravrajita</s>) arose in the world.

body.text: p.34.1/.api tu brāhmaṇa ekaiva saṃjñā loka udapādi/ tāṃ te pravakṣyāmi/
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a single designation arose in the world. I shall tell you about it.

body.text:
p.35.1/.brahmā loke +asmin imān vedān vācayati/ brahmā devānāṃ parama^tāpasaḥ/ indrasya kauśikasya vedān vācayati sma/ indraḥ kauśiko +araṇemi gautamaṃ vedān vācayati/ araṇemi gautamaḥ śvetaketuṃ vedān vācayati/ śvetaketuḥ śukaṃ paṇḍitaṃ vedān vācayati/ śukaḥ paṇḍitaś ca vedān vibhajati sma/ tad yathā puṣyo bahv^ṛcānāṃ paṃktiś chantogānām eka^viṃśatir adhvaryavaḥ/
kratur artha^vaṇikānāṃ/ bahv^ṛcānām ete brāhmaṇāḥ/ sarve te vyākhyāyante/ puṣya eko bhūtvā pañca^viṃśatidhā bhinnaḥ/ tad yathā śuklā valkalā māṇḍavyā iti/ tatra daśa śuklāḥ/ aṣṭau valkalāḥ/ sapta māṇḍavyāḥ/ itīyaṃ brāhmaṇa bahv^ṛcānāṃ śākhā/ puṣya eko bhūtvā pañca^viṃśatidhā bhinnaḥ/
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> teaches these <s>Vedas</s> in this world. <s>Brahmā</s>, the supreme ascetic among the gods, taught the <s>Vedas</s> to <s>Indra</s> <s>Kauśika</s>. <s>Indra</s> <s>Kauśika</s> taught the <s>Vedas</s> to <s>Araṇemi</s> <s>Gautama</s>. <s>Araṇemi</s> <s>Gautama</s> taught the <s>Vedas</s> to <s>Śvetaketu</s>. <s>Śvetaketu</s> taught the <s>Vedas</s> to the learned <s>Śuka</s>. The learned <s>Śuka</s> divided the <s>Vedas</s>. Namely: <s>Puṣya</s> for the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (Ṛgvedins), the <s>Paṅkti</s> for the <s>Chandogas</s> (Sāmavedins), and twenty-one for the <s>Adhvaryus</s> (Yajurvedins). <s>Kratu</s> for the <s>Arthavaṇikas</s> (Atharvavedins). These are the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>Bahvṛcas</s>. All these are expounded. <s>Puṣya</s>, being one, was divided into twenty-five parts, namely: <s>Śuklā</s>, <s>Valkalā</s>, and <s>Māṇḍavyā</s>. Of these, ten are <s>Śuklā</s>, eight are <s>Valkalā</s>, seven are <s>Māṇḍavyā</s>. This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the branch of the <s>Bahvṛcas</s>. <s>Puṣya</s>, being one, was divided into twenty-five.

body.text: p.35.2/.anumānam api brāhmaṇa pramāṇaṃ chandogānāṃ/ brāhmaṇāḥ sarva ete chandogāḥ/ paṃktir ety ekā bhūtvā sa^aśīti^sahasradhā bhinnā/ tad yathā śīlavalkā araṇemikā laukākṣāḥ kauthumā brahma^samā mahā^samā mahā^yāgikāḥ sa^atyam ugrāḥ samanta^vedāḥ/
body.translated_text: The inference is also the authority for the <s>Chandogas</s> (Sāmavedins). All these are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>Chandogas</s>. The <s>Paṅkti</s>, being one, was divided into eighty thousand parts, namely: <s>Śīlavalkā</s>, <s>Araṇemikā</s>, <s>Laukākṣā</s>, <s>Kauthumā</s>, <s>Brahmasamā</s>, <s>Mahāsamā</s>, <s>Mahāyāgikā</s>, <s>Satyam Ugrā</s>, and <s>Samantavedā</s>.

body.text: p.36.1/.tatra śīlavalkā viṃśatiḥ/ araṇemikā viṃśatiḥ/ laukākṣāś catvāriṃśat/ kauthumānāṃ śataṃ/ brahma^samānāṃ śataṃ/ mahā^samānāṃ pañca^śatāni/ mahā^yāgikānāṃ śataṃ/ sa^atyam ugrāṇāṃ śataṃ / samanta^vedānāṃ śataṃ/ itīyaṃ brāhmaṇa^chandogānāṃ śākhā/ paṃktir ity ekā bhūtvā sa^aśīti sahasradhā bhinnā/
body.translated_text: Of these, the <s>Śīlavalkā</s> are twenty; the <s>Araṇemikā</s> are twenty; the <s>Laukākṣā</s> are forty; the <s>Kauthumā</s> are one hundred; the <s>Brahmasamā</s> are one hundred; the <s>Mahāsamā</s> are five hundred; the <s>Mahāyāgikā</s> are one hundred; the <s>Satyam Ugrā</s> are one hundred; the <s>Samantavedā</s> are one hundred. This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the branch of the <s>Chandogas</s>. The <s>Paṅkti</s>, being one, was divided into eighty thousand.

body.text:
p.36.2/.anumānam api pramāṇam adhvaryūṇāṃ/ ete brāhmaṇā eka^viṃśaty adhvaryavo bhūtvā eka^uttaraśatadhā bhinnāḥ/ tad yathā kaṭhāḥ kaṃinā vājasaneyino jātukarṇāḥ proṣṭhapadā ṛṣayaḥ/ tatra daśa kaṭhā daśa kaṇimā ekādaśa vājasaneyinaḥ/trayodaśa jātukarnāḥ/ ṣoḍaśa proṣṭhapadāḥ/ eka catvāriṃśad ṛṣayaḥ/ itīyaṃ brāhmaṇādhvaryūṇāṃ śākhā/ eka^viṃśatyadhvaryavo bhūtvā
eka^uttaraśatadhā bhinnāḥ/
body.translated_text: The inference is also the authority for the <s>Adhvaryus</s> (Yajurvedins). These <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, being twenty-one <s>Adhvaryus</s>, were divided into one hundred and one parts, namely: <s>Kaṭhas</s>, <s>Kaṇimas</s>, <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, <s>Jātukarṇas</s>, <s>Proṣṭhapadas</s>, and <s>Ṛṣis</s>. Of these, ten are <s>Kaṭhas</s>, ten are <s>Kaṇimas</s>, eleven are <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, thirteen are <s>Jātukarṇas</s>, sixteen are <s>Proṣṭhapadas</s>, and forty-one are <s>Ṛṣis</s>. This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the branch of the <s>Adhvaryus</s>. The twenty-one <s>Adhvaryus</s>, being one, were divided into one hundred and one.

body.text: p.36.3/.anumānam api brāhmaṇa pramāṇam atharvaṇikānāṃ / ete mantrāḥ sarve te +atharvaṇikāḥ/ kratur eko bhūtvā dvidhā bhinnaḥ/ dvidhā bhūtvā caturdhā bhinnaḥ/caturdhā bhūtvā +aṣṭadhā bhinnaḥ/ aṣṭadhā bhūtvā [nava]daśadhā bhinnaḥ/ itīyaṃ brāhmaṇātharvaṇikānāṃ śākhā/ kratur ekaḥ ṣoḍaśa^uttaradvādaśa^śatadhā bhinnaḥ/
body.translated_text: [p.36.3] Inference too, O Brahmin, is authoritative for the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s> (followers of the Atharvaveda). All these <s>mantras</s> belong to the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s>. The ritual (<s>kratu</s>) was one, then split into two; having become two, it split into four; having become four, it split into eight; having become eight, it split nineteen-fold. Thus is this branch of the Brahminical <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s>. The one ritual was split into one thousand two hundred and sixteen divisions.

body.text:
p.36.4/.anumānam api brāhmaṇa pramāṇaṃ pratītya etāni dvādaśa^bhedaśatāni ṣoḍaśabhedāś ca ye brāhmaṇaiḥ paurāṇaiḥ samyag dṛṣṭāḥ/ chandasi vā vyākaraṇe vā lokāyate vā (37) padamīmāṃsāyāṃ vā na caiṣāmūhāpohaḥ prajñāyate/ yad uta eka^jātyo nāmeti viditvā bandhur bhavitum arhati/ tat te vrāhmaṇa bravīmi saṃjñāmātrakam etal lokasya yad uta brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya
iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/ ekam idaṃ sarvam idam ekaṃ/ putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaram utsṛja bhāryā^arthāya yāvantaṃ kula^śulkaṃ manyase tāvantam anupradāsyāmi/
body.translated_text: [p.36.4] Inference too, O Brahmin, is authoritative — based on these twelve hundred divisions and sixteen subdivisions, which were correctly perceived by the ancient Brahmins, whether in the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic meter), in grammar, in <s>Lokāyata</s> (materialism), [folio 37] or in <s>Padamīmāṃsā</s> (word-analysis) — yet no critical examination of these is discerned. Knowing that they are of one birth, one ought to become a kinsman. Therefore I tell you, O Brahmin: this is merely a conventional designation (<s>saṃjñāmātra</s>) of the world — namely 'Brahmin,' or 'Kṣatriya,' or 'Vaiśya,' or 'Śūdra.' All this is one, this entirety is one. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> for the purpose of marriage; whatever bride-price you think fitting, that much I shall pay.

body.text: p.37.1/.idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī tuṣṇīṃbhūto madgubhūtaḥ srastaskandho +adhomukho niṣpratibhaḥ pradhyānaparo +asthāt/
body.translated_text: [p.37.1] Having heard this further speech of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, the Brahmin <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> stood silent, dejected, with drooping shoulders, face downward, without reply, absorbed in deep thought.

body.text:
p.37.2/.dadarśa triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rājo brāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇaṃ tṛṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ madgubhūtaṃ srasta^skandham adhomukhaṃ niṣpratibhaṃ pradhyānaparaṃ sthitaṃ/ dṛṣṭvā ca punar idam abravīt/ yad api te brāhmaṇa evaṃ syād asadṛśena saha sambandho bhaviṣyati^iti/ na punastvayā brāhmaṇa^evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ/ (38)tat kasya hetoḥ/ ye pramāṇaśrutiśīlapraññādayo guṇā agyrā
lokasya te mama putrasya śārdūlakarṇasya saṃvidyante/ yad api te brāhmaṇa evaṃ syāt --- ye vājapiyaṃ yajñaṃ yajanti/ aśvamedhaṃ puruṣa^medhaṃ śāmyaprāśaṃ nirargaḍaṃ yajñaṃ yajanti, sarve te kāyasya bhedātsugatau svarga^loke deveṣūpapadyanta iti/ na punarbrāhmaṇa tvaya^evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ/ tat kasya hetoḥ/vājapeyaṃ brāhmaṇa yajñaṃ yajamānā aśvamedhaṃ puruṣa^medhaṃ
śāmyaprāśaṃ nirargaḍaṃ yajñaṃ ca yajamānā bahudhā mantrān pravartayantaḥ prāṇihiṃsāṃ ca pravartayanti/ tasmāt te brāhmaṇa bravīmi na hy eṣa mārgaḥ svargāya/ ahaṃ te brāhmaṇa mārgaṃ svargāya vyākhāmi/ tac chṛṇu/
body.translated_text: [p.37.2] <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, saw the Brahmin <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> standing silent, dejected, with drooping shoulders, face downward, without reply, absorbed in deep thought. Having seen him, he spoke again thus: 'Even if you should think, O Brahmin, that an alliance with an unequal will come about — you should not view it so, O Brahmin. [folio 38] For what reason? Those foremost qualities of the world — authority, learning, moral conduct, wisdom, and the rest — are found in my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>. And even if you should think, O Brahmin — those who perform the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, who perform the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), the <s>Puruṣamedha</s> (human sacrifice), the <s>Śāmyaprāśa</s>, and the <s>Nirargaḍa</s> sacrifice — that all of them, at the breaking up of the body, are reborn in the happy realm, the heavenly world, among the gods — you should not view it so, O Brahmin. For what reason? Those who perform the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, O Brahmin, and those who perform the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, the <s>Puruṣamedha</s>, the <s>Śāmyaprāśa</s>, and the <s>Nirargaḍa</s> sacrifice, while employing many <s>mantras</s>, also engage in the killing of living beings (<s>prāṇihiṃsā</s>). Therefore I tell you, O Brahmin: this is not the path to heaven. I shall explain to you, O Brahmin, the path to heaven. Listen to that:'

body.text: p.38.1ab/.śīlaṃ rakṣeta medhāvī prārthayānaḥ sukha^trayaṃ/
body.translated_text: [p.38.1ab] The wise one who desires the threefold happiness should guard moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) —

body.text: p.38.1cd/.praśaṃsāṃ vitta^lābhaṃ ca pretya svarge ca modanaṃ//
body.translated_text: [p.38.1cd] praise, gain of wealth, and after death, rejoicing in heaven.

body.text: p.38.2/.yair brāhmaṇa itaḥ pūrvaṃ vājapeyo yajña iṣṭaḥ/ yair aśvamedho yaiḥ puruṣa^medho yaiḥ śāmyaprāśo yair nirargaḍo yajña iṣṭaḥ, parigṛhītas tair nirargalaṃ ca kāmaiḥ kāmaḥ/ ito nākaḥ paryeṣyate/ ye brāhmaṇa itaḥ paścād vājapeyaṃ yajñaṃ yakṣyanti ye +aśvamedhaṃ puruṣa^medhaṃ ye śāmyaprāśaṃ nirargaḍaṃ yajñaṃ yakṣyanti te nirarthakaṃ mahā^vighātaṃ saṃyokṣyanti/
body.translated_text: [p.38.2] Those, O Brahmin, who in former times performed the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, who performed the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, the <s>Puruṣamedha</s>, the <s>Śāmyaprāśa</s>, and the <s>Nirargaḍa</s> sacrifice — they obtained their desires without restraint. From here, heaven was attainable. But those, O Brahmin, who hereafter will perform the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, who will perform the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, <s>Puruṣamedha</s>, <s>Śāmyaprāśa</s>, and <s>Nirargaḍa</s> sacrifice — they will meet with futile, great destruction.

body.text: p.38.3/.tasmāt te brāhmana bravīmi --- ehi tvaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ sambandhaṃ yojayasvā/ tat kasya hetoḥ/ dharmeṇa hi caṇḍālā ajugupsanīyā bhavanti/ api ca/
body.translated_text: [p.38.3] Therefore I tell you, O Brahmin — come, enter into an alliance with me. For what reason? For by <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct), even <s>Caṇḍālas</s> (outcastes) become non-despicable. Moreover:

body.text: p.39.1ab/.śraddhā śīlaṃ tapastyāgaḥ śrutir jñānaṃ dayaiva ca/
body.translated_text: [p.39.1ab] Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>), learning (<s>śruti</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and compassion (<s>dayā</s>),

body.text: p.39.1cd/.darśanaṃ sarva^vedānāṃ svargavrata^padāni vai//
body.translated_text: [p.39.1cd] and the vision of all the <s>Vedas</s> — these are truly the steps on the vow to heaven.

body.text:
p.39.2/.pramāṇam aṣṭaprakāraṃ svargāya/ tad ebhir aṣṭābhiḥ prakāraiḥ svargagamanam iṣyate/ ye prāyeṇa jānanti viśeṣeṇa khalv apy anekair vividhari yajñaiḥ/ aṣṭau cemā brāhmaṇa nirdiṣṭā mātṛtulyā bhaginyo loke pravartante/ tad yathā aditir devānāṃ mātā/ divit dānavānāṃ/ manur mānavānāṃ/ surabhiḥ saurabheyānāṃ/ vinatā suparṇānāṃ/ kadrur nāgānāṃ/ pṛthivī bhūtānāṃ
mātā sarva^bījānāṃ/ marutāṃ mahāmahaḥ/ mahā^kāśyapaṃ manasā vidanti ṛṣayaḥ/
body.translated_text: [p.39.2] The eightfold authoritative means to heaven: by these eight modes, the path to heaven is prescribed. Those who generally know — and especially through various manifold sacrifices — and these eight, O Brahmin, are declared as the mothers who are like sisters operating in the world, namely: <s>Aditi</s>, mother of the gods; <s>Diti</s>, of the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons); <s>Manu</s>, of the <s>Mānavas</s> (humans); <s>Surabhī</s>, of the <s>Saurabheyās</s> (cattle); <s>Vinatā</s>, of the <s>Suparṇas</s> (birds); <s>Kadrū</s>, of the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents); <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth), mother of all beings and all seeds; <s>Mahāmaha</s>, of the <s>Maruts</s> (storm gods). The sages know great <s>Kāśyapa</s> through the mind.

body.text:
p.39.3/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin brāhmaṇānāṃ saptagotrāṇi vyākhyāsyāmi tāni śrūyantāṃ/ tad yathā gautamā vātsyāḥ kautsāḥ kauśikāḥ kāśyapā vāśiṣṭhā māṇḍavyā ity etāni brāhmaṇa saptagotrāṇi/ eṣām ekaikaṃ gotraṃ saptadhā bhinnaṃ/ atra ye gautamās te kauthumāste gargās te bharadvājāsta ārṣṭiṣeṇās te vaikhānasās te (40) vajrapādāḥ/ tatra ye vātsyāsta ātreyās
te maitreyās te bhārgavās te sāvarṇyā ste salolās te bahujātāḥ/ tatra ye kautsās te maudgalyāyanās te gauṇāyanās te lāṅgalāste lagnāste daṇḍalagnāste soma^bhuvāḥ[vah}/ tatra ye kauśikās te kātyāyanās te darbhakātyāyanās te valkalinas te pakṣiṇas te laukākṣās te lohita^āyanāḥ (lohityāyanāḥ) / tatra ye kāśyapās te maṇḍanās te iṣṭās te śauṇḍāyanās te rocaneyās
te +anapekṣās te +agniveśyāḥ/ tatra ye vaḥśiṣṭhās te jātukarṇyās te dhānyāyanās te pārāśarās te vyāghranakhās ta āṇḍāyanasta aupamanyavāḥ/ tatra ye māṇḍavyās te bhāṇḍāyanās te dhaumrāyaṇās te kātyāyanās te khalv avāhanās te sugandhārāyaṇās te kāpiṣṭhalāyanāḥ/
body.translated_text: [p.39.3] Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the seven <s>gotras</s> (lineages) of the Brahmins — listen to them. They are: <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Vātsya</s>, <s>Kautsa</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, and <s>Māṇḍavya</s> — these are the seven <s>gotras</s> of the Brahmins, O Brahmin. Each one of these <s>gotras</s> is divided sevenfold. Among the <s>Gautamas</s>: the <s>Kauthumās</s>, the <s>Gargās</s>, the <s>Bharadvājās</s>, the <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇās</s>, the <s>Vaikhānasās</s>, [folio 40] and the <s>Vajrapādās</s>. Among the <s>Vātsyās</s>: the <s>Ātreyās</s>, the <s>Maitreyās</s>, the <s>Bhārgavās</s>, the <s>Sāvarṇyās</s>, the <s>Salolās</s>, and the <s>Bahujātās</s>. Among the <s>Kautsās</s>: the <s>Maudgalyāyanās</s>, the <s>Gauṇāyanās</s>, the <s>Lāṅgalās</s>, the <s>Lagnās</s>, the <s>Daṇḍalagnās</s>, and the <s>Somabhuvās</s>. Among the <s>Kauśikās</s>: the <s>Kātyāyanās</s>, the <s>Darbhakātyāyanās</s>, the <s>Valkalinās</s>, the <s>Pakṣiṇās</s>, the <s>Laukākṣās</s>, and the <s>Lohitāyanās</s>. Among the <s>Kāśyapās</s>: the <s>Maṇḍanās</s>, the <s>Iṣṭās</s>, the <s>Śauṇḍāyanās</s>, the <s>Rocaneyās</s>, the <s>Anapekṣās</s>, and the <s>Agniveśyās</s>. Among the <s>Vāsiṣṭhās</s>: the <s>Jātukarṇyās</s>, the <s>Dhānyāyanās</s>, the <s>Pārāśarās</s>, the <s>Vyāghranakhās</s>, the <s>Āṇḍāyanās</s>, and the <s>Aupamanyavās</s>. Among the <s>Māṇḍavyās</s>: the <s>Bhāṇḍāyanās</s>, the <s>Dhaumrāyaṇās</s>, the <s>Kātyāyanās</s>, the <s>Khalvavāhanās</s>, the <s>Sugandhārāyaṇās</s>, and the <s>Kāpiṣṭhalāyanās</s>.

body.text: p.40.1/.ity etāni brāhmaṇa evam ekonapañcāśad gotrāṇi brāhmaṇaiḥ paurāṇaiḥ samyag dṛṣṭāni chandasi vyākaraṇe padamīmāṃsāyāṃ/ anyāni ca gotrāṇi vistarato mayā vācitāni/ tāni anyair na jñāyante/
body.translated_text: [p.40.1] Thus, O Brahmin, these forty-nine <s>gotras</s> were correctly perceived by the ancient Brahmins in the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic meter), in grammar, and in <s>Padamīmāṃsā</s> (word-analysis). Other <s>gotras</s> too have been recited by me in detail; those are not known by others.

body.text: p.40.2/.yad utaikatvam iti viditvā bhavān bandhur bhavitum arhati/ tasmāt te brāhmaṇa bravīmi sāmānyaṃ saṃjñāmātrakam idaṃ lokasya yad uta brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/ ekam idaṃ sarvam idam ekaṃ / pppppputrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃduhitaram utsṛja bhāryā^arthāya/ yāvantaṃ kula^śulkaṃ manyase tāvantam anupradāsyāmi/
body.translated_text: [p.40.2] Knowing that there is oneness, you ought to become a kinsman. Therefore I tell you, O Brahmin: this is merely a common conventional designation (<s>saṃjñāmātra</s>) of the world — namely 'Brahmin,' or 'Kṣatriya,' or 'Vaiśya,' or 'Śūdra.' All this is one, this entirety is one. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> for the purpose of marriage. Whatever bride-price you think fitting, that much I shall pay.

body.text: p.41.1/.idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī tṛṣṇīṃ bhūto madgubhūtaḥ srastaskandho +adhomukho niṣpratibhaḥ pradhyānaparaḥ sthito +abhūt/ adrākṣīt triśaṅkur mātaṅga^rājaḥ puṣkarasāriṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tūṣṇīṃ bhūtaṃ madgubhūtaṃ srastaskandham abhomukhaṃ niṣpratibhaṃ pradhyānaparaṃ sthitaṃ/ dṛṣṭvā ca punar idam avocat/
body.translated_text: [p.41.1] Having heard this further speech of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, the Brahmin <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> stood silent, dejected, with drooping shoulders, face downward, without reply, absorbed in deep thought. <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, saw the Brahmin <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> standing silent, dejected, with drooping shoulders, face downward, without reply, absorbed in deep thought. Having seen him, he spoke again thus:

body.text: p.41.2ab/.yādṛśaṃ vāpyate bījaṃ tādṛśaṃ labhyate phalaṃ/
body.translated_text: [p.41.2ab] Whatever seed is sown, such is the fruit obtained;

body.text: p.41.2cd/.prajāpater hi caikatve nirviśeṣo bhavaty ataḥ//
body.translated_text: [p.41.2cd] since <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of Creatures) is one, therefore there is no distinction.

body.text: p.41.3ab/.na ca^indriyāṇāṃ nānātvaṃ kriyābhedaś ca dṛśyate/
body.translated_text: [p.41.3ab] No diversity of sense-organs, nor difference in their functions, is observed

body.text: p.41.3cd/.brāhmaṇe vānya^jātau vā naiṣāṃ kiñcid viśiṣyate//
body.translated_text: [p.41.3cd] in a Brahmin or in one of another caste — nothing whatsoever distinguishes them.

body.text: p.41.4ab/.na hy ātmanaḥ samutkarṣaḥ śreṣṭha tvam iha yujyate/
body.translated_text: [p.41.4ab] No self-exaltation or claim of superiority is justified here,

body.text: p.41.4cd/.śukra^śoṇita^sambhūtaṃ yonito hy ubhayaṃ samaṃ//
body.translated_text: [p.41.4cd] for what is born from semen and blood — from the womb, both are equal.

body.text: p.41.5ab/.cāturvarṇyaṃ pravakṣyāmi paśu^dharma^kathāṃ tava/
body.translated_text: [p.41.5ab] I shall speak of the four-caste system (<s>cāturvarṇya</s>) — a tale of animal-law (<s>paśudharma</s>) for you:

body.text: p.41.5cd/.bhavet te bhaginī bhāryā naitad brāhmaṇa yujyate//
body.translated_text: [p.41.5cd] your sister would become your wife — this, O Brahmin, is not fitting.

body.text: p.41.6ab/.yadi tāvad ayaṃ loko brahmaṇā janitaḥ svayaṃ/
body.translated_text: [p.41.6ab] If indeed this world was created by <s>Brahmā</s> himself,

body.text: p.41.6cd/.brāhmaṇī brāhmaṇa^svasā kṣatriyā kṣatriyasvasā//
body.translated_text: [p.41.6cd] then a Brahmin woman is a Brahmin's sister, a Kṣatriya woman is a Kṣatriya's sister,

body.text: p.41.7ab/.atha vaiśyasya vaiśyā vai śūdrā śūdrasya vā punaḥ/
body.translated_text: [p.41.7ab] a Vaiśya woman belongs to the Vaiśya, and a Śūdra woman to the Śūdra;

body.text: p.41.7cd/.na bhāryā bhaginī yuktā brahmaṇā janitā yadi//
body.translated_text: [p.41.7cd] a wife who is a sister is not proper, if they were begotten by <s>Brahmā</s>.

body.text: p.41.8ab/.na sattvā brahmaṇo jātāḥ kleśajāḥ karmajāstvamī/
body.translated_text: [p.41.8ab] Beings are not born from <s>Brahmā</s> — they are born from affliction, born from <s>karma</s> (action);

body.text: p.41.8cd/.nīcaiś ca^uccaiś ca dūśyante sattvā nānā^āśrayāḥ pṛthak//
body.translated_text: [p.41.8cd] both low and high, beings are corrupted, of various abodes, each distinct.

body.text: p.41.9ab/.teṣāṃ ca jātisāmānyād brāhmaṇe kṣatriye tathā/
body.translated_text: [p.41.9ab] And since their birth is common, whether in a Brahmin or a Kṣatriya,

body.text: p.41.9cd/.atha vaiśye ca śūdre ca samaṃ jñānaṃ pravartate//
body.translated_text: [p.41.9cd] or in a Vaiśya or a Śūdra — knowledge operates equally in all.

body.text: p.42.1ab/.ṛgvedo +atha yajurvedaḥ sāmavedopy atharvāṇaṃ/
body.translated_text: [p.42.1ab] The <s>Ṛgveda</s>, and the <s>Yajurveda</s>, and the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and the <s>Atharvaveda</s>,

body.text: p.42.1cd/.itihāso nighaṇṭaś ca kutaś chando nirarthakaṃ//
body.translated_text: [p.42.1cd] the <s>Itihāsa</s> (epic) and the <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> (glossary) — whence comes the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic meter) that is purposeless?

body.text: p.42.2ab/.asmākam apy adhyayane maitrī vidyā tathā śikhī/
body.translated_text: [p.42.2ab] We too have our learning: <s>Maitrī Vidyā</s> (the science of friendship), and <s>Śikhī</s>,

body.text: p.42.2cd/.saṃkrāmaṇī prakāmaṇī stambhanī kāma^rūpiṇī//
body.translated_text: [p.42.2cd] <s>Saṃkrāmaṇī</s> (the transmitting one), <s>Prakāmaṇī</s> (the impelling one), <s>Stambhanī</s> (the paralyzing one), and <s>Kāmarūpiṇī</s> (the shape-shifting one),

body.text: p.42.3ab/.manojavā ca gāndhārī ghorī vidyā vaśaṅkarī/
body.translated_text: [p.42.3ab] <s>Manojavā</s> (swift as thought), <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Ghorī</s> (the terrible one), <s>Vidyā Vaśaṅkarī</s> (the subjugating science),

body.text: p.42.3cd/.kāka^vāṇī ca mantraṃ ca; indrajālaṃ ca bhañjanī//
body.translated_text: [p.42.3cd] <s>Kākavāṇī</s> (crow-speech) and the <s>Mantra</s> (spell), <s>Indrajāla</s> (net of Indra, magic), and <s>Bhañjanī</s> (the shattering one).

body.text: p.42.4ab/.asmākam āsīt puruṣā vidyāsvākhyātapaṇḍitāḥ/
body.translated_text: [p.42.4ab] Among us there were men learned and renowned in these sciences,

body.text: p.42.4cd/.maṇi^puṣpāś ca; ṛṣayo bhāsvarāś ca maharṣayaḥ//
body.translated_text: [p.42.4cd] <s>Maṇipuṣpas</s> and sages, and radiant great seers (<s>maharṣis</s>),

body.text: p.42.5ab/.saṃprāptā devatā;ṛddhiṃ kiṃ cikitsāsi vidyayā/
body.translated_text: [p.42.5ab] who attained the supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>) of the gods — what do you accomplish through mere learning?

body.text: p.42.5cd/.aśikṣitāś ca caṇḍālā brāhmaṇā veda^pāragāḥ//
body.translated_text: [p.42.5cd] Untrained <s>Caṇḍālas</s> and Brahmins who have mastered the <s>Vedas</s> —

body.text:
p.42.6ab/.kapiñjalādyā janito mantrāṇāṃ pārabhiṃgataḥ/
p.42.6cd/.na hy asau brāhmaṇīputraḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇa manyase//
body.translated_text: [p.42.6ab] <s>Kapiñjala</s> and others generated <s>mantras</s>, having gone to the furthest shore. [p.42.6cd] He was not the son of a Brahmin woman — what do you say to that, O Brahmin?

body.text: p.43.1a/.niṣādyajanayatkālī putraṃ dvaipāyānaṃ muniṃ/
body.translated_text: [p.43.1a] A <s>Niṣāda</s> (fisherwoman) named <s>Kālī</s> gave birth to the sage <s>Dvaipāyana</s> (Vyāsa),

body.text: p.43.1b/.ugraṃ tejasvinaṃ bhīṣmaṃ pañcābhijñaṃ mahā^tapaṃ/
body.translated_text: [p.43.1b] fierce, radiant, awe-inspiring, possessing the five supernatural knowledges (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>), of great austerity.

body.text: p.43.2ab/.na hy asau brāhmaṇīputraḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇa vakṣyasi//
body.translated_text: [p.43.2ab] He was not the son of a Brahmin woman — what will you say to that, O Brahmin?

body.text: p.43.2cd/.kṣatriyā reṇukā nāma jajñe rāmaṃ mahā^muniṃ/
body.translated_text: [p.43.2cd] A Kṣatriya woman named <s>Reṇukā</s> gave birth to <s>Rāma</s> (Paraśurāma), the great sage,

body.text: p.43.2ef/.paṇḍitaṃ ca vinītaṃ ca sarva^śāstra^viśāradaṃ/
body.translated_text: [p.43.2ef] learned, disciplined, and expert in all the <s>śāstras</s> (sciences).

body.text: p.43.3ab/.na hy asau brāhmaṇīputraḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇa vakṣyasi//
body.translated_text: [p.43.3ab] He was not the son of a Brahmin woman — what will you say to that, O Brahmin?

body.text: p.43.3cd/.ye ca te manujā; āsan tejasā tapasā yutāḥ/
body.translated_text: [p.43.3cd] And those men who were endowed with splendor and austerity,

body.text: p.43.4ab/.paṇḍitāś ca vinītāś ca loke ca; ṛṣisammatāḥ/
body.translated_text: [p.43.4ab] learned and disciplined, and honored in the world as sages —

body.text: p.43.4cd/.na hi te brāhmaṇīputrāḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇa vakṣyasi//
body.translated_text: [p.43.4cd] they were not sons of Brahmin women — what will you say to that, O Brahmin?

body.text: p.43.5ab/.saṃjñā kṛteyaṃ lokasya brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyās tathā/
body.translated_text: [p.43.5ab] This designation was created for the world: 'Brahmins' and 'Kṣatriyas,'

body.text: p.43.5cd/.vaiśyāx ca^eva tathā śūdrāḥ saṃjñeyaṃ saṃprakīrtitā//
body.translated_text: [p.43.5cd] and likewise 'Vaiśyas' and 'Śūdras' — this designation has been proclaimed.

body.text: p.43.6/.tasmāt te brāhmaṇa bravīmi saṃjñāmātrakam idaṃlokasya yad uta brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdara iti vā/ ekam idaṃ sarvam idam ekaṃ/ putrāya me (44) śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaram anuprayaccha bharyarthāya/ yāvantaṃ kula^śulkaṃ manyase tāvantam anupradāsyāmi/
body.translated_text: [p.43.6] Therefore I tell you, O Brahmin: this is merely a conventional designation (<s>saṃjñāmātra</s>) of the world — namely 'Brahmin,' or 'Kṣatriya,' or 'Vaiśya,' or 'Śūdra.' All this is one, this entirety is one. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son [folio 44] <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> for the purpose of marriage. Whatever bride-price you think fitting, that much I shall pay.

body.text:
p.44.1/.idaṃ ca punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya bbrāhmaṇaḥ puskarasārī triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅga^rājam idam avocat/ kiṃ gotro bhavān/ āha ātreyagotro +asmi/ hiṃpūrvaḥ/ āha/ ātreyaḥ/ kiṃcaraṇaḥāha kāleyamaitrāyaṇīyaḥ/ kati pravarāḥ/ āha trayaḥ pravarāḥ/ tad yathā vātsyāḥ kautsyā bharadvājāś ca/ ke bhavantaḥ sabrahma^cāriṇaḥ/ chandogāḥ/ kati chantogānāṃ
bhedāḥ/ ṣaṭ/ te katame/ āha/ tad yathā/ kauthumāḥ/ ca^arāyaṇīyāḥ/ lāṅgalāḥ/ sauvarcasāḥ/ kāpiñjaleyāḥ/ ārṣṭiṣeṇā iti/
body.translated_text: And having heard this repeated statement, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> said this to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, king of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>: What is your <s>gotra</s> (lineage)? He said: I am of the <s>Ātreya</s> lineage. Beginning with 'hiṃ' [the sacred syllable]. He said: <s>Ātreya</s>. What is your <s>caraṇa</s> (Vedic school)? He said: <s>Kāleyamaitrāyaṇīya</s>. How many <s>pravaras</s> (ancestral sages)? He said: Three <s>pravaras</s>. Namely: <s>Vātsya</s>, <s>Kautsya</s>, and <s>Bhāradvāja</s>. Who are your fellow <s>brahmacārins</s> (Vedic students)? <s>Chandogas</s> (followers of the Sāmaveda). How many divisions of the <s>Chandogas</s> are there? Six. Which are they? He said: Namely: <s>Kauthumas</s>, <s>Cārāyaṇīyas</s>, <s>Lāṅgalas</s>, <s>Sauvarcasas</s>, <s>Kāpiñjaleyas</s>, and <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇas</s>.

body.text: p.44.2/.kiṃ bhavato mātṛjaṃ gotraṃ/ āha/ pārāśarīyaṃ/ paṭhatu bhavān sāvitrīṃ/ kathaṃ bhavati/ katyakṣarā sāvitrī/ kathigaṇḍā/ katipadā/
body.translated_text: What is your maternal <s>gotra</s>? He said: <s>Pārāśarīya</s>. Let your honor recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. How does it go? How many syllables has the <s>Sāvitrī</s>? How many sections? How many feet?

body.text: p.44.3/.caturviṃśatyakṣarā sāvitrī/ trigaṇḍā/ aṣṭākṣarapadā/ uccārayatu bhavān sāvitrīṃ/atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin sotpattikāṃ sāvitrīṃ pravakṣyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/
body.translated_text: The <s>Sāvitrī</s> has twenty-four syllables, three sections, and feet of eight syllables each. Let your honor pronounce the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall declare the <s>Sāvitrī</s> with its origin. Listen to it.

body.text: p.44.4/.kathayatu bhavān/
body.translated_text: Let your honor recite it.

body.text:
p.44.5/.bhūta^pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇātīte +adhvani vasur nāma ṛṣir bhūva/ pañcābhijña ugratejā mahānubhāvo dhyānānāṃ lābhī/ tena tatra takṣakaduhitā kapilā nāma āsāditā bhāryā^arthaṃ/ sa tatra saṃrakta^cittas tayā kanyayā sārdhaṃ maithunam agacchat/ sa ṛṣi (45) ṛddhyā bhraṣṭo dhyānebhyo vañcitaḥ/ ṛddhiparihīnaḥ sa vipratisārī ātmano duścaritaṃ vigarhamāṇas tasyāṃ
velāyāṃ sāvitrīṃ bhāṣate sma/ tad yathā/
body.translated_text: Long ago, in a past age of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, there was a sage named <s>Vasu</s>. He was one of five supernatural powers, of fierce radiance, of great might, and an attainer of the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions). He obtained a girl named <s>Kapilā</s>, daughter of <s>Takṣaka</s>, for the purpose of marriage. With his mind impassioned, he engaged in sexual union with that maiden. That sage fell from his supernatural powers and was deprived of the <s>dhyānas</s>. Bereft of his powers, full of remorse, and reproaching his own misconduct, at that moment he uttered the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Namely:

body.text: p.45.1/.oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ/ tat savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi/ dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt/
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>. We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>; may he stimulate our thoughts.

body.text: p.45.2/.iti hi brāhmaṇa ajñāna^śodhanārtham imam eva mantraṃ sa brāhmaṇo divā^rātraṃ japati sma/ iyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sāvitrī/ pūrvajaḥ prajāpatiḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, for the purpose of purifying ignorance, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> chanted this very <s>mantra</s> day and night. This is the <s>Sāvitrī</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. The first-born <s>Prajāpati</s>,

body.text: p.45.3ab/.jaṭilastāpaso bhūtvā gahanaṃ vanam āśritaḥ/
body.translated_text: having become a matted-haired ascetic, resorted to a dense forest,

body.text: p.45.3cd/.gambhīrāv abhāse tatra hy ātmārāmas taporataḥ/
body.translated_text: in a deep and luminous [place], there, delighting in the self, devoted to austerity.

body.text: p.45.4/.devasya śreṣṭhakaṃ bhījanam apanābhyo paviṣṭa imaṃmantram ajapat/ iyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ sāvitrī/
body.translated_text: Having purified himself from sins, he chanted this <s>mantra</s> regarding the seed of the divine supreme being. This is the <s>Sāvitrī</s> of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>.

body.text: p.45.5/.oṃ citraṃ hi vaiśyakanyakā/ atha sā kanyā arthataḥ pravīṇā/
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, wonderful indeed is the <s>Vaiśya</s> maiden. And that maiden was skilled in matters of wealth.

body.text: p.46.1/.iyaṃ vaiśyānāṃ sāvitrī/ om atapaḥ sutapaḥ/ jīvema śaradāṃ śataṃ/ paśyema śaradāṃ śataṃ/ iyaṃ śūdrāṇāṃ sāvitrī/ oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ/
body.translated_text: This is the <s>Sāvitrī</s> of the <s>Vaiśyas</s>. <s>Oṃ</s>, [with] austerity and intense austerity: May we live a hundred autumns. May we see a hundred autumns. This is the <s>Sāvitrī</s> of the <s>Śūdras</s>. <s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>.

body.text: p.46.2ab/.kāmā hi loke paramāḥ prajānāṃ kleśaprahāṇe bhūtā antarāyāḥ/
body.translated_text: For desires are the supreme [obstacles] of beings in the world, obstacles to the elimination of suffering.

body.text: p.46.2cd/.tasmād bhavantaḥ prajahantu kāmān tato +atulaṃ prāpsy atha brahma^lokaṃ/
body.translated_text: Therefore, let you all abandon desires; then you shall attain the incomparable world of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: p.46.3/.itīyaṃ brāhmaṇa brahmaṇā sahāpatinā sāvitrī bhāṣitā, pūrvakaiś ca samyak saṃbuddhair abhyanumoditā/
body.translated_text: Thus this <s>Sāvitrī</s> was spoken by <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Sahāpati</s> (the Lord) and was approved by the perfectly enlightened ones of the past.

body.text: %nakṣatravaṃśaḥ āgotra 46
body.translated_text: [Chapter heading: The Lineage of the Nakṣatras, up to gotra, p. 46]

body.text: p.46.4/.paṭha bhos triśaṅko nakṣatra^vaṃśaṃ/ atha kiṃ/ bhoḥ kathayatu bhavān/ śrūyatāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatra^vaṃśaṃ kathayiṣyāmi/ tad yathā/
body.translated_text: Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lineage of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions). What then? Let your honor relate it. Listen, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall tell the lineage of the <s>nakṣatras</s>. Namely:

body.text: p.46.5/.kṛttikā rohiṇī mṛgaśirā ārdrā punarvashḥ puṣyaḥ aśleṣā maghā pūrvaphalgunī uttaraphalgunī hastā citrā svātī viśākhā anurādhā jyeṣṭhā mūlā pūrvāṣāḍhā uttarāṣāḍhā abhijit śravaṇā dhaniṣṭhā śatabhiṣā pūrvabhādrapadā uttarabhādrapadā revatī aśvinī bharaṇī / ity etāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭāviṃśati^nakṣatrāṇī/
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśirā</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Aśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>, <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, <s>Hastā</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Mūlā</s>, <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Śravaṇā</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Bharaṇī</s>. These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>.

body.text: p.46.6/.kati^tārakāṇi kati^saṃsthānāni kati^muhūrta^yogāni kim^āhārāṇi kiṃ^daivatāni kiṃ^gotrāṇi/
body.translated_text: How many stars [does each have]? How many configurations? How many <s>muhūrta</s>-conjunctions? What are their foods? What are their presiding deities? What are their <s>gotras</s>?

body.text:
p.46.7/.kṛttikā bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatraṃ ṣaṭtāraṃ kṣura^saṃsthānaṃ triṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ (47) dadhyāhāram agnidaivataṃ vaiśyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ rohiṇī^nakṣatraṃ pañca^tārakaṃ śakaṭākṛti^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^catvāriṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ mṛgamāṃsāhāraṃ prajāpati^daivataṃ bhāradvājaṃ gotreṇa/ mṛgaśirā^nakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ mṛgaśīrṣa^saṃsthānaṃ triṃśan muhūrta^yogaṃ
phalamūlāhāraṃ soma^daivataṃ mṛgāyaṇīyaṃ gotreṇa/ ārdra^nakṣatram eka^tāraṃ tilaka^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^daśa^muhūrta^yogaṃ sarpirmaṇḍāhāraṃ sūrya^daivataṃ hārītītāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ punarvasu^nakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ pada^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^catvāriṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ madhy?āhāram aditidaivataṃ vāśiṣṭhaṃ gotreṇa/ puṣya^nakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ vardhamāna^saṃsthānaṃ triśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ
madhu^maṇḍāhāraṃ bṛhaspati^daivatam aupamanyavīyaṃ gotreṇa/ aśleṣā^nakṣatram eka^tāraṃ tilaka^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^daśa^muhūrta^yogaṃ pāyasa^bhojanaṃ sarpa^daivataṃ maitrāyaṇīyaṃ gotreṇa/
body.translated_text: The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Kṛttikā</s>, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, has six stars, the configuration of a razor, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, curd as its food, <s>Agni</s> as its deity, and <s>Vaiśyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Rohiṇī</s> has five stars, the configuration of a cart, a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, deer-meat as its food, <s>Prajāpati</s> as its deity, and <s>Bhāradvāja</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Mṛgaśirā</s> has three stars, the configuration of a deer's head, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, fruits and roots as its food, <s>Soma</s> as its deity, and <s>Mṛgāyaṇīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Ārdrā</s> has one star, the configuration of a tilaka-mark, a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, clarified butter as its food, <s>Sūrya</s> as its deity, and <s>Hārītītāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Punarvasu</s> has two stars, the configuration of a foot, a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, honey(?) as its food, <s>Aditi</s> as its deity, and <s>Vāśiṣṭha</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Puṣya</s> has three stars, the configuration of a prosperous mark, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, honey-gruel as its food, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as its deity, and <s>Aupamanyavīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Aśleṣā</s> has one star, the configuration of a tilaka-mark, a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, milk-rice as its food, <s>Sarpa</s> (the Serpent) as its deity, and <s>Maitrāyaṇīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>.

body.text:
p.47.1/.iti^imāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārin sapta^nakṣatrāṇi pūrva^dvārakāṇi/ maghā^nakṣatraṃ (48)pañca^tāraṃ nadī^kubja^saṃsthānaṃ triśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ tila^kṛsarāhāraṃ pitṛdaivataṃ piṅgalāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ pūrvaphalgunī^nakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ padaka^saṃsthānaṃ triśan muhūrta^yogaṃ vilvabhojanaṃ bhavadevataṃ gautamīyaṃ gotreṇa/ uttaraphalgunī^nakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ
padaka^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^catvāriṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ godhūmamatsyāhāram aryamādaivataṃ kauśikaṃ gotreṇa/ hasta^nakṣatraṃ pañca^tāraṃ hasta^saṃsthānaṃ triṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ śyāmākabhojanaṃ sūrya^daivataṃ kāśyapaṃ gotreṇa/ citrā^nakṣatram eka^tāraṃ tilaka^saṃsthānaṃ triṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ mudgakṛsaraghṛta^pūpāhāraṃ tvaṣṭṛdaivataṃ kātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
body.translated_text: These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the eastern gate. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Maghā</s> has five stars, the configuration of a crooked river, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, sesame-rice as its food, the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors) as its deity, and <s>Piṅgalāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> has two stars, the configuration of a small foot, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, bilva-fruit as its food, <s>Bhava</s> as its deity, and <s>Gautamīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s> has two stars, the configuration of a small foot, a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, wheat-and-fish as its food, <s>Aryaman</s> as its deity, and <s>Kauśika</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Hastā</s> has five stars, the configuration of a hand, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, millet as its food, <s>Sūrya</s> as its deity, and <s>Kāśyapa</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Citrā</s> has one star, the configuration of a tilaka-mark, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, mung-bean-rice-ghee-cakes as its food, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> as its deity, and <s>Kātyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>.

body.text: p.48.1/.svātī^nakṣatram eka^tāraṃ tilaka^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^daśa^muhūrta^yogaṃ mudgakṛsaraphalāhāraṃ vāyudaivataṃ kātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ viśākhā^nakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ viṣāṇa^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^catvāriṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ tila^puṣpāhāram indrāgnidaivataṃ śāṃkhāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
body.translated_text: The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Svātī</s> has one star, the configuration of a tilaka-mark, a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, mung-bean-rice-and-fruit as its food, <s>Vāyu</s> as its deity, and <s>Kātyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Viśākhā</s> has two stars, the configuration of a horn, a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, sesame-and-flower as its food, <s>Indrāgni</s> as its deity, and <s>Śāṃkhāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>.

body.text: p.49.1.ity etāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārin sapta^nakṣatrāṇi dakṣiṇādvārakāṇi/
body.translated_text: These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the southern gate.

body.text:
p.49.2/.anurādhā^nakṣatraṃ catustāraṃ ratnābalī^saṃsthānaṃ triśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ surāmāṃsāhāraṃ mitradaivatam ālaṃbāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ jyeṣṭhā^nakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ yavamadhya^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^daśa^muhūrta^yogaṃ śāliyavāgubhojanam indradaivataṃ dīrghakātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ mūla^nakṣatraṃ saptatāraṃ vṛścika^saṃsthānaṃ triśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ mūlaphalāhāraṃ nairṛtidaivataṃ
kātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ pūrvāṣāḍhā^nakṣatraṃ catustāraṃ govikrama^saṃsthānaṃ triśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ nyagrodhakaṣāyāhāraṃ toyadaivataṃ darbhakātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ uttarāṣāḍhā^nakṣatraṃ catustāraṃ gajavikrama^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^catvāriṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ madhu^lājāhāraṃ viśva^daivataṃ maudgalāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ abhijin^nakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ gośīrsa^saṃsthānaṃ ṣaṇ^muhūrta^yogaṃ
(50) vāyuāhāraṃ brahma^daivataṃ brahmāvatīyaṃ gotreṇa/ śravaṇā^nakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ yavamadhya^saṃsthānaṃ triṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ pakṣimāṃsāhāraṃ viṣṇudaivataṃ kātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
body.translated_text: The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Anurādhā</s> has four stars, the configuration of a jewel-garland, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, meat-and-liquor as its food, <s>Mitra</s> as its deity, and <s>Ālambāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> has three stars, the configuration of a barley-grain-middle, a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, rice-and-barley-gruel as its food, <s>Indra</s> as its deity, and <s>Dīrghakātyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Mūla</s> has seven stars, the configuration of a scorpion, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, roots-and-fruits as its food, <s>Nairṛti</s> as its deity, and <s>Kātyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> has four stars, the configuration of a cow's step, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, banyan-tree-decoction as its food, the Waters (<s>Toya</s>) as its deity, and <s>Darbhakātyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> has four stars, the configuration of an elephant's step, a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, honey-and-parched-grain as its food, the <s>Viśvadevas</s> as its deity, and <s>Maudgalāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Abhijit</s> has three stars, the configuration of a cow's head, a conjunction of six <s>muhūrtas</s>, wind(?) as its food, <s>Brahmā</s> as its deity, and <s>Brahmāvatīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Śravaṇā</s> has three stars, the configuration of a barley-grain-middle, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, bird-meat as its food, <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its deity, and <s>Kātyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>.

body.text: p.50.1/.ity etāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārin sapta^nakṣatrāṇi paścimadvārakāṇi/
body.translated_text: These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the western gate.

body.text:
p.50.2/.dhaniṣṭhā^nakṣatraṃ catustāraṃ śakuna^saṃsthānaṃ triṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ kulatthapūpāhāraṃ vasudaivataṃ kauṇḍinyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ śatabhiṣā^nakṣatram eka^tāraṃ tilaka^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^daśa^muhūrta^yogaṃ yavāgubhojanaṃ varuṇadaivataṃ tāṇḍyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/ pūrvabhādrapadā^nakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ padaka^saṃsthānaṃ triṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ māṃsa^rudhirāhāram
ahirbudhnyadaivataṃ jātūkarṇyaṃ gotreṇa/ uttarabhādrapadā^nakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ padaka^saṃsthānaṃ pañca^catvāriṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ (51)māṃsāhāram aryamādaivataṃ dhyānadrāhyāyaṇīyaṃ gotreṇa/ revatī^nakṣatram eka^tāraṃ tilaka^saṃsthānaṃ triśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ dadhyāhāraṃ pūṣadaivatam aṣṭabhaginīyaṃ gotreṇa/ aśvinī^nakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ turagaśīrṣa^saṃsthānaṃ
triṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ madhu^pāyasabhojanaṃ gandharva^daivataṃ maitrāyāṇīyaṃ gotreṇa/ bharaṇī^nakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ bhaga^saṃsthānaṃ triṃśan^muhūrta^yogaṃ tila^taṇḍūlāhāraṃ yamadaivataṃ bhārgavīyaṃ gotreṇa/
body.translated_text: The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> has four stars, the configuration of a bird, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, horse-gram-cakes as its food, the <s>Vasus</s> as its deity, and <s>Kauṇḍinyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> has one star, the configuration of a tilaka-mark, a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, barley-gruel as its food, <s>Varuṇa</s> as its deity, and <s>Tāṇḍyāyanīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> has two stars, the configuration of a small foot, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, meat-and-blood as its food, <s>Ahirbudhnya</s> as its deity, and <s>Jātūkarṇya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> has two stars, the configuration of a small foot, a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, meat as its food, <s>Aryaman</s> as its deity, and <s>Dhyānadrāhyāyaṇīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Revatī</s> has one star, the configuration of a tilaka-mark, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, curd as its food, <s>Pūṣan</s> as its deity, and <s>Aṣṭabhaginīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Aśvinī</s> has two stars, the configuration of a horse's head, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, honey-and-milk-rice as its food, the <s>Gandharvas</s> as its deity, and <s>Maitrāyāṇīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Bharaṇī</s> has three stars, the configuration of the female organ, a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, sesame-and-rice as its food, <s>Yama</s> as its deity, and <s>Bhārgavīya</s> as its <s>gotra</s>.

body.text: p.51.1/.ity etāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārin sapta^nakṣatrāṇi uttara^dvārakāṇi/
body.translated_text: These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the northern gate.

body.text: p.51.2/.amīṣāṃ bhoḥ pppuṣkarasārinn aṣṭāviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ ṣaṇ^nakṣatrāṇi pañca^catvāriṃśan^muhūrta^yogāni/ tad yathā/ rohiṇī punarvasu uttaraphalgunī viśākhā uttarāṣāḍhā uttarabhādrapadā ceti/
body.translated_text: Of these twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, six <s>nakṣatras</s> have a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>. Namely: <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, and <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>.

body.text: p.51.3/.pañca^nakṣatrāṇi pañca^daśa^muhūrta^yogāni/ tad yathā/ ārdrā aśleṣā svātī jyeṣṭhā śatabhiṣā ceti/ eko +abhijit ṣaṇ^muhūrta^yogaḥ/ avaśiṣṭāni triṃśan^muhūrta^yogāni/
body.translated_text: Five <s>nakṣatras</s> have a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>. Namely: <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Aśleṣā</s>, <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>. One, <s>Abhijit</s>, has a conjunction of six <s>muhūrtas</s>. The remaining ones have a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>.

body.text:
p.52.1/.amīṣāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin saptānāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ pūrva^dvārikāṇāṃ kṛttikā prathamā nāmāśleṣā paścimā nāma/ amīṣāṃ saptānāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ dakṣiṇa^dvārikāṇāṃ maghā prathamā nāma viśākhā paścimā nāma/ amīṣāṃ paścimadvārikāṇāṃ saptānāṃ nakṣatrāṇām anurādhā prathamā nāma śravaṇā paścimā nāma/ amīṣāṃ saptānāṃ nakṣatrāṇām uttara^dvārikāṇāṃ dhaniṣṭhā prathamā
nāma bharaṇī paścimā nāma/
body.translated_text: Of these seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the eastern gate, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, <s>Kṛttikā</s> is the first and <s>Aśleṣā</s> is the last. Of these seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the southern gate, <s>Maghā</s> is the first and <s>Viśākhā</s> is the last. Of these seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the western gate, <s>Anurādhā</s> is the first and <s>Śravaṇā</s> is the last. Of these seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the northern gate, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> is the first and <s>Bharaṇī</s> is the last.

body.text:
p.53.2/.amīṣāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭāviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ sapta balāni/ katamāni sapta/ yad uta trīṇi pūrvāṇi viśākhānurādhā punarvashḥ svātiś ca/ trīṇi dāruṇāni/ ārdrā aśleṣā bharaṇī ceti/ catvāri sammānanīyāni/ yad uta trīṇi uttarāṇi rohiṇī ceti/ pañca mṛdukāni/ śravaṇā dhaniṣṭhā śatabhiṣā jyeṣṭhā mūlā iti/ pañca dhāraṇīyāni/ hastā citrā aśleṣā maghā
abhijic ceti/ catvāri kṣipra^karaṇīyāni/ yad uta kṛttikā mṛgaśirā puṣyā aśvinī ceti/
body.translated_text: Of these twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, there are seven powers. Which seven? Three are 'preliminary' (<s>pūrva</s>): <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, and <s>Svātī</s>. Three are 'fierce' (<s>dāruṇa</s>): <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Aśleṣā</s>, and <s>Bharaṇī</s>. Four are 'honorable' (<s>sammānanīya</s>): the three <s>uttara</s> [nakṣatras] and <s>Rohiṇī</s>. Five are 'gentle' (<s>mṛduka</s>): <s>Śravaṇā</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Mūlā</s>. Five are 'sustaining' (<s>dhāraṇīya</s>): <s>Hastā</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Aśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, and <s>Abhijit</s>. Four are 'swift-acting' (<s>kṣiprakaraṇīya</s>): <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Mṛgaśirā</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, and <s>Aśvinī</s>.

body.text: %nakṣatrāṇāṃ yogaḥ
body.translated_text: [Chapter heading: The Conjunction of the Nakṣatras]

body.text:
p.52.3/.amīṣāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭaviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ trayo yogā bhavanti/ ṛṣabhānusārī yogaḥ/ vatsānusārī yogaḥ/ yuganaddho yogaḥ/ tatra nakṣatraṃ yadi purastād gacchati candraś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ, ayam ucyate ṛṣabhānusārī yoga iti/ yad uta candraḥ purastād gacchati nakṣatraṃ ca pṛṣṭhataḥ, tadā bhavati vatsānusārī yogaḥ/ yadi punaś candro nakṣatraṃ ca^ubhau
samau yugapad gacchataḥ, tadāyam ucyate yuganaddho yoga iti/
body.translated_text: Of these twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, there are three conjunctions (<s>yoga</s>). The <s>ṛṣabhānusārī</s> (bull-following) conjunction, the <s>vatsānusārī</s> (calf-following) conjunction, and the <s>yuganaddha</s> (yoked-together) conjunction. Of these, when the <s>nakṣatra</s> goes ahead and the moon follows behind, this is called the <s>ṛṣabhānusārī</s> conjunction. When the moon goes ahead and the <s>nakṣatra</s> follows behind, then it is the <s>vatsānusārī</s> conjunction. And when the moon and the <s>nakṣatra</s> both move equally and simultaneously, this is called the <s>yuganaddha</s> conjunction.

body.text: %grahaḥ 53
body.translated_text: [Section:] Planets

body.text: p.53.1/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin grahān pravakṣyāmi tac chrūyatāṃ/ tad yathā śukro bṛhaspatiḥ śanaiścaro budho +aṅgārakaḥ sūryas tārādhipatiś ceti/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the planets (<s>graha</s>); listen to that. They are as follows: <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), and the Lord of the Stars (the Moon) — these [are the seven planets].

body.text: %rātridivasayor hrāsavṛddhī 53
body.translated_text: [Section:] The decrease and increase of night and day

body.text: p.53.2/.evaṃ viparivartamāne loke nakṣatreṣu pravibhakteṣu kathaṃ rātridivasānāṃ hrāso vṛddhiś ca bhavati/ tad ucyate/
body.translated_text: As the world revolves and the <s>nakṣatras</s> are distributed, how does the decrease and increase of nights and days occur? This is stated:

body.text: p.53.3/.hemantānāṃ dvitīye māsi rohiṇyām aṣṭamyāṃ dvādaśa^muhūrto divaso bhavati/ aṣṭādaśa^muhūrtā rātriḥ/ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse rohiṇyām aṣṭamyām aṣṭādaśa^muhūrto divaso bhavati/ dvādaśa^muhūrtā rātriḥ/ varṣāṇāṃ paścime māse rohiṇyām aṣṭamyāṃ catur^daśa^muhūrto divaso bhavati/ ṣoḍaśa^muhūrtā rātriḥ/
body.translated_text: In the second month of winter, on the eighth [day] under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the day consists of twelve <s>muhūrtas</s> and the night of eighteen <s>muhūrtas</s>. In the last month of summer, on the eighth [day] under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the day consists of eighteen <s>muhūrtas</s> and the night of twelve <s>muhūrtas</s>. In the last month of the rains, on the eighth [day] under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the day consists of fourteen <s>muhūrtas</s> and the night of sixteen <s>muhūrtas</s>.

body.text: p.53.4/.kiṃ bhos triśaṅko rātridivasānāṃ prasthānaṃ/ divasānudivasaṃ/ kiṃ pakṣasya prasthānaṃ/ (54)pratipad/ kiṃ saṃvatsarasya prasthānaṃ/ pauṣaḥ/ kim ṛtūnāṃ prasthānaṃ/ prāvṛṭ/
body.translated_text: O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, what is the beginning of nights and days? Day by day. What is the beginning of the fortnight (<s>pakṣa</s>)? The <s>pratipad</s> (first day). What is the beginning of the year? [The month of] <s>Pauṣa</s>. What is the beginning of the seasons? The rainy season (<s>prāvṛṭ</s>).

body.text: %^muhūrtanāmāni 54
body.translated_text: [Section:] Names of the <s>muhūrtas</s>

body.text: p.54.1/.kiṃ bhos triśaṅko kṣaṇasya parimāṇaṃ / kiṃ lavasya/ kiṃ muhūrtasya/
body.translated_text: O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, what is the measure of a <s>tatkṣaṇa</s> (sub-instant)? What is [the measure] of a <s>lava</s>? What is [the measure] of a <s>muhūrta</s>?

body.text: p.54.2/.tad yathā bhoḥ puṣkarasārin striyā nātidīrghahrasvaḥ kartinyāḥ sūtrodyāmaḥ/ evaṃ dīrghas tatkṣaṇaḥ/ viṃśatyadhikaṃ tatkṣaṇaśatam ekaḥ kṣaṇaḥ/ ṣaṣṭikṣaṇā eko lavaḥ/ triṃśallavā eko muhūrtaḥ/ etena kramasambandhena triṃśan^muhūrtam ekaṃ rātridivasam anumīyate/ teṣāṃ muhūrtānām imāni nāmāni bhavanti/
body.translated_text: Now, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, a woman's thread-drawing from a spindle, neither too long nor too short — that length is one <s>tatkṣaṇa</s>. One hundred and twenty <s>tatkṣaṇas</s> make one <s>kṣaṇa</s> (instant). Sixty <s>kṣaṇas</s> make one <s>lava</s>. Thirty <s>lavas</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>. By this sequential reckoning, thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> are reckoned as one day-and-night. The names of these <s>muhūrtas</s> are as follows:

body.text: p.54.3/.āditya udayati ṣaṇṇavati^pauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ caturojā nāma muhūrto bhavati/ ṣaṣṭipauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ śveto nāma muhūrto bhavati/ dvādaśa^pauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ samṛddho nāma muhūrto bhavati/ ṣaṭpauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ śarapatho nāma muhūrto bhavati/
body.translated_text: When the sun rises, at a shadow of ninety-six [man-lengths], the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Caturojā</s> occurs. At a shadow of sixty man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Śveta</s> occurs. At a shadow of twelve man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Samṛddha</s> occurs. At a shadow of six man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Śarapatha</s> occurs.

body.text: p.55.1/.pañca^pauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyām atisamṛddho nāma muhūrto bhavat/ catuḥ^pauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyām udgato nāma muhūrto bhavati/ tripauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ sumukho nāma muhūrto bhavati/ sthite madhyāhne vajrako nāma muhūrto bhavati/ parivṛtte madhyāhne tripuruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ rohito nāma muhūrto bhavati/
body.translated_text: At a shadow of five man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Atisamṛddha</s> occurs. At a shadow of four man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Udgata</s> occurs. At a shadow of three man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Sumukha</s> occurs. At midday standing [i.e., when the shadow is stationary], the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Vajraka</s> occurs. After midday has turned, at a shadow of three man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Rohita</s> occurs.

body.text: p.55.2/.catuḥ^pauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ balo nāma muhūrto bhavati/ pañca^pauruṣāyāṃ chayayaṃ vijayo nāma muhūrtaḥ/ ṣaṭpauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ sarva^raso nāma muhūrtaḥ/ dvādaśa^paruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ vasur nāma muhūrtaḥ/ ṣaṣṭipauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ sundaro nāma muhūrtaḥ/ avataramāṇa āditye ṣaṇṇavati^pauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ parabhayo nāma muhūrto bhavati/
body.translated_text: At a shadow of four man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Bala</s> occurs. At a shadow of five man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Vijaya</s>. At a shadow of six man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Sarvarasa</s>. At a shadow of twelve man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Vasu</s>. At a shadow of sixty man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Sundara</s>. As the sun descends, at a shadow of ninety-six man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Parabhaya</s> occurs.

body.text: p.55.3/.ity etāni divasasya muhūrtāni/
body.translated_text: These are the <s>muhūrtas</s> of the day.

body.text:
p.55.4/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin rātryā muhūrtāni vyākhyāsyāmi/astaṃgata āditye raudro nāma muhūrtaḥ/ tatas tārāvacaro nāma muhūrtaḥ/ saṃyamo nāma muhūrtaḥ (56) sāṃpraiyako nāma muhūrtaḥ/ ananto nāma muhūrtaḥ/ gardabhā nāma muhūrtaḥ/ rākṣaso nāma muhūrtaḥ/ sthite +ardharātre +avayavo nāma muhūrtaḥ/ atikrānte +ardharātre brahmā nāma muhūrtaḥ/ ditir nāma
muhūrtaḥ/ ātapāgnir nāma muhūrta/ abhijin nāma muhūrtaḥ/ ity etāni rātrer muhūrtanāmāni/ iti bhoḥ puṣkarasārin imāni triśan muhūrtāni yair aho^rātraṃ prajñāyate/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the <s>muhūrtas</s> of the night. When the sun has set, [there is] the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Raudra</s>. Then the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Tārāvacara</s> (Star-wanderer). The <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Saṃyama</s> (Restraint). The <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Sāṃpraiyaka</s>. The <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Ananta</s> (Infinite). The <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Gardabhā</s> (Donkey). The <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Rākṣasa</s> (Demonic). At midnight standing, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Avayava</s> (Limb). After midnight has passed, the <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Brahmā</s>. The <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Diti</s>. The <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Ātapāgni</s> (Heat-fire). The <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Abhijit</s> (Victorious). These are the names of the nighttime <s>muhūrtas</s>. Thus, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, these are the thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> by which the day-and-night is known.

body.text:
p.56.1/.tatkṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇo lavo muhūrtaḥ / tatra triṃśatitamo bhāgo muhūrtasya lavaḥ/ ṣaṣṭitamo bhāgo lavasya kṣaṇaḥ/ viṃśatyuttarabhāgaśataṃ kṣaṇasya tatkṣaṇaḥ/ tad yathā striyā nātidīrghahrasvaḥ kartinyāḥ sūtrodyāmaḥ/ evaṃ dīrghas tatkṣaṇaḥḥ/ viṃśatyuttarakṣaṇaśataṃ tatkṣaṇasyaikaḥ kṣaṇaḥ/ ṣaṣṭikṣaṇā eko lavaḥ/ triṃśallavā eko muhūrtaḥ/ etena kramayogena
triṃśan^muhūrtam ekam aho^rātraṃ/ triṃśad ahorātrāṇy eko māsaḥ/ dvādaśa^māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ/ caturojāḥ śvetaḥ samṛddhaḥ śarapatho +atisamṛddha udgataḥ (57) sumukho vajrako rohito balo vijayaḥ sarva^raso vasuḥ sundaraḥ para^bhayaḥ/ raudras tārāvacaraḥ saṃyamaḥ sāṃpraiyako +annanto gardabho rākṣaso +avayavo brahmā ditir arko vidhamano āgneya ātapāgnir abhijit/
body.translated_text: <s>Tatkṣaṇa</s>, <s>kṣaṇa</s>, <s>lava</s>, <s>muhūrta</s> — of these, the thirtieth part of a <s>muhūrta</s> is a <s>lava</s>; the sixtieth part of a <s>lava</s> is a <s>kṣaṇa</s>; one hundred and twenty [parts] of a <s>kṣaṇa</s> is a <s>tatkṣaṇa</s>. That is, a woman's thread-drawing from a spindle, neither too long nor too short — that length is one <s>tatkṣaṇa</s>. One hundred and twenty <s>tatkṣaṇas</s> make one <s>kṣaṇa</s>. Sixty <s>kṣaṇas</s> make one <s>lava</s>. Thirty <s>lavas</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>. By this sequential reckoning, thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> make one day-and-night. Thirty day-and-nights make one month. Twelve months make one year. <s>Caturojā</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Samṛddha</s>, <s>Śarapatha</s>, <s>Atisamṛddha</s>, <s>Udgata</s>, <s>Sumukha</s>, <s>Vajraka</s>, <s>Rohita</s>, <s>Bala</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Sarvarasa</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Sundara</s>, <s>Parabhaya</s>; <s>Raudra</s>, <s>Tārāvacara</s>, <s>Saṃyama</s>, <s>Sāṃpraiyaka</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Gardabha</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Avayava</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Vidhamana</s>, <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>Ātapāgni</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>.

body.text: p.57.1/.iti^imāni muhūrtānāṃ nāmāni/
body.translated_text: These are the names of the <s>muhūrtas</s>.

body.text: %kāla^utpattiḥ 57
body.translated_text: [Section:] The origin of time

body.text: p.57.2ab/.kālotpattim api te brāhmaṇa vakṣyāmi śṛṇu/
body.translated_text: I shall tell you also the origin of time (<s>kālotpatti</s>), O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; listen.

body.text: p.57.2cd/.kālasya kiṃ pramāṇam iti tad ucyate/
body.translated_text: What is the measure of time? This is stated:

body.text: p.57.3/.dvāvakṣinimeṣāv eko lavaḥ/ asṭau lavā ekā kāṣṭhā/ ṣoḍaśakāṣṭhā ekā kalā/ kalānāṃ triṃśadeko nāḍikā/ tatra dve nāḍika eko muhūrtaḥ/
body.translated_text: Two eye-blinks (<s>akṣinimeṣa</s>) make one <s>lava</s>. Eight <s>lavas</s> make one <s>kāṣṭhā</s>. Sixteen <s>kāṣṭhās</s> make one <s>kalā</s>. Thirty <s>kalās</s> make one <s>nāḍikā</s>. Two <s>nāḍikās</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>.

body.text: p.57.4/.nāḍikāyāḥ punaḥ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ/ tad ucyate/
body.translated_text: What then is the measure of a <s>nāḍikā</s>? This is stated:

body.text:
p.57.5/.droṇaṃ salilasyaikaṃ/ taddharaṇato dve palaśate bhavataḥ/ nālikāchidrasya kiṃ pramāṇaṃ/ suvarṇa^mātraṃ/ upari catur^aṅgulā suvarṇa^śalākā kartavyā/ (58) vṛttaparimaṇḍalā samāntāc caturasrā āyatā/ yadā ca^evaṃ śīryeta tat toyaṃ ghaṭasya tadaikā nāḍikā/ etena nālikāpramāṇena vibhakte dve nāḍika eko muhūrtaḥ/ etena bho brāhmaṇa triṃśan muhūrtāḥ/ yai
rātridivasā anumīyanta iti/
body.translated_text: One <s>droṇa</s> (measure) of water; from carrying that, there are two hundred <s>palas</s> (weight units). What is the measure of the <s>nālikā</s>-hole? The size of a <s>suvarṇa</s> (gold coin). Above it, a golden rod of four <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) should be made — round, circular, even on all sides, and elongated. When the water thus drains from the vessel, that is one <s>nāḍikā</s>. By this <s>nālikā</s> measurement, when divided, two <s>nāḍikās</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>. By this [reckoning], O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, there are thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> by which day-and-nights are measured.

body.text: p.58.1/.tataḥ ṣoḍaśa nimeṣā ekā kāṣṭhā/ ṣoḍaśa kāṣṭhā ekā kalā/ ṣaṣṭikalā eko muhūrtaḥ/ triṃśan^muhūrtā ekam ahorātram/ triṃśad ahorātrāṇy eko māsaḥ/ dvādaśa^māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ/
body.translated_text: Further: sixteen eye-blinks make one <s>kāṣṭhā</s>. Sixteen <s>kāṣṭhās</s> make one <s>kalā</s>. Sixty <s>kalās</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>. Thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> make one day-and-night. Thirty day-and-nights make one month. Twelve months make one year.

body.text: p.58.2/.etena punarakṣinimeṣeṇa ṣoḍaśakoṭayo +aṣṭapañcāśac ca śata^sahasrāṇi aṣṭāśīti^sahasrāṇi sa evaṃ māpitaḥ/ tac ca brāhmaṇa kālotpattir vyākhyātā/
body.translated_text: Furthermore, by this [standard of the] eye-blink, [the total number of eye-blinks in a year amounts to] sixteen <s>koṭis</s> (crores), fifty-eight hundred-thousands, and eighty-eight thousand — thus measured. And so, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of time has been explained.

body.text: %krośayojana^utpattiḥ 58
body.translated_text: [Section:] The origin of <s>krośa</s> and <s>yojana</s>

body.text:
p.58.3/.sṛṇu brāhmaṇa krośayojanānām utpattiṃ/ sapta paramāṇava eko +aṇur bhavati/ saptāṇavaḥ sarva^sūkṣmaṃ dṛsyate/ tad ekaṃ vātāyanarajaḥ/ vātāyanarajāṃsi sapta, śaśa^karajaḥ/ sapta śaśa^karajāṃsy eḍa^karajaḥ/ sapta eḍa^karajāṃśyekaṃ gorajaḥ/ saptagorajāṃsy ekā yūkā/ saptayūkā ekā likṣā/ saptalikṣā eko yavaḥ/ sapta yavā ekāṅguliḥ/ dvādaśāṅgulayo vitastiḥ/
dve vitastī eko hastaḥ/ catvāro hastā ekaṃ dhanuḥ/ dhanuḥ^sahasram ekaḥ krośaḥ/ catvāraḥ krośā eko māgadhayojanaḥ/ yojanasya pramāṇaṃ piṇḍitāṃ/
body.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, to the origin of <s>krośas</s> and <s>yojanas</s>. Seven <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms) make one <s>aṇu</s> (molecule). Seven <s>aṇus</s> make the very finest visible [particle] — that is one mote in a sunbeam (<s>vātāyanarajas</s>). Seven sunbeam-motes make one <s>śaśakarajas</s> (rabbit-foot dust). Seven <s>śaśakarajas</s> make one <s>eḍakarajas</s> (sheep-foot dust). Seven <s>eḍakarajas</s> make one <s>gorajas</s> (cow-foot dust). Seven <s>gorajas</s> make one <s>yūkā</s> (louse). Seven <s>yūkās</s> make one <s>likṣā</s> (nit). Seven <s>likṣās</s> make one <s>yava</s> (barleycorn). Seven <s>yavas</s> make one <s>aṅguli</s> (finger-breadth).
