Twelve <s>aṅgulis</s> make one <s>vitasti</s> (span). Two <s>vitastis</s> make one <s>hasta</s> (cubit). Four <s>hastas</s> make one <s>dhanus</s> (bow-length). One thousand <s>dhanus</s> make one <s>krośa</s> (league). Four <s>krośas</s> make one <s>Māgadha</s> <s>yojana</s>. The total measure of a <s>yojana</s> [in paramāṇus]:

body.text: p.59.1/.paramāṇūnāṃ koṭiśata^sahasrāṇi catur^viṃśatiś caikonatriṃśatkoṭi^sahasrāṇi dvādaśa ca śata^sahasrāṇi/ evaṃ māpitaṃ yojanam iti/
body.translated_text: One million <s>koṭis</s> of <s>paramāṇus</s> — twenty-four times twenty-nine thousand <s>koṭis</s> and twelve hundred thousand. Thus is a <s>yojana</s> measured.

body.text: p.59.2/.śṛṇu brāhmaṇa suvarṇasya parimāṇotpattiṃ/ tatkathayatu bhavān/
body.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, to the origin of the measure of gold (<s>suvarṇa</s>). Let the venerable one explain it.

body.text: p.59.3/.dvādaśa yavā māṣakaḥ/ ṣoḍaśa māsakā ekaḥ karṣaḥ/suvarṇasya parimāṇaṃ piṇḍitam iti/ dve koṭī pañca^viṃśatiś ca sahasrāṇi pañca^śatāny aṣṭau ca paramāṇavaḥ/ evaṃ māpitā brāhmaṇa suvarṇasya parimāṇa^utpattiḥ/
body.translated_text: Twelve <s>yavas</s> (barleycorns) make one <s>māṣaka</s>. Sixteen <s>māṣakas</s> make one <s>karṣa</s>. The total measure of a <s>suvarṇa</s> [in paramāṇus]: two <s>koṭis</s>, twenty-five thousand, five hundred, and eight <s>paramāṇus</s>. Thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of the measure of gold has been explained.

body.text: p.59.4/.śṛṇu brāhmaṇa palapramāṇaṃ/ catuḥṣaṣṭi^māṣakāḥ palaṃ māgadhakaṃ/ māgadhakayā tulayā palasya parimāṇaṃ piṇḍitaṃ/ paramāṇūnām aṣṭakoṭayaḥ saptacatvāriṃśac ca śata^sahasrāṇi sapta ca sahasrāṇi dve śate +aśītiś ca paramāṇavaḥ/ evaṃ māpitaṃ brāhmaṇa palasya parimāṇam iti/
body.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, to the measure of a <s>pala</s> (weight unit). Sixty-four <s>māṣakas</s> make one <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>pala</s>. The total measure of a <s>pala</s> by the <s>Māgadhaka</s> scale [in paramāṇus]: eight <s>koṭis</s>, forty-seven hundred-thousands, seven thousand, two hundred, and eighty <s>paramāṇus</s>. Thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the measure of a <s>pala</s> has been explained.

body.text: p.59.5/.śṛṇu brāhmaṇa rasa^parimāṇasya^utpattiṃ/ catur^viṃśati^palāni māgadhakaḥ/ prasthaḥ/ tat rasa^parimāṇaṃ/ māgadhakayā tulayā prasthāsya parimāṇaṃ piṇḍitaṃ/ dve koṭiśate tisraś ca koṭaya ekonatiṃśac ca śata^sahasrāṇi catuḥsaptati (60) sahasrāṇi sapta ca śatāni viṃśatiś ca paramāṇavaḥ/ evaṃ māpitā brāhmaṇa rasa^mānasya^utpattir iti/
body.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, to the origin of the measure of liquid (<s>rasa</s>). Twenty-four <s>palas</s> make one <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>prastha</s> (volume measure). That is the liquid measure. The total measure of a <s>prastha</s> by the <s>Māgadhaka</s> scale [in paramāṇus]: two hundred <s>koṭis</s> and three <s>koṭis</s>, twenty-nine hundred-thousands, seventy-four thousand, seven hundred, and twenty <s>paramāṇus</s>. Thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of the liquid measure has been explained.

body.text: p.60.1/.śṛṇu brāhmaṇa dhānya^parimāṇasya^utpattiṃ/ ekonatriṃśati^palāny eka^karṣeṇonāni māgadhaḥ prasthaḥ/ māpitaṃ dhānya^parimāṇaṃ/ māgadhakayā tulayā prasthasya parimāṇaṃ piṇḍitaṃ/ koṭiśatam aṣṭapañcāśac ca koṭayo dvir aśītiś ca śata sahasrāṇi eka^ṣaṣṭiś ca sahasrāṇi pañca^śatāni triṃśac ca paramāṇavaḥ/ evaṃ māpitaṃ brāhmaṇa dhānyasya parimāṇam iti/
body.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, to the origin of the measure of grain (<s>dhānya</s>). Twenty-nine <s>palas</s> less one <s>karṣa</s> make one <s>Māgadha</s> <s>prastha</s>. Thus is the grain measure measured. The total measure of a <s>prastha</s> by the <s>Māgadhaka</s> scale [in paramāṇus]: one hundred <s>koṭis</s>, fifty-eight <s>koṭis</s>, and twice eighty-two hundred-thousands, sixty-one thousand, five hundred, and thirty <s>paramāṇus</s>. Thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the measure of grain has been explained.

body.text: %nakṣatravyā^karaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: [Section:] The grammar of <s>nakṣatras</s>

body.text: p.60.2/.paṭha bhos triśaṅko nakṣatra^vyākaranaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ/ atha khalu bho brāhmaṇa nakṣatra^vyākaranaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ kathayatu bhavān/
body.translated_text: Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the chapter called 'the grammar of <s>nakṣatras</s>.' Now then, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I shall explain the chapter called 'the grammar of <s>nakṣatras</s>.' Listen to that. Let the venerable one explain.

body.text:
p.61.1/.kṛttikāsu jāto mānavo yaśasvī bhavati/ rohiṇyāṃ jātaḥ subhago bhavati bhogavāṃś ca/ mṛgaśirasi jāto yuddhārthī bhavati/ ārdrāyāṃ jāta utso +anna^pānānāṃ bhavati/ punarvasau jātaḥ kṛṣimān bhavati gorakṣaś ca/ puṣye jātaḥ śīlavān bhavati/ aśleṣāyāṃ jātaḥ kāmuko bhavati/ maghāyāṃ jāto matimān bhavati, mahā^ātmā ca/ pūrvaphalgunyāṃ jāto +alpa^ayuṣko
bhavati/ uttaraphalgunyāṃ jāta upavāsaśīlo bhavati, svargaparāyaṇaś ca/ haste jātaś cauro bhavati/ citrāyāṃ jāto nṛtyagītakuśalo bhavati, ābharaṇa^vidhijñaś ca/ svātyāṃ jāto gaṇako bhavati, gaṇaka^mahāmātro vā/ viśākhāyāṃ jāto rāja^bhaṭo bhavati/ anurādhāyāṃ jāto vāṇijako bhavati sārthikaḥ/ jyeṣṭhāyāṃ jāto +alpa^ayuṣko bhavati, alpa^bhogaś ca/ mūle jātaḥ
putravān bhavati, yaśasvī ca/ pūrvāṣāḍhāyāṃ jāto yogācāro bhavati/ uttarāṣāḍhāyāṃ jāto bhakteśvaraḥ kulīnaś ca bhavati/ abhijiti jātaḥ kīrtimān puruṣo bhavati/ śravaṇe jāto (62) rāja^pūjito bhavati/ dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ jāto dhanāḍhyo bhavati/ śatabhiṣāyāṃ jāto mūliko bhavati/ pūrvabhādrapadāyāṃ jātaś caura^senāpatir bhavati/ uttarabhādrapadāyāṃ jāto gandhiko bhavati,
gandharvaś ca/ revatyāṃ jāto nāviko bhavati/ aśvinyāṃ jāto +aśvavāṇijako bhavati/ bharaṇyāṃ jāto vadhyaghātako bhavati/ ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatra^vyākaraṇo nāma/
body.translated_text: A person born under <s>Kṛttikā</s> becomes famous. One born under <s>Rohiṇī</s> becomes fortunate and wealthy. One born under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> becomes eager for battle. One born under <s>Ārdrā</s> becomes a source of food and drink. One born under <s>Punarvasu</s> becomes a farmer and a cowherd. One born under <s>Puṣya</s> becomes virtuous. One born under <s>Aśleṣā</s> becomes lustful. One born under <s>Maghā</s> becomes wise and great-souled. One born under <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> becomes short-lived. One born under <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s> becomes inclined to fasting and devoted to heaven. One born under <s>Hasta</s> becomes a thief. One born under <s>Citrā</s> becomes skilled in dance and song, and knowledgeable in the art of ornaments. One born under <s>Svātī</s> becomes an accountant, or a chief accountant. One born under <s>Viśākhā</s> becomes a royal soldier. One born under <s>Anurādhā</s> becomes a merchant and caravan leader. One born under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> becomes short-lived and of little enjoyment. One born under <s>Mūla</s> becomes blessed with sons and famous. One born under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> becomes a practitioner of <s>yoga</s>. One born under <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> becomes a lord of provisions and of noble birth. One born under <s>Abhijit</s> becomes a renowned person. One born under <s>Śravaṇa</s> becomes honored by kings. One born under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> becomes wealthy. One born under <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> becomes an herbalist. One born under <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> becomes a chief of a band of thieves. One born under <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> becomes a perfumer and a <s>gandharva</s> (celestial musician). One born under <s>Revatī</s> becomes a boatman. One born under <s>Aśvinī</s> becomes a horse-dealer. One born under <s>Bharaṇī</s> becomes an executioner. This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is called the exposition of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions).

body.text: %nakṣatranirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: Section: Determination of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>

body.text: p.62.1/.paṭha bhos triśaṅko nakṣatra^nirdeśaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ/ atha bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatra^nirdeśaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi tac chrūyatāṃ / kathayatu bhavān/
body.translated_text: Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the chapter called the Determination of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>. Now, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called the Determination of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>; listen to it. Let the venerable one speak.

body.text: p.62.2ab/.kṛttikāsu niviṣṭaṃ vai nagaraṃ jvalati śriyā/
body.translated_text: A city founded under <s>Kṛttikā</s> blazes with glory;

body.text: p.62.2cd/.prabhūratnojvalaṃ ca^eva tan nagaraṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: That city should be described as resplendent with abundant jewels.

body.text: p.62.3ab/.rohiṇyāṃ tu niviṣṭaṃ vai nagaraṃ tad vinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: A city founded under <s>Rohiṇī</s> should be described thus:

body.text: p.62.3cd/.dhārmiko +atra jano bhūyāt prabhūta^dhana^sañcayaḥ/
body.translated_text: The people there would be righteous, with abundant accumulation of wealth,

body.text: p.62.3ef/.vidyā^prakṛti^sampannaḥ svadārābhir ato +api ca//
body.translated_text: endowed with learning and good nature, and devoted to their own wives.

body.text: p.62.4ab/.mṛgaśīrṣe niviṣṭaṃ tu strībhir gobhir dhanais tathā/
body.translated_text: A city founded under <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>, with women, cattle, and wealth,

body.text: p.62.4cd/.mālyabhogaiś ca saṅkīrṇam adbhutaiś ca puraskṛtaṃ//
body.translated_text: filled with garlands and enjoyments, and distinguished by wonders.

body.text: p.63.1ab/.ārdrāyāṃ matsya^māṃsāni bhakṣyabhojyadhanāni ca/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Ārdrā</s>, there are fish and meat, food, delicacies, and wealth,

body.text: p.63.1cd/.bhavanti krūrapuruṣā mūrkhaprakṛtayaḥ pure//
body.translated_text: but the men in the city are cruel, of foolish disposition.

body.text: p.63.2ab/.punarvasau niviṣṭe tu nagaraṃ dīpyate śriyā/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Punarvasu</s>, the city shines with glory,

body.text: p.63.2cd/.prabhūta^dhana^dhānyaṃ ca bhūtvā vā^api vinaśyati//
body.translated_text: abounding in wealth and grain, but having prospered, it may also perish.

body.text: p.63.3ab/.srīmatpuṣye niviṣṭe tu prajā duṣṭā prasīdati/
body.translated_text: When founded under auspicious <s>Puṣya</s>, even wicked people become calm;

body.text: p.63.3cd/.yuktāḥ śriyā ca dharmiṣṭhās tathiva cirajīvinaḥ//
body.translated_text: they are endowed with glory, righteous, and likewise long-lived.

body.text: p.63.4ab/.tejasvinaś ca dīrghāyur^dhana^dhānya^rasānvitāḥ/
body.translated_text: They are radiant, long-lived, and endowed with wealth, grain, and flavors;

body.text: p.63.4cd/.vanaspatis tathā kṣipraṃ puṣyet tatra punaḥ punaḥ//
body.translated_text: and trees there bear fruit quickly, again and again.

body.text: p.63.5ab/.aśleṣāyāṃ niviṣṭe tu durbhagāḥ kalaha^priyāḥ/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Aśleṣā</s>, the people are unfortunate and quarrelsome,

body.text: p.63.5cd/.duḥśīlā duḥkhabhājaś ca nivasanti narādhamāḥ//
body.translated_text: of bad character and prone to suffering — the basest of men dwell there.

body.text: p.63.6ab/.maghāyāṃ ca niviṣṭe tu vidyāvanto mahā^dhanāḥ/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Maghā</s>, there are learned and greatly wealthy people;

body.text: p.63.6cd/.svadārā^abhiratā martyā jāyante suparākramāḥ//
body.translated_text: mortals devoted to their own wives are born there, of great valor.

body.text: p.64.1ab/.phalgunyāṃ tu striyo mālyaṃ bhojanācchādanaṃ śubhaṃ/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Phalgunī</s>, women, garlands, fine food and clothing,

body.text: p.64.1cd/.gandhopetāni dhanyāni niviṣṭe nagare bhavet//
body.translated_text: fragrant and excellent things would be found in the founded city.

body.text: p.64.2ab/.uttarāyāṃ tu phālgunyāṃ dhānyāni ca dhanāni ca/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, there would be grain and wealth,

body.text: p.64.2cd/.mūrkhā janā jitāḥ strībhir niviṣṭe nagare bhavet//
body.translated_text: but foolish people dominated by women would be found in the founded city.

body.text: p.64.3ab/.haste ca viniviṣṭe tu vidyāvanto mahā^dhanāḥ/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Hasta</s>, there are learned and greatly wealthy people;

body.text: p.64.3cd/.parasparaṃ ca rucitaṃ śayanaṃ nagare bhavet//
body.translated_text: pleasant resting places appreciated by one another would be found in the city.

body.text: p.64.4ab/.citrāyāṃ ca niviṣṭe tu strī^jitāḥ sarva^mānavāḥ/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Citrā</s>, all men are dominated by women;

body.text: p.64.4cd/.śrīmat^kāntaṃ ca nagaraṃ jvalantaṃ tad vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: that city should be described as glorious, beautiful, and radiant.

body.text: p.64.5ab/.svātyāṃ pure niviṣṭe tu prabhūta^dhana^sañcayāḥ/
body.translated_text: When a city is founded under <s>Svātī</s>, there are people with abundant accumulated wealth,

body.text: p.64.5cd/.lubdhāḥ krūrāś ca mūrkhāś ca prabhūtā nagare bhavet//
body.translated_text: but the greedy, the cruel, and the foolish would abound in the city.

body.text: p.64.6ab/.viśākhāyāṃ niviṣṭaṃ tu nagaraṃ jvalati śriyā/
body.translated_text: A city founded under <s>Viśākhā</s> blazes with glory;

body.text: p.64.6cd/.yāyajūkajanākīrṇaṃ śastrāntaṃ ca vinirdiśed//
body.translated_text: filled with people devoted to sacrifice, and one should predict it ends by the sword.

body.text: p.64.7ab/.anurādhāniviṣṭe tu dharma^śīlā jitendriyāḥ/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Anurādhā</s>, the people are righteous, self-controlled,

body.text: p.64.7cd/.svadāraniratāḥ puṇyā japahomaparāyaṇāḥ//
body.translated_text: devoted to their own wives, meritorious, and devoted to prayer and oblation.

body.text: p.65.1ab/.jyeṣṭhāyāṃ sanniviṣṭaṃ tu bahu^ratnadhanānvitaiḥ/
body.translated_text: A city established under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, endowed with abundant jewels and wealth,

body.text: p.65.1cd/.sattvair veda^vidaiḥ pūrṇaṃ śaśvatsamabhivardhate//
body.translated_text: filled with beings learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, ever flourishes.

body.text: p.65.2ab/.mūlena saniviṣṭaṃ tu puraṃ dhānya^dhanānvitaṃ/
body.translated_text: A city established under <s>Mūla</s>, endowed with grain and wealth,

body.text: p.65.2cd/.duḥśīlajana^saṅkīrṇaṃ pāṃsunā ca vinaśyati//
body.translated_text: crowded with ill-natured people, perishes through dust [i.e., destruction].

body.text: p.65.3ab/.pūrvāṣāḍhāniviṣṭaṃ tu puraṃ syād dhana^dhānya^bhāk/
body.translated_text: A city established under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> would possess wealth and grain,

body.text: p.65.3cd/.lubdhāḥ krūrāś ca mūrkhāś ca nivasanti narādhamāḥ//
body.translated_text: but the greedy, cruel, and foolish — the basest of men — dwell there.

body.text: p.65.4ab/.niviṣṭe tūttarāyāṃ ca dhana^dhānya^samuccayaḥ/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, there is an accumulation of wealth and grain,

body.text: p.65.4cd/.vidyāprakṛtisampanno janaś ca kalaha^priyaḥ//
body.translated_text: and people endowed with learning and good nature, but fond of quarrels.

body.text: p.65.5ab/.abhijiti niviṣṭe tu nagare tatra moditāḥ/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Abhijit</s>, the people there are happy;

body.text: p.65.5cd/.narāḥ sarve sadā hṛṣṭāḥ parasparānurāgiṇaḥ//
body.translated_text: all men are always joyful and affectionate toward one another.

body.text: p.65.6ab/.śravaṇāyāṃ niviṣṭaṃ tu puraṃ dhānya^dhanānvitaṃ/
body.translated_text: A city founded under <s>Śravaṇā</s>, endowed with grain and wealth,

body.text: p.65.6cd/.arogijana^bhūyiṣṭhasahitaṃ tad vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: should be described as having an abundance of healthy people.

body.text: p.65.7ab/.dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ niviṣṭaṃ tu strī^jitaṃ puram ādiśet/
body.translated_text: A city founded under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> should be declared as dominated by women,

body.text: p.65.7cd/.prabhūta^vastramālyaṃ ca kāma^bhoga^vivirjitam//
body.translated_text: abundant in garments and garlands, but devoid of the pleasures of love.

body.text: p.65.8ab/.pure śatabhiṣā^yukta mūrkhaśāṭhya^priyā jahāḥ/
body.translated_text: In a city [founded] under <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, foolish people fond of deceit are found;

body.text: p.65.8cd/.strīṣu pāneṣu saṃsaktāḥ salilena vinaśyati//
body.translated_text: attached to women and drink, it perishes by water.

body.text: p.66.1ab/.pure proṣṭhapadādhyakṣe narās tatra sukha^priyāḥ/
body.translated_text: In a city presided over by <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s> (Pūrvabhādrapadā), the men there are fond of pleasure,

body.text: p.66.1cd/.paropatāpino mūrkhā mānakāmavivarjitāḥ//
body.translated_text: afflicting others, foolish, devoid of honor and desire.

body.text: p.66.2ab/.uttarāyāṃ niviṣṭe tu śaśvadvṛddhir anuttarā/
body.translated_text: When founded under <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, there is perpetual unsurpassed growth;

body.text: p.66.2cd/.pūrṇaṃ ca dhana^dhānyābhyāṃ ratnāḍhyaṃ ca vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: full of wealth and grain, and rich in jewels, one should declare it.

body.text: p.66.3ab/.pure niviṣṭe raivatyāṃ sundarī janatā bhavet/
body.translated_text: In a city founded under <s>Revatī</s>, the people would be beautiful;

body.text: p.66.3cd/.kharoṣṭraṃ ca^eva gāvaś ca prabhūta^dhana^dhānyatā//
body.translated_text: there would be donkeys, camels, and cows, and abundance of wealth and grain.

body.text: p.66.4ab/.aśvinyāṃ viniviṣṭaṃ tu nagaraṃ śivam ādiśet/
body.translated_text: A city founded under <s>Aśvinī</s> should be declared auspicious;

body.text: p.66.4cd/.arogijana^sampūrṇaṃ darśanīyajanākulam//
body.translated_text: filled with healthy people, and bustling with handsome folk.

body.text: p.66.5ab/.bharaṇyāṃ sanniviṣṭe tu durbhagāḥ kalaha^priyāḥ/
body.translated_text: When established under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, the people are unfortunate and quarrelsome,

body.text: p.66.5cd/.duḥśīlā duḥkhabhājaś ca vasanti puruṣādhamāḥ//
body.translated_text: of bad character and prone to suffering — the basest of men dwell there.

body.text: p.66.6ab/.purāṇi rāṣṭraṇi tathā gṛhāṇi nakṣatra^yogaṃ prasamīkṣya vidvān/
body.translated_text: Cities, kingdoms, and homes — having examined the conjunction of <s>nakṣatras</s>, the wise one

body.text: p.66.6cd/.iṣṭe praśaste ca niveśayet tu pūrve ca janme +adhigataṃ mayedaṃ//
body.translated_text: should establish them under a desired and auspicious [asterism]; this I have learned from a previous birth.

body.text: p.67.1/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatra^nirdeśo nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called the Determination of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>.

body.text: %nakṣatrāṇāṃ sthāna^nirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: Section: Designation of the Places of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>

body.text: p.67.2/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭāviṃśatīnāṃ(28Åh) nakṣatrāṇāṃ sthāna^nirdeśaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi/ etac chrūyatāṃ/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall teach the chapter called the Designation of Places of the twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>. Listen to this.

body.text: p.67.3/.kathayatu bhagavān/
body.translated_text: Let the venerable one speak.

body.text:
p.67.4/.kṛttikā bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatraṃ kaliṅga^magadhānāṃ / rohiṇī sarva^prajāyāḥ/ mṛgaśirā videhānāṃ rājopasevakānāṃ ca/ evam ārdrā kṣatriyāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ ca/ punarvasuḥ sauparṇānāṃ/ puṣya^nakṣatraṃ sarveṣām avadāta^vadāta^vasanānāṃ/ rāja^padasevakānāṃ ca/ aśleṣā nāgānāṃ haimavatānāṃ ca/ maghā^nakṣatraṃ gauḍikānāṃ/ pūrvaphalgunī caurāṇāṃ/ uttaraphalgunī
avantīnāṃ/ hastā saurāṣṭrikāṇāṃ/ citrā pakṣiṇāṃ dvipadānāṃ/ svātī sarveṣāṃ pravrajyāsamāpannānāṃ/ viśākhā audakānāṃ/ anurādhā vāṇijakānāṃ śākaṭikānāṃ ca/ jyeṣṭhā dauvālikānāṃ/ (68) mūlā pathikānāṃ/ pūrvāṣāḍhā vāhlīkānāṃ ca/ uttarāṣāḍhā kāmbojānāṃ/ abhijit sarveṣāṃ dakṣiṇāpathikānāṃ tāmraparṇikānāṃ ca/ śravaṇā ghādakānāṃ caurāṇāṃ ca/ dhaniṣṭhā kuru^pāñcālānāṃ/
śatabhiṣā maulikānām ārthavaṇikānāṃ ca/ pūrvabhādrapadā gandhikānāṃ yavana^kāmbojānāṃ ca/ uttarabhādrapadā gandharvāṇāṃ/ revatī nāvikānāṃ ca/ aśvinī aśvavāṇijānāṃ ca/ bharaṇī bhadrapadakarmaṇāṃ bhadrakāyākānāṃ ca/
body.translated_text: O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, the <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Kṛttikā</s> belongs to the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> and <s>Magadhans</s>. <s>Rohiṇī</s> to all peoples. <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> to the <s>Videhas</s> and attendants of kings. Likewise <s>Ārdrā</s> to the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. <s>Punarvasu</s> to the <s>Suparṇas</s> (Garuḍa-folk). The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Puṣya</s> to all who wear white and pure garments, and to attendants of royal courts. <s>Aśleṣā</s> to the <s>Nāgas</s> and the Himalayan peoples. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Maghā</s> to the <s>Gauḍikas</s>. <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> to thieves. <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s> to the people of <s>Avanti</s>. <s>Hasta</s> to the <s>Saurāṣṭrians</s>. <s>Citrā</s> to birds and bipeds. <s>Svātī</s> to all those who have entered the wandering life. <s>Viśākhā</s> to the aquatic people. <s>Anurādhā</s> to merchants and cart-drivers. <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> to gatekeepers. <s>Mūla</s> to travelers. <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> to the <s>Bāhlīkas</s>. <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> to the <s>Kāmbojas</s>. <s>Abhijit</s> to all the peoples of the southern region and the <s>Tāmraparṇīs</s>. <s>Śravaṇā</s> to assassins and thieves. <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> to the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāñcālas</s>. <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> to herbalists and physicians. <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> to perfumers, and to the <s>Yavanas</s> and <s>Kāmbojas</s>. <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> to the <s>Gandharvas</s>. <s>Revatī</s> to boatmen. <s>Aśvinī</s> to horse-dealers. <s>Bharaṇī</s> to those who perform funeral rites and to the noble-bodied.

body.text: p.68.1/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatrāṇāṃ sthāna^nirdeśa^vyākaraṇo nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called the Designation of Places of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>.

body.text: %ṛtuvarṣaḥ
body.translated_text: Section: Seasonal Rainfall

body.text: p.68.2/.paṭha bhos triśaṅko ṛtuvarṣaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ/ tad ahaṃ vakṣye śrūyatāṃ/ kathayatu bhagavān/
body.translated_text: Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the chapter called Seasonal Rainfall. I shall now speak it; listen. Let the venerable one speak.

body.text: p.68.3/.kṛttikāsu grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati catuḥṣaṣṭy^āḍhakāni pravarṣati/ varṣo daśa^rātrikaḥ/ śravaṇāyuktaproṣṭhapadāyām agnodako varṣārātro bhavati/ paścād varṣaṃ saṃjanayati/ hemante grīṣme grīṇi ca^atra (69) bhaya^pragrahāṇi bhavanti/ agni^bhayaṃ śastra^bhayaṃ ca^udaka^bhayaṃ ca bhavati/ uktaṃ kṛttikāsu/
body.translated_text: O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, if during the last month of summer, when <s>Kṛttikā</s> [is predominant], the god rains here, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s> (measures). The rainfall lasts ten nights. On the night when <s>Śravaṇā</s> conjoins <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>, the rain-night is mixed with fire and water. Afterwards it produces rain. In winter and summer, three dangers arise here: danger from fire, danger from weapons, and danger from water. Thus is stated for <s>Kṛttikā</s>.

body.text: p.69.1/.rohiṇyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati eka^viṃśatyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ tatra nimnāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/ eṣa ca varṣārātraḥ sāroparodhaḥ sasyaṃ ca saṃpādayati/ dvau ca^atra rogau prabalau bhavataḥ/ kukṣirogaś cakṣūrogaś ca/ caura^bahulāś ca^atra diśo bhavanti/ uktaṃ ca rohiṇyāṃ/
body.translated_text: If during the last month of summer, when <s>Rohiṇī</s> [is predominant], the god rains here, he rains twenty-one <s>āḍhakas</s>. There, farming should be done in lowlands; uplands should be avoided. This rainy season, with intermittent showers, brings the crops to fruition. Two diseases become prevalent there: stomach disease and eye disease. And the directions become full of thieves. Thus is stated for <s>Rohiṇī</s>.

body.text: p.69.2/.mṛgaśirasi grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati catuḥṣaṣṭy^āḍhakāni pravarṣati/ sāroparodho varṣārātraḥ/ paścād varṣaṃ saṃjanayati/ nikṣiptaśastrāś ca^atra (70) rājāno bhavanti/ kṣemiṇaḥ sunītikāś ca diśo bhavanti/ muditāś ca^atra janapadā bhavanti/ uktaṃ mṛgaśirasi/
body.translated_text: If during the last month of summer, when <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> [is predominant], the god rains here, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s>. The rainy season has intermittent showers. Afterwards it produces rain. Kings there lay down their weapons; the directions are peaceful and well-governed; and the people of the countryside are happy. Thus is stated for <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>.

body.text:
p.70.1/.ārdrāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati aṣṭādaśāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ tatra nimnāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/ nidhayaś ca rakṣayitavyāḥ/ caura^bahulāś ca^atra diśo bhavanti/ nikṣiptaśastrāś ca rājāno bhavanti/ trayaś ca^atra rogāḥ prabalā bhavanti/ jvaraḥ śvāso galagrahaś ca/ bālānāṃ dārakadārikāṇāṃ ca maraṇaṃ
bhavati/ ity uktam ārdrāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: If during the last month of summer, when <s>Ārdrā</s> [is predominant], the god rains here, he rains eighteen <s>āḍhakas</s>. There, farming should be done in lowlands; uplands should be avoided; and stores should be protected. The directions become full of thieves. Kings lay down their weapons. Three diseases become prevalent there: fever, asthma, and throat-constriction. There is death among children — boys and girls. Thus is stated for <s>Ārdrā</s>.

body.text: p.70.2/.punarvasau grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati/ navatyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ mahā^meghān utpādayati/ āṣāḍhāyāṃ praviṣṭāyāṃ mṛdūni pravarṣati/ anantaraṃ ca nirantareṇa pravarṣati/ nikṣiptaśastrāś ca rājāno bhavanti/ uktaṃ punarvasau/
body.translated_text: If during the last month of summer, when <s>Punarvasu</s> [is predominant], the god rains here, he rains ninety <s>āḍhakas</s>. He produces great clouds. When <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> has set in, he rains gently. Then he rains continuously without interruption. Kings lay down their weapons. Thus is stated for <s>Punarvasu</s>.

body.text:
p.71.1/.puṣye grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati dvātriṃśadāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ atra nimnāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/ vyaktaṃ pradhāna^varṣāṇi bhavanti/ sasyaṃ ca niṣpādayati/ brāhmaṇa^kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca virodho bhavati/ daṃṣṭriṇaś ca^atra prabalā bhavanti/ tatra trayo rogāś ca bhavanti/ gaṇḍāḥ piṭakāḥ pāmāni ca / ity uktaṃ
puṣye/
body.translated_text: [Page 71.1] If, in the <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) <s>Puṣya</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains thirty-two <s>āḍhakas</s> (measures of rainfall). In this case, lowlands should be cultivated; highlands should be avoided. The rains will clearly be abundant. And it brings the crops to fruition. There will be conflict between <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. And fanged animals become powerful here. Three diseases arise there: boils, abscesses, and skin eruptions. Thus it is spoken for <s>Puṣya</s>.

body.text: p.71.2/.aśleṣāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati eka^viṃśatyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ tatra nimnāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/ viṣamāś ca vāyavo vānti/ saṃvignāś ca^atra jñānino rājānaś ca bhavanti/ eṣo varṣaḥ sarva^sasyāni sampādayati/ jāyāpatikānāṃ rājāmātyānāṃ ca virodho bhavati/ uktam aśleṣāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 71.2] If, in <s>Aśleṣā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains twenty-one <s>āḍhakas</s>. In this case, lowlands should be cultivated; highlands should be avoided. Irregular winds blow. The wise and the kings become anxious here. This rainfall brings all crops to fruition. There will be conflict between husbands and wives, and between kings and ministers. Thus it is spoken for <s>Aśleṣā</s>.

body.text: p.71.3/.maghāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati catuḥṣaṣṭy^āḍhakāni (72) pravarṣati/ eṣo varṣaḥ sarva^sasyāni sampādayati/ mṛgapakṣipaśumanuṣyāṇāṃ ca^atra garbhā vinaśyanti/ jana^maraṇaṃ ca^atra bhaviṣyati^iti/ uktaṃ maghāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 71.3] If, in <s>Maghā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s>. [Page 72] This rainfall brings all crops to fruition. But the embryos of wild animals, birds, livestock, and humans perish here. And there will be mass death of people. Thus it is spoken for <s>Maghā</s>.

body.text: p.72.1/.pūrvaphalgunyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati catuḥṣaṣṭy^āḍhakāni pravarṣati/ eṣo varṣaḥ sarva^sasyāni sampādayati/ tac ca sasyaṃ janayitvā para^cakra^pīḍitā manuṣyā na sukhenopabhuñjate/ paśūnāṃ maṇuṣyāṇāṃ ca^atra garbhāḥ sukhino bhavanti/ uktaṃ pūrvaphalgunyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 72.1] If, in <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s>. This rainfall brings all crops to fruition. But having produced those crops, people afflicted by enemy armies do not enjoy them in comfort. The embryos of livestock and humans thrive here. Thus it is spoken for <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>.

body.text: p.72.2/.uttaraphalgunyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati aśītyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ eṣo varṣaḥ sarva^sasyāni ca sampādayati/ nikṣiptaśastrāś ca^atra rājāno bhavanti/ brahma^kṣatriyayoś ca virodho bhavati/ kṣipraṃ ca anītikāḥ prajā vinaśyanti/ ca^uktam uttaraphalgunyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 72.2] If, in <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains eighty <s>āḍhakas</s>. This rainfall brings all crops to fruition. And kings here lay down their weapons. But there will be conflict between <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. And the people, though free from calamity, quickly perish. Thus it is spoken for <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>.

body.text: p.72.3/.haste grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati ekonapañcāśadāḍhakāni (73) pravarṣati/ devaś ca tad yathā parikṣipati/ patitāni ca sasyāni janasyārasāgrāṇi anudagrāṇi alpa^sārāṇy alpodakāni/ durbhikṣaś ca^atra bhaviṣyati/ uktaṃ haste/
body.translated_text: [Page 72.3] If, in <s>Hasta</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains forty-nine <s>āḍhakas</s>. [Page 73] And the sky-god scatters it about. The crops that grow are tasteless at the tips, stunted, of little substance, and lacking moisture. And there will be famine here. Thus it is spoken for <s>Hasta</s>.

body.text: p.73.1/.citrāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati catuḥṣaṣṭy^āḍhakāni pravarṣati/ sāroparodhas tataḥ paścād varṣaṃ saṃjanayati/ nikṣiptaśastrāś ca rājāno bhavanti/ muditāś ca^atra janapadā bhavanti/ uktaṃ citrāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 73.1] If, in <s>Citrā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s>. After an obstruction of the essential rains, it subsequently produces rainfall. Kings lay down their weapons. And the people of the countryside are joyful here. Thus it is spoken for <s>Citrā</s>.

body.text: p.73.2/.svātyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati eka^viṃśatyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ nikṣiptaśastrāś ca rājāno bhavanti/ caurāś ca^atra balavattarā bhavanti/ uktaṃ svātyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 73.2] If, in <s>Svātī</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains twenty-one <s>āḍhakas</s>. Kings lay down their weapons. But thieves become very powerful here. Thus it is spoken for <s>Svātī</s>.

body.text: p.73.3/.viśākhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati aśītyāḍhakāni (74) pravarṣati/ eṣā varṣaḥ sarva^sasyāni sampādayati/ rājānaś ca^atra chidra^yuktā bhavanti/ agnidāhāś ca^atra prabalā bhavanti/ daṃṣṭriṇaś ca^atra balavanto +api kṣayaṃ gacchanti/ uktaṃ viśākhāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 73.3] If, in <s>Viśākhā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains eighty <s>āḍhakas</s>. [Page 74] This rainfall brings all crops to fruition. But kings here become vulnerable to attack. And conflagrations become fierce here. And even powerful fanged animals here meet destruction. Thus it is spoken for <s>Viśākhā</s>.

body.text: p.74.1/.anurādhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati ṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ eṣo varṣaḥ sasyaṃ sampādayati/ mitrāṇi ca^atra dṛḍhāni bhavanti/ uktam anurādhāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 74.1] If, in <s>Anurādhā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty <s>āḍhakas</s>. This rainfall brings the crops to fruition. And friendships become firm here. Thus it is spoken for <s>Anurādhā</s>.

body.text: p.74.2/.jyeṣṭhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati ṣoḍaśāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ tatra kṛṣi^karmān tāni pratisaṃhartavyāni/ yugavaratrāṇi varjayitavyāni/ svadhānyāni upasaṃhartavyāni/ agnayaḥ pratisaṃhartavyāḥ/ lāṅgalāni pratisaṃhartavyāni/ avaśyam anena janapadena vinaṣṭavyaṃ bhavati/ para^cakra^pīḍito bhavati/ uktaṃ jyeṣṭhāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 74.2] If, in <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixteen <s>āḍhakas</s>. In that case, agricultural implements should be put away. Yoke-straps should be set aside. One's own grain stores should be gathered up. Fires should be secured. Ploughs should be put away. This country will inevitably face ruin. It will be afflicted by enemy armies. Thus it is spoken for <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>.

body.text: p.74.3/.mūle grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati catuṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni (75) pravarṣati/ eṣo varṣaḥ sasyaṃ sampādayati/ caura^bahulāś ca^atra diśo bhavanti/ trayaś ca^atra vyādhayo balavanto bhavanti/ vāta^gaṇḍaḥ pārśvaśūlam akṣirogaś ca/ puṣpa^phalāni ca^atra samṛddhāni bhavanti/ nikṣiptaśastrāś ca^atra rājāno bhavanti/ uktaṃ mūle/
body.translated_text: [Page 74.3] If, in <s>Mūla</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s>. [Page 75] This rainfall brings the crops to fruition. But the regions become overrun with thieves here. And three diseases become powerful here: flatulence with swelling, pain in the sides, and eye disease. But flowers and fruits flourish here. And kings lay down their weapons here. Thus it is spoken for <s>Mūla</s>.

body.text: p.75.1/.pūrvasyām āṣāḍhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati ṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ dvau ca^atra grāhau bhavataḥ / proṣṭhapade vā +aśvayujau vā pakṣe/ eṣo varṣaḥ sarva^sasyāni sampādayati/ dvau ca^atra rogau prabalau bhavataḥ/ kukṣirogo +akṣirogaś ca / uktaṃ pūrvāṣāḍhāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 75.1] If, in <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty <s>āḍhakas</s>. And two eclipses occur here, in the fortnight of either <s>Proṣṭhapada</s> or <s>Aśvayuj</s>. This rainfall brings all crops to fruition. And two diseases become powerful here: abdominal disease and eye disease. Thus it is spoken for <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>.

body.text: p.75.2/.uttarasyām āṣāḍhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati pūrṇam āḍhakaśataṃ pravarṣati/ tatra sthalāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ nimnāni parivarjayitavyāni/ mahā^srotāṃsi ca^atra pravahanti/ agrodakā ca^atra varṣā bhavati/ sarva^sasyāni niṣpādayati/ trayaś ca^atra rogāḥ prabalā bhavanti/ gaṇḍaḥ kacchaḥ kaṇṭha^roga iti/ uktam uttarāṣāḍhāyām//
body.translated_text: [Page 75.2] If, in <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains a full one hundred <s>āḍhakas</s>. In that case, highlands should be cultivated; lowlands should be avoided. Great torrents flow here. And the rainfall here comes with water at its front. It brings all crops to fruition. And three diseases become powerful here: swelling, skin disease, and throat disease. Thus it is spoken for <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>.

body.text: p.75.3/.abhijiti grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra pravarṣati catuḥṣaṣṭy^āḍhākāni (76) pravarṣati/ maṇḍalavarṣaṃ ca devaḥ pravarṣati/ paścād varṣaḥ sasyaṃ janayati/ audakānāṃ bhūtānām utsargo bhavati/ uktam abhijiti/
body.translated_text: [Page 75.3] If, in <s>Abhijit</s>, in the last month of summer, it rains, it rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s>. [Page 76] And the sky-god rains in circular patterns. Afterwards, the rainfall produces crops. There is an abundance of aquatic creatures. Thus it is spoken for <s>Abhijit</s>.

body.text:
p.76.1/.śravaṇe tu grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati catuṣṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ maṇḍalavarṣaṃ ca devo varṣati/ paścād varṣā sasyaṃ sampādayati/ audakānāṃ bhūtānām utsargo bhavati/ vyādhi^bahulāś ca narā bhavanti/ rājānaś ca tīvra^daṇḍā bhavanti/ uktaṃ śravaṇe/
p.76.2/.dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati eka^pañcāśadāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ vibhaktāś ca^atra varṣā bhavanti/ tatra nimnāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/ durmukho rātrau varṣo bhavati/ sasyāni sampādayati/ ekaś ca^atra rogo bhavati/ gaṇḍa^vikāraḥ/ śastra^samādānāś ca rājāno bhavanti/ uktaṃ dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 76.1] If, in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s>. And the sky-god rains in circular patterns. Afterwards, the rain brings the crops to fruition. There is an abundance of aquatic creatures. And people become afflicted with many diseases. And kings impose severe punishments. Thus it is spoken for <s>Śravaṇa</s>. [Page 76.2] If, in <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains fifty-one <s>āḍhakas</s>. And the rains are distributed unevenly here. In this case, lowlands should be cultivated; highlands should be avoided. The ill-faced rain falls at night. It brings the crops to fruition. And one disease arises here: swelling disorder. And kings take up weapons. Thus it is spoken for <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>.

body.text: p.76.3/.śatabhiṣāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati ṣoḍaśāḍhakāni (77) pravarṣati/ tatra nimnāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/ eṣo varṣaḥ sarva^sasyāni sampādayati/ cakra^samārūḍhā janapadā bhavanti/ manuṣyā dārakadārikāś ca skandhe kṛtvā deśa^antaraṃ gacchanti/ uktaṃ śatabhiṣāyaṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 76.3] If, in <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixteen <s>āḍhakas</s>. [Page 77] In this case, lowlands should be cultivated; highlands should be avoided. This rainfall brings all crops to fruition. But the people of the countryside come under the power of invading armies. People, carrying their sons and daughters on their shoulders, flee to other lands. Thus it is spoken for <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>.

body.text:
p.77.1/.pūrvasyāṃ bhādrapadāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati catuḥṣaṣṭy^āḍhakāni pravarṣati/ varṣāmukhe ca^atra ekonaviṃśati rātriko +avagraho bhavati/ puṣpa^sasyaṃ ca nāśayati/ etāś ca varṣā bahu^caurā bhavanti/ dvau ca^atra mahā^vyādhī bhavataḥ/ prathamaṃ pittatāpajvaro bhavati/ paścād balavān mahā^graho bhavati/ martyānāṃ nārīṇāṃ
ca maraṇaṃ bhavati/ uktaṃ pūrvabhādrapadāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 77.1] If, in <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty-four <s>āḍhakas</s>. And at the onset of the rainy season, there is a drought lasting nineteen nights here. It destroys the flowering crops. And these rains bring many thieves. Two great diseases arise here: first there is a bilious burning fever, and afterwards a powerful great seizure afflicts. There is death of men and women. Thus it is spoken for <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>.

body.text:
p.77.2/.uttarasyāṃ bhādrapadāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati pūrṇam āḍhakaśataṃ pravarṣati/ mahā^srotāṃsi pravahanti/ grāma^nagara^nigamāḥ srotasā uhyante/ catvāraś ca^atra vyādhayaḥ prabalā bhavanti/ tad yathā kukṣirogo +akṣirogaḥ (78) kāśo jvaraś ceti/ bālānāṃ dārakadārikāṇāṃ maraṇāṃ bhavati/ atra sthalāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ nimnāni
parivarjayitavyāni/ etāś ca varṣāḥ puṣpāṇi phalāni ca sampādayanti/ uktam uttarabhādrapadāyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 77.2] If, in <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains a full one hundred <s>āḍhakas</s>. Great torrents flow. Villages, cities, and market towns are swept away by the floods. And four diseases become powerful here, namely: abdominal disease, eye disease, [Page 78] cough, and fever. There is death of infants, young boys, and young girls. Here, highlands should be cultivated; lowlands should be avoided. And these rains bring flowers and fruits to fruition. Thus it is spoken for <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>.

body.text:
p.78.1/.revatyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati eka^ṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ tatra nimnāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/ eṣā paribhuñjate/ nikṣiptaśastra^daṇḍāś ca rājāno bhavanti/ anudvignāś ca janapadā bhavanti/ udvignāś ca dānapatayo bhavanti/ deva^nakṣatra^samāyuktāś ca janapadā bhavanti/ mitrāṇi samāyuktāni bhavanti/
uktaṃ revatyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 78.1] If, in <s>Revatī</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains sixty-one <s>āḍhakas</s>. In this case, lowlands should be cultivated; highlands should be avoided. This rainfall is enjoyed. And kings lay down their weapons and punishments. And the people of the countryside are free from anxiety. But the donors become anxious. The people of the countryside are favored by the <s>devas</s> (gods) and the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions). And friendships are harmonious. Thus it is spoken for <s>Revatī</s>.

body.text: p.78.2/.aśvinyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati aṣṭacatvāriṃśadāḍhakāni pravarṣati/ yac ca madhye varṣā bhavati/ tatra nimnāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/ eṣā varṣā sarva^sasyāni sampādayati/ (79) bhaya^samāyuktāś ca^atra janapadā bhavanti/ caurāś ca prabalā bhavanti/ uktam aśvinyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 78.2] If, in <s>Aśvinī</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains forty-eight <s>āḍhakas</s>. And whatever rain falls in between — in this case, lowlands should be cultivated; highlands should be avoided. This rainfall brings all crops to fruition. [Page 79] But the people of the countryside become gripped by fear here. And thieves become powerful. Thus it is spoken for <s>Aśvinī</s>.

body.text: p.79.1/.bharaṇyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yady atra devaḥ pravarṣati pūrṇam āḍhakaśataṃ pravarṣati/ tatra sthalāni kṛṣi^kartavyāni/ nimnāni parivarjayitavyāni/ durbhikṣas ca^atra bhavati/ jarāmaraṇaṃ janānāṃ bhavati/ rājānaś ca^atra anyonyaghātakā bhavanti/ putrapautrāṇāṃ ca kalaho bhavati/ uktaṃ bharaṇyāṃ/
body.translated_text: [Page 79.1] If, in <s>Bharaṇī</s>, in the last month of summer, the sky-god rains, it rains a full one hundred <s>āḍhakas</s>. In that case, highlands should be cultivated; lowlands should be avoided. And there will be famine here. There will be death from old age among the people. And kings here become mutual slayers. And there will be quarrel among sons and grandsons. Thus it is spoken for <s>Bharaṇī</s>.

body.text: p.79.2/.ayaṃ ghoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatra^rtuvarṣādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: [Page 79.2] This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter on <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), seasons, and rainfall.

body.text: % rāhugrahe phalavipākaḥ
body.translated_text: Results and consequences at the time of an eclipse by <s>Rāhu</s>

body.text: p.79.3/.amīṣāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aśṭāviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ rāhugrahe phalavipākaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
body.translated_text: [Page 79.3] For these twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the results and consequences at the time of an eclipse by <s>Rāhu</s>.

body.text:
p.79.4./kṛttikāsu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin yadi candra^graho bhavati kaliṅgamagadhānām upapīḍā bhavati/ yadi rohiṇyāṃ candra^graho bhavati prajānām upapīḍā bhavati/ yadi mṛgaśirasi candra^graho bhavati videhānāṃ janapadānām upapīḍā bhavati/ rājopasevakanāṃ ca/ evam ārdrāyāṃ punarvasau puṣye ca vaktavyaṃ/ aśleṣāyāṃ yadi candra^graho bhavati nāgānāṃ haimavatānāṃ
ca pīḍā bhavati/ yadi maghāsu candra^graho bhavati gauḍikānām upapīḍā bhavati/ yadi pūrvaphalgunyāṃ somo gṛhyate caurāṇām upapīḍā (80) bhavati/ yady uttaraphalgunyāṃ somo gṛhyate +avantīnām upapīḍā bhavati/ yadi hasteṣu somo gṛhyate saurāṣṭrikāṇām upapīḍā bhavati/ yadi citrāyāṃ somo gṛhyate pakṣiṇāṃ dvipadānāṃ ca pīḍā bhavati/ yadi svātyāṃ somo gṛhyate
sarveṣāṃ pravrajyāsamāpannānām upapīḍā bhavati/ yady anurādhāsu somo gṛhyate vaṇijānām upapīḍā bhavati śākaṭikānāṃ ca/ yadi jyeṣṭhāyāṃ somo gṛhyate dauvālikānāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ yadi mūle somo gṛhyate +adhvagānāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ yadi pūrvāṣāḍhāyāṃ somo gṛhyate +avantīnāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ yady uttarāṣāḍhāyāṃ somo gṛhyate kāmbojakānāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ bāhlīkānāṃ ca/
yady abhijiti somo gṛhyate dakṣiṇāpathikānāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ tāmraparṇikānāṃ ca/ yadi śravaṇeṣu somo gṛhyate caurāṇāṃ ghātakānāṃ ca^upapīḍā bhavati/ yadi dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ somo gṛhyate kurupāñcālanāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ yadi śatabhiṣāyāṃ somo gṛhyate maulikānām ātharvaṇikānāṃ ca pīḍā bhavati/ yadi pūrvabhādrapadāyāṃ somo gṛhyate gāndhikānāṃ yavana^kāmbojakānāṃ ca pīḍā
bhavati/ yady uttarabhādrapadāyāṃ somo gṛhyate (81) gandharvāṇāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ yadi revatyāṃ somo gṛhyate nāvikānāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ yady aścviṇijānāṃ pīḍā bhavati/ yadi bharaṇyāṃ somo gṛhyate bharukacchānāṃ pīḍā bhavati/
body.translated_text: O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, if a lunar eclipse occurs in <s>Kṛttikā</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> and <s>Magadhas</s>. If a lunar eclipse occurs in <s>Rohiṇī</s>, there is affliction for the people. If a lunar eclipse occurs in <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Videha</s> countries and for those in royal service. The same should be stated for <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, and <s>Puṣya</s>. If a lunar eclipse occurs in <s>Āśleṣā</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Nāgas</s> and the <s>Haimavatans</s>. If a lunar eclipse occurs in <s>Maghā</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Gauḍikas</s>. If the Moon is seized in <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s>, there is affliction for thieves. If the Moon is seized in <s>Uttaraphālgunī</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Avantīs</s>. If the Moon is seized in <s>Hasta</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Saurāṣṭrikas</s>. If the Moon is seized in <s>Citrā</s>, there is affliction for birds and bipeds. If the Moon is seized in <s>Svātī</s>, there is affliction for all those who have undertaken the renunciant life. If the Moon is seized in <s>Anurādhā</s>, there is affliction for merchants and cart-drivers. If the Moon is seized in <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, there is affliction for gatekeepers. If the Moon is seized in <s>Mūla</s>, there is affliction for travelers. If the Moon is seized in <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Avantīs</s>. If the Moon is seized in <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Kāmbojas</s> and the <s>Bāhlīkas</s>. If the Moon is seized in <s>Abhijit</s>, there is affliction for the people of the southern region and the <s>Tāmraparṇikas</s>. If the Moon is seized in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, there is affliction for thieves and assassins. If the Moon is seized in <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, there is affliction for the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāñcālas</s>. If the Moon is seized in <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, there is affliction for herbalists and <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s> (practitioners of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>). If the Moon is seized in <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, there is affliction for perfumers, <s>Yavanas</s> (Greeks), and <s>Kāmbojas</s>. If the Moon is seized in <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, there is affliction for <s>Gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians). If the Moon is seized in <s>Revatī</s>, there is affliction for sailors. If [the Moon is seized] in <s>Aśvinī</s>, there is affliction [for them]. If the Moon is seized in <s>Bharaṇī</s>, there is affliction for the people of <s>Bharukaccha</s> (Broach).

body.text: p.81.1/.evaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatre candra^graho bhavati tasya tasya deśasya pīḍā bhavati/ ity ukto rāhugrahaphalavipākādhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, when a lunar eclipse occurs in a <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), there is affliction for the corresponding region. This concludes the chapter on the ripening of the effects of eclipses by <s>Rāhu</s>.

body.text: % nakṣatrakarma^nirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: Instruction on Activities According to the <s>Nakṣatras</s>

body.text: p.81.2/.prati^nakṣatra^vaṃśaśāstre yathoktaṃ karma tac chṛṇu/
body.translated_text: Listen to what is prescribed as activity in the treatise on lineages according to each <s>nakṣatra</s>.

body.text: p.81.3ab/.ucyamānam idaṃ vipra;ṛṣīṇāṃ vacanaṃ yathā/
body.translated_text: This is spoken, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, in accordance with the sayings of the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages).

body.text: p.81.3cd/.ṣaṭtārāṃ kṛttikāṃ vidyād āśrayaṃ tāsu kārayet/
body.translated_text: One should know <s>Kṛttikā</s> as having six stars; one should undertake the following under them:

body.text: p.81.3ef/.agnyādhānaṃ pākayajñaḥ samṛddhiprasavaś ca yaḥ//
body.translated_text: The establishment of the sacred fire, sacrificial cooking, and rites that promote prosperity.

body.text: p.81.4ab/.sarpirviloḍayet tatra gavāṃ veśma ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: One should churn ghee there and build a cow-shed.

body.text: p.81.4cd/.ajaiḍakāś ca kretavyā gavāṃ ca vṛṣam utsṛjet//
body.translated_text: Goats and sheep should be purchased, and one should release a bull among the cows.

body.text: p.81.5ab/.aśmasāramayaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ sarvam atra tu kārayet/
body.translated_text: Vessels made of iron should all be fashioned under this [<s>nakṣatra</s>].

body.text: p.81.5cd/.hiraṇyakārakarma^antamiṣv astraṃ ca^upakārayet//
body.translated_text: And among goldsmith's work and the like, one should prepare weapons.

body.text: p.81.6ab/.metṛko māpayed atra kuṭikāgniniveśanaṃ/
body.translated_text: A surveyor should measure here the cottage and the fire-house.

body.text: p.81.6cd/.pītalohita^puṣpāṇāṃ bījāny atra tu ghāpayet//
body.translated_text: Seeds of yellow and red flowers should be planted here.

body.text: p.82.1ab/.gṛhaṃ ca māpayet atra tathā +avāsaṃ prakalpayet/
body.translated_text: One should have a house measured here, and likewise arrange a dwelling.

body.text: p.82.1cd/.navaṃ ca chādayed vastraṃ krayaṇaṃ na^atra kārayet//
body.translated_text: One should cover oneself with new cloth; buying and selling should not be done here.

body.text: p.82.2ab/.krūrakarmāṇi sidhyanti yuddhasaṃrodhabandhanam/
body.translated_text: Cruel deeds succeed — war, siege, and imprisonment;

body.text: p.82.2cd/.parapīḍām athātraiva vidvān naiva prayojayet//
body.translated_text: but the wise should never employ the affliction of others here.

body.text: p.82.3ab/.śastrāṇi kṣurakarmāṇi sarvāṇy atra tu kārayet/
body.translated_text: Deeds involving weapons and razor-work should all be done here.

body.text: p.82.3cd/.tejasāni ca bhāṇḍāni kārayec ca krīṇīta ca//
body.translated_text: Sharp vessels should be made and also purchased.

body.text: p.82.4ab/.āyuṣyaṃ ca śiraḥ^snānāṃ strīṇāṃ viṣkambhaṇāni ca/
body.translated_text: A life-promoting head-bath, and restraining rites for women,

body.text: p.82.4cd/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ced devasya na^atra vairaṃ praśāmyati//
body.translated_text: and if the god rains [under this <s>nakṣatra</s>], enmity is not pacified here.

body.text: p.82.5ab/.krodhano harṣaṇaḥ śūras tejasvī sāhasa^priyaḥ/
body.translated_text: One born here is wrathful, joyful, heroic, radiant, fond of daring,

body.text: p.82.5cd/.āyuṣmāṃś ca yaśasvī ca yajña^śīlo +atra jāyate//kṛttikāsu
body.translated_text: long-lived, famous, and devoted to sacrifice. [Under <s>Kṛttikā</s>.]

body.text: p.82.6ab/.sarvaṃ kṛṣi^padaṃ karma rohiṇyāṃ saṃprayojayet/
body.translated_text: All agricultural work should be undertaken under <s>Rohiṇī</s>;

body.text: p.82.6cd/.kṣetravastuvihārāṃś ca navaṃ veśma ca kārayet//
body.translated_text: fields, estates, pleasure-gardens, and a new house should be built.

body.text: p.82.7ab/.prayojayec cakrān vārān dāsāṃś ca^eva gṛhe paśūn/
body.translated_text: One should set to work wheels, barriers, servants, household animals;

body.text: p.82.7cd/.vāpayet sarvabījāni dhruvaṃ vāsāṃsi kārayet//
body.translated_text: one should sow all seeds and have permanent garments made.

body.text: p.83.1ab/.ṛṇaṃ na dadyāt tatra^eva vairam atra tu vardhate/
body.translated_text: One should not lend money here; enmity increases here.

body.text: p.83.1cd/.saṃgrāmaṃ ca surāyogaṃ dvayam eva vivarjayet//
body.translated_text: Battle and the preparation of liquor — both should be avoided.

body.text: p.83.2ab/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya janma ca^atra praśasyate/
body.translated_text: If the god rains [here], and birth here is praiseworthy.

body.text: p.83.2cd/.sānukrośaḥ kṣamāyuktaḥ strī^kāmo bhakṣalolupaḥ/
body.translated_text: One [born here] is compassionate, endowed with patience, fond of women, gluttonous,

body.text: p.83.2ef/.āyuṣmān paśumān dhanyo mahā^bhogo +atra jāyate//rohiṇyāṃ//
body.translated_text: long-lived, possessed of cattle, prosperous, and of great enjoyment. [Under <s>Rohiṇī</s>.]

body.text: p.83.3ab/.saumyaṃ mṛgaśiro vidyād ṛju tisraś ca tārakāḥ/
body.translated_text: One should know <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> as gentle, with three straight stars.

body.text: p.83.3cd/.mṛdūni yāni karmāṇi tāni sarvāṇi kārayet/
body.translated_text: All gentle activities should be performed under it;

body.text: p.83.3ef/.yāni karmāṇi rohiṇyāṃ tāni sarvāṇi kārayet//
body.translated_text: all the activities prescribed for <s>Rohiṇī</s> should also be performed.

body.text: p.83.3ab/.sakṣīrān vāpayed vṛkṣān bījāni kṣīravanti ca/
body.translated_text: One should plant trees that yield milk and seeds that are milky.

body.text: p.83.3cd/.rāja^prāsādavalabhīchatrāṇy api ca kārayet//
body.translated_text: Royal palaces, upper stories, and parasols should also be made.

body.text: p.83.4ab/.sarvakarmakathāḥ kuryāc caryāvāsān na kārayet/
body.translated_text: All kinds of work-related discussions should be held; rest-houses should not be built.

body.text: p.83.4cd/.uṣṭrāṃś ca balīvardāṃś ca damayed api kṛṣṭaye//
body.translated_text: Camels and bullocks should be tamed for plowing.

body.text: p.83.5ab/.ācchādayen navaṃ vāsaś ca^alaṅkāraṃ ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: One should put on new garments and have ornaments made.

body.text: p.83.5cd/.dvijātīnāṃ tu karmāṇi sarvāṇy evātra kārayet//
body.translated_text: All rites for the twice-born should be performed here.

body.text: p.83.6ab/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya suvṛṣṭiṃ ca^atra nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: If the god rains [here], one should predict good rainfall.

body.text: p.83.6cd/.svapnaśīlas tathā trāsī medhāvī sa ca jāyate//mṛgaśirasi//
body.translated_text: One born here is given to sleep, timid, yet intelligent. [Under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>.]

body.text: p.84.1ab/.ārdrāyāṃ mṛgayed arthān bhadraṃ karma ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Ārdrā</s>, one should seek wealth and perform auspicious rites.

body.text: p.84.1cd/.krūrakarmāṇi sidhyanti tāni vidvān vivarjayet//
body.translated_text: Cruel deeds succeed [here]; the wise should avoid them.

body.text: p.84.2ab/.udapāna^parīkhāṃś ca taḍāgāny atra kārayet/
body.translated_text: Wells and trenches, and reservoirs should be built here.

body.text: p.84.2cd/.ūheta(ūhayet) prathamāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ vikrīṇīyāc ca na^atra gāṃ/
body.translated_text: One should anticipate the first rain; one should not sell cows here.

body.text: p.84.2ef/.tila^pīḍāni karmāṇi śauṇḍikānāṃ tathāpaṇaṃ//
body.translated_text: Activities involving pressing of sesame, and shops of liquor-sellers [are suitable here].

body.text: p.84.3ab/.pīḍayed ikṣudaṇḍāni; ikṣubījāni vāpayet/
body.translated_text: One should press sugarcane stalks; sugarcane seeds should be planted.

body.text: p.84.3cd/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya vidyād bahu^parisravaṃ/
body.translated_text: If the god rains [here], one should know it to be with abundant moisture.

body.text: p.84.3ef/.krodhano mṛgayāśīlo māmsakāmo +atra jāyate//ārdrāyāṃ//
body.translated_text: One born here is wrathful, fond of hunting, and desirous of meat. [Under <s>Ārdrā</s>.]

body.text: p.84.4ab/.punarvasau tu yukte +atra kuryād vai vrata^dhāraṇaṃ/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Punarvasu</s>, one should undertake the observance of vows;

body.text: p.84.4cd/.godānaṃ ca^upanāyanaṃ sarvam atra prasidhyati//
body.translated_text: the gift of cows and the initiation ceremony — everything succeeds here.

body.text: p.84.5ab/.prajāyamānāṃ pramadāṃ gṛhītvā gṛham ānayet/
body.translated_text: One should take a woman who is about to give birth and bring her into the house.

body.text: p.84.5cd/.punaḥ punar yadīccheta tatra karmāṇi kārayet//
body.translated_text: If one wishes [an activity] to recur again and again, one should perform actions there.

body.text: p.85.1ab/.cikitsanaṃ na kurvīta yadīcchen na parābhavaṃ/
body.translated_text: One should not perform medical treatment if one does not wish defeat.

body.text: p.85.1cd/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya janma ca^atra praśasyate//
body.translated_text: If the god rains [here], birth here is praiseworthy.

body.text: p.85.2ab/.alīlaś ca^atra jāyeta strī^lolaś ca^api mānavaḥ/
body.translated_text: One born here is without play, and a man fond of women,

body.text: p.85.2cd/.citra^śīlaś ca naikatrārpitacittaḥ sa; ucyate//punarvasau//
body.translated_text: of varied disposition and not fixated on one thing, it is said. [Under <s>Punarvasu</s>.]

body.text: p.85.3ab/.dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ puṣye nityaṃ prayojayet/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Puṣya</s>, one should always undertake what is auspicious, glorious, and life-promoting.

body.text: p.85.3cd/.sarveṣāṃ ca dvijātīnāṃ sarvakarmāṇi kārayet//
body.translated_text: All rites for all the twice-born should be performed.

body.text: p.85.4ab/.rājāmātyaṃ prayuñjīta śuśrūṣāṃ vinayaṃ caret/
body.translated_text: One should appoint a royal minister, perform service, and practice discipline.

body.text: p.85.4cd/.rājānam abhipiñced ca; alaṃkuryāt svakāṃ tanu//
body.translated_text: One should approach the king and adorn one's own body.

body.text: p.85.5ab/.śmaśrukarmāṇi kuryāc ca vapanaṃ nakhalomataḥ/
body.translated_text: One should perform beard-trimming, and shaving of nails and body hair.

body.text: p.85.5cd/.purohitaṃ ca kurvīta dhvaja^agraṃ ca prakārayet//
body.translated_text: One should appoint a family priest and erect the top of a banner.

body.text: p.85.6ab/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya mandavarṣaṃ samādiśet/
body.translated_text: If the god rains [here], one should predict light rain.

body.text: p.85.6cd/.na ca rogo na cauraś ca kṣemaṃ ca^atra sadā bhavet//
body.translated_text: There is no disease, no thieves, and prosperity always prevails here.

body.text: p.85.7ab/.puṣyeṇa nitya^yuktaḥ san sarvakarmāṇi sādhayet/
body.translated_text: One who is constantly connected with <s>Puṣya</s> accomplishes all tasks.

body.text: p.85.7cd/.vaireṇātropanāhaiś ca ye janās tān vivarjayet/
body.translated_text: One should avoid those people who are hostile and bear grudges.

body.text: p.85.7ef/.āyuṣmāṃś ca yaśasvī ca mahā^bhogaḥ prajāyate//puṣye//
body.translated_text: One born here is long-lived, famous, and of great enjoyment. [Under <s>Puṣya</s>.]

body.text: p.86.1ab/.sidhyate dāruṇaṃ karma; aśleṣāyāṃ ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: Cruel deeds succeed under <s>Āśleṣā</s>, and should be performed.

body.text: p.86.1cd/.kuryād ābharaṇāny atra prākāram upakalpayet//
body.translated_text: Ornaments should be made here, and a rampart should be prepared.

body.text: p.86.2ab/.dehabandhaṃ nadī^bandhaṃ sandhikarma ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: Binding of bodies, damming of rivers, and joining work should be done.

body.text: p.86.2cd/.prabhūta^daṃśamaśakaṃ varṣaṃ mandaṃ ca varṣati/
body.translated_text: There are abundant gnats and mosquitoes, and it rains lightly.

body.text: p.86.2ef/.krodhanaḥ svapnaśīlaś ca kuhakaś ca^atra jāyate//aśleṣāyāṃ//
body.translated_text: One born here is wrathful, given to sleep, and deceitful. [Under <s>Āśleṣā</s>.]

body.text: p.86.3ab/.maghāsu sarvadhānyāni vāpayet saṃhared api/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Maghā</s>, all grains should be sown and also harvested.

body.text: p.86.3cd/.saṃghātakarma kurvīta sumukhaṃ ca^atra kārayet//
body.translated_text: Collective work should be done, and a festive gateway should be made.

body.text: p.86.4ab/.koṣṭha^āgārāṇi kurvīta phalaṃ ca^atra niveśayat/
body.translated_text: Storehouses and granaries should be built, and fruits should be stored here.

body.text: p.86.4cd/.sarvadā pitṛdevebhyaḥ śrāddhaṃ caiva^atra kārayet//
body.translated_text: Offerings to the ancestors and <s>śrāddha</s> (funeral rites) should always be performed here.

body.text: p.86.5ab/.sasyānāṃ bahulī^bhāvo yadi devo +atra varṣati/
body.translated_text: If the god rains here, there will be an abundance of crops.

body.text: p.86.5cd/.suhṛc ca dvārikaś ca^eva rasa^kāmaś ca jāyate/
body.translated_text: One born here is friendly, a gatekeeper, and desirous of pleasures,

body.text: p.86.5ef/.āyuṣmān bahu^putraś ca strī^kāmo bhakta^lolupaḥ//
body.translated_text: long-lived, having many sons, fond of women, and gluttonous.

body.text: p.86.6ab/.saṃgrāmaṃ jīyate tatra yadi pūrvaṃ pravartate/
body.translated_text: One who initiates battle there is defeated.

body.text: p.86.6cd/.dāruṇāni ca karmāṇi tāni vidvān vivarjayet//maghāsu//
body.translated_text: The wise should avoid cruel deeds [here]. [Under <s>Maghā</s>.]

body.text: p.87.1ab/.phalgunīṣu ca pūrvāsu saubhāgyārthāni kārayet/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s>, one should perform acts for good fortune,

body.text: p.87.1cd/.viśeṣād āmalakyādi phalānām upakārayet//
body.translated_text: and especially prepare fruits such as <s>āmalakī</s> (Indian gooseberry) and the like.

body.text: p.87.2ab/.kumārīmaṅgalārthāni snāpanāni ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: Auspicious rites for maidens and bathing ceremonies should be performed.

body.text: p.87.2cd/.kanyā^pravahanārthāya vihāraṃ ca^eva kārayet//
body.translated_text: For the purpose of escorting the bride, and a pleasure garden should be built.

body.text: p.87.3ab/.veśmāni kārayet tatra vaśya(vaiśya)m atra prayojayet/
body.translated_text: Houses should be built there; a <s>vaiśya</s> (merchant) should be employed here.

body.text: p.87.3cd/.bhāgaṃ ye ca^upajīvanti teṣāṃ karma prayojayet//
body.translated_text: Those who live on a share [of profits] — their work should be undertaken.

body.text: p.87.4ab/.avyaktakeśo +akeśaḥ subhagaś ca^atra jāyate/
body.translated_text: One born here has indistinct hair or no hair, and is fortunate.

body.text: p.87.4cd/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya suvṛṣṭim abhinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: If the god rains [here], one should predict good rainfall.

body.text: p.87.4ef/.naṣṭaṃ viddhaṃ kṛtaṃ ca^api na tad asti^iti nirdiśet//pūrvaphalgunyāṃ//
body.translated_text: What is lost, struck, or done — one should declare it as non-existent. [Under <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s>.]

body.text: p.87.5ab/.uttarāyāṃ tu phalgunyāṃ sarvakarmāṇi kārayet/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Uttaraphālgunī</s>, all activities should be performed.

body.text: p.87.5cd/.medhāvī darśanīyaś ca yaśasvī ca^atra jāyate//
body.translated_text: One born here is intelligent, handsome, and famous.

body.text: p.87.6ab/.athātra naṣṭaṃ dagdhaṃ vā sarvam asti^iti nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: And here, what is lost or burnt — one should declare everything as existing.

body.text: p.87.6cd/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya vidyāt saṃpadanuttamāṃ//uttaraphalgunyāṃ//
body.translated_text: If the god rains [here], one should know the harvest will be unsurpassed. [Under <s>Uttaraphālgunī</s>.]

body.text: p.88.1ab/.hastena laghu^karmāṇi sarvāṇy eva prayojayet/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Hasta</s>, all light tasks should be undertaken.

body.text: p.88.1cd/.sarveṣāṃ ca dvijātīnāṃ sarvakarmāṇi kārayet//
body.translated_text: All rites for all the twice-born should be performed.

body.text: p.88.2ab/.hastyārohaṃ mahā^mātraṃ puṣkariṇīṃ ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: Elephant-mounting, the appointment of a chief minister, and a lotus-pond should be made.

body.text: p.88.2cd/.cauryaṃ ca sidhyate tatra tac ca vidvān vivarjayet//
body.translated_text: Theft also succeeds there; the wise should avoid it.

body.text: p.88.3ab/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya varṣā viśrāvaṇī bhavet/
body.translated_text: If the god rains [here], the rains will be of the spreading kind.

body.text: p.88.3cd/.athātra jātaṃ jānīyāc chūraṃ cauraṃ vicakṣaṇaṃ/
body.translated_text: One born here should be known as a hero, a thief, discerning,

body.text: p.88.3ef/.kuśalaṃ sarvavidyāsu; ārogaṃ cirajīvinaṃ//haste//
body.translated_text: skilled in all arts, healthy, and long-lived. [Under <s>Hasta</s>.]

body.text: p.88.4ab/.citrāyām āhataṃ vastraṃ bhūṣaṇāni ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Citrā</s>, new cloth, and ornaments should be made.

body.text: p.88.4cd/.rājānaṃ bhūṣitaṃ paśyet senāvyūhaṃ ca darśayet//
body.translated_text: One should see the king adorned, and display the army formation.

body.text: p.88.5ab/.hiraṇyaṃ rajataṃ dravyaṃ nagarāṇi ca māpayet/
body.translated_text: Gold, silver, treasure, and cities should be measured.

body.text: p.88.5cd/.alaṅkuryāt tathātmānaṃ gandha^mālyavilepanaiḥ//
body.translated_text: One should adorn oneself with fragrances, garlands, and unguents.

body.text: p.88.6ab/.gaṇakānāṃ ca vidyāṃ ca vādyaṃ nartanagāyanaṃ/
body.translated_text: The science of astrologers, instrumental music, dancing, and singing,

body.text: p.88.6cd/.pūrvikāṃ rūpakārāṃś ca rathakārāṃś ca śikṣayet/
body.translated_text: the ancient art, sculptors, and chariot-makers should be trained.

body.text: p.88.6ef/.citra^karāṃś ca lekhakān pustakarma ca kārayet//
body.translated_text: And one should employ skilled painters and have manuscript work done.

body.text: p.89.1ab/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya citra^varṣaṃ vinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god [<s>Indra</s>], one should predict a colorful (mixed) rainfall.

body.text: p.89.1cd/.medhāvī darśanīyaś ca citrākṣo bhakta^lolupaḥ//
body.translated_text: One born [under <s>Citrā</s>] is intelligent, good-looking, bright-eyed, and fond of food,

body.text: p.89.2ab/.mṛdu^śīlaś ca bhīruś ca calacittaḥ kutūhalī/
body.translated_text: gentle in character, timid, fickle-minded, and curious,

body.text: p.89.2cd/.āyuṣmān subhagaś ca^eva strī^lolaś ca^atra jāyate//citrāyāṃ//
body.translated_text: long-lived, fortunate, and lustful toward women. // [Under <s>Citrā</s>] //

body.text: p.89.3ab/.svātyāṃ prayojayed yodhān aśvān aśvatarīṃ kharān/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Svātī</s>, one should deploy warriors, horses, she-mules, and donkeys,

body.text: p.89.3cd/.kṣipraṃ gamanīyaṃ bhakṣyaṃ laṅghakān adhvamānikān//
body.translated_text: fast-moving food supplies, acrobats, and road-measurers.

body.text: p.89.4ab/.bherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavān murajān ca^upanāhayet/
body.translated_text: One should have kettledrums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, <s>paṇavas</s>, and <s>murajas</s> bound [with new leather].

body.text: p.89.4cd/.āvāhaṃś ca vivāhaṃś ca sauhṛdyaṃ ca^atra kārayet//
body.translated_text: One should perform welcoming ceremonies, wedding ceremonies, and acts of friendship here.

body.text: p.89.5ab/.nirvāsanam amitrāṇāṃ svayaṃ na pravased gṛhāt/
body.translated_text: One should banish enemies but not leave one's own house.

body.text: p.89.5cd/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya vāta^vṛṣṭir abhīkṣṇaśaḥ/
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god, [one should predict] wind and rain frequently.

body.text: p.89.5ef/.medhāvī roga^bahulaś calacittaś ca jāyate//svātau//
body.translated_text: One born [under <s>Svātī</s>] is intelligent, prone to many illnesses, and fickle-minded. // [Under <s>Svātī</s>] //

body.text: p.89.6ab/.lāṅgalāni viśākhāsu karṣaṇaṃ ca prayojayet/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Viśākhā</s>, one should employ ploughs and set to plowing.

body.text: p.89.6cd/.yavagodhūmakarma^antān śamīdhānyaṃ ca varjayet//
body.translated_text: One should complete work with barley and wheat, and avoid <s>śamī</s> grain.

body.text: p.89.7ab/.śālayas tila^māṣāś ca ye ca vṛkṣāḥ suśākhinaḥ/
body.translated_text: Rice, sesame, <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), and trees with good branches —

body.text: p.90.1ab/.ropayet tān viśākhāsu gṛhakarma ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: one should plant these under <s>Viśākhā</s>, and should have house construction done.

body.text: p.90.1cd/.śiraḥ^snānāni kurvīta medhyaṃ prāyaś ca kārayet//
body.translated_text: One should perform head-ablutions and generally perform purificatory rites.

body.text: p.90.2ab/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya vidyāt kalpa^parisravaṃ/
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god, one should know it as a steady flow (<s>kalpa-parisrava</s>).

body.text: p.90.2cd/.manasvī darśanīyaś ca medhāvī ca^atra jāyate/
body.translated_text: One born [under <s>Viśākhā</s>] is spirited, good-looking, and intelligent,

body.text: p.90.2ef/.krodhano +alpasutaś ca^eva durbhago bhakta^lolupaḥ//viśākhāsu//
body.translated_text: wrathful, with few sons, unfortunate, and fond of food. // [Under <s>Viśākhā</s>] //

body.text: p.90.3ab/.anurādhāsu kurvīta mitraiḥ sadbhiś ca saṅgatiṃ/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Anurādhā</s>, one should associate with good friends,

body.text: p.90.3cd/.sarvāṇi mṛdu^karmāṇi mādhuryaṃ ca^atra kārayet//
body.translated_text: and should perform all gentle works and acts of sweetness here.

body.text: p.90.4ab/.kṣauraṃ ca kārayet atra śastra^karmāṇi kārayet/
body.translated_text: One should have shaving done here and should perform works with sharp instruments.

body.text: p.90.4cd/.saṃyuktāntaprayogāṃś ca sandhiṃ kuryāc ca nityaśaḥ/
body.translated_text: One should employ combined practices and always make alliances.

body.text: p.90.4ef/.naṣṭaṃ paryupataptaṃ vā svalpāyasena(yāsaṃvi)nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: What is lost or afflicted should be predicted as [recoverable] with little effort.

body.text: p.90.5ab/.suhṛnmitrakṛtaś ca^atra dharma^śīlaś ca jāyate/
body.translated_text: One born here is friendly, of good character, and devoted to <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: p.90.5cd/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya suvṛṣṭim abhinirdiśet//anurādhāyāṃ//
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god, one should predict good rainfall. // [Under <s>Anurādhā</s>] //

body.text: p.90.6ab/.jyeṣṭhāyāṃ pūrva^kārī syād rājānaṃ ca^abhiṣiñcayet/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, one should be the first to act and should consecrate a king.

body.text: p.90.6cd/.nagaraṃ nigamaṃ grāmaṃ māpayed ārabheta ca/
body.translated_text: One should plan and commence [the building of] a city, a market-town, or a village,

body.text: p.90.6ef/.kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca rājñāṃ ca sarvakarmāṇi kārayet//
body.translated_text: and should have all works for <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and kings performed.

body.text: p.91.1ab/.bhrātṛṇāṃ bhavati jyeṣṭho jyeṣṭāyāṃ yo +abhijāyate/
body.translated_text: One born under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> becomes the eldest among brothers,

body.text: p.91.1cd/.āyuṣmāṃś ca yaśasvī ca vidvatsu ca kutūhalī//
body.translated_text: long-lived, famous, and curious among the learned.

body.text: p.91.2ab/.prāsādam ārohec ca^atra gajam aśvaṃ rathaṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: One should ascend a palace here, and [mount] an elephant, horse, or chariot likewise.

body.text: p.91.2cd/.grāma^nigamarāṣṭreṣu sthāpayec chreṣṭhināṃ balaṃ//
body.translated_text: One should establish the power of guild-leaders in villages, market-towns, and kingdoms.

body.text: p.91.3ab/.naṣṭaṃ paryupataptaṃ vā kleśenaiveti nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: What is lost or afflicted should be predicted as [recoverable] only with difficulty.

body.text: p.91.3cd/.dāruṇāny atra sidhyanti tāni vidvān vivarjayet/
body.translated_text: Harsh [enterprises] succeed here — the wise should avoid them.

body.text: p.91.3ef/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya suvṛṣṭim abhinirdiśet//jyeṣṭhāyāṃ//
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god, one should predict good rainfall. // [Under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>] //

body.text: p.91.4ab/.mūle tu mūlajātāni mūlakandālukāny api/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Mūla</s>, [one should employ] things born from roots — roots, tubers, and bulbs,

body.text: p.91.4cd/.sūlādyāni ca sarvāṇi bījāny atra prayojayet//
body.translated_text: and all [things beginning with] skewers, and seeds should be put to use here.

body.text: p.91.5ab/.ṛṇaṃ vai yat purāṇaṃ syād artho ca^asyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ/
body.translated_text: Any old debt, and wealth standing before one —

body.text: p.91.5cd/.mūle siddhartham ārabhyaṃ tathā sarvaṃ varāṅgakaṃ//
body.translated_text: under <s>Mūla</s>, one should undertake [collecting] the accomplished [debts], and all excellent [enterprises].

body.text: p.91.6ab/.cikitsitāni yānīha strīṇāṃ dārakakanyayoḥ/
body.translated_text: Medical treatments here for women, boys, and girls,

body.text: p.91.6cd/.nadīṣu snapanaṃ ca^eva mūle sarvān prayojayet//
body.translated_text: and bathing in rivers — under <s>Mūla</s>, all [these] should be employed.

body.text: p.92.1ab/.dāruṇāny atra sidhyanti maṅgalāni ca kārayet/
body.translated_text: Harsh [enterprises] succeed here, and one should perform auspicious rites.

body.text: p.92.1cd/.kiṇvayogān surāyogān na kuryāc chatrubhiḥ saha//
body.translated_text: One should not prepare fermented preparations or liquor-preparations with enemies.

body.text: p.92.2ab/.dhana^vān bahu^putraś ca mūlavān atra jāyate/
body.translated_text: One born here is wealthy, having many sons, and well-rooted (<s>mūlavān</s>).

body.text: p.92.2cd/.athātra naṣṭaṃ dagdhaṃ vā naitad asti^iti nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: And what is lost or burnt here should be predicted as 'it does not exist [anymore].'

body.text: p.92.2ef/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya suvṛṣṭim abhinirdiśet//mūle//
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god, one should predict good rainfall. // [Under <s>Mūla</s>] //

body.text: p.92.3ab/.āṣāḍhāyāṃ ca pūrvasyāṃ saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, [one should construct] rivers, lakes,

body.text: p.92.3cd/.vāpīkūpaprapāś ca^eva taḍāgāni ca kārayet//
body.translated_text: wells, cisterns, drinking-water stations, and reservoirs.

body.text: p.92.4ab/.utpādyāni ca puṣpāṇi tathā mūlaphalāni ca/
body.translated_text: Flowers that are to be cultivated, as well as roots and fruits —

body.text: p.92.4cd/.ārāmāṃś ca prakurvīta bhaikṣakāṃś ca prayojayet/
body.translated_text: one should create gardens and employ mendicants.

body.text: p.92.4ef/.yāni ca^ugrāṇi karmāṇi sidhyanty atra tu tāni ca//
body.translated_text: Fierce works succeed here as well.

body.text: p.92.5ab/.naṣṭaṃ paryupataptaṃ vā naitad asti^iti nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: What is lost or afflicted should be predicted as 'it does not exist [anymore].'

body.text: p.92.5cd/.āyuṣmān puṇyaśīlaś ca darśanīyo +atra jāyate//pūrvāṣāḍhe//
body.translated_text: One born [under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>] is long-lived, of virtuous character, and good-looking. // [Under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>] //

body.text: p.92.6ab/.uttarasyām āṣāḍhāyāṃ vairāṇi na samācaret/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, one should not engage in hostilities.

body.text: p.92.6cd/.vāyayet sarvavāsāṃsi navaṃ nācchādayed iti//
body.translated_text: One should have all garments woven, and should not put on new [garments].

body.text: p.93.1ab/.na saṃhared bhedayed vā vāstukarma na sidhyati/
body.translated_text: One should not collect or distribute; architectural work does not succeed.

body.text: p.93.1cd/.śālākarma gava^ādīnāṃ grāme grāmaṇinas tathā/
body.translated_text: Stables for cattle and the like, village headmen likewise,

body.text: p.93.1c/.śreṇavindhaṃ ca rājā nu samayaṃ ca^atra kārayet//
body.translated_text: guilds and assemblies — the king should make agreements here.

body.text: p.93.2ab/.pragalbhaś ca sabhāśīlaḥ kṛtī ca^atra prajāyate/
body.translated_text: One born here is bold, accustomed to assemblies, and accomplished,

body.text: p.93.2cd/.suhṛdām abhiyogī ca mantra^bhāṣye vicakṣaṇaḥ//
body.translated_text: devoted to friends, and skilled in the art of counsel.

body.text: p.93.3ab/.naṣṭaṃ vā^apy upataptaṃ vā; astīty evaṃ vinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: What is lost or afflicted should be predicted as 'it exists.'

body.text: p.93.3cd/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya suvṛṣṭim abhinirdiśet//uttarāṣāḍhāyāṃ//
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god, one should predict good rainfall. // [Under <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>] //

body.text: p.93.4/.abhijiti na kurvīta brahma^devasya hy arcanaṃ//abhijiti//
body.translated_text: Under <s>Abhijit</s>, one should not perform [anything] except the worship of <s>Brahmā</s>. // [Under <s>Abhijit</s>] //

body.text: p.93.5ab/.śravaṇe na ca kurvīta sarvāḥ saṃgrāmikāḥ kriyāḥ/
body.translated_text: Under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, one should not perform any activities related to battle.

body.text: p.93.5cd/.gītaśikṣādhyayanaṃ ca na cireṇa hi sidhyati//
body.translated_text: Instruction in singing and study — these do not take long to succeed.

body.text: p.93.6ab/.karṇayor vedhanaṃ kuryād rājānaṃ ca^abhiṣiñcayet/
body.translated_text: One should have ears pierced and should consecrate a king.

body.text: p.93.6cd/.dvijātīnāṃ tu karmāṇi sarvāṇy eva prayojayet//
body.translated_text: One should employ all rites for the twice-born.

body.text: p.94.7ab/.bali^kṛtyāni kurvīta darśayec ca balāny api/
body.translated_text: One should perform <s>bali</s> (offering) rites and also display armies.

body.text: p.94.7cd/.medhāvī arogī balavān yajña^śīlo +atra jāyate//
body.translated_text: One born [under <s>Śravaṇa</s>] is intelligent, healthy, strong, and devoted to sacrifice.

body.text: p.94.8ab/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya suvṛṣṭim abhinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god, one should predict good rainfall.

body.text: p.94.8cd/.naṣṭaṃ ca labhyate tatra śravanasthe niśākare//śravaṇe//
body.translated_text: What is lost is recovered there when the moon is in <s>Śravaṇa</s>. // [Under <s>Śravaṇa</s>] //

body.text: p.94.9ab/.dhaniṣṭhā laghu nakṣatraṃ sarvakarmasu pūjitaṃ/
body.translated_text: <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> is a swift <s>nakṣatra</s>, honored in all undertakings.

body.text: p.94.9cd/.adhītya brāhmaṇaḥ snāyād rājānam abhiṣiñcayet//
body.translated_text: Having studied, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should bathe [ceremonially], and one should consecrate a king.

body.text: p.94.10ab/.sarveṣāṃ ca dvijātīnāṃ sarvakarmāṇi kārayet/
body.translated_text: One should have all rites of all the twice-born performed.

body.text: p.94.10cd/.śreṣṭhinaṃ sthāpayed deśe gaṇādhyakṣaṃ gaṇeśv api//
body.translated_text: One should establish a guild-master in the region and a superintendent of guilds among the guilds.

body.text: p.94.11ab/.medhāvī ca yaśasvī ca mahā^bhogī mahā^dhanaḥ//
body.translated_text: One born [under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>] is intelligent, famous, having great enjoyments, and very wealthy,

body.text: p.94.11cd/.bahv^apatyo mṛdur dānto mahā^ātmā ca^atra jāyate/
body.translated_text: with many offspring, gentle, self-controlled, and great-souled.

body.text: p.94.11c/.pravarṣaṇaṃ ca devasya vidyāc ca^atra suvṛṣṭitāṃ//dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ//
body.translated_text: Regarding the rainfall of the god, one should know there will be good rainfall here. // [Under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>] //

body.text: p.94.12ab/.nityaṃ śatabhiṣāyoge bhaiṣajyāni prayojayet/
body.translated_text: Always, when the conjunction is with <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, one should employ medicines.

body.text: p.94.12cd/.kīrtikarma ca kurvīta sidhyanty ātharvaṇāni ca//
body.translated_text: One should perform works of fame, and <s>Ātharvanic</s> (rites from the <s>Atharvaveda</s>) succeed.

body.text: p.94.13ab/.prasārayec ca paṇyāni śauṇḍikaṃ ca prayojayet/
body.translated_text: One should display merchandise and employ brewers.

body.text: p.94.13cd/.adadhiṃ khānāyet tatra tila^māṣāṃś ca vāpayet//
body.translated_text: One should dig wells there and sow sesame and <s>māṣa</s> (black gram).

body.text: p.95.1ab/.(95)sāmudrikāṇi paṇyāṇi nāvinaś ca prayojayet/
body.translated_text: Maritime merchandise and sailors should be employed.

body.text: p.95.1cd/.ādeyaṃ ca tadā +adadyād vyayaṃ ca^atra na kārayet//
