body.text: u3.6ab/.śīrṣe tu dhana^dhānyābhyāṃ kāntaye subhagāya ca/
body.translated_text: A mark on the top of the head signifies wealth, grain, beauty, and good fortune;

body.text: u3.6cd/.upaghātaṃ bhrūvor vidyāt strī^lābho bhrūvasaṅgame//
body.translated_text: a harmful mark on the eyebrows should be known — a mark at the junction of the eyebrows means the attainment of a wife.

body.text: u3.7ab/.akṣisthāne tu piṭakaḥkaroti priya^darśanaṃ/
body.translated_text: A <s>piṭaka</s> at the location of the eyes makes one pleasant to behold.

body.text: u3.7cd/.akṣibhrūbhāge śokāya gaṇḍe putravadho dhruvaṃ//
body.translated_text: A [mole] born in the region of the eye and brow indicates sorrow; on the cheek, the death of a son is certain.

body.text: u3.8ab/.aśrūpātaḥ dhruvaṃ śokaḥ śravaṇe goṣu nāśakaḥ/
body.translated_text: Falling of tears certainly [indicates] grief; on the ear, destruction of cattle.

body.text: u3.8cd/.karṇa^pīṭhe vibhūṣāya nāsāvaṃśe tu jātaye//
body.translated_text: On the base of the ear, [it indicates] adornment; on the bridge of the nose, [it portends] offspring.

body.text: u3.9ab/.nāsāgaṇḍe putra^lābhaṃ vastra^lābhaṃ dhruvaṃ vadet/
body.translated_text: On the side of the nose, one should declare the gain of a son; on the cheek [near the nose], the gain of garments is certain.

body.text: u3.9cd/.nāsa^agre jātenāpnoti gandha^bhogān abhīpsitān//
body.translated_text: One born at the tip of the nose obtains the desired enjoyment of fragrances.

body.text: u3.10ab/.uttaroṣṭhe tathādhare ca^anna^pānaṃ śubha^aśubhaṃ/(p.152)
body.translated_text: On the upper lip and the lower lip, [it indicates] auspicious or inauspicious food and drink.

body.text: u3.10cd/.cibuke hanudeśe ca dhanaṃ gāvaḥ satāṃ śriyaḥ//
body.translated_text: On the chin and the jaw region, [it indicates] wealth, cattle, and the prosperity of the good.

body.text: u3.11ab/.gale tu dānam āpnoti pānam ābharaṇāni ca/
body.translated_text: On the throat, one obtains gifts, drink, and ornaments.

body.text: u3.11cd/.śiraḥ^sandhau ca grīvāyāṃ śiraśchedanam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: At the junction of the head and on the neck, one should predict beheading.

body.text: u3.12ab/.jāto +ayaṃ śiraso mūle hanuni ca dhana^kṣayaḥ/
body.translated_text: A [mole] born at the base of the head and on the jaw [indicates] loss of wealth.

body.text: u3.12cd/.bhaikṣacaryā bhavet sandhau hṛdaye priya^saṅgamaḥ//
body.translated_text: At the joint, there will be a life of begging; on the heart, the meeting of a beloved.

body.text: u3.13ab/.pṛṣṭhe tu duḥkhaśayyāyai; anna^pānakṣayāya ca/
body.translated_text: On the back, [it portends] a bed of suffering and the loss of food and drink.

body.text: u3.13cd/.pārśve tu sukha^śayyāyai stane tu sutajanyatā//
body.translated_text: On the side, [it indicates] a comfortable bed; on the breast, the birth of a son.

body.text: u3.14ab/.jātena śivam āpnoti na ca^apriya^samāgamaḥ/
body.translated_text: One born [with such a mark] obtains auspiciousness, and there is no meeting with the unpleasant.

body.text: u3.14cd/.bāhvoḥ śatru^vināśāya yuktaṃ strī^lābha; eva ca//
body.translated_text: On the arms, [it portends] the destruction of enemies, and also the gain of a wife.

body.text: u3.15ab/.dadāty ābharaṇaṃ jātaḥ prabāhvoḥ kurpare kṣudhā/
body.translated_text: A [mole] born on the forearms gives ornaments; on the elbow, hunger.

body.text: u3.15cd/.maṇibandhe niyamanamaṃsābhyāṃ harṣa; eva ca//
body.translated_text: On the wrist and the flesh of the arms, [it indicates] joy.

body.text: u3.16ab/.saubhagaṃ dhana^lābhaṃca jātaḥ pāṇau dadāti ca/
body.translated_text: A [mole] born on the palm gives good fortune and the gain of wealth.

body.text: u3.16cd/.puṣpito hy ekadeśe tu daśaneṣu nakheṣu ca//
body.translated_text: And when it blossoms in one particular spot, on the teeth and on the nails —

body.text: u3.17ab/.jātena hṛdi jānīyād bhrātṛputrasamāgamaṃ/
body.translated_text: By a [mole] born on the heart, one should know [there will be] the meeting of a brother or son.

body.text: u3.17cd/.jaṭhare soma^dānāya nābhyāṃ strī^lābham ādiśet//
body.translated_text: On the belly, [it indicates] the gift of <s>Soma</s>; at the navel, one should predict the gain of a wife.

body.text: u3.18ab/.jaghane vyasanaṃ vidyān nārya dauḥśīlyam eva ca/
body.translated_text: On the hip, one should know there will be calamity; for women, bad conduct.

body.text: u3.18cd/.putrotpattis tu vṛṣaṇe liṅge bhāryā tu śobhanā//
body.translated_text: The birth of a son [is indicated by a mark] on the testicles; on the penis, a beautiful wife.

body.text: u3.19ab/.pṛṣṭhānte sukha^bhāgitvaṃ sphici ca^api dhana^kṣayaḥ/
body.translated_text: At the end of the back, [it indicates] a share of happiness; on the buttocks, loss of wealth.

body.text: u3.19cd/.ūrujātāś ca piṭakā dhana^saubhāgyadāyakāḥ//
body.translated_text: Moles born on the thigh are givers of wealth and good fortune.

body.text: u3.20ab/.jānau śatru^bhayaṃ vidyāt tathā^eva ca dhana^kṣayaṃ/
body.translated_text: On the knee, one should know there will be fear from enemies, and also loss of wealth.

body.text: u3.20cd/.jānu^saṃdhau vijānīyān meḍhrake hy atha jātakaiḥ/
body.translated_text: At the knee-joint, one should know, and on the penis indeed, by the marks of birth,

body.text: u3.20ef/.vijayaṃ jñāna^lābhaṃ ca putra^janma vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one should declare victory, the gain of knowledge, and the birth of a son.

body.text: u3.21ab/.strī^lābhaṃ vakṣasi ca^eva bhaved anyo nirarthakaḥ/
body.translated_text: On the chest, [there will be] the gain of a wife; any other [location] is fruitless.

body.text: u3.21cd/.jaṅghāyāṃ parasevā tu paradeśāt tu bhujyate//
body.translated_text: On the shin, [it indicates] service to others; one enjoys [the fruits] from a foreign land.

body.text: u3.22ab/.maṇibandhe tu piṭako bandhanaṃ nirdiśed dhruvaṃ/(p.153)
body.translated_text: A mole on the wrist certainly indicates imprisonment.

body.text:
u3.22cd/.parivādhaṃ sa labhate bandhanaṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ/
u3.22ef/.pārśve gulphe ca jānīyāc chastreṇa maraṇaṃ dhruvaṃ//
body.translated_text: He obtains slander and imprisonment — there is no doubt. On the side and ankle, one should know death by a weapon is certain.

body.text: u3.23ab/.aṅgulīṣu dhruvaṃ śoko vyādhiś ca^aṅguliparvasu/
body.translated_text: On the fingers, there is certainly grief; and disease on the finger-joints.

body.text: u3.23cd/.pravāsaṃ pravasen nityaṃ tathā^eva^uttarapādake//
body.translated_text: One will always travel abroad; likewise on the upper part of the foot.

body.text: u3.24ab/.yasya pāda^tale jātas tathā hasta^tale +api ca/
body.translated_text: One who has [a mole] born on the sole of the foot and also on the palm of the hand

body.text: u3.24cd/.dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ sutā gāvaḥ striyo yānāni ca^apnuyāt//
body.translated_text: will obtain wealth, grain, sons, cattle, women, and vehicles.

body.text:
u3.25ab/.snigdhaṃ snigdheṣu vijñeyaṃ caleṣu ca calaṃ phalaṃ/
u3.25cd/.sthāna^sthe vipulaṃ dadyāt phalaṃ nṛṇāṃ śubhodayaṃ//
body.translated_text: On soft [body parts], the result should be known as favorable; on moving parts, the result is unstable. When situated in a fixed place, [the mole] gives an abundant result of auspicious arising for men.

body.text: u3.26ab/.vivarṇo viparītaś ca phalaṃ sarvaṃ prayacchati/
body.translated_text: One that is discolored or reversed gives the opposite of all results.

body.text: u3.26cd/.puṃsāṃ madhye ye snigdhāś ca deśe dakṣiṇataś ca ye/
body.translated_text: Among men, those [moles] that are smooth and those that are on the right side,

body.text: u3.26ef/.tathā ca^abhyantare ca^eva sthāne tu pratipūjitāḥ//
body.translated_text: and likewise those that are on the inner side, are honored in their location.

body.text: u3.27ab/.strīṇāṃ mṛduṣu deśeṣu vaktrān teṣu ca parvataḥ/
body.translated_text: For women, on soft body parts, and on those [areas] the mountain-like [moles] from the face —

body.text: u3.27cd/.tattvaṃ vijñāya pinyānaṃ sthānaṃ varṇaṃ ca janma ca//
body.translated_text: having ascertained the true nature of the mole — its location, color, and origin —

body.text: u3.28ab/.sthāna^asthānaṃ ca matimān vikāraṃ gatim eva ca/
body.translated_text: its proper and improper placement, its alteration and movement,

body.text: u3.28cd/.ādiśet tu naraḥ paścād yatha^evaṃ samudāhṛtaṃ//
body.translated_text: the wise person should then predict, exactly as has been described.

body.text: u3.29ab/.vāmabhāge tu nārīṇāṃ vijñeeyāḥ piṭakāḥ śubhāḥ/
body.translated_text: For women, auspicious moles should be known on the left side.

body.text: u3.29cd/.dakṣiṇe tu manuṣyāṇāṃ bhavanti hy artha^sādhakāḥ//
body.translated_text: For men, on the right side, they bring about the accomplishment of goals.

body.text: u3.30ab/.viparītās tu piṭakā moghās tu bahavaḥ smṛtāḥ/
body.translated_text: Moles in the reversed [position] are considered fruitless — indeed many [are so].

body.text: u3.30cd/.yathoktānaṃ ca sandhisthāḥ sarve viphaladāḥ smṛtāḥ//
body.translated_text: And those of the aforementioned [types] that are situated at joints are all said to give no results.

body.text: u3.31ab/.siddhāḥ dhruvā vraṇā bhidyās tathā sadyaḥ^kṛtāś ca ye/
body.translated_text: Those that are established, permanent, [like] wounds, fissures, and those freshly made,

body.text: u3.31cd/.dharma^kīlasamāś ca^eva sarve te piṭakāḥ smṛtāḥ//
body.translated_text: and those that are like pegs of <s>dharma</s> — all these are considered moles.

body.text: u3.32ab/.guṇadoṣāś ca sarveṣāṃ tathā^apy^anye prakīrttitāḥ/
body.translated_text: The virtues and faults of all of them, and others as well, have been proclaimed.

body.text: u3.32cd/.ity āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ śiṣyebhyo nitya^darśanaṃ//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> — a constant teaching — to his disciples.

body.text: u3.33ab/.na nakhena na śastreṇa na^āyasena kathaṃcana/(p.154)
body.translated_text: Not with a nail, not with a weapon, not with iron in any way,

body.text: u3.33cd/.kāñcanena suvarṇena dahed viprāṃś ca bhojayed//
body.translated_text: but with gold — with fine gold — one should cauterize [the mole], and feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: u3.34/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin piṭakādhyāya^nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'The Chapter on Moles.'

body.text: u3.35/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin svapna^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagavān/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the Chapter on Dreams. Listen to it. Now what? Let the blessed one speak.

body.text: u4 svapna^adhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Chapter 4: The Chapter on Dreams

body.text: u4.1ab/.śubha^aśubhaṃ ca svapnānāṃ yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtaṃ/
body.translated_text: The auspicious and inauspicious results of dreams that have been described —

body.text: u4.1cd/.devatā^brāhmaṇau gāvau bahniṃ prajvalitaṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: deities, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, cows, and a blazing fire —

body.text: u4.1ef/.yas tu paśyati svapna^ante kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate//
body.translated_text: he who sees [these] at the end of a dream, his family prospers.

body.text: u4.2ab/.yas tu paśyati svapna^ante rājānnaṃ kuñjaraṃ hayaṃ/
body.translated_text: He who sees at the end of a dream royal food, an elephant, a horse,

body.text: u4.2cd/.suvarṇaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ ca^eva kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate/
body.translated_text: gold, and a bull — his family prospers.

body.text: u4.3ab/.sārasāṃś ca śukān haṃsān krauñcān śvetāṃś ca pakṣiṇaḥ/
body.translated_text: <s>Sārasa</s> cranes, parrots, <s>haṃsas</s> (geese), <s>krauñca</s> herons, and white birds —

body.text: u4.3cd/.yas tu paśyati svapne vai kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate/
body.translated_text: he who sees [these] in a dream — his family prospers.

body.text: u4.4ab/.samṛddhāni ca śasyāni navāni surabhīṇi ca/
body.translated_text: Flourishing and fresh and fragrant crops,

body.text: u4.4cd/.padminīṃ puṣpitāṃ ca^api purṇa^kumbhāṃs tathā^eva ca//
body.translated_text: a blooming lotus pond, and full water-pots likewise,

body.text: u4.5ab/.prasannam udakaṃ ca^eva puṣpāṇi vividhāni ca/
body.translated_text: clear water, and various flowers —

body.text: u4.5cd/.yas tu paśyati svapna^ante kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate//
body.translated_text: he who sees [these] at the end of a dream — his family prospers.

body.text: u4.6ab/.pāṇau pāde +atha vā jānau śasterṇa dhanuṣā^api vā/
body.translated_text: On the hand, the foot, or the knee, whether by weapon or by bow,

body.text: u4.6cd/.prahārā yasya dīyante tasya^ambaro +abhivardhate//
body.translated_text: he upon whom blows are struck — his garments increase.

body.text: u4.7ab/.tārā^candramasau sūryaṃ nakṣatrāṇi grahāṃs tathā/
body.translated_text: Stars, the moon, the sun, the <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations), and the planets —

body.text: u4.7cd/.yas tu paśyati svapna^ante kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate//
body.translated_text: he who sees [these] at the end of a dream — his family prospers.

body.text: u4.8ab/.aśva^pṛṣṭhaṃ gaja^skandhaṃ yānāni śayanāni ca/
body.translated_text: The back of a horse, the shoulder of an elephant, vehicles, and beds —

body.text: u4.8cd/.yo +abhirohati svapna^ante mahad^aiśvaryam āpnuyāt//
body.translated_text: he who mounts [these] at the end of a dream obtains great sovereignty.

body.text: u4.9ab/.patitaś ca^aruhed bhūyas tatrasthaś ca vibudhyate/(p.155)
body.translated_text: If one has fallen and climbs up again, and awakens while standing there,

body.text: u4.9cd/.aiśvarya^dhana^lābhāya naṣṭa^lābhāya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one should predict [this portends] the gain of sovereignty and wealth, and the recovery of what was lost.

body.text: u4.10ab/.goyutaṃ ca rathaṃ svapne hayaṃ vā yo +abhirohati/
body.translated_text: He who mounts in a dream a chariot yoked with oxen, or a horse,

body.text: u4.10cd/.tatrasthaś ca vibudhyeta; aiśvaryam adhigacchati//
body.translated_text: and awakens while standing there — he attains sovereignty.

body.text: u4.11ab/.prapātaṃ parvataṃ ca^eva yo +abhirohati mānavaḥ/
body.translated_text: A man who climbs a precipice or a mountain,

body.text: u4.11cd/.tatrasthaś ca vibudhyeta; aiśvaryam adhigacchati//
body.translated_text: and awakens while standing there — he attains sovereignty.

body.text: u4.12ab/.āsane śayane yane śarīre +atha gṛhe kṣayaḥ/
body.translated_text: Destruction of a seat, a bed, a vehicle, a body, or a house — for those for whom mounting is praised, from mounting [in a dream] comes destruction;

body.text: u4.12cd/.yeṣām ārohaṇaṃ śastaṃ teṣām ārohaṇāt kṣayaḥ/
body.translated_text: for those for whom mounting [normally] brings faults,

body.text: u4.12ef/.yeṣām ārohaṇād doṣās teṣām ārohaṇād guṇāḥ//
body.translated_text: from mounting [in a dream] come virtues.

body.text: u4.13ab/.tri^sāhasraṃ bhavet kaṇṭhe daśa śīrṣasya chedane/
body.translated_text: Three thousand [coins] if [seen] at the throat; ten [thousand] if the head is severed.

body.text: u4.13cd/.rājyaṃ śata^sahasraṃ vā labhate śīrṣa^bhakṣaṇe//
body.translated_text: A kingdom, or a hundred thousand, one obtains if the head is devoured [in a dream].

body.text: u4.14ab/.śuṣkāṃ nadīṃ hradaṃ vā^api śūnya^āgāra^praveśanaṃ/
body.translated_text: Seeing a dried-up river or lake, entering an empty dwelling,

body.text: u4.14cd/.śuṣka^udapāna^ṃ tu labhate svapne dṛṣṭvā dhruvaṃ bhayaṃ//
body.translated_text: or a dried-up well in a dream — one certainly encounters fear.

body.text: u4.15ab/.śṛgālaṃ mānuṣaṃ nagnaṃ godhā^vṛścika^sūkaraṃ/
body.translated_text: A jackal, a naked person, a monitor lizard, a scorpion, a boar,

body.text: u4.15cd/.ajāṃ vā paśyataḥ svapne vyādhi^kleśaṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: or a goat — for one who sees [these] in a dream, one should predict illness and distress.

body.text: u4.16ab/.kākaṃ śyenam ulūkaṃ vā gṛdhraṃ vā^apy atha vartakaṃ/
body.translated_text: A crow, a hawk, an owl, a vulture, or a quail,

body.text: u4.16cd/.mayūraṃ paśyataḥ svapne tasya vyasanam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: or a peacock — for one who sees [these] in a dream, one should predict calamity.

body.text: u4.17ab/.nagnaṃ paśyati hy ātmānaṃ pāṃśunā dhvastam eva vā/
body.translated_text: If one sees oneself naked, or covered with dust,

body.text: u4.17cd/.kardamena^upaliptaṃ vā vyādhi^kleśam avāpnuyāt//
body.translated_text: or smeared with mud — one will experience illness and distress.

body.text: u4.18ab/.kuṇḍthāḥ striyo +atha saṃlokya caurān dyūta^karāṃs tathā/
body.translated_text: If one sees in a dream lame women, thieves, gamblers,

body.text: u4.18cd/.kuśīlāṃś cāraṇān dhūrtān svapne dṛṣṭvā dhruvaṃ bhayaṃ//
body.translated_text: actors, wandering performers, and rogues — fear is certain.

body.text: u4.19ab/.vami^mūtra^purīṣāṇi virekaṃ vasāno janaḥ/
body.translated_text: A person wearing [garments stained with] vomit, urine, or excrement, or undergoing purging,

body.text: u4.19cd/.udvartanaṃ vā kurvāṇaḥ svapna^ante rogam arcchati//
body.translated_text: or performing an oil-massage — at the end of the dream, he encounters illness.

body.text: u4.20ab/.dhvajaṃ chatraṃ vitānaṃ vā svapna^ante yasya dhāryate/
body.translated_text: If at the end of a dream a banner, an umbrella, or a canopy is held [over one],

body.text: u4.20cd/.tatrastho +api vibudhyeta mahad^aiśvaryam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: and one awakens while standing there — one should predict great sovereignty.

body.text: u4.21acd/.antrais tu yasya nagaraṃ samantāt parivāryate/(p.156)
body.translated_text: He whose city is completely encircled by entrails,

body.text: u4.21cd/.grasate candra^sūryau tu mahad^aiśvaryam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: and who swallows the moon and the sun — one should predict great sovereignty.

body.text: u4.22ab/.manuṣyaṃ bhūmi^bhāgaṃ vā svapna^ante grasate yadi/
body.translated_text: If at the end of a dream one swallows a human being or a portion of land,

body.text: u4.22cd/.hradaś ca vā samudro +ayaṃ mahad^aiśvaryam āpnuyāt//
body.translated_text: or a lake or an ocean — one will obtain great sovereignty.

body.text: u4.23ab/.dhanuḥ praharaṇaṃ śastraṃ raktam ābharaṇaṃ dhvajaṃ/
body.translated_text: If one obtains in a dream a bow, a striking weapon, a blade, a red ornament, a banner,

body.text: u4.23cd/.kavacaṃ vā labhet svapne dhana^lābhaṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: or armor — one should predict the gain of wealth.

body.text: u4.24ab/.prapātaṃ parvataṃ tālaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ kuñjaraṃ hayaṃ/
body.translated_text: A precipice, a mountain, a palm tree, a bull, an elephant, a horse,

body.text: u4.24cd/.toraṇaṃ nagaraṃ dvāraṃ candra^ādityau satārakau/
body.translated_text: a gateway-arch, a city, a gate, the moon and the sun with their stars —

body.text: u4.24ef/.svapne prapatitau dṛṣṭvā rājñāṃ vyasanam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: seeing [these] fallen in a dream, one should predict calamity for kings.

body.text: u4.25ab/.udayaṃ candra^sūryāṇaṃ svapne dṛṣṭaṃ praśasyate/
body.translated_text: The rising of the moon and the sun seen in a dream is praiseworthy.

body.text: u4.25cd/.tayor astaṃ gataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājño vyasanam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: Seeing their setting, one should predict calamity for the king.

body.text: u4.26ab/.śmaśāna^vṛkṣa^yūpaṃ vā naro yady abhirohati/
body.translated_text: If a man climbs a cremation-ground tree or a sacrificial post,

body.text: u4.26cd/.valmīkaṃ bhasma^rāśiṃ vā svapne vyasanam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: an anthill, or a heap of ashes — one should predict calamity in the dream.

body.text: u4.27ab/.kṛṣṇa^vastrā tu yā nārī kālī kāmayate naraṃ/
body.translated_text: A woman clad in black garments, dark-complexioned, who desires a man

body.text: u4.27cd/.karavīra^srajā svapne tadantaṃ tasya jīvitaṃ//
body.translated_text: with a garland of <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) in a dream — that is the end of his life.

body.text: u4.28ab/.tamasi praviśet svapne śambhor vā ca^amaraṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: If in a dream one enters darkness, or [enters] the [realm] of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) or of the immortals,

body.text: u4.28cd/.vṛkṣād vā prapatet svapne maraṇaṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: or falls from a tree in a dream — one should predict his death.

body.text: u4.29ab/.vṛkṣāṃ kāṣṭhaṃ tṛṇaṃ vā^api virucaṃ yas tu paśyati/
body.translated_text: If one sees a tree, a piece of wood, or grass, or a creeper,

body.text: u4.29cd/.svapne śīrṣaṃ śarīraṃ vā maraṇaṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: [growing from] the head or body in a dream — one should predict his death.

body.text: u4.30ab/.devo vā varṣate yatra yatra ca^eva^aśaniḥ patet/
body.translated_text: Where the rain-god rains, where a thunderbolt falls,

body.text: u4.30cd/.bhūmir vā kampate yatra svapne vyasanam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: or where the earth trembles — one should predict calamity in the dream.

body.text: u4.31ab/.candra^ādityau yadi svapne khaṇḍau bhinnau ca paśyati/
body.translated_text: If in a dream one sees the moon and the sun broken, shattered,

body.text: u4.31cd/.patitau patamānau vā cakṣus tasya vinaśyati//
body.translated_text: fallen, or falling — his eyesight will be destroyed.

body.text: u4.32ab/.kāṣāya^prāvṛtāṃ muṇḍāṃ nārīṃ malina^vāsasaṃ/
body.translated_text: Seeing a woman wrapped in ochre robes, shaven-headed, wearing dirty garments,

body.text: u4.32cd/.nīla^rakta^ambarāṃ dṛṣṭvā; āyāsam adhigacchati//
body.translated_text: or dressed in blue and red — one encounters distress.

body.text: u4.33ab/.trapu^sīse; ayastāmraloharajatam añjanaṃ/(p.157)
body.translated_text: Tin, lead, iron, copper, base metal, silver, or antimony —

body.text: u4.33cd/.labdhvā tu puruṣaḥ svapne dhana^nāśaṃ samarcchati//
body.translated_text: if a man obtains [these] in a dream, he encounters loss of wealth.

body.text: u4.34ab/.gāyantī vā hasantī vā nṛtyantī vā vibudhyate/
body.translated_text: If one awakens while [a woman is] singing, laughing, or dancing,

body.text: u4.34cd/.vāditravādyamānair vā; āyāsaṃ tatra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: or with musical instruments being played — one should predict distress there.

body.text: u4.35ab/.kardame yadi vā paṅke sikatāsvavasīdati/
body.translated_text: If one sinks in mud, mire, or sand,

body.text: u4.35cd/.tatrastho vā vibudhyeta vyādhiṃ samadhigacchati//
body.translated_text: and awakens while standing there — one encounters illness.

body.text: u4.36ab/.aṣṭāpadair athānyair vā krīḍej jaya^parājaye/
body.translated_text: If one plays with chess pieces or other [gaming pieces], in victory or defeat,

body.text: u4.36cd/.krīḍed akuśalāṅkair vā svapne dṛṣṭvā dhruvaṃ kaliḥ//
body.translated_text: or plays with inauspicious marks — seeing [this] in a dream, strife is certain.

body.text: u4.37ab/.āsane śayane yane vāstre sābharaṇe gṛhe/
body.translated_text: If a seat, a bed, a vehicle, garments, ornaments, or a house

body.text: u4.37cd/.naṣṭe bhraṣṭe viśīrṇe vā; āyāsam adhigacchati//
body.translated_text: is lost, fallen away, or disintegrated — one encounters distress.

body.text: u4.38ab/.surāmaireyapānāni śārkaram āsavaṃ madhu/
body.translated_text: Liquor, <s>maireya</s> wine, sugarcane drink, distilled spirits, and honey —

body.text: u4.38cd/.pivate puruṣaḥ svapne; āyāsam adhigacchati//
body.translated_text: if a man drinks [these] in a dream — he encounters distress.

body.text: u4.39ab/.prasanne +ambhasi ca^ādarśe chāyāṃ paśyati nātmanaḥ/
body.translated_text: If in clear water or in a mirror one does not see one's own reflection —

body.text: u4.39cd/.utpadyate dhruvaṃ tasya skandha^nyāso na saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: There will certainly arise for him a burden upon the shoulders, without doubt.

body.text: u4.40ab/.abhīkṣṇaṃ varṣate devo jalaṃ pāṃśum atha^api vā/
body.translated_text: If the god rains down water, or dust,

body.text: u4.40cd/.aṅgāraṃ vā^api varṣeta maraṇaṃ tatra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: or rains down charcoal — one should predict death there.

body.text: u4.41ab/.jana^ghātaṃ vijānīyāt tatra deśe mahā^bhayaṃ/
body.translated_text: One should recognize slaughter of people and great danger in that land.

body.text: u4.41cd/.rajju jālena vā svapne para^cakrād vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: A rope or a net in a dream should indicate [an attack by] a hostile army.

body.text: u4.42ab/.udakena samantād vai nagaraṃ parivāryate/
body.translated_text: If a city is surrounded on all sides by water,

body.text: u4.42cd/.jālenānyena vā svapne para^cakra^udgamo bhavet//
body.translated_text: or by a net or other [barrier] in a dream, there will be an invasion by a hostile army.

body.text: u4.43ab/.taila^kardama^lipta^aṅgo rakta^kaṇṭha^guṇo naraḥ/
body.translated_text: A man whose body is smeared with oil and mud, wearing a red garland around his neck,

body.text: u4.43cd/.gāyate hasate ca^eva prahāraṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: who sings and laughs — one should predict a beating for him.

body.text: u4.44ab/.yaṃ kṛṣṇa^vasanā nārī; ārdrā vā malinātha vā/
body.translated_text: If a woman wearing black garments, or one who is wet, dirty, or wretched,

body.text: u4.44cd/.pariṣvajet naraṃ svapne bandhanaṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: embraces a man in a dream — one should predict imprisonment for him.

body.text: u4.45ab/.kṛṣṇa^sarpo yadi svapne hy abhirohati yaṃ naraṃ/
body.translated_text: If a black serpent in a dream climbs upon a man,

body.text: u4.45cd/.gātrāṇi veṣṭayed vā^api bandhanaṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: or wraps around his limbs — one should predict imprisonment for him.

body.text: u4.46ab/.latābhiḥ sthāṇu^vṛndair vā yantrai vā parivāryate/(p.158)
body.translated_text: If a person in a dream is surrounded by creepers, clusters of stumps, or snares,

body.text: u4.46cd/.svapna^ante puruṣo yas tu bandhanaṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one should predict imprisonment for that person.

body.text: u4.47ab/.yantrāṇi yadi sarvāṇi vāgurābandhanāni vā/
body.translated_text: If all snares and trap-bindings

body.text: u4.47cd/.yasya chidyeran svapna^ante bandhanāt sa vimucyate//
body.translated_text: are cut at the end of a dream — he is released from bondage.

body.text: u4.48ab/.viṣamāṇi ca nimnāni parvatān nagarāṇi ca/
body.translated_text: Whoever sees at the end of a dream uneven terrain, hollows, mountains, and cities,

body.text: u4.48cd/.yas tu paśyati svapna^ante kṣipraṃ kleśād vimucyate//
body.translated_text: that person is quickly released from affliction.

body.text: u4.49ab/.pūtanā vā piśācā vā duścalā malinā^atha vā/
body.translated_text: If <s>Pūtanā</s> demons, <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), or restless and dirty [beings],

body.text: u4.49cd/.evaṃrūpāṇi rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā svapne dhruvaṃ kaliḥ//
body.translated_text: and forms of such kinds are seen in a dream — strife is certain.

body.text: u4.50ab/.susnātaṃ ca suveśaṃ ca sugandhaṃ śukla^vāsasaṃ/
body.translated_text: A person — whether man or woman — who is well-bathed, well-dressed, fragrant, and wearing white garments,

body.text: u4.50cd/.puruṣaṃ vā^atha nārīṃ vā dṛṣṭvā svapne mahat^sukhaṃ//
body.translated_text: if seen in a dream, [portends] great happiness.

body.text: u4.51ab/.tṛṇaṃ vṛkṣama atho kāṣṭhaṃ virūḍhaṃ yatra dṛśyate/
body.translated_text: Wherever grass, a tree, or wood is seen sprouting,

body.text: u4.51cd/.gṛhe vā yadi vā kṣetre kṣipraṃ dravya^kṣayo bhavet//
body.translated_text: whether in a house or in a field — there will quickly be loss of wealth.

body.text: u4.52ab/.bhadrāsane vā^śbhyāsīno śayane vā susaṃskṛte/
body.translated_text: Seated on a splendid seat or on a well-prepared bed,

body.text: u4.52cd/.naro vā labhate nārīṃ nārī vā labhate naraṃ//
body.translated_text: a man obtains a woman, or a woman obtains a man.

body.text: u4.53ab/.naraḥ śuklam atho vastraṃ śukla^gandha^anulepitaṃ/
body.translated_text: If a man sees at the end of a dream a white garment anointed with white unguent,

body.text: u4.53cd/.svapna^ante yas tu paśyeta strī^lābhaṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one should predict the acquisition of a wife for him.

body.text: u4.54ab/.yas tu hy annāni paśyeta bhūṣaṇaṃ nigaḍais tathā/
body.translated_text: Whoever sees food, ornaments, and also fetters —

body.text: u4.54cd/.naras tu labhate bhāryāṃ nārī vā labhate patiṃ//
body.translated_text: a man obtains a wife, or a woman obtains a husband.

body.text: u4.55ab/.mekhalāṃ karṇikāṃ mālāṃ strīṇām ābharaṇāni ca/
body.translated_text: A girdle, ear-ornament, garland, and women's jewelry —

body.text: u4.55cd/.labdhvā naro labhed bhāryāṃ nārī ca labhate patiṃ//
body.translated_text: a man who obtains these shall obtain a wife, and a woman obtains a husband.

body.text: u4.56ab/.kuñjaraṃ vṛṣabhaṃ nāgaṃ candra^ādityau satārakau/
body.translated_text: An elephant, a bull, a serpent, the moon and sun with stars —

body.text: u4.56cd/.abhivadeta yā nārī patiṃ sā labhate +acirāt//
body.translated_text: a woman who salutes [any of] these obtains a husband before long.

body.text: u4.57ab/.eṣām anyatamaḥ kuṣau praviśec ca yadi striyāḥ/
body.translated_text: If any one of these enters the womb of a woman,

body.text: u4.57cd/.sā kāle sarva^pūrṇa^aṅgaṃ śrīmat^putraṃ prasūyate//
body.translated_text: she will in due time give birth to a son with all perfect limbs, a glorious son.

body.text: u4.58ab/.phalāni ca samagrāṇi vanāni haritāni ca//
body.translated_text: Whole fruits and green forests —

body.text: u4.58cd/.svapna^ante labhate nārī śrīmat^putraṃ prasūyate//
body.translated_text: a woman who obtains [these] at the end of a dream gives birth to a glorious son.

body.text: u4.59ab/.utpalaṃ kumudaṃ padmaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ sakuḍmalaṃ/(p.159)
body.translated_text: A blue lotus, a white water-lily, a lotus, a white lotus with its bud —

body.text: u4.59cd/.labdhā nārī tu svapna^ante śrīmat^putraṃ prasūyate//
body.translated_text: a woman who obtains [any of these] at the end of a dream gives birth to a glorious son.

body.text: u4.60ab/.upāyana^sūtrayor antaḥ sajjaṃ tatra tu piṇḍakaṃ/
body.translated_text: Within the sacrificial cord and the investiture thread, a lump is prepared there —

body.text: u4.60cd/.svapne yā labhate nārī sā^api putraṃ prasūyate/
body.translated_text: a woman who obtains this in a dream will also give birth to a son.

body.text: u4.60ef/.yamaṃ tu bhājanaṃ ca^api yamaṃ tu sā prasūyate//
body.translated_text: If [she obtains] a twin vessel also — she will give birth to twins.

body.text: u4.61ab/.mlāyantīm atha grīṣmān te taruṇīm ātmikām api/
body.translated_text: Seeing in a dream a young woman wilting in summer heat, or [seeing] oneself

body.text: u4.61cd/.śuṣkāṃ dṛṣṭvā tathā svapne svapakṣa^maraṇaṃ bhavet//
body.translated_text: withered — there will be death among one's own side.

body.text: u4.62ab/.bāhavo yasya vardhante cakṣur aṅgulayo +api vā/
body.translated_text: If one's arms increase in number, or eyes, or fingers,

body.text: u4.62cd/.jñātayo tasya vardhante śatruṇāṃ maraṇaṃ bhavet//
body.translated_text: one's kinsmen will increase and enemies will die.

body.text: u4.63ab/.badhyante bāhavo yasya cakṣuś ca vyākulaṃ bhavet/
body.translated_text: If one's arms are bound, or the eye becomes disturbed,

body.text: u4.63cd/.bāhur vā prapated yasya sva^pakṣa^maranaṃ bhavet//
body.translated_text: or if one's arm falls off — there will be death among one's own side.

body.text: u4.64ab/.devo vā yadi vā preto nāryā vastraṃ phalāni vā/
body.translated_text: If a god or a departed spirit gives a woman garments or fruits

body.text: u4.64cd/.svapne prayacchate yasyāḥ putras tasyāḥ prajāyate//
body.translated_text: in a dream — a son is born to her.

body.text: u4.65ab/.apakṛṣṭo rudanyo vā nagno +atha malinaḥ kṛśaḥ/
body.translated_text: If [one appears] degraded, weeping, naked, dirty, and emaciated,

body.text: u4.65cd/.krodhaṃ va (lacuna) vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one should predict anger... [lacuna].

body.text: u4.66ab/.carma yantraṃ gaṇitaṃ vā kīlaṃ vā^atha kilāṭakaṃ/
body.translated_text: A hide, a device, a calculation, a peg, or curdled milk —

body.text: u4.66cd/.svapne labdhvā ca prāpnu[jānī]yād dhruvaṃ vastra^āgamo bhavet//
body.translated_text: if obtained in a dream, one should know that the acquisition of garments will certainly occur.

body.text: u4.67ab/.amānuṣo +atha rājā vā devaḥ preto +atha brāhmaṇaḥ/
body.translated_text: A non-human being, or a king, or a deity, a departed spirit, or a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> —

body.text: u4.67cd/.svapne yathā te jalpa^nti sa tathā^artho bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: whatever they speak in a dream, that meaning will come to pass accordingly.

body.text: u4.68ab/.(lacuna) pūrvavicintitaṃ/
body.translated_text: [lacuna] ...what was previously contemplated,

body.text: u4.68cd/.yac ca^anusmarate dṛṣṭvā yac ca^api bahu paśyati//
body.translated_text: and what one recalls after seeing, and what one sees repeatedly —

body.text: u4.69ab/.abhyutthito yathā mārge svapna^ante pratibudhyate/
body.translated_text: when one awakes as if risen upon a path at the end of a dream,

body.text: u4.69cd/.viṣamaṃ vā tathā^adhvānaṃ chidraṃ vā pratipadyate//
body.translated_text: or encounters a rough road or a gap —

body.text: u4.70ab/.agniṃ prajvalitaṃ taptaṃ śamitvā tu praśasyate/(p.160)
body.translated_text: seeing fire blazing and hot, then extinguished, is praised.

body.text: u4.70cd/.gṛhāṇāṃ karaṇaṃ śastaṃ bhedanaṃ na praśasyate//
body.translated_text: The building of houses is commended; their destruction is not praised.

body.text: u4.71ab/.nirmalaṃ gaganaṃ śastaṃ sameghaṃ na praśasyate//
body.translated_text: A clear sky is commended; one with clouds is not praised.

body.text: u4.71cd/.prasannam udakaṃ śastaṃ kaluṣaṃ na praśasyate/
body.translated_text: Clear water is commended; turbid [water] is not praised.

body.text: u4.72ab/.adhvānaṃ gamanaṃ śastaṃ na kvacit saṃnivartanaṃ/
body.translated_text: Journeying on a road is commended; turning back anywhere is not.

body.text: u4.72cd/.suvarṇa^darśanaṃ śastaṃ dhāraṇaṃ na praśasyate//
body.translated_text: Seeing gold is commended; holding [it] is not praised.

body.text: u4.73ab/.māṃsasya darśanaṃ sādhu bhakṣaṇaṃ na praśasyate/
body.translated_text: Seeing meat is good; eating [it] is not praised.

body.text: u4.73cd/.madyasya darśanaṃ śastaṃ pānaṃ tu na praśasyate//
body.translated_text: Seeing liquor is commended; drinking [it] is not praised.

body.text: u4.74ab/.pṛthivī haritā śastā vivarṇā na praśasyate/
body.translated_text: Green earth is commended; discolored [earth] is not praised.

body.text: u4.74cd/.yānasya^ārohaṇaṃ śastaṃ patanaṃ na praśasyate//
body.translated_text: Mounting a vehicle is commended; falling [from it] is not praised.

body.text: u4.75ab/.svapneṣu ruditaṃ śastaṃ hasitaṃ na praśasyate/
body.translated_text: Weeping in dreams is commended; laughing is not praised.

body.text: u4.75cd/.pracchanna^darśanaṃ śastaṃ nagnaṃ naiva praśasyate//
body.translated_text: Seeing [oneself] clothed is commended; naked is never praised.

body.text: u4.76ab/.mālyasya darśanaṃ śastaṃ dhāraṇaṃ na praśasyate/
body.translated_text: Seeing a garland is commended; wearing [it] is not praised.

body.text: u4.76cd/.gātraṃ vikartitaṃ sādhu prokṣitaṃ na praśasyate//
body.translated_text: Having the body cut is good; being sprinkled is not praised.

body.text: u4.77ab/.mṛduḥ praśasyate vāto na^ativātaḥ praśasyate/
body.translated_text: A gentle wind is praised; an excessive wind is not praised.

body.text: u4.77cd/.vyādhito malinaḥ śasto bhūṣito na praśasyate/
body.translated_text: Being sick and dirty is commended; being adorned is not praised.

body.text: u4.77ef/.parvata^ārohaṇaṃ śastaṃ na tu tatra^avatāraṇaṃ//
body.translated_text: Climbing a mountain is commended; but descending from it is not.

body.text: u4.78ab/.dhūmrā ghanā dundubhi^śaṅkha^śabdo vāto +abhra^vṛṣṭiś ca tathā samantāt/
body.translated_text: Smoky, dense [clouds], the sound of drums and conches, wind, and rain from clouds all around,

body.text: u4.78cd/.sarva^sthirāṇāṃ ca calaś ca yaḥ syād ye ca^antare doṣa^kṛtā vikārāḥ//
body.translated_text: and whatever among all stationary things moves, and whatever disturbances are caused by flaws in between —

body.text: u4.79ab/.pūrveṣu rūpeṣu yathāvad iṣṭā rāja^rṣayo deva^gaṇāś ca sarve/
body.translated_text: In the aforementioned forms, royal sages and all hosts of deities are duly auspicious,

body.text: u4.79cd/.yad brāhmaṇa^gātra^vikartanaṃ ca; etāni sarvāṇy api śobhanāni//
body.translated_text: as is the cutting of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s body — all these are favorable.

body.text: u4.80ab/.yat pūrva^rūpeṣu bhavet praśastaṃ duḥsvapnam etāni śamaṃ nayanti/
body.translated_text: What would be praiseworthy in the aforementioned forms — these [auspicious signs] bring bad dreams to peace.

body.text: u4.80cd/.gāvaḥ pradānaṃ dvija^pūjanaṃ ca duḥsvapnam etena parijitaṃ syāt//
body.translated_text: Giving cows, making gifts, and honoring <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — by these, a bad dream may be conquered.

body.text: u4.81ab/.devaṃ ca yaṃ bhaktigato manuṣyas taṃ tu parāṃś ca^arcayituṃ yateta/(p.161)
body.translated_text: One devoted to a deity should strive to worship that deity and others.

body.text: u4.81cd/.svapnaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā prathame pradoṣe saṃvatsara^ante +asya vipākam āhuḥ//
body.translated_text: A dream seen in the first watch of the night — they say its fruition is at the end of a year.

body.text: u4.82ab/.ṣaṇ^māsikaṃ yac ca bhaved dvitīye ṣaṭpākṣikaṃ yat tu bhavet tṛtīye/
body.translated_text: What occurs in the second [watch] takes six months; what occurs in the third takes six fortnights.

body.text: u4.82cd/.adhyardha^māse taram eva yat syāt phalec caturthe rajanī^prabhāte//
body.translated_text: What occurs [in the period of] a month and a half comes very quickly; [a dream] in the fourth [watch] bears fruit at daybreak.

body.text: u4.83ab/.dvijottame vā tila^pātra^dānaṃ śānti^kriyāḥ svastyayana^prayogāḥ/
body.translated_text: Giving a vessel of sesame to an excellent <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, performing pacificatory rites, and employing benedictory ceremonies,

body.text: u4.83cd/.pūjā gurūṇāṃ parimiṣṭam annaṃ duḥsvapnam etāni vināśayanti//
body.translated_text: worshipping teachers, and offering well-prepared food — these destroy bad dreams.

body.text: u4.84ab/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin svapna^adhyāya^nāma^adhyāyaḥ/ atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aparam api svapna^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called the 'Chapter on Dreams.' Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound another chapter on dreams as well. Listen to it. What then? Let the venerable <s>Triśaṅku</s> relate it.

body.text: u5 aparaḥ svapna^adhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Chapter 5: Another Chapter on Dreams

body.text: u5.1ab/.śubha^aśubhānāṃ svapnānāṃ yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtaṃ/
body.translated_text: The fruit that has been declared of auspicious and inauspicious dreams,

body.text: u5.1cd/.nimittaṃ yādṛśaṃ yasya śṛṇu vakṣyāmi tatvataḥ//
body.translated_text: and what kind of sign belongs to what — listen, I shall tell it truly.

body.text: u5.2ab/.jāgrato yadi vā trasto divā svapnāni paśyati/
body.translated_text: If while awake or frightened, one sees dreams during the day,

body.text: u5.2cd/.na tu bhayaṃ bhavet tasya jānīyād eva buddhimān//
body.translated_text: no fear shall come to that person — the wise should know this.

body.text: u5.3ab/.yasya tu yo bhavec chatrur yasya vidheyam icchati/
body.translated_text: Whoever has an enemy of any kind, or desires something to be accomplished,

body.text: u5.3cd/.svapne tu kalahaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣipraṃ prītir bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon seeing a quarrel in a dream, affection will quickly arise.

body.text: u5.4ab/.rajanyāṃ purime yāme yo +adrākṣīt sukha^duḥkhadaṃ/
body.translated_text: In the first watch of the night, whoever sees what brings happiness or suffering —

body.text: u5.4cd/.adhvānaṃ cira^kālena tathā hy eṣa nivartate//
body.translated_text: that journey takes a long time, for thus it comes to pass.

body.text: u5.5ab/.madhyame bhavate naiva kṣipraṃ bhavati paścime/
body.translated_text: In the middle [watch] it does not come about; in the last [watch] it comes quickly.

body.text: u5.5cd/.vaivārgaṃ tvaritaṃ dṛṣṭvā strī^lābham abhinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: Having seen a marriage ceremony quickly, one should predict the acquisition of a wife.

body.text: u5.6ab/.dṛṣṭvā jalacarān matsyān evaṃ jānīta buddhimān/
body.translated_text: Having seen aquatic fish, the wise should know thus:

body.text: u5.6cd/.yat kiñcid ārabhiṣyāmi kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: Whatever I shall undertake will come about very quickly.

body.text: u5.7ab/.campāyāṃ dhṛṣaṇaṃ haste dhṛṣet svapna^antareṣu vā/
body.translated_text: If one holds a churning-stick in hand at <s>Campā</s> or in the midst of dreams,

body.text: u5.7cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād varṇam evaṃ bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know: such a complexion will come about.

body.text: u5.8ab/.sarvāṇi khalu pānāni madhurāṇi sukhāni ca/
body.translated_text: All drinks that are sweet and pleasant —

body.text: u5.8cd/.yas tu pibati svapna^ante sa ca lābhaiḥ prayujyate//
body.translated_text: whoever drinks them at the end of a dream will be blessed with gains.

body.text: u5.9ab/.śva^śṛgālair bhakṣyate +atra svapne saṃparivāryate/(p.162)
body.translated_text: If in a dream one is eaten or surrounded by dogs and jackals,

body.text: u5.9cd/.pratibuddhas tu jānīyāt śatrur eva pramūrcchati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know: the enemy is indeed gathering strength.

body.text: u5.10ab/.upari kākā gṛdhrāś ca dhāvanty upari yānti ca/
body.translated_text: If crows and vultures run and fly overhead,

body.text: u5.10cd/.pratibaddho vijānīyāc chatrur mā vadhayiṣyati//
body.translated_text: the afflicted one should know: an enemy will slay me.

body.text: u5.11ab/.yasya para^gṛha^śvāno dvāre mūtraṃ prakurvate/
body.translated_text: If dogs from another's house urinate at one's door,

body.text: u5.11cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād bhāryā me jāram icchati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know: my wife desires a lover.

body.text: u5.12ab/.ekaś ca dharaṇau pādo dvitīyaḥ śirasi sthitaḥ/
body.translated_text: If one foot is on the ground and the second is placed on the head,

body.text: u5.12cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād rājya^lābho bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know: the acquisition of a kingdom will come about.

body.text: u5.13ab/.samudraṃ yadi paśyed vā pātum icchati tajjalaṃ/
body.translated_text: If one sees the ocean or desires to drink its water,

body.text: u5.13cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād rājya^lābho bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know: the acquisition of a kingdom will come about.

body.text: u5.14ab/.vṛkṣaṃ parvatam āruhya nāgaṃ ca turagaṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: Having climbed a tree, a mountain, an elephant, or a horse,

body.text: u5.14cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād rājya^lābho bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know: the acquisition of a kingdom will come about.

body.text: u5.15ab/.yas tu svapna^antare paśyet pitṝn yān iha ca^anyathā/
body.translated_text: Whoever sees in a dream the ancestors or other [deceased relatives] in a different [form],

body.text: u5.15cd/.tathā mātā pitā ca^eva tasya jīvanti te ciraṃ//
body.translated_text: and also mother and father — they will live long.

body.text: u5.16ab/.yas tu svapna^antare paśyet keśa^śmaśrū^vikartitaṃ/
body.translated_text: Whoever sees in a dream the cutting of hair and beard,

body.text: u5.16cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād artha^siddhir bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening should know: success in attaining wealth will come about.

body.text: u5.17ab/.ānanaṃ ca^udake dṛṣṭvā madhye +agnau ca vidhāvitaṃ/
body.translated_text: Having seen one's face in water and having run through fire,

body.text: u5.17cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād kula^vṛddhir bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know: increase of the family will come about.

body.text: u5.18ab/.dhāvanaṃ laṅghanaṃ ca^eva grāmāṇāṃ parivartanaṃ/
body.translated_text: Running, jumping, and moving between villages —

body.text: u5.18cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād ātmānaṃ śātitam iti//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know: 'I have been struck down.'

body.text: u5.19ab/.caurāṇām api sāmagrīṃ svapna^ante yas tu paśyati/
body.translated_text: Whoever at the end of a dream sees an assembly of thieves,

body.text: u5.19cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād ātmānaṃ śātitam iti//
body.translated_text: upon awakening should know: 'I have been struck down.'

body.text: u5.20ab/.kṛṣṇa^sarpa^gṛhītaṃ tu svapna^ante yas tu paśyati/
body.translated_text: Whoever at the end of a dream sees [oneself] seized by a black serpent,

body.text: u5.20cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyāc chatrupīḍā bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening should know: affliction from enemies will come about.

body.text: u5.21ab/.kaṭakān karṇikāś ca^eva haṃsa^keyūra^kuṇḍalaṃ/(p.163)
body.translated_text: Bracelets, ear-ornaments, a goose-[shaped ornament], armlets, and earrings —

body.text: u5.21cd/.yas tu ca^ābharaṇaṃ paśyed bandhu^vargo bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: And one who sees ornaments [in a dream] — a group of kinsmen will come.

body.text: u5.22ab/.kuḍye ca gṛha^prākāre dhāvatīha parasparaṃ/
body.translated_text: On a wall or a house-enclosure, [if a wagtail] runs back and forth,

body.text: u5.22cd/.nāvike dhana^saṃyoge; aṃgate kṣaṇayaṃ khajaḥ//
body.translated_text: [it portends] a union of wealth for a boatman; on a limb, an instant's [good or bad] fortune.

body.text: u5.23ab/.yas tu svapna^antare paśyec ca^ātmānam agnitāpitaṃ/
body.translated_text: One who sees in a dream himself scorched by fire,

body.text: u5.23cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyāj jvaraṃ kṣipraṃ bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening should know that fever will come swiftly.

body.text: u5.24ab/.rājānaṃ kupitaṃ dṛṣṭvā; ātmānaṃ malinīkṛtaṃ/
body.translated_text: Seeing an angry king, or oneself made dirty,

body.text: u5.24cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyāt kuṭumbaṃ tasya naśyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know that his household will perish.

body.text: u5.25ab/.kāṣṭhabhāraṃ tṛṇaṃ ca^eva bahu^bhāram abhīkṣṇaśaḥ/
body.translated_text: Seeing a load of wood and grass, and repeatedly heavy burdens,

body.text: u5.25cd/.ātmanaḥ śiraso dṛṣṭvā guru^vyādhir bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon one's own head — a serious illness will come.

body.text: u5.26ab/.yastu bānara^yuktena gacchate pur imāṃ diśaṃ/
body.translated_text: One who travels in this direction yoked with monkeys,

body.text: u5.26cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād rātrir eṣā hy apaścimā//
body.translated_text: upon awakening should know that this is his final night [i.e., death is near].

body.text: u5.27ab/.candra^sūryau ca saṃgṛhya pāṇinā parimārjati//
body.translated_text: Seizing the moon and the sun with his hand and wiping them,

body.text: u5.27cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād ārya^dharmāgamo hi saḥ//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know — this signifies the attainment of the noble <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: u5.28ab/.sumanāṃ vārṣikaṃ [kīṃ] ca^eva kumudāny utpalāni ca/
body.translated_text: Jasmine flowers, seasonal flowers, water-lilies, and blue lotuses —

body.text: u5.28cd/.yastu paśyati svapna^ante dakṣiṇīyasamāgamaḥ//
body.translated_text: one who sees these in a dream [should know] there will be an encounter with a worthy recipient [of offerings].

body.text: u5.29ab/.brāhmaṇaṃ śramaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣapaṇaṃ suranāyakaṃ/
body.translated_text: Seeing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, an ascetic, a <s>Kṣapaṇa</s> (Jain monk), or a chief of the gods,

body.text: u5.29cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād yakṣā me hy anukampakāḥ//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know — the <s>Yakṣas</s> are compassionate toward me.

body.text: u5.30ab/.rudhireṇa villiptasya snātvā caiva^ātma^lohitaiḥ/
body.translated_text: One smeared with blood, and bathing in one's own blood —

body.text: u5.30cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād aiśvaryādhisamāgamaḥ//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know — there will be an attainment of sovereignty.

body.text: u5.31ab/.mudgamāṣayavāṃś ca^eva dhānyaṃ jvalanadarśanaṃ/
body.translated_text: Mung beans, black beans, barley, grain, and the sight of fire —

body.text: u5.31cd/.yas tu svapna^antare paśyet subhikṣaṃ tatra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one who sees these in a dream should indicate prosperity there.

body.text: u5.32ab/.suvarṇaṃ ca tathā rūpyaṃ muktāhāraṃ tathāiva ca/
body.translated_text: Gold, silver, and pearl necklaces —

body.text: u5.32cd/.yas tu svapna^antare paśyan nidhiṃ tatra vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one who sees these in a dream should indicate a treasure there.

body.text: u5.33ab/.bandhanaṃ bahu dṛṣṭvā tu chedanaṃ kuṭṭanaṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: Seeing much binding, cutting, and beating,

body.text: u5.33cd/.pratibuddho vijānīyād artha^siddhir bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: upon awakening one should know — the accomplishment of one's purpose will come.

body.text: u5.34/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aparaḥ svapna^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the other chapter on dreams.

body.text: u5.35/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin māsa^parīkṣā^nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/ tac chūyatāṃ/ kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ//(E)35
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the chapter called 'Examination of Months.' Listen to that. Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text: u6 māsa^parīkṣā (p.164)
body.translated_text: Chapter 6: Examination of Months

body.text: u6.1/.yadi phālgune māse nirghoṣa upari bhavet manuṣyāṇāṃ maraṇaṃ codayati/ navacandro lohita^ābhāso dṛśyate/ sarva^sasya^anutpattiṃ codayati/ yadi devo garjati prathamaṃ mahā^sasyāni bhavanti/ paścimasasyaṃ na bhavet/ kalahaṃ codayati/
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Phālguna</s> thunder occurs overhead, it foretells the death of people. If the new moon appears with a reddish hue, it foretells the non-production of all crops. If the sky thunders first, there will be great crops, [but] the later crops will not come. It foretells conflict.

body.text: u6.2/.yadi caitre māse devo garjati tadā sarva^sasya^samutpattiṃ codayati/ yadi candra^graho bhavati mahān sannipāto bhavati/ śūnyāni grāma^kṣetrāṇi bhaviṣyanti/ yadi nīhāraṃ bhūmiṃ chādayati subhikṣaṃ codayati/
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Caitra</s> the sky thunders, then it foretells the production of all crops. If there is a lunar eclipse, a great epidemic occurs; villages and fields will become empty. If mist covers the earth, it foretells prosperity.

body.text: u6.3/.yadi vaiśākhe māse devo garjati subhikṣaṃ codayati/ yadi pūrve paścime śaṅkhe candra^graho bhavati kṣemaṃ codayati/ yadi ca^ulkā^pāto bhavati yasmiṃś ca janapade nipatati tatra deśe pradhāna^puruṣasya vināśo bhavati/ yadi bhūmi^cālo bhavati subhikṣaṃ codayati/
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s> the sky thunders, it foretells prosperity. If there is a lunar eclipse in the first or last quarter, it foretells peace. If a meteor falls, in whichever territory it falls, there will be the destruction of the chief man of that region. If there is an earthquake, it foretells prosperity.

body.text:
u6.4/.yadi jeyṣṭhe māse devo garjati rogaṃ codayati/ yadi sūrya^graho bhavati manuṣyāṇāṃ vināśaṃ codayati/ pūrve paścime vā śaṅkhe yadi candrasya sūryasya kiñcin nimittaṃ lakṣyate tadā kṣemaṃ codayati/ yadi madhya^rātrau candra^graho bhavati manuṣyāṇām anyonya^ghātaṃ codayati/ yadi ca^upari nirghoṣo bhavati adhyakṣa^puruṣasya pīḍāṃ codayati/ para^cakrāgamaṃ
ceti/
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> the sky thunders, it foretells disease. If there is a solar eclipse, it foretells the destruction of people. If in the first or last quarter any portent of the moon or sun is observed, then it foretells peace. If a lunar eclipse occurs at midnight, it foretells mutual slaughter among people. If there is thunder overhead, it foretells affliction of the chief man, and the approach of a foreign army.

body.text: u6.5/.āṣāḍhe māse yadi sūrya^graho rucira^ābhāso bhavati subhikṣaṃ codayati/ yadi candra^graho bhavati rogaṃ codayati/ yadi vidyun niścarati kalpāṇaṃ codayati/ yadi nīhāraṃ bhūmiṃ chādayati/
body.translated_text: In the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, if there is a solar eclipse with a bright hue, it foretells prosperity. If there is a lunar eclipse, it foretells disease. If lightning flashes forth, it foretells good fortune. If mist covers the earth [the prediction continues].

body.text:
u6.6/.śrāvaṇa^māse yadi sūrya^graho bhavati rājyaṃ parivartate/ yadi candra^graho bhavati prathame māse durbhikṣaṃ codayati/ śarabhaiḥ śobhana^śasyanāśo bhaviṣyati/ yadi (p.165) tārakā yatra deśe patanti tatra yuddhaṃ codayati/ yadi ca^atiśayaṃ bhūmi^cālo bhavati rogaṃ codayati/ yadi nirghoṣo bhavati tatra gṛhe yo gṛha^svāmī bhavati tasya vināśaṃ codayati/
atra ca māse +abhinavaṃ prāvaraṇaṃ na prāvaritavyaṃ/ āvāho vivāho na kartavyaḥ/ paribhūto bhavati/
body.translated_text: In the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, if there is a solar eclipse, the kingdom will change. If there is a lunar eclipse, the first month foretells famine. Locusts will cause destruction of fine crops. If stars fall in whichever region, it foretells war there. If there is an excessive earthquake, it foretells disease. If there is thunder, it foretells the destruction of the householder whose house [is struck]. In this month, new garments should not be worn. Marriage ceremonies should not be performed — one will be disgraced.

body.text: u6.7/.yady aśvayuje māse devo garjati manuṣyāṇāṃ vināśanaṃ codayati/ yadi sūrya^uparāgo bhavati mahā^puruṣa^vināśaṃ codayati/ yadi pūrve yāme candrasya nimittaṃ dṛśyate subhikṣaṃ codayati/ yadi bhūmi^cālo bhavati ākulaṃ codayati/ pararājā deśaṃ haniṣyati/ tatra ca manuṣyā anyonyaṃ vadhayiṣyanti^iti codayati/
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Aśvayuj</s> the sky thunders, it foretells the destruction of people. If there is a solar eclipse, it foretells the destruction of a great man. If a portent of the moon is seen in the first watch, it foretells prosperity. If there is an earthquake, it foretells turmoil — a foreign king will attack the country, and the people there will slay one another — so it foretells.

body.text: u6.8/.yadi kārttike māse devo varṣati mahad^ākulaṃ codayati/ prāṇakāś ca dhānyaṃ khādiṣyanti/ yady eka^antarūpaṃ vāto vāti tatra ca manuṣyā jalena vibhramiṣyanti/ mahā^ātmanaḥ puruṣasya vināśaṃ codayati/ yadi pūrve yāme utpāto bhavati mahā^varṣaṃ bhavati/ mahā^puruṣasya ca maraṇaṃ bhavati/ yadi nirghoṣo bhavati rogaṃ codayati/
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Kārttika</s> the sky rains, it foretells great turmoil. And insects will eat the grain. If a crosswise wind blows, the people there will be swept away by water. It foretells the destruction of a great-souled man. If a calamity occurs in the first watch, there will be great rain, and the death of a great man occurs. If there is thunder, it foretells disease.

body.text: u6.9/.yadi mārgaśīrṣe māsi devo garjati śasya^vināśo bhavati/ anyaś ca tatra svāmī bhavati/ yadi ca^ākāśe nirghoṣo bhavati yat pūrva^bhāgīyā manuṣyās teṣām āmayaṃ codayati/ yadi bhūmi^cālo bhavati yas tatra janapade pradhāna^puruṣo sa vadhān mokṣyati/
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> the sky thunders, there will be destruction of crops, and another ruler will come there. If there is thunder in the sky, it foretells sickness for the people of the eastern quarter. If there is an earthquake, the chief man of that territory will be released from execution.

body.text:
u6.10/.yadi pauṣe māse devo garjati prathame yāme janapada^nāśo bhavati/ dvitīye mahā^ātmanaḥ puruṣasya bandhanaṃ codayati/ prathame yāme ca yadi candra^uparāgo bhavati lohita^varṇaś ca dṛśyate udaka^āgamaṃ codayati/ mahā^ātmamanuṣyaṃ codayati/ yadi sūrya^graho bhavati śuddhapuruṣaṇāṃ raṇaṃ/ yadi tārakāḥ patantyo vidṛśyante tatra janapade ākulaṃ codayati/
yaty ākāśe nirghoṣo bhavati manuṣyāṇāṃ maraṇaṃ codayati/ yadi dvitīye nirghoṣo bhavati amnuṣyāś caurair hanyante/ yady atraiva māse tārakā utsṛṣṭā na candro dṛsyate sasyaṃ saṃcodayati/ yadi bhūmi^cālo bhavati mahāmanuṣyasya maraṇaṃ bhavati/ atraiva māse deva^sthānaṃ kartavyaṃ/ vṛkṣā ropayitavyāḥ/ sūlavāstu pratiṣṭhāpayitavyaṃ/
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s> the sky thunders in the first watch, there will be destruction of the territory. In the second [watch], it foretells imprisonment of a great-souled man. If a lunar eclipse occurs in the first watch and a reddish color is seen, it foretells the coming of water [floods], and portends for a great-souled person. If there is a solar eclipse, there will be strife among righteous men. If falling stars are seen, it foretells turmoil in that territory. If there is thunder in the sky, it foretells the death of people. If there is thunder a second time, people are slain by thieves. If in this very month the stars are released and the moon is not seen, it promotes crops. If there is an earthquake, a great man will die. In this very month, a temple should be built, trees should be planted, and a well-foundation should be established.

body.text: u6.11/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin māsa^parīkṣā^nāma^adhyāyaḥ/(p.166)
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Examination of Months.'

body.text: u6.12/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin khañjarīṭaka^jñānaṃ^nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagavān triśaṅkuḥ//mchecked
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the chapter called 'Knowledge of the Wagtail.' Listen to that. What then? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text: u7 khañjarīṭaka^jñānaṃ
body.translated_text: Chapter 7: Knowledge of the Wagtail (<s>Khañjarīṭaka-jñāna</s>)

body.text: u7.1ab/.khañjarīṭaka^śāstraṃ vai parvate gandha^mādane/
body.translated_text: The science of the wagtail [was taught] on mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>;

body.text: u7.1cd/.kucarair dṛśyate saumya^kucarasya mahā^bhayaṃ//
body.translated_text: it is seen by wanderers — for the wanderer there is great danger.

body.text: u7.2ab/.yāni tāni nimittāni darśayet khañjarīṭakaḥ/
body.translated_text: Whatever omens the wagtail shows,

body.text: u7.2cd/.pracarato bhaved dṛṣṭvā pañca^uttarapado dvijaḥ//
body.translated_text: seeing [the wagtail] moving about, the bird with five upper steps [portends] —

body.text: u7.3ab/.tatra sarve pravarteyur yatra yeṣu bhaved bhavet/
body.translated_text: There, all [predictions] would proceed wherever and for whomever they apply.

body.text: u7.3cd/.śādvale bahu^celatvaṃ gomayeṣu prabandhatā//
body.translated_text: On green grass — abundance of clothing; on cow-dung — bondage.

body.text: u7.4ab/.kañcāre bahu^celatvaṃ kardame bahu^bhakṣatā/
body.translated_text: On a bronze [vessel] — abundance of clothing; on mud — abundance of food.

body.text: u7.4cd/.kṛkare svalpa^celatvaṃ purīṣe tu dṛśaṃ śravaḥ//
body.translated_text: On a cock — scant clothing; on excrement — the sight of weeping.

body.text:
u7.5ab/.bhasme vivādam aphalaṃ vālukāyāṃ tu saṃbhramaḥ/
u7.5cd/.deva^dvāre tu sammānaṃ padmeṣu bahu^vittatā/
body.translated_text: On ashes — a fruitless quarrel; on sand — commotion. At a temple gate — honor; on lotuses — great wealth.

body.text: u7.5ef/.phale +artha^anuguṇaṃ proktaṃ puṣpeṣu priya^saṃamaḥ//
body.translated_text: On fruit — a result proportionate to one's purpose; on flowers — the meeting of a beloved one.

body.text: u7.6ab/.bhayaṃ prākāra^śṛṅgeṣu kaṭakeṣv aridarśanaṃ/
body.translated_text: On battlement peaks — danger; in army camps — the sight of an enemy.

body.text: u7.6cd/.pakṣayā carate vyādhiḥ patito mṛtyum ādiśet//
body.translated_text: Moving with one wing — illness; fallen [from a perch] — it portends death.

body.text: u7.7ab/.sugandha^taila^bhūtāni methune nidhi^darśanaṃ/
body.translated_text: On fragrant oil — [good] fortune; in mating — the sight of a treasure.

body.text: u7.7cd/.vṛkṣa^agre vidyate pānaṃ gṛheṣv atha ... lasaḥ//
body.translated_text: On the top of a tree — there will be a drink; in houses — [good] delight.

body.text: u7.8ab/.deśa^bhaṅgaḥ pravāde ca bandhanaṃ vigrahīkṛte/
body.translated_text: In disputation — ruin of the region; when confrontational — imprisonment.

body.text: u7.8cd/.amṛtaṃ ca sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā; odanaṃ na^atra saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: Seeing [the wagtail] standing still — [there will be] immortality (i.e., nectar/excellent food); cooked rice — there is no doubt.

body.text: u7.9ab/.gavāṃ pṛṣṭhe dhruvaṃ siddhir aśvapṛṣṭhe dhruvaṃ jayaḥ/
body.translated_text: On the back of a cow — certain success; on the back of a horse — certain victory.

body.text: u7.9cd/.avikānām ajānāṃ ca pṛṣṭhe sarvatra śasyate//
body.translated_text: On the back of sheep and goats — it is auspicious everywhere.

body.text: u7.10ab/.uṣṭrapṛṣṭhe ghruvaṃ kleśaḥ śvānapṛṣṭhe ca vidravaḥ/(p.167)
body.translated_text: On the back of a camel — certain hardship; on the back of a dog — flight.

body.text: u7.10cd/.pṛṣṭhe ca gardabhasya^iha maraṇaṃ na^atra saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: On the back of a donkey — death, there is no doubt.

body.text: u7.11ab/.kīle tu maraṇaṃ vidyād yūpa^agre ca na saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: On a stake, one should know [it means] death; on the top of a sacrificial post — no doubt.

body.text: u7.11cd/.kumbha^sthāne śmaśāne vā mṛto vā yatra dṛśyate//
body.translated_text: In a pot-stand or at a cremation ground, or wherever a dead [person] is seen —

body.text: u7.12ab/.antarīkṣe praḍīnaṃ tu; aphalaṃ tu vinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: [if the wagtail] has flown into the sky — one should indicate a fruitless [journey].

body.text: u7.12cd/.dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ vāsaṃ prahṛṣṭaṃ khañjarīṭakaṃ/
body.translated_text: Seeing the wagtail arrived joyfully at its resting place,

body.text: u7.12ef/.yathā^sthānaṃaṃ yathāvarṇaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one should indicate [the omen] to people according to the place and according to the color.

body.text: u7.13ab/.viṣame svalpa^kakṣeṣu prasaktaḥ kalaho bhavet/
body.translated_text: On uneven ground or in low thickets — a quarrel will arise.

body.text: u7.13cd/.sameṣu samake kṣetre samān varṇān vinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: On even, level ground — one should indicate even/equal fortunes.

body.text: u7.13ef/.nadyāṃ tu śaila^vāhinyāṃ pravāsam abhinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: On a mountain-fed river — one should indicate a journey abroad.

body.text: u7.14ab/.kāṣṭheṣu nātikā cintā tathā^asthiṣu dhana^kṣayaḥ/
body.translated_text: On wood — not much worry; on bones — loss of wealth.

body.text: u7.14cd/.yāṃ diśaṃ samudāgacchat pañca^uttarapadaḥ khagaḥ/
body.translated_text: In whichever direction the bird with five upper steps approaches,

body.text: u7.14ef/.tāṃ diśaṃ gamanaṃ vidyād yathā tasya tathā punaḥ//
body.translated_text: one should know [one's] journey [will be] in that direction — as [the bird] goes, so [shall one go].

body.text: u7.15ab/.kīṭā vā^atha pataṅgā vā bhayaṃ yad iha dṛśyate/
body.translated_text: Whether insects or moths — whatever fearful [thing] is seen there,

body.text: u7.15cd/.pracurā^api yadā jñeyā narasya^asthīni nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: when they are abundant, one should know it indicates [finding] human bones.

body.text: u7.16ab/.apāṃ samīpe gajamastake vā sūrya^udaye brāhmaṇa^sannidhau vā/
body.translated_text: Near water, or on the head of an elephant, or at sunrise, or near a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

body.text: u7.16cd/.mukhya prakāśe +apy ahimastake vā yaḥ paśyate khañjanakaṃ sa dhanyaḥ//
body.translated_text: at a prominent bright [place], or on the head of a snake — one who sees the wagtail [there] is blessed.

body.text: u7.17ab/.mātaṅga^rājo matimāṃs triśaṅkuḥ provāca tattvaṃ kañjanaṃ ca śāstraṃ/
body.translated_text: The elephant-king, the wise <s>Triśaṅku</s>, spoke the true science of the wagtail —

body.text: u7.17cd/.snigdhe sarukṣe viṣame same ca ādeśa yad doṣa^guṇair yathoktaiḥ/
body.translated_text: whether on smooth or rough, on uneven or even [ground], the indication with its faults and merits as stated;

body.text: u7.17ef/.tamādiśet tatra samīkṣya vidvān śubha^aśubhaṃ tatphalam ādiśec ca//
body.translated_text: a learned person should examine and indicate the auspicious and inauspicious result thereof.

body.text: u7.18/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin khañjarīṭaka^jñānaṃ nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Knowledge of the Wagtail.'

body.text: u7.19/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin śivā^rutaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃvyākhyāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagavān triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the chapter called 'The Cry of the Jackal.' Listen to that. What then? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text: u8.śivā^rutaṃ (p.168)
body.translated_text: Chapter 8: The Cry of the Jackal (<s>Śivā-ruta</s>)

body.text: u8.1/.namaḥ sarveṣām āryāṇāṃ/ namaḥ sarveṣāṃ satyavādināṃ/ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ tapasā vīryeṇa ca imaṃ śivā^rutaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhāmi/
body.translated_text: Salutations to all the noble ones. Salutations to all who speak the truth. By the austerity and power of all of them, I shall explain this chapter called 'The Cry of the Jackal.'

body.text:
u8.2/.ity āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/ śāṇḍilyam idam abravīt/ yādṛśaṃ ca yathā vāśet teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ vāśān śṛṇotha me/ pūrvasyāṃ diśi yadi vāśet śivā pūrva^mukhaṃ sthitvā trīn vārān vāśed vṛddhiṃ nivedayati/ caturo vārān yadi vāśed atra maṅgalaṃ nivedayati/ pañca vārān vāśed varṣāṃ nivedayati/ ṣaḍvārān vāśet para^cakra^bhayaṃ nivedayati/ saptavārān vāśed bandhanaṃ
nivedayati/ aṣṭa vārān vāśet priya^samāgamaṃ nivedayati/ abhīkṣṇaṃ vāśet para^cakra^bhayaṃ nivedayati/ ity āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>. He said this to <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>: 'Now hear from me the nature and manner of the cries of all of them. If the <s>śivā</s> (she-jackal) cries facing east while standing in the eastern direction — if she cries three times, she announces prosperity. If she cries four times, she announces good fortune. If she cries five times, she announces rain. If she cries six times, she announces danger from a foreign army. If she cries seven times, she announces imprisonment. If she cries eight times, she announces the meeting of a dear one. If she cries continuously, she announces danger from a foreign army.' Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
u8.3/.dakṣiṇāyāṃ dakṣiṇa^mukhaṃ sthitvā trivārān vāśed `atṛ atṛ' kurute maraṇaṃ tatra nivedayati/ caturo vārān vāśati dakṣiṇa^mukhaṃ sthitvā dakṣiṇāyā eva diśāyāḥ priya^samāgamaṃ nivedayati/ artha^lābhaṃ ca nivedayati/ pañca^vārān vāśed arthaṃ nivedayati/ ṣaḍvārān vāśet siddhiṃ nivedayati/ saptavārān vāśed vivāda^kalahaṃ nivedayati/ aṣṭavārān vāśed bhayaṃ
nivedayati/ abhīkṣṇaṃ vāśed ākulaṃ nivedayati/ ety āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: If, standing facing south in the southern direction, she cries three times making the sound 'atṛ atṛ,' she announces death there. If she cries four times standing facing south, she announces from the southern direction itself the meeting of a dear one, and also announces the gain of wealth. If she cries five times, she announces wealth. If she cries six times, she announces success. If she cries seven times, she announces dispute and quarrel. If she cries eight times, she announces danger. If she cries continuously, she announces confusion. Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text: u8.4/.paścimāyāṃ paścima^abhimukhaṃ sthitvā śivā trivārān vāśati maraṇaṃ nivedayati/ caturvārān vāśati bandhanaṃ nivedayati/ pañca^vārān vāśati varṣaṃ nivedayati/ ṣaḍvārān vāśati anna^pānaṃ nivedayati/ saptavārān vāśati maithunaṃ nivedayati/ aṣṭavārān vāśati artha^siddhiṃ nivedayati/ abhīkṣṇaṃ vāśati mahā^meghaṃ nivedayati/ ity āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: If, standing facing west in the western direction, the <s>śivā</s> cries three times, she announces death. If she cries four times, she announces imprisonment. If she cries five times, she announces rain. If she cries six times, she announces food and drink. If she cries seven times, she announces sexual union. If she cries eight times, she announces the attainment of wealth. If she cries continuously, she announces a great cloud. Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
u8.5/.uttarasyāṃ diśi uttara^abhimukhaṃ sthitvā trivārān vāśati puruṣasya prasthitasya nirarthakaṃ gamanaṃ bhavati/ caturvārān vāśati rāja^pratibhayaṃ nivedayati/ pañca^vārān śāśati vivādaṃ nivedayati/ ṣaḍvārān vāśati kuśalaṃ nivedayati/ saptavārān vāśati varṣāṃ nivedayati/ aṣṭavārān vāśati rāja^kula^daṇḍaṃ nivedayati/ (p.169)abhīkṣṇaṃ vāśati
yakṣa^rākṣasa^piśāca^kumbhāṇḍa^bhayaṃ nivedayati/ ity āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: If, standing facing north in the northern direction, she cries three times, the journey of a man who has set out will be fruitless. If she cries four times, she announces danger from the king. If she cries five times, she announces dispute. If she cries six times, she announces well-being. If she cries seven times, she announces rain. If she cries eight times, she announces punishment from the royal court. If she cries continuously, she announces danger from <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>. Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text: u8.6/.diśi vidiśi ca^eva giri^prāgbhāreṣu śikhareṣu nirdeśaṃ taṃ ca śṛṇotha me/ ``amūṃ tuṣyet pipāsārtā vidyāsiddhyai tathā^eva ca''/
body.translated_text: In the cardinal and intermediate directions, on mountain slopes and peaks — hear from me the instruction regarding these: 'May one who is thirsty be satisfied with this, and likewise for the accomplishment of knowledge.'

body.text: u8.7ab/.vidyālambhaṃ dhana^lambhaṃ nirdiśec ca vicakṣaṇaḥ/
body.translated_text: The discerning one should predict the attainment of knowledge and the gain of wealth

body.text: u8.7cd/.tīrtha^ākāra^vṛkṣa^mūle vāśatī yadi dṛśyate//
body.translated_text: if the <s>śivā</s> is seen crying at a sacred ford, at a temple, or at the root of a tree.

body.text:
u8.8/.sarvatra siddhiṃ nirdiśet/ na ca śṛgāla^bhaye śivā (vā) me sameti apramattena smṛtimatā pūjayitavyā śivā nityaṃ/ gandha^puṣpa^upahāreṇa śuśrūṣā kartavyā/ evam arcāyamānā (?) sarva^siddhiṃ nivedayiṣyati/ evaṃ ``sarve +arthās tasya sidhyanti triśaṅkor vacanaṃ yathā'' / krauṣṭriko yadi vāśati artha^lambhaṃ nivedayati/ adhomukho yadi vāśati nidhānaṃ tatra
nivedayati/ ūrdhva^mukho yadi vāśati varṣāṃ tatra nivedayati/ dvipathe yadi vāśati pūrva^mukhaṃ sthitvā artha^lābhaṃ nivedayati/ dakṣiṇa^abhimukho yadi vāśati yathā priya^samāgamanaṃ nivedayati/ dvipathe paścima^abhimukho yadi vāśati kalahaṃ vivādaṃ vigrahaṃ maraṇaṃ ca nivedayati/ kūpakaṇṭhake yadi vāśati arthaṃ tatra nivedayati/ śādvale yadi vāśati artha^siddhiṃ
nivedayati/ atimṛdukaṃ yadi vāśati vyādhikaṃ tatra nivedayati/ gītahāreṇa yadi vāśati artham anarthaṃ ca nivedayati/ tribhir vārair arthaṃ caturbhir anarthaṃ pañcabhiḥ priya^samāgamaṃ ṣaḍbhir bhojanaṃ saptabhir bhayam aṣṭabhir vigrahaṃ vivādaṃ ca/ ity āha bhagavāṃs trisaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: One should predict success everywhere. One should not approach the <s>śivā</s> in the presence of jackal-danger. One who is vigilant and mindful should always worship the <s>śivā</s>. Service should be performed with offerings of fragrance and flowers. When thus worshipped, she will announce complete success. Thus, 'all purposes are accomplished, as spoken by <s>Triśaṅku</s>.' If a male jackal cries, it announces the gain of wealth. If it cries facing downward, it announces a hidden treasure there. If it cries facing upward, it announces rain there. If it cries at a crossroads while standing facing east, it announces the gain of wealth. If it cries facing south, it announces the meeting of a dear one. If at a crossroads it cries facing west, it announces quarrel, dispute, strife, and death. If it cries at the edge of a well, it announces wealth there. If it cries on green grass, it announces the attainment of wealth. If it cries very softly, it announces sickness there. If it cries in a melodious manner, it announces both wealth and misfortune. Three times — wealth; four times — misfortune; five times — the meeting of a dear one; six times — food; seven times — danger; eight times — strife and dispute. Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
u8.9/.``atha bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi anupūrvaṃ śṛṇotha me'' / nānā^āhāre yadi vāśati mārge saṃsthitasya^api sarvaṃ vakṣyāmi taṃ śṛṇotha me/ saṃprasthitasya puruṣasya śivā vāśati vā yā pūrva^mukhaṃ sthitvā kṣipra^gamanam artha^siddhiṃ nivedayati/ atha dakṣiṇa^mukhaṃ vāśati yā artha^siddhiṃ nivedayati/ pañcān mukhaṃ vāśati bhayaṃ nivedayati/ atha^uttaramukhaṃ
vāśati artha^lābhaṃ nivedayati/ atha saṃprasthitasya vāśati yā purataḥ sthitvā upakleśaṃ nivedayati/ atha dakṣiṇe vāśati yadi dakṣiṇa^mukhā eva diśaḥ (p.170) karma^siddhiṃ ca nivedayati/ paścimato yadi vāśati caurato +ahitam asya duḥkha^daurmanasyaṃ nivedayati/ atha mārge vrajato dakṣiṇato vāśati mahā^vyādhim anarthaṃ caurā muṣanti tan nivedayati/ glānasya
yadi vāśati dakṣiṇa^mukhaṃ, ``na sa cikitsituṃ śakyo mṛtyu^dūtena coditaḥ''/ glānasya yadi vāśati uttara^mukhaṃ sthitvā ārogyadhana^lābhaṃ ca nivedayati/ atha mūrdhnā vāśati yā upakreśaṃ nivedayati/ atha paścimamukhaṃ sthitvā yā anyonyaṃ vyāharate yama^śāsanaṃ [nivedayati]/ nānā^āhāre yadi vāśati, yā saṃkṣobhaṃ nivedayati/ ity āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: 'Now I shall speak further; hear from me in due order.' If the <s>śivā</s> cries regarding various foods while one is standing on the road, I shall declare everything — hear from me. If, for a man who has set out, the <s>śivā</s> cries standing facing east, she announces swift travel and the attainment of wealth. If she cries facing south, she announces the attainment of wealth. If she cries facing west, she announces danger. If she cries facing north, she announces the gain of wealth. If, for one who has set out, she cries standing in front, she announces distress. If she cries on the right side facing the southern direction, she announces the success of the task. If she cries from the west, she announces from a thief — misfortune, sorrow, and dejection. If, while one is walking on the road, she cries from the right side, she announces a great illness, misfortune, and that thieves will rob — this she announces. If the <s>śivā</s> cries facing south for one who is sick, 'he cannot be cured — he is urged on by the messenger of death.' If the <s>śivā</s> cries standing facing north for one who is sick, she announces the gain of health and wealth. If she cries from above the head, she announces distress. If, standing facing west, she utters sounds to and fro, she announces the decree of <s>Yama</s> (death). If she cries regarding various foods, she announces agitation. Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
u8.10/.śivā purataḥ puruṣasya mārga^prayātasya yadi vāśati, yā agrataḥ kṣema^mārgaṃ vijñāpayati/ artha^siddhiṃ nivedayati/ mārgaṃ vrajato +asya śivā vāmena^āgatya gacchate dakṣiṇa^mukhaṃ kṣema^mārgaṃ vijānīyād artha^siddhiṃ ca nivedayati/ mārge vrajataḥ puruṣasya śivā vāmena^āgatya puratā vāśati yā tathā sabhayaṃ mārgaṃ vijñāpayati/ nivarteta vicakṣaṇaḥ/
dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ vāmaṃ gatvā vāmataḥ parivarteta ``na tan mārgeṇa gantavyaṃ triśaṅku^vacanaṃ yathā'' / purataḥ śivā gatvā agrataś ca niṣīdati sabhayaṃ mārgaṃ vijānīyāt/ nivarteta vicakṣaṇaḥ/ śivā purata āgatya vāmena parivartate bhayam etīha+a tena^api bhayaṃ jānīyād vicakṣaṇaḥ/ senāyām āvāhitāyāṃ śivā vaśati paścimaṃ nivartanaṃ nivedayati/ yadi gacchet parājayaḥ/
senā na gacchet/ senāyāṃ vraja^mānāyāṃ śivā āgacched agrataḥ senājayaṃ nivedayati/ para^cakra^parājayaṃ ca nivedayati/ sārthasya vrajamānasya śivā gacchaty agrataḥ kṣemamārgaṃ nivedayati/ artha^siddhiṃ tathā^eva ca/ puruṣasya pathi vrajato vāmato vāśati mārgaṃ nivedayati/ ``tanmārgeṇa [hi} gantavyaṃ triśaṅku^vacanaṃ yathā''/
body.translated_text: If the <s>śivā</s> cries in front of a man who has set out on a road, she announces a safe path ahead and the attainment of wealth. If, while he is walking on the road, the <s>śivā</s> comes from the left and goes facing south, one should know the path is safe, and she announces the attainment of wealth. If, while a man is walking on the road, the <s>śivā</s> comes from the left and cries in front of him, she thereby announces a dangerous path. The discerning one should turn back. Having gone to the southern direction on the left, one should turn around from the left: 'One should not go by that road, as spoken by <s>Triśaṅku</s>.' If the <s>śivā</s>, having gone ahead, sits down in front, one should know the path is dangerous; the discerning one should turn back. If the <s>śivā</s>, having come from the front, turns to the left, one should know there is danger here too; the discerning one should recognize the danger. When an army is assembled and the <s>śivā</s> cries, she announces retreat to the rear; if it advances, there will be defeat. The army should not advance. When an army is marching and the <s>śivā</s> comes from the front, she announces victory for the army and defeat of the enemy force. When a caravan is traveling and the <s>śivā</s> goes ahead, she announces a safe path and also the attainment of wealth. If she cries from the left side of a man walking on the road, she announces the [correct] path: 'One should go by that road, as spoken by <s>Triśaṅku</s>.'

body.text: u8.11/.``grāmasya nagarasya^api caityasthāne tathā^eva ca''/ pūrveṇa^uttareṇa^api śivā vāśati kṣemaṃ tatra nivedayati/ dakṣiṇe paścime yadi vāśati yā bhayaṃ tatra nivedayati/
body.translated_text: 'For a village, a city, or a sacred shrine as well' — if the <s>śivā</s> cries from the east or the north, she announces well-being there. If she cries from the south or the west, she announces danger there.

body.text: u8.12ab/.vāmato na praśaṃsanti tathā^eva vidiśāsu ca/
body.translated_text: They do not commend [cries] from the left, nor from the intermediate directions;

body.text: u8.12cd/.atidīrghātirūkṣā vā kāle māsāntike tathā/
body.translated_text: nor one that is excessively long or excessively harsh, nor at the turn of the month.

body.text: u8.13ab/.adharāṃ tu bhayaṃ vakṣye triśaṅku^vacanaṃ yathā//
body.translated_text: I shall declare the lower [cry] as [portending] danger, as spoken by <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text: u8.13cd/.madhu^svarāṃśivāṃ jñātvā kāle vele upasthite/(p.171)
body.translated_text: Having recognized a <s>śivā</s> with a honey-sweet voice, when the proper time and moment has arrived,

body.text: u8.14ab/.kṣemaṃ caiva^arthasiddhiś ca cintitavyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ//
body.translated_text: well-being and the attainment of wealth should be contemplated by the discerning.

body.text:
u8.15/.vyādhir upadravāś ca, ``sava tu praśamaṃ yānti triśaṅku^vacanaṃ yathā'' / śivā^rutasya^upacāro dig^vidiśāsu nimittā grahītavyāḥ/ yaḥ śivāyā divaso bhavati sa divaso jñātavyaḥ/ puṣpa^gandha^mālya^upahāras taddivase upapādayitavyaḥ/ nityaṃ devatā^gurukeṇa bhavitavyaṃ/ daivyāgurukeṇa bhavitavyaṃ/ devyai śuśrūṣā kartavyā/ sarvārthān sampādayiṣyati/ sarva^kāryāṇi
nivedayati/
body.translated_text: Diseases and calamities — 'all these go to pacification, as spoken by <s>Triśaṅku</s>.' The interpretation of the <s>śivā</s>'s cry — omens should be understood according to the cardinal and intermediate directions. The day that belongs to the <s>śivā</s> — that day should be known.
