On that day, offerings of flowers, fragrance, and garlands should be presented. One should always be devoted to the deity. One should be devoted to the divine teacher. Service should be performed to the goddess. She will accomplish all purposes and announce all matters.

body.text: u8.16/.yat kiñcit kāryam ārabhiṣyati tatsarvaṃ nivedayati/ devyai sarjjaraso guggulu ca dhūpayitavyaṃ/ puṣpa^baliś ca yathā^kāle dāpayitavyaḥ/ ity āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: Whatever task one is about to undertake, she announces all of it. The goddess should be fumigated with <s>sarjja</s>-resin and <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium). Flower-offerings should be given at the appropriate time. Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text: u8.17/.śivā^ruta^kathāne +atra vidyāṃ vakṣyāmi yathāsatyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
body.translated_text: In this account of the <s>śivā</s>'s cry, I shall declare the knowledge that will come true.

body.text: u8.18/.nama āraṇyāyai/ cīriṇyai svāhā sarjja^rasa^dhūpaṃ/
body.translated_text: Homage to the Forest Goddess! To the One clad in bark, <s>svāhā</s>! [Fumigate with] <s>sarjja</s>-resin incense.

body.text: u8.19/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin śivā^ruta^nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'The Cry of the <s>Śivā</s>.'

body.text: u8.20/.athātaḥ puṣkarasārin pāṇi^lekhā^nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'Palmistry.' Listen to it. Now what does the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> say?

body.text: u9 pāṇilekhā (p.172)
body.translated_text: Chapter 9: Palmistry

body.text: u9.1ab/.athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi narāṇāṃ kara^saṃsthitaṃ/
body.translated_text: Now I shall speak about what is situated on the hands of men —

body.text: u9.1cd/.lakṣaṇaṃ sukha^duḥkhānāṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā//
body.translated_text: the marks of happiness and sorrow, of life and death.

body.text: u9.2ab/.aṅguṣṭhamūlam āśritya ūrdhva^rekhā pravartate/
body.translated_text: Resting at the base of the thumb, an upward line extends;

body.text: u9.2cd/.tatra jātaṃ sukhataraṃ dvitīyā jñānam antare//
body.translated_text: there, what is born is most auspicious; the second concerns knowledge.

body.text: u9.3ab/.tṛtīyā sā lekhā yatra pradeśinyā pravartate/
body.translated_text: The third is that line which extends toward the index finger;

body.text: u9.3cd/.tatroktā hetavaḥ śāstre samāsena catur^vidhāḥ//
body.translated_text: the causes described in the treatise are, in brief, fourfold.

body.text: u9.4ab/.aparvasu ca parvāṇi nakṣtrāṇām upadravaḥ/
body.translated_text: When there are no joints, and joints [appear], there is calamity of the <s>nakṣatras</s>;

body.text: u9.4cd/.dviniḥsṛto viśuddha^ātmā jīved varṣaśataṃ hi saḥ//
body.translated_text: one who emerges with two [lines], being of purified soul, lives a hundred years.

body.text: u9.5ab/.triṃśat tribhāgena jāyīyād ardhe pañcāśad āyuṣaḥ/
body.translated_text: One should determine [the lifespan] by a third of thirty; at half, fifty years of life;

body.text: u9.5cd/.saptatis tryaṃśabhāgeṣu atyantānugate śataṃ//
body.translated_text: seventy at three-third portions; when completely extended, a hundred.

body.text: u9.6ab/.āuir;eljā pradṛśya^evaṃ vyantarāyaḥ prakāśyate/
body.translated_text: Having thus examined the lines, the obstacle is revealed;

body.text: u9.6cd/.nakṣatra^saṃjñayā jñeyā manujair arthaśas tathā//
body.translated_text: it should be known by humans according to the <s>nakṣatra</s> designation, in terms of meaning.

body.text: u9.7ab/.aṅguṣṭha^udaramārge tu yāvatyo yasya rājayaḥ/
body.translated_text: On the belly-path of the thumb, however many lines a person has,

body.text: u9.7cd/.tasyāpatyāni jānīyāt tāvanti na^atra saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: one should know that many are his offspring — there is no doubt in this.

body.text: u9.8ab/.dīrghāyuṣaṃ vijānīyād dīrghalekhā tu yā bhavet/
body.translated_text: One should know a person to be long-lived if the line is long;

body.text: u9.8cd/.hrasvāyuṣaṃ vijānīyād dhrasvalekhā tu yā bhavet//
body.translated_text: one should know a person to be short-lived if the line is short.

body.text: u9.9ab/.aṅguṣṭhamūle yavako rātrau janmābhinirdiśed/
body.translated_text: A barley-grain mark at the base of the thumb indicates birth at night;

body.text: u9.9cd/.divā tu janma nirdiṣṭam aṅguṣṭha^yavake dhravaṃ//
body.translated_text: a barley-grain mark on the thumb certainly indicates birth during the day.

body.text: u9.10ab/.avyakto yavako yatra tatra lagnaṃ vinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: Where the barley-grain mark is indistinct, one should declare the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant);

body.text: u9.10cd/.lagnaṃ puṃsaṃjñako jñeyo +aho^rātraṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: the <s>lagna</s> designated as masculine should be declared as indicating day and night.

body.text: u9.11ab/.divasaṃ janma nirdiśed rātrau strī^saṃjñako bhavet/(p.173)
body.translated_text: One should declare daytime birth; at night it is designated as feminine.

body.text: u9.11cd/.rātriḥ sandhyā samākhyātā bhāgair anyair na saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: Night and twilight are designated; by the other portions there is no doubt.

body.text: u9.11ef/.puṃsaṃjñād udayaṃ teṣām ahorātrāntikaṃ vadet//
body.translated_text: From the masculine designation, one should declare their rising throughout the day and night.

body.text: u9.12ab/.aṅguṣṭhamūle yavake śale saukhyaṃ vidhīyate/
body.translated_text: At the barley-grain mark at the base of the thumb, at the rice-grain, happiness is ordained;

body.text: u9.12cd/.aśvād bhadraṃ vijānīyād aṅguṣṭha^yavakeṣv iha//
body.translated_text: from the horse [-mark], one should know good fortune, at the barley-grain marks on the thumb.

body.text: u9.13ab/.yavamālā ca matsyaḥ syād aṅguṣṭha^yavako ratau/
body.translated_text: A barley-garland and a fish [mark] — the barley-grain on the thumb [indicates] love;

body.text: u9.13cd/.bālayauvanamadhyānte sukhaṃ tasyābhinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: in childhood, youth, and middle age and at the end, one should predict happiness for him.

body.text: u9.14ab/.yasya syād yavakaś ca^api ca^apo vā svastikas tathā/
body.translated_text: For one who has a barley-grain mark, or a water-mark, or a <s>svastika</s> likewise —

body.text: u9.14cd/.taleṣu yeṣu dṛśyante dhanyās te puruṣā hy amī//
body.translated_text: On whose palms these are seen — fortunate indeed are those men!

body.text: u9.15ab/.matsyo dhānyaṃ bhaved bhogāyāmiṣādau yave dhanaṃ/
body.translated_text: A fish [mark] indicates grain and enjoyment; from [marks beginning with] meat, barley indicates wealth;

body.text: u9.15cd/.bhoga^saubhāgyaṃ jānīyān mīnādau na^atra saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: one should know enjoyment and good fortune from [marks beginning with] the fish — there is no doubt in this.

body.text: u9.16ab/.patākābhir dhvajair vā^api śaktibhis tomarais tathā/
body.translated_text: By flags, banners, spears, and javelins likewise,

body.text: u9.16cd/.talasthāir aṅkuśaiś ca^api vijñeyaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ/
body.translated_text: and by goads situated on the palm, one should know [the person to be] a ruler of the earth;

body.text: u9.16ef/.rāja^vaṃśaprasūtaṃ ca rāja^mātraṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: and one born of a royal lineage should be designated as of royal rank.

body.text: u9.17ab/.prekṣyante śākhyā pañca haste catvāra eva ca/
body.translated_text: Five branches are seen on the hand, and four [more] —

body.text: u9.17cd/.kṣatriyo vā bhaved bhogī rājabhiś ca^api satkṛtaḥ//
body.translated_text: such a person will be a <s>Kṣatriya</s> or one of great enjoyment, honored even by kings.

body.text: u9.18ab/.vaiśyo +atha kṣatriyo vāgmī dhana^dhānyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s> or a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, eloquent — wealth and grain without doubt;

body.text: u9.18cd/.śūdro vipulabhāgī syāt parvaśīlo +atha naiṣṭhikaḥ//
body.translated_text: a <s>Śūdra</s> will be of abundant share, observing festivals, and devoted to religious vows.

body.text: u9.19ab/.satatam abhipūjyaḥ syāt sarveṣāṃ ca priyaṃvadaḥ/
body.translated_text: He will be constantly honored and will speak sweetly to all;

body.text: u9.19cd/.viśīlaḥ śīlakuñco vā bahubhir na bahus tathā//
body.translated_text: [if the lines are] lacking in character or curled in character, [he will] not [be honored] by many in the same way.

body.text: u9.20ab/.śyāmavarṇā +atha bhinnā vā sā lekhā duḥkhabhāginī/
body.translated_text: If the line is dark-colored or broken, it indicates one who shares in sorrow;

body.text: u9.20cd/.ktilekhā yasya dṛśyante yasya pūrṇāḥ karathitāḥ/
body.translated_text: [certain] lines are seen on whose [palm], whose [lines] are full and well-drawn —

body.text: u9.20ef/.mahā^bhogo mahā^vidvān jīved varṣaśataṃ ca saḥ//
body.translated_text: he will be of great enjoyment and great learning, and will live a hundred years.

body.text: u9.21ab/.ajapadaṃ rāja^chatraṃ śaṅkhacakra^puraskṛtaṃ/(p.174)
body.translated_text: A goat-hoof [mark], a royal umbrella, preceded by a conch and discus —

body.text: u9.21cd/.taleṣu yasya dṛśyante taṃ vidyāt pṛthivīpatiṃ//
body.translated_text: on whose palms these are seen, know him to be a ruler of the earth.

body.text: u9.22ab/.bhagas tu bhāgyāya dhvajaiḥ patākair hastyaśvamālāṅkuśataś ca rājā/
body.translated_text: A vulva [mark] is for fortune; by flags and banners, [marks of] elephants, horses, garlands, and goads — a king;

body.text: u9.22cd/.matsyo nu pānāya yavo dhanāya vedis tu yajñāya gavāṃ ca goṣṭhaḥ//
body.translated_text: a fish indeed is for drink; barley for wealth; a sacrificial altar for ritual sacrifice; and a cow-pen for cattle.

body.text: u9.23ab/.anāmikāparva atikramed yadi kaniṣṭhikā varṣaśataṃ sa jīvati/
body.translated_text: If the little finger extends beyond the joint of the ring finger, he lives a hundred years;

body.text: u9.23cd/.sametvaśītir varṣāṇi saptabhir yathā nadīnāṃ bharitāya nirdiśed//
body.translated_text: if it reaches, eighty years; with seven [marks], one should predict the filling of rivers.

body.text: u9.24ab/.śarīravarṇa^prabhavāṃ tu lekhāṃ savaiśikhāṃ varṇa^vihīnakāṃ ca/
body.translated_text: Having examined the line arising from the body's complexion, along with the topknot, and the one devoid of color,

body.text: u9.24cd/.samīkṣya nīcottamamadhyamānāṃ dāridyrmadhye caratāṃ vijānatāṃ//
body.translated_text: observing them as low, high, and middling — one should recognize those living in the midst of poverty.

body.text: u9.25ab/.abhyañjanodvartana satkarī[ṣaira]dhyakṣa cūrṇaiś ca vimṛjya pāṇiṃ/
body.translated_text: Having anointed [the hand] with unguent, rubbed it with cosmetic powders,

body.text: u9.25cd/.prakṣālya caika^antaraghṛṣṭa^lekhām ekāgracittas tu karaṃ parīkṣet//
body.translated_text: washed it, and scraped the lines in a secluded place — one should examine the hand with focused mind.

body.text: u9.26ab/.valayasamanarādhipaṃ bhajantyaḥ samanugatā maṇibandhane tu tisraḥ/
body.translated_text: Three [lines] encircling the wrist, following the bracelet-circle like a ruler —

body.text: u9.26cd/.dvir api ca [sa] bhava^antare mahā^ātmā vippuladhana^śriya āha vastra^lābhaḥ//
body.translated_text: and even twice [three] in another birth, being a great soul — one of abundant wealth and prosperity; and [it indicates] the gain of garments.

body.text: u9.27ab/.dadati satatam unnatas tu pāṇir bhavati cirāya tu dīrghapīnapāṇiḥ/
body.translated_text: One whose palm is constantly raised [upward] gives [generously]; and one with a long, fleshy palm endures for a long time;

body.text: u9.27cd/.paripatati śirāviruddhapāṇir dhanam adhigacchati māṃsa^gūḍhapāṇiḥ//
body.translated_text: one whose palm is covered with [visible] veins wastes [wealth]; one whose palm has flesh-covered [veins] obtains wealth.

body.text: u9.28ab/.sudṛśa[kara^talaiś ca]sādhavaste kuṭilakṛtair vinimīlitaiś ca dhūrtāḥ/
body.translated_text: Those with straight, beautiful palms are virtuous; those with crooked, closed [palms] are rogues;

body.text: u9.28cd/.bhavati rudhirasannibhaḥ suraktaś ciram iha piṇḍitapāṇirīśvaraḥ syāt//
body.translated_text: one whose [palm] resembles blood, deeply red — one who has a firm, compact palm will long be a master here.

body.text: u9.29ab/.dhṛtaruciramanāḥ śilāravindair jvalanakaṣāya suvarṇa^pāṇirā[ji]+/
body.translated_text: One who has a firm and beautiful mind, [with lines like] stone lotuses, with a fiery, astringent, golden-hued palm line —

body.text: u9.29cd/.bhavati bahu^dhano nigūḍhapāṇiś ciram iha jīvati pāna^bhoga^bhogī//
body.translated_text: will be very wealthy; one with a concealed palm lives long here, enjoying drink and enjoyment.

body.text: u9.30ab/.subhaga iha tathoṣṇadīrghapāṇir dhruvam iha śītalapāṇikas tu śaṇṭhaḥ/
body.translated_text: A handsome one here, likewise, has a warm, long palm; one with a cold palm is certainly a eunuch here;

body.text: u9.30cd/.iha hi bahu^dhano balena yuktaḥ sutanu susañcitapāṇirekhako yaḥ//
body.translated_text: one who here is very wealthy and endowed with strength is one whose palm lines are well-gathered.

body.text: u9.31ab/.dhanam upanayatīha pāṇilekhā kṛta^janitā jalavac ca yā sudīrghā/(p.175)
body.translated_text: A palm line brings wealth here — one that is born as if drawn by [flowing] water, which is very long;

body.text: u9.31cd/.jalavadanugatā suvarṇa^varṇā dhanam adhigacchati nimnaśonnatā yā//
body.translated_text: one that follows like water, golden in color — one who has a line that is low, high, and [alternating] obtains wealth.

body.text: u9.32ab/.dhanam upalabhate surakta^pāṇir vipulamatho ca nirantarāṅguliḥ syāt/
body.translated_text: One with a deeply red palm obtains wealth, and with a broad [palm], having fingers without gaps;

body.text: u9.32cd/.bali^puruṣam api tyajeddhi vittaṃ ditavivaśā ca viśīrṇavarṇa^lekhā//
body.translated_text: but wealth abandons even a powerful man — [if] the lines are scattered in color and helpless.

body.text: u9.33ab/.apagataghṛta^varṇa^pāṇilekho bhavati naro dhanavān balena yuktaḥ/
body.translated_text: One whose palm lines are free of the ghee-color becomes a man wealthy and endowed with strength;

body.text: u9.33cd/.asubhṛti sadṛśā bhavet tathā bhūṣaṇa^vṛta[rūpavatī śubhā]eka^bhāryā//
body.translated_text: such would also be his life-breath — beautiful, adorned, one wife who is auspicious.

body.text: u9.34ab/.bhavati bahu^dhano dhanair vihīnaḥ śrutam adhigamya viśālapāṇilekhaḥ/
body.translated_text: One becomes very wealthy [then] deprived of wealth, [then] having attained learning, with broad palm lines;

body.text: u9.34cd/.[su]ṛjubhir ahinīla^nirmalā[bhiḥ] kara^tala^rāji[bhirīśvaraḥ sa dhanya]ḥ//
body.translated_text: one with straight, serpent-blue, spotless palm-ridge lines is a lord — he is fortunate.

body.text: u9.35/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin kara^tala^lekhānām ādhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter on palm lines.

body.text: u9.36/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vāyasa^rutaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhāsyāmi tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/ namo +arhatāṃ/ teṣāṃ namaskṛtvā/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'The Cry of Crows.' Listen to it. Now what? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak. Homage to the Worthy Ones (<s>Arhats</s>)! Having paid obeisance to them:

body.text: u10 vāyasa^rutaṃ
body.translated_text: Chapter 10: The Cry of Crows

body.text: u10.1ab/.idaṃ śāstraṃ pravakṣyāmi vāyasānāṃ śubha^aśubhaṃ/
body.translated_text: I shall now declare this science of the auspicious and inauspicious [omens] of crows —

body.text: u10.1cd/.jayam parājayaṃ ca^eva lābha^alābhaṃ tathā^eva ca//
body.translated_text: victory and defeat, and likewise gain and loss,

body.text: u10.2ab/.sukhaduḥkhaṃ priyāpriyaṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: happiness and sorrow, the pleasant and unpleasant, life and death —

body.text: u10.2cd/.vāyasānāṃ vacaḥsiddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvidhi//
body.translated_text: I shall declare the truth of crows' utterances, according to proper method.

body.text: u10.3ab/.devāḥ pravadanti śreṣṭhā vāyasānāṃ namā namaḥ/
body.translated_text: The excellent gods proclaim: homage, homage to the crows!

body.text: u10.3cd/.āgatā mānuṣaṃ lokaṃ vāyasā bali^bhojanāḥ//
body.translated_text: The crows have come to the human world as eaters of offerings (<s>bali</s>).

body.text: u10.4ab/.prasthitasya yadā +adhvānam agrato vāyaso bhavet/
body.translated_text: When a crow appears in front of one who has set out on a journey,

body.text: u10.4cd/.vyāharan kṣīravṛkṣa^stho nirdiśed artha^siddhitāṃ//
body.translated_text: crying while perched on a milk-yielding tree, it indicates the success of one's purpose.

body.text: u10.5ab/.svareṇa parituṣṭena phalavṛkṣa^samāśritaḥ/
body.translated_text: With a contented voice, perched on a fruit-bearing tree,

body.text: u10.5cd/.punar āgamanaṃ ca^eva siddhar artha^niveditaṃ//
body.translated_text: it indicates a return journey and the accomplishment of the indicated purpose.

body.text: u10.6ab/.vivṛddhavṛkṣa^patrāṇi madhuraṃ ca^anuvāsati/(p.176)
body.translated_text: Perched on [a tree with] lush, growing leaves, it cries sweetly —

body.text: u10.6cd/.asūpaṃ nirdiśed bhojyaṃ guḍamiśraṃ tu gorasaṃ//
body.translated_text: it indicates food without soup, and milk-products mixed with <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery).

body.text: u10.7ab/.dṛṣṭas tu tuṇḍapādena ātmanaḥ parimārjati/
body.translated_text: If seen cleaning itself with beak and feet,

body.text: u10.7cd/.pāyasaṃ sarpiṣā miśraṃ tatra vidyānnasaṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: it indicates rice-porridge (<s>pāyasa</s>) mixed with ghee — there should be no doubt about food there.

body.text: u10.8ab/.rūkṣaṃ nirgharṣate tuṇḍaṃ śiraś ca parimārjati/
body.translated_text: If it rubs its rough beak and cleans its head,

body.text: u10.8cd/.saphalaṃ vṛkṣam āsthāya dhruvaṃ māṃsena bhojanaṃ//
body.translated_text: perched on a fruit-bearing tree, it certainly indicates a meal of meat.

body.text: u10.9ab/.locayati vyāharati phalavṛkṣa^samāśritaḥ/
body.translated_text: If it tears [at something] and cries while perched on a fruit-bearing tree,

body.text: u10.9cd/.vyādhena ca hataṃ māṃsaṃ nivedayati bhojanaṃ//
body.translated_text: it announces food — meat killed by a hunter.

body.text: u10.10ab/.ghoraṃ vyāharate kāryaṃ vāyaso vṛkṣa^māśritaḥ/
body.translated_text: If a crow, perched on a tree, cries in a terrible manner,

body.text: u10.10cd/.kalahaṃ saṃgrāma^bhayaṃ tatra vidyānna saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: it indicates quarrel, battle, and danger — there should be no doubt about this.

body.text: u10.11ab/.śuṣkavṛkṣe niṣīditvā kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vyāharet/
body.translated_text: If, perched on a dry tree, it cries in a weak and pitiful manner,

body.text: u10.11cd/.kalahaṃ sumahat kṛtvā na ca^arthaṃ tatra sidhyati//
body.translated_text: it indicates that after a great quarrel, no purpose will be accomplished there.

body.text: u10.12ab/.kṣīravṛkṣe niṣīditvā kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vyāharet/
body.translated_text: If, perched on a milk-yielding tree, it cries in a weak and pitiful manner,

body.text: u10.12cd/.krameṇa yugamātreṇa na ccārthaṃ tatra sidhyati//
body.translated_text: it indicates that gradually, within a short while, no purpose will be accomplished there.

body.text: u10.13ab/.śuṣkavṛkṣe niṣīditvā kāmukākaṃ pravāśati/
body.translated_text: If, perched on a dry tree, it cries out [calling] a lusty crow,

body.text: u10.13cd/.tatkṣaṇaṃ sannivedeti tatra caura^bhayaṃ bhavet//
body.translated_text: it announces at that very moment that there will be danger from thieves.

body.text: u10.14ab/.śuṣkavṛkṣe niṣīditvā kāmukākaṃ pravāśati/
body.translated_text: If, perched on a dry tree, it cries out [calling] a lusty crow

body.text: u10.14cd/.pṛṣṭhena darśayed bhāraṃ kṣudhāpīḍāṃ ca nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: and shows its back [as] a burden, it indicates affliction from hunger.

body.text: u10.15ab/.pakṣaṃ vidhūyamāno yaḥ paśyan pathasya vāśati/
body.translated_text: One which, shaking its wings, cries while watching the road —

body.text: u10.15cd/.na tatra gamanaṃ kuryāc cauraiḥ patham upadrutaṃ//
body.translated_text: one should not travel there, for the road is beset by thieves.

body.text: u10.16ab/.rajjuṃ vā phalakaṃ vā^api yadi karṣati vāyasaḥ/
body.translated_text: If a crow drags a rope or a plank,

body.text: u10.16cd/.na tatra gamanaṃ śreyaś cauraiḥ patham upadrutaṃ//
body.translated_text: it is not auspicious to travel there — the road is beset by thieves.

body.text: u10.17ab/.gomaye śuṣkakāṣṭhe vā yadi vāśati vāyasaḥ/
body.translated_text: If a crow cries while on cow-dung or dry wood,

body.text: u10.17cd/.kalahaḥ kuvaco vyādhir na ca^arthaṃ tatra sidhyati//
body.translated_text: it indicates quarrel, harsh words, and disease — no purpose will be accomplished there.

body.text: u10.18ab/.tṛṇaṃ vā yadi vā kāṣṭhaṃ darśayec ca yadā khagaḥ/(p.177)
body.translated_text: If the bird shows a [piece of] grass or a stick —

body.text: u10.18cd/.purataḥ śuṣkapāṇis tu tatra caura^bhayaṃ bhavet//
body.translated_text: and [one sees] a dried-handed [person] in front, there will be danger from thieves.

body.text: u10.19ab/.sārthopari niṣīditvā kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vyāharet/
body.translated_text: If, perched above a caravan, it cries in a weak and pitiful manner,

body.text: u10.19cd/.nipatet sārthamadhye +asmin caura^sainyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: and falls in the midst of this caravan — a thief-army [will come], without doubt.

body.text: u10.20ab/.yadā pradakṣiṇaṃ trastaṃ vāśanti vividhaṃ khagāḥ/
body.translated_text: When frightened birds cry in various [tones] circling to the right,

body.text: u10.20cd/.śuṣkavṛkṣe niṣīditvā tatra vidyān mahā^bhayaṃ//
body.translated_text: perched on a dry tree — one should know great danger [is near].

body.text: u10.21ab/.bhītas trastaḥ parītaś ca yas tu vyāharate khagaḥ/
body.translated_text: A bird that cries frightened, alarmed, and terrified,

body.text: u10.21cd/.paribādhan diśaḥ sarvās tatra bhayam upasthitaṃ//
body.translated_text: harassing [from] all directions — danger has arrived there.

body.text: u10.22ab/.gacchantaṃ samanugacchet puraḥ sthitvā tu vyāharet/
body.translated_text: If [a crow] follows one who is traveling, stands in front and cries —

body.text: u10.22cd/.na tatra gamanaṃ kkuryān mārgam atra praśātanaṃ//
body.translated_text: one should not travel there, for the road ahead is destroyed.

body.text: u10.23ab/.vāstumadhye pratisthāne kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vyāharet/
body.translated_text: If it cries weakly and pitifully in the middle of a dwelling or settlement,

body.text: u10.23cd/.vyādhiṃ tatra vijānīyād vāse vā gṛha^svāmināṃ//
body.translated_text: one should know there will be disease or [trouble] for the householders in that residence.

body.text: u10.24ab/.śakaṭasya yathā śabdaṃ viśrabdhaṃ vāśati vāyasaḥ/
body.translated_text: If a crow cries confidently, like the sound of a cart,

body.text: u10.24cd/.dūrād abhyāgataṃ jñātvā prasiddhiṃ ca^abhinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: knowing that someone has come from far away, it indicates fame.

body.text: u10.25ab/.gargare ghaṭake ca^eva sthālikapiṭhareṣu vā/
body.translated_text: If a crow sits and cries on a water-jar, a pot, a cooking vessel, or a pitcher,

body.text: u10.25cd/.niṣaṇṇo vāśate kākaḥ prasiddhaṃ gamanaṃ dhruvaṃ//
body.translated_text: it certainly indicates a well-known journey [is coming].

body.text: u10.26ab/.āsane śayane vā^api sthito vāśati vāyasaḥ/
body.translated_text: If a crow cries while standing on a seat or a bed,

body.text: u10.26cd/.prasiddhaṃ gamanaṃ brūyāt proṣitena samāgamaḥ//
body.translated_text: one should say a well-known journey [is coming] and a meeting with one who has been away.

body.text: u10.27ab/.brahma^sthāne niṣīditvā dhruvaṃ vāśati vāyasaḥ/
body.translated_text: If a crow cries steadily while perched in a place of worship (<s>brahma-sthāna</s>),

body.text: u10.27cd/.artha^lābhaṃ vijānīyād dhana^lābhaṃ ca ākaret//
body.translated_text: one should know the gain of purpose and predict the gain of wealth.

body.text: u10.28ab/.brahma^sthāne niṣīditvā kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vāśati/
body.translated_text: If it cries weakly and pitifully while perched in a place of worship,

body.text: u10.28cd/.sandhisthāne harec cauras tatra vai nāsti saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: a thief will steal from a junction point — there is indeed no doubt about this.

body.text: u10.29ab/.devatā^devatānāṃ ca devasya^upavanāni ca/
body.translated_text: At [shrines of] deities and of minor deities, and in the pleasure groves of the gods —

body.text: u10.29cd/.yasya vācaṃ vadet tasya^artha^lābhaṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: for whomever it utters a cry, one should predict the gain of purpose.

body.text: u10.30ab/.lākṣāharidrāmañjiṣṭhāharitālamanaḥśilāḥ/
body.translated_text: If it carries lac, turmeric, madder, orpiment, or realgar

body.text: u10.30cd/.yasyāharet purastasya svarṇa^lābhaṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: before someone, one should predict the gain of gold for that person.

body.text: u10.31ab/.pātraṃ ca pātrakaṃ ca^eva mṛttikāvarabhājanaṃ/(p.178)
body.translated_text: If [it carries] a vessel, a small cup, or an earthenware container

body.text: u10.31cd/.yasya yasya haret tasya dravya^lābhaṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: for someone, one should predict the gain of goods for that person.

body.text: u10.32ab/.saṅghībhūtvā yugamātraṃ śubhaṃ tiṣṭhati vāyasaḥ/
body.translated_text: If crows, gathered together, remain auspicious for a short while;

body.text: u10.32cd/.kāṣṭhaṃ vā vāyasā yatra gṛham āropayanti ca/
body.translated_text: or where crows carry wood [and] pile [it] upon a house,

body.text: u10.32ef/.nigadanty atra vijānīyād yācakāt tu mahā^bhayaṃ//
body.translated_text: and cry there — one should know great danger from supplicants.

body.text: u10.33ab/.nīlaṃ pītaṃ lohitaṃ ca pratisaṃharaṇāni ca/
body.translated_text: If crows seize blue, yellow, red, or reclaimed [objects],

body.text: u10.33cd/.nigṛhṇanti yatra kākā vyādhiṃ tatra vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: wherever they seize them, one should predict disease there.

body.text: u10.34ab/.grāmante bhayam ākhyāti kāko vā vāśati dhruvaṃ/
body.translated_text: At the edge of a village, a crow crying steadily announces danger;

body.text: u10.34cd/.pratyekato vā vāśanti vidyāt tatra mahā^bhayaṃ//
body.translated_text: or if they cry one by one, one should know great danger [is near].

body.text: u10.35ab/.vāyaso +asthi gṛhītvā vai pragacched anudakṣiṇaṃ/
body.translated_text: If a crow, having seized a bone, goes counter-clockwise,

body.text: u10.35cd/.niṣīdan saphale vṛkṣe sa vaden māṃsa^bhojanaṃ//
body.translated_text: and perches on a fruit-bearing tree, it announces a meal of meat.

body.text: u10.36ab/.yasya śīrṣe niṣīditvā karṇaṃ karṣati vāyasaḥ/
body.translated_text: If a crow, perched on someone's head, pulls the ear,

body.text: u10.36cd/.abhyantare sapta^rātrān maraṇaṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one should predict death for that person within seven nights.

body.text: u10.37ab/.karake ca^udake ca^eva snigdhadeśeṣu vāśati/
body.translated_text: If [a crow] cries at a water-pot or near water, or in moist places,

body.text: u10.37cd/.ūrdhva^mukhaṃ nirīkṣantu jagadvṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: looking upward — one should predict rainfall upon the world.

body.text: u10.38ab/.svareṇa parituṣṭena tīrthavṛkṣeṣu vāśati/
body.translated_text: If, with a contented voice, it cries at trees near a sacred ford,

body.text: u10.38cd/.ūrdhva^mukhaṃ tathā vakti vāta^vṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: and likewise speaks looking upward — one should predict wind and rain.

body.text: u10.39ab/.kāyaṃ kilakilāyantu snigdhadeśeṣu vāśati/
body.translated_text: If, making a shrill cry, it cries in moist places

body.text: u10.39cd/.vakṣo vidhnvanvāyasaḥ sadyo vṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: while beating its chest — the crow predicts immediate rain.

body.text: u10.40ab/.svareṇa parituṣṭena snigdhaṃ madhuraṃ vāśati/
body.translated_text: If, with a contented voice, it cries softly and sweetly,

body.text: u10.40cd/.sakṣara^sadravaṃ bhāgaṃ vāśati bhojanaṃ bhavet//
body.translated_text: [and indicates] a portion with flowing liquids — crying thus, there will be food.

body.text: u10.41ab/.prakāre toraṇa^agre vā yadi vāśati vāyasaḥ/
body.translated_text: If a crow cries on a rampart or at the top of a gateway,

body.text: u10.41cd/.abhīkṣṇaṃ gharṣate tuṇḍaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ tatra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: and rubs its beak frequently — one should predict battle there.

body.text: u10.42ab/.maṇḍalāni vāvartāni bahir vā nagarasya ca/
body.translated_text: Circles and whirlpools [of crows], and outside the city too —

body.text: u10.42cd/.vairaṃ ca vigrahaṃ ghoraṃ tatra ca^eva vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: and one should declare enmity and terrible conflict there as well. //

body.text: u10.43ab/.grāme vā nagare vā^api kurvate yatra maṇḍalaṃ/(p.179)
body.translated_text: In a village or in a city, where they form a circle,

body.text: u10.43cd/.ūrdhva^mukhaṃ vāśanto vai viṣaṇṇatvaṃ samutthitaṃ//
body.translated_text: crying with upturned face — dejection has arisen. //

body.text: u10.44ab/.pūrveṇa ca^eva grāmasya yadā sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: When a female crow nests to the east of a village,

body.text: u10.44cd/.alpodakenotplavanti vanāni nagarāṇi ca//
body.translated_text: with little water, villages and forests will be flooded. //

body.text: u10.45ab/.purastād dakṣiṇe pārśve yadi sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: In front, on the southern side, if a female crow nests,

body.text: u10.45cd/.varṣati prathame māse paścād devo na varṣati/
body.translated_text: it rains in the first month, but afterward the sky does not rain;

body.text: u10.45ef/.kṛṣṇa^dhānyāni vardhante māṣadhānyaṃ vinaśyati//
body.translated_text: dark grains flourish, but <s>māṣa</s> (black gram) perishes. //

body.text: u10.46ab/.dakṣiṇe vṛkṣa^śikahre yadā sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: On the southern treetop, when a female crow nests,

body.text: u10.46cd/.maṇḍūkakīṭakam akṣā cauraś ca bahulībhavet//
body.translated_text: frogs, insects, and dice-games will multiply, and thieves will become numerous. //

body.text: u10.47ab/.paścima^uttarapārśve tu yadā sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: On the western-northern side, when a female crow nests,

body.text: u10.47cd/.madhyamaṃ ca bhaved varṣaṃ madhya^śasyaṃ ca jāyate//
body.translated_text: there will be moderate rainfall, and moderate crops will be produced. //

body.text: u10.48ab/.paścima^uttarapārśve tu yadā sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: On the western-northern side, when a female crow nests,

body.text: u10.48cd/.aśanir nipatet tatra bhayaṃ ca mṛgapakṣīṇāṃ//
body.translated_text: lightning will strike there, and there will be danger for beasts and birds. //

body.text: u10.49ab/.uttare vṛkṣa^śikhare yadā sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: On the northern treetop, when a female crow nests,

body.text: u10.49cd/.pūrvam uptaṃ vijānīyāc chasyaṃ samupajāyate//
body.translated_text: one should know that what was sown earlier — that crop will grow. //

body.text: u10.50ab/.upari vṛkṣa^śikhare yadā sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: On top of the treetop, when a female crow nests,

body.text: u10.50cd/.alpa^udakaṃ vijānīyāt sthale bījāni ropayet//
body.translated_text: one should know there will be little water; one should plant seeds on high ground. //

body.text: u10.51ab/.yadā tu madhye vṛkṣasya nilayaṃ karoti vāyasī/
body.translated_text: When a female crow makes her nest in the middle of the tree,

body.text: u10.51cd/.madhyamaṃ varṣate varṣaṃ madhya^śasyaṃ prajāyate//
body.translated_text: there will be moderate rainfall, and moderate crops will be produced. //

body.text: u10.52ab/.skandha^mūle tu vṛkṣasya yadā sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: At the trunk-base of the tree, when a female crow nests,

body.text: u10.52cd/.anāvṛṣṭir bhaved ghorā durbhikṣaṃ tatra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: there will be terrible drought; one should predict famine there. //

body.text: u10.53ab/.caturaḥ pañca vā potān yadā sūyati vāyasī/
body.translated_text: When a female crow lays four or five chicks,

body.text: u10.53cd/.subhikṣaṃ ca bhavet tatra phalānām uditaṃ bhavet//
body.translated_text: there will be abundance of food there, and the harvest of fruits will be abundant. //

body.text: u10.54/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vāyasa^rutaṃ nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'The Cry of the Crow.'

body.text: u10.55/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dvāra^lakṣaṇaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'Characteristics of Doors.' Listen to it. Now what? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text: u11 dvāra^lakṣaṇaṃ (p.180)
body.translated_text: Chapter 11: Characteristics of Doors

body.text: u11.1ab/.māhendram atha divyaṃ ca māṅgalyaṃ pūrvataḥ smṛtaḥ/
body.translated_text: Of <s>Mahendra</s> (Indra), divine and auspicious — this is declared as the eastern [door];

body.text: u11.1cd/.dakṣiṇe tu diśo bhāge pūṣā ca pitryam eva ca//
body.translated_text: in the southern direction, <s>Pūṣan</s> and the ancestral [door]. //

body.text: u11.2ab/.sugrīvaṃ puṣpa^dantaṃ ca paścimenātra nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Puṣpadanta</s> should be assigned to the west;

body.text: u11.2cd/.bhallātakaṃ rāja^yakṣmaṃ vidyād uttarataḥ śubhaṃ//
body.translated_text: one should know <s>Bhallātaka</s> and <s>Rājayakṣma</s> as the auspicious [doors] of the north. //

body.text: u11.3ab/.janma^saṃpadvipatkṣetrakṣemapratyarisādhanaṃ/
body.translated_text: Birth, prosperity, calamity, field, security, means against enemies,

body.text: u11.3cd/.atha vai dhanmitraṃ ca paramaṃ maitram eva ca//
body.translated_text: and also wealth-friendship, and supreme amity. //

body.text: u11.4ab/.uvāca vidhivat prājño viśva^karmā mahā^matiḥ/
body.translated_text: The wise <s>Viśvakarman</s> (the divine architect) of great intellect spoke in due order:

body.text: u11.4cd/.vāstūnāṃ guṇadauṣau ca pravakṣyāmy anupūrvaśaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'I shall declare the merits and faults of building sites, in sequence.' //

body.text: u11.5ab/.samaṃ syāc caturasraṃ ca vistīrṇā ca^eva mṛttikā/
body.translated_text: Level and square, with broad soil,

body.text: u11.5cd/.kṣīravṛkṣākulaṃ dhanyaṃ brāhmaṇasya praśasyate//
body.translated_text: abounding in milk-bearing trees — this auspicious [site] is recommended for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. //

body.text: u11.6ab/.pūrvāyatanatayā vāstu rathacakrākṛti ca yat/
body.translated_text: A site elongated toward the east, and one shaped like a chariot wheel,

body.text: u11.6cd/.rakta^pāṃśur bhaved yatra rājñāṃ tat tu praśasyate//
body.translated_text: where the soil is red — that is recommended for kings. //

body.text: u11.7ab/.trikoṇaṃ kuśasaṃstīrṇam uttānaṃ madhuraṃ ca yat/
body.translated_text: Triangular, strewn with <s>kuśa</s> grass, elevated and sweet,

body.text: u11.7cd/.vyāyām ato jalaṃ ca^eva vāstu tasya dhanauṣadhī//
body.translated_text: with water from exercise — that site [brings] wealth and herbs. //

body.text: u11.8ab/.aṅgārākāra^saṃsthānaṃ gomukhaṃ śakaṭākṛti/
body.translated_text: A site shaped like charcoal, cow-faced, or cart-shaped —

body.text: u11.8cd/.anāvāsyaṃ ca tat proktaṃ yac ca putrakṣayāvahaṃ//
body.translated_text: that is declared uninhabitable, and it brings the loss of sons. //

body.text: u11.9ab/.yat tu kañjalakakṣais tat tyaktaṃ varṣodakena ca/(p.181)
body.translated_text: That which is [overgrown] with thorny bushes, and abandoned by rainwater,

body.text: u11.9cd/.apasavya^udakaṃ ca^eva dūrataḥ parivarjayet//
body.translated_text: and where water flows counter-clockwise — one should avoid it from afar. //

body.text: u11.10ab/.viprasya caturasraṃ tu kṣātriyaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ/
body.translated_text: For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a square [plot]; for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a circular one;

body.text: u11.10cd/.daśa dvādaśakaṃ vaiśye śūdrasya tatra lekhanaṃ//
body.translated_text: for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, one of ten or twelve [units]; for a <s>Śūdra</s>, a line-drawing there. //

body.text: u11.11ab/.vāstupūrva^uttare deśe gokulaṃ tatr kārayet/
body.translated_text: In the northeastern part of the building site, one should place the cowshed;

body.text: u11.11cd/.tathā^eva ca^agniśālāṃ tu pūrva^dakṣiṇato diśe//
body.translated_text: and likewise the fire-hall, in the southeastern direction. //

body.text: u11.12ab/.varṣavṛṣyāyudhāgārān dakṣīṇena niveśayet/
body.translated_text: Rain-shelters and armories should be established to the south;

body.text: u11.12cd/.paścima^uttarataś ca^atra vaṇigbhāṇḍaṃ niveśayet//
body.translated_text: and in the northwest, one should place the merchant's goods. //

body.text: u11.13ab/.uttarāyāṃ tu kartavyaṃ varcaḥ sthānām anuttaraṃ/
body.translated_text: In the north, the unsurpassed privy should be built;

body.text: u11.13cd/.aiśānyām eva sarvāṇi prāsādaś ca puromukhaḥ//
body.translated_text: in the northeast, all [sacred things], and the palace should face east. //

body.text: u11.14ab/.avidhiparivartena tatra vairaṃ vadho bhavet/
body.translated_text: By improper arrangement there, enmity and death will result;

body.text: u11.14cd/.racitasarva^dvārāṇām āyāmo dviguṇo mataḥ//
body.translated_text: for all doors when built, the height should be twice [the width], it is said. //

body.text: u11.15ab/.kuryāt surabhavanānāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ dvārakāṇy api/
body.translated_text: One may make doors of beautiful buildings as one wishes;

body.text: u11.15cd/.taddvāra^bāhuparyante striyo dṛṣṭā doṣāvahāḥ//
body.translated_text: but women seen at the door-posts are fault-bringing. //

body.text: u11.16ab/.vidviṣasya salokasya dvāre syān nu karagrahaḥ/
body.translated_text: At the door of an enemy's dwelling, there may be seizure;

body.text: u11.16cd/.mahendre pure vā rājyaṃ sūrye sūraprabhāvatā//
body.translated_text: in <s>Mahendra</s>'s [door], sovereignty over the city; in <s>Sūrya</s>'s (the Sun's), the radiance of a hero. //

body.text: u11.17ab/.satye mṛdur mṛge sūro +antarīkṣe dhana^kṣayaḥ/
body.translated_text: In <s>Satya</s>'s [door], gentleness; in <s>Mṛga</s>'s (the Deer's), heroism; in <s>Antarikṣa</s>'s (the Sky's), loss of wealth;

body.text: u11.17cd/.vāyavye tu bahu^vyādhir bhage bhāgyaviparyayaḥ//
body.translated_text: in <s>Vāyavya</s>'s (the Northwest's), many diseases; in <s>Bhaga</s>'s, reversal of fortune. //

body.text: u11.18ab/.puṣpe tu subhago nityaṃ vitathe +apy aśubho bhavet/
body.translated_text: In <s>Puṣpa</s>'s (the Flower's) [door], one is always fortunate; in <s>Vitatha</s>'s (the False one's), there will be inauspiciousness;

body.text: u11.18cd/.śoke bhūta^vikāraḥ syāt soṣe tasya viṣaṇṇatā//
body.translated_text: in <s>Śoka</s>'s (Grief's), there will be disturbance by spirits; in <s>Śoṣa</s>'s (Desiccation's), dejection for that person. //

body.text: u11.19ab/.ballātake gṛhe vāso rāja^yakṣme samāvṛtiḥ/(p.182)
body.translated_text: In <s>Bhallātaka</s>'s, dwelling in the house; in <s>Rājayakṣma</s>'s (Royal Consumption's), enclosure;

body.text: u11.19cd/.hrade reṇu pariśrāva āditye tu kalir dhruvaṃ//
body.translated_text: in <s>Hrada</s>'s (the Pool's), dust and filtering; in <s>Āditya</s>'s (the Sun's), strife is certain. //

body.text: u11.20ab/.nāga^rāje nāga^bhayaṃ mahaśceed dīrgham āyuṣaṃ/
body.translated_text: In <s>Nāgarāja</s>'s (the Serpent King's), danger from serpents; in <s>Mahaś</s>, long life;

body.text: u11.20cd/.bhaved asya ca yad dvāraṃ tatra^agni^bhayam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: and at whatever door [faces that direction], one should predict danger from fire there. //

body.text: u11.21ab/.kṣayaṃ vidyāt tasya tasya dhanasya ca kulasya ca/
body.translated_text: One should know the decline of that one's wealth and family;

body.text: u11.21cd/.yame mṛtyuṃ vijānīyāt kule śreṣṭha^uttamasya ca/
body.translated_text: in <s>Yama</s>'s (Death's), one should know death of the foremost and best in the family;

body.text: u11.21ef/.bhṛṅgirāje t matimān gandharve gandhamālyatā//
body.translated_text: in <s>Bhṛṅgirāja</s>'s, wisdom; in <s>Gandharva</s>'s, [love of] fragrance and garlands. //

body.text: u11.22ab/.bhṛṅge krodhaḥ kaliś ca^eva pitari bhoga^sampadaḥ/
body.translated_text: In <s>Bhṛṅga</s>'s (the Bee's), anger and strife; in <s>Pitṛ</s>'s (the Ancestors'), wealth of enjoyments;

body.text: u11.22cd/.dauvārike svalpa^dhanaṃ sugrīve rāja^pūjitaḥ//
body.translated_text: in <s>Dauvārika</s>'s (the Gatekeeper's), small wealth; in <s>Sugrīva</s>'s, honored by the king. //

body.text: u11.23ab/.puṣpa^dante dhanāvāptir varuṇe jalacitratā/
body.translated_text: In <s>Puṣpadanta</s>'s, gain of wealth; in <s>Varuṇa</s>'s, abundance of water;

body.text: u11.23cd/.asurare maraṇaṃ ghoraṃ roge tu bahu^doṣatā//
body.translated_text: in <s>Asura</s>'s, terrible death; in <s>Roga</s>'s (Disease's), many faults. //

body.text: u11.24ab/.balīṃś ca upahārāṃś ca pravakṣyāṃi yathāgṛhaṃ/
body.translated_text: I shall declare the offerings and oblations according to each house:

body.text: u11.24cd/.cicitrair vidiśair gandhaiḥ praipūjya baliṃ haret//
body.translated_text: having worshipped with various directional fragrances, one should make the offering. //

body.text: u11.25ab/.kalatre hetubījāni madhyame +arjitam eva tu/
body.translated_text: In the wife's [quarter], seed-grains; in the middle, what is earned;

body.text: u11.25cd/.mahendre mukta^puṣpāṇi pāvake ca payo dadhi//
body.translated_text: in <s>Mahendra</s>'s, released flowers; and in <s>Pāvaka</s>'s (Fire's), milk and curds. //

body.text: u11.26ab/.āditye parideyaṃ tu bhaktaṃ ca^eva priyaṅgavaḥ/
body.translated_text: In <s>Āditya</s>'s (the Sun's), one should offer cooked rice and <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet);

body.text: u11.26cd/.antarīkṣe jalaṃ divyaṃ puṣpāṇi jalajāni ca//
body.translated_text: in <s>Antarikṣa</s>'s (the Sky's), divine water and lotus-flowers. //

body.text: u11.27ab/.nandā pratipādā jñeyā ṣaṣṭhī trayodaśī jayā/
body.translated_text: <s>Nandā</s> is known as the first <s>tithi</s>, the sixth and thirteenth are <s>Jayā</s> (victorious);

body.text: u11.27cd/.tāsu tāsu dhruvaṃ kuryāt prājño hy evaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ//
body.translated_text: on those respective [days], the discerning and wise one should certainly perform [the rites]. //

body.text: u11.28/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dvāra^lakṣaṇaṃ nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Characteristics of Doors.'

body.text: u11.29/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dvādaśa^rāśikaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ / kathāyatu bhagavān triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'The Twelve Signs.' Listen to it. Now what? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text: u12 dvādaśa^rīśikaḥ (p.183)
body.translated_text: Chapter 12: The Twelve Signs

body.text: u12.1ab/.ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi cittavijñāna^kāṇḍakaṃ/
body.translated_text: Hereafter I shall declare the section on mind-divination (<s>cittavijñāna</s>),

body.text: u12.1cd/.yathā dṛṣṭāntenaivainaṃ narāṇāṃ samudāhṛtaṃ//
body.translated_text: as it has been taught to men by means of examples. //

body.text: u12.2ab/.tad ahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi cittavijñānam uttamaṃ/
body.translated_text: I shall now declare the supreme knowledge of the mind (<s>cittavijñāna</s>);

body.text: u12.2cd/.dvādaśaiva tu cittās te ye loke pracaranti vai//
body.translated_text: there are indeed twelve mental states that circulate in the world. //

body.text: u12.3ab/.tān ahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śṛṇu tattvena me tataḥ/
body.translated_text: I shall declare them; hear from me then the truth of them.

body.text: u12.3cd/.dvādaśa^eva tu kuryāc ca maṇḍalāni vicakṣaṇaḥ/.
body.translated_text: The discerning one should make twelve circles (<s>maṇḍalas</s>). //

body.text: u12.4ab/.prathamaṃ meṣo nāma syād dvitīyaṃ tu vṛṣaḥ smṛtaḥ/
body.translated_text: The first is called <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries); the second is known as <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus);

body.text: u12.4cd/.tṛtīyaṃ mithunaṃ nāma caturthaṃ ca^api karkaṭaḥ//
body.translated_text: the third is called <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini); and the fourth is <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer). //

body.text: u12.5ab/.pañcamaṃ ca^api siṃhas tu ṣaṣṭhaṃ kanyā iti smṛtaṃ/
body.translated_text: The fifth is <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo); the sixth is known as <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo);

body.text: u12.5cd/.tulā tu saptamaṃ jñeyā vṛścikas tu tahtāṣṭamaṃ//
body.translated_text: <s>Tulā</s> (Libra) should be known as the seventh; and <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio) is the eighth. //

body.text: u12.6ab/.dnavī tu navamaṃ jñeyā daśamaṃ makaraḥ smṛtaḥ/
body.translated_text: <s>Dhanu</s> (Sagittarius) should be known as the ninth; the tenth is known as <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn);

body.text: u12.6cd/.kumbhaś caikādaśaṃ jñeyo dvādaśaṃ mīna ucyate//
body.translated_text: <s>Kumbha</s> (Aquarius) should be known as the eleventh; the twelfth is called <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces). //

body.text: u12.7ab/.horā śarīraṃ jātasya dvitīye cintitaṃ dhanaṃ/
body.translated_text: The <s>horā</s> (hour/ascendant) [signifies] the body of the one born; in the second, wealth is contemplated;

body.text: u12.7cd/.tṛtīye bhrātura ca^eva caturthe svajanas tathā//
body.translated_text: in the third, a brother; and in the fourth, one's own family. //

body.text: u12.8ab/.cintyate pañcame putraḥ ṣaṣṭhe maṇḍale śatrutā/
body.translated_text: In the fifth, a son is contemplated; in the sixth circle, enmity;

body.text: u12.8cd/.saptame dārasaṃyogo hy aṣṭame naidhanaṃ smṛtaṃ//
body.translated_text: in the seventh, union with a spouse; and in the eighth, death is declared. //

body.text: u12.9ab/.navame cintyate dharmo daśame darmajaṃ phalaṃ/
body.translated_text: In the ninth, <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) is contemplated; in the tenth, the fruit born of <s>dharma</s>;

body.text: u12.9cd/.ekādaśe ca^artha^lābho dvādaśe vyartha^saṃbhavaḥ//
body.translated_text: in the eleventh, gain of wealth; in the twelfth, fruitless occurrence. //

body.text: u12.10ab/.ete dvādaśa^cittās tu yathā dṛṣṭā maharṣibhiḥ/
body.translated_text: These are the twelve mental states, as seen by the great sages;

body.text: u12.10cd/.sarva^bhūtātmabhūtāś ca yathājñeyāsta dehināṃ//
body.translated_text: being the self of all beings, they should be known accordingly by embodied beings. //

body.text: u12.11ab/.āgastya pṛcchate kaścit prathamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/(p.184)
body.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s> asks: if someone touches the first circle,

body.text: u12.11cd/.śiras tu spṛśate yaś ca śabdaś ca upalakṣyate//
body.translated_text: and touches the head, and a sound is perceived, //

body.text: u12.12ab/.vyādhitaṃ ca^eva hy ātmānam āgneyāś ca vinaṣṭayaḥ/
body.translated_text: and the person himself is afflicted, and there are fiery destructions —

body.text: u12.12cd/.yadi brūyāt tadā tasya ātmārthaṃ cintitaṃ bhavet//
body.translated_text: if he should speak thus, then that person's thought concerns himself. //

body.text: u12.13ab/.kāñcanaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ lauhaṃ ca^eva bhṛśaṃ havet/
body.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, and iron are intensely consumed;

body.text: u12.13cd/.sa ca sarva^gataś ca^eva agnir aśnāti niścitaṃ//
body.translated_text: and that all-pervading fire certainly devours [them]. //

body.text: u12.14ab/.etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātam āgneyaṃ tasya nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: Seeing such a portent, one should declare it as fiery;

body.text: u12.14cd/.yādṛśaś ca bhavec chabdas tādṛśaṃ tena cintitaṃ//
body.translated_text: and whatever kind of sound there is, such is the thought of that person. //

body.text: u12.15ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatya dvitīyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the second circle,

body.text: u12.15cd/.grīvāṃ vā parimārjayed galaṃ ca cibukaṃ punaḥ//
body.translated_text: or wipes the neck, and then the throat or chin, //

body.text: u12.16ab/.yadi śabdaś ca śrūyeta dṛṣṭā gāvas tathā^eva ca/
body.translated_text: if a sound is heard there, and likewise cows are seen,

body.text: u12.16cd/.īdṛśaṃ ca dṛXṭvotpātaṃ gośabdaṃ tatra nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: seeing such a portent, one should declare it as relating to cattle;

body.text: u12.16ef/.atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdas tādṛśaṃ tena cintitam//
body.translated_text: or else, whatever kind of sound there is, such is the thought of that person. //

body.text: u12.17ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatya tṛtīyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the third circle,

body.text: u12.17cd/.mārjayen mukhadeśaṃ tu strī^cittaṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: and wipes the face area — one should declare his thought concerns a woman. //

body.text: u12.18ab/.atha śabdo bhavet tatra śrūyantāṃ tādṛśās tu te/
body.translated_text: If a sound occurs there, let those of such [nature] be heard:

body.text: u12.18cd/.jātaṃ prajātam upajātaṃ tathā jāto bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: 'born, newly born, about to be born' — thus, something has been born or will be born. //

body.text: u12.19ab/.etādṛśaṃ dṛZṭvotpātaṃ garbhaṃ tasya vinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: Seeing such a portent, one should declare it concerns a pregnancy;

body.text: u12.19cd/.atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdas tādṛśaṃ tena cintitaṃ//
body.translated_text: or else, whatever kind of sound there is, such is the thought of that person. //

body.text: u12.20ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatya caturthaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the fourth circle,

body.text: u12.20cd/.kacchapaṃ spṛśate yas tu kalahaṃ tatra nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: and touches the armpit, one should declare quarrel there;

body.text: u12.20ef/.svajanaṃ vyavahāras tu sati kalahe na saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: the dispute is with one's own family, and when there is quarrel, there is no doubt. //

body.text: u12.21ab/.ākaṭṭā kaṭṭeti śabdā bhavanti ca nirantaraṃ/(p.185)
body.translated_text: Sounds like 'ākaṭṭā kaṭṭa' occur continuously;

body.text: u12.21cd/.etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā^utpātaṃ kalahaṃ tatra nridiśet//
body.translated_text: seeing such a portent, one should declare quarrel there. //

body.text: u12.22ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatya pañcamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the fifth circle,

body.text: u12.22cd/.hṛdayaṃ spṛśate yas tu apatyaṃ tatra cintitaṃ//
body.translated_text: and touches the heart — the thought there concerns offspring. //

body.text: u12.23ab/.pravāsakaś ca vijñeyaḥ paragrāma^gato mṛtaḥ/
body.translated_text: One should know he is an exile; gone to another village, he has died;

body.text: u12.23cd/.śastra^dravyaṃ ca yat tasya brāhmaṇānaṃ kule sthitaṃ//
body.translated_text: and whatever weapon-property of his is kept in the family of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. //

body.text: u12.24ab/.atha śabdo bhavet tatra yaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu maharṣibhiḥ/
body.translated_text: If a sound occurs there, having seen which the great sages [declare] —

body.text: u12.24cd/.putraputreti yacchabdo yad gataṃ gatam eva ca/
body.translated_text: sounds like 'son, son!' and 'what is gone is gone indeed' —

body.text: u12.24ef/.etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā^utpātaṃ maraṇaṃ tatra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: seeing such a portent, one should declare death there. //

body.text: u12.25ab/.puruṣaḥ kaś cid āgatya ṣaṣṭhaṃ tu maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the sixth circle,

body.text: u12.25cd/.spṛśate ca^api pārśvāni gātracintā tu cintitā//
body.translated_text: and touches the sides — the thought concerns bodily [affliction]. //

body.text: u12.26ab/.vigrahas tu mahā^ghoraḥ śatruś ca^api pravadhyate/
body.translated_text: The conflict is indeed very terrible, and the enemy is also slain.

body.text: u12.26cd/.atha vā tatra ye śabdāḥ śrotavyās te na saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: Or else, whatever sounds are heard there, they should be noted — there is no doubt.

body.text: u12.27ab/.ayaṃ tu prakṣaraś ca^eva hataś ca vihatas tathā/
body.translated_text: This one is indeed wounded, struck down, and destroyed likewise.

body.text: u12.27cd/.etādṛśaṃ dṛZṭvā^utpātam arivigraham ādiśet/
body.translated_text: Having seen such a portent, one should predict conflict with enemies;

body.text: u12.27ef/.atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdas tādṛśaṃ tena cintitaṃ//
body.translated_text: or else, whatever kind of sound is heard, such is what is being contemplated by that person.

body.text: u12.28ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatāy saptamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the seventh <s>maṇḍala</s> (zodiacal circle),

body.text: u12.28cd/.hastena mardayed hastaṃ tathā nāḍīṃ ca mardayed//
body.translated_text: he rubs one hand with the other, and likewise rubs the forearm.

body.text:
u12.29ab/.niveśacintā vijñeyā anyagrāma^gatā bhavet/
u12.29cd/.tatreme bhavanti śabdāḥ śrotavyā bhūmim icchatā//
body.translated_text: One should know that his thought concerns a dwelling; it may be about going to another village. These are the sounds to be heard by one desiring land:

body.text: u12.30ab/.sthitaṃ niviṣṭaṃ vartañ ca kṛtaṃ hasta^gataṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: "Settled," "established," "proceeding," "done," "in hand" — such terms;

body.text: u12.30cd/.etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā^utpātaṃ niveśaṃ tasya nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: having seen such a portent, one should declare that his thought concerns a dwelling.

body.text: u12.30ef/.yādṛśo vā śrutaḥ śabdas tādṛśaṃ tena cintitaṃ//
body.translated_text: Or whatever sound is heard, such is what is being contemplated by that person.

body.text: u12.31ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatya aṣṭamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/(p.186)
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the eighth <s>maṇḍala</s> (zodiacal circle),

body.text: u12.31cd/.udaraṃ ca^eva phicakaṃ dve ime parimārjayet//
body.translated_text: and rubs both the belly and the buttocks,

body.text: u12.32ab/.nidhanaṃ dṛśyate tasya maraṇaṃ ca^api dṛśyate/
body.translated_text: destruction is foreseen for him, and death too is foreseen.

body.text: u12.32cd/.yadi bhaved bhaven mṛtyur yaś ca^anya^priya^saṅgamaḥ//
body.translated_text: If it should come to pass, there will be death, or else separation from a loved one.

body.text: u12.33ab/.tatreme śabdāḥ śrotavyā mṛta eva bhaviṣyati/
body.translated_text: These are the sounds to be heard: he will certainly die.

body.text: u12.33cd/.etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā^utpātaṃ vyāpattiṃ tasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: Having seen such a portent, one should declare calamity for him.

body.text: u12.34ab/.puruṣaḥ kaś cid āgatya navamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the ninth <s>maṇḍala</s> (zodiacal circle),

body.text: u12.34cd/.ūruṃ ca spṛśate bhūyā dharma^cintā ca cintitā//
body.translated_text: and further touches the thigh, then his thought concerns <s>dharma</s> (religious duty).

body.text: u12.35ab/.tatra śabdāś ca śrotavyā bhavanti hi na saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: The sounds to be heard there are indeed these, without doubt:

body.text: u12.35cd/.yaja hi yājakaś ca^eva yajamānas tathāiva ca/
body.translated_text: "Sacrifice," "sacrificer," and "patron of the sacrifice" likewise —

body.text: u12.35ef/.śabdānevaṃvidhān śrūtvā yajña^cintāṃ tu nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: hearing such sounds, one should declare that his thought concerns a <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice).

body.text: u12.36ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatya daśamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the tenth <s>maṇḍala</s> (zodiacal circle),

body.text: u12.36cd/.karmacintā vicintyeti gṛha^karma na saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: his thought concerns work — household work, without doubt.

body.text: u12.37ab/.spṛśate jānunī ca^eva karma^cintāṃ tu nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: He touches both knees — one should declare that his thought concerns work.

body.text: u12.37cd/.tatra śabdā ahbvantīme śrotavyāś ca na saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: The sounds that arise there are to be heard, without doubt:

body.text: u12.38ab/.bhūmikarma ca kṣetraṃ ca kṣetrakarma tathāiva ca/
body.translated_text: "Field-work," "cultivated land," and "agricultural labor" likewise —

body.text: u12.38cd/.etādṛśaṃ dṛZṭvā^utpātaṃ karma^cintāṃ vinirdiset//
body.translated_text: having seen such a portent, one should declare that his thought concerns work.

body.text: u12.39ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatya ekādaśaṃ tu saṃspṛśet/
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the eleventh <s>maṇḍala</s> (zodiacal circle),

body.text: u12.39cd/.jaṅghe tu spṛśate bhūyo hy artha^lābhaṃ vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: and further touches the shins, one should declare gain of wealth.

body.text: u12.40ab/.tatreme śabdāḥ śrotavyā bhavantīha na saṃśayaḥ/
body.translated_text: These are the sounds to be heard — they arise here, without doubt:

body.text: u12.40cd/.paṇasuvarṇa^celāni dhānyaṃ samaṇikuṇḍalaṃ//
body.translated_text: "Coins," "gold," "garments," "grain," "earrings" —

body.text: u12.41ab/.etādṛśaṃ ravaṃ śrūtvā hiraṇyaṃ tasya nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: hearing such sounds, one should declare riches for him.

body.text: u12.41cd/.atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdas tādṛśaṃ phalam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: Or else, whatever kind of sound is heard, such is the result one should predict.

body.text: u12.42ab/.puruṣaḥ kaścid āgatya dvādaśaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/(p.187)
body.translated_text: If some person, having come, touches the twelfth <s>maṇḍala</s> (zodiacal circle),

body.text: u12.42cd/.pādau ca spṛśate pṛcchan cittaṃ vā^apy anarthikaṃ//
body.translated_text: and touches his feet while asking, or his mind is without purpose,

body.text: u12.43ab/.yas tu tac cintito hy artha^āśā āgantukā ca yā/
body.translated_text: whatever purpose he has thought of, his expectation is that of a newcomer.

body.text: u12.43cd/.atha vā śabdāḥ śrotavyā nimitta^jñāna^pāragaiḥ//
body.translated_text: Or else, sounds are to be heard by those who have mastered the science of omens:

body.text: u12.44ab/.nirāśaś ca^eva ghoṣaś ca nirāśaṃ tasya nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: "Hopeless" and such utterances — one should declare hopelessness for him.

body.text: u12.44cd/.atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdas tādṛśaṃ tena cintitaṃ//
body.translated_text: Or whatever kind of sound is heard, such is what is being contemplated by that person.

body.text: u12.45/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dvādaśa^rāśiko nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called "The Twelve Zodiacal Signs."

body.text: u12.46/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin kanyā^lakṣaṇaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ / atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagvāṃs triśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called "Characteristics of Maidens." Listen to it. What then? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text:
u13 kanyā^lakṣaṇaṃ
u13.1ab/.tatvaṃ vijñāyate yena yena śubham upasthitaṃ/
body.translated_text: Chapter 13: Characteristics of Maidens. That by which the truth is known, by which the auspicious is recognized,

body.text: u13.1cd/.ninditaṃ ca praśastaṃ ca strīṇāṃ vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇaṃ//
body.translated_text: I shall describe the characteristics of women, both the blameworthy and the praiseworthy.

body.text: u13.2ab/.pitaraṃ mātaram ca^eva mātulaṃ bhrātaraṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: One should examine the father, the mother, the maternal uncle, and the brother,

body.text: u13.2cd/.vimbād vimbaṃ parīkṣeta triśaṅku^vacanaṃ yathā//
body.translated_text: comparing one reflection with another, according to the words of <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text: u13.3ab/.muhūrte tithi^sampanne nakṣatre ca^api pūjite/
body.translated_text: At an auspicious <s>muhūrta</s> (moment), on a suitable <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), and under a favorable <s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation),

body.text: u13.3cd/.tad vijñaiḥ saha saṅgamya kanyāṃ paśyeta śāstra^vit//
body.translated_text: having assembled with wise persons, one learned in the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) should examine the maiden.

body.text: u13.4ab/.hastau pādau nirīkṣeta nakhāni hy aṅgulīs tathā/
body.translated_text: One should inspect the hands and feet, the nails and fingers,

body.text: u13.4cd/.pāṇilekhāś ca jañghae ca kaṭinābhyūrum eva ca//
body.translated_text: the lines on the palms, the shins, the hips, the navel, and the thighs.

body.text: u13.5ab/.oṣṭhau jihvāṃ ca dantāṃś ca kapolau nāsikāṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: The lips, the tongue, the teeth, the cheeks, and the nose,

body.text: u13.5cd/.akṣibhravau lalāṭaṃ ca karṇau keśāṃs tathā^eva ca//
body.translated_text: the eyes, the eyebrows, the forehead, the ears, and the hair likewise.

body.text: u13.6ab/.romarājīṃ savaraṃ varṇaṃ mantritaṃ gatim eva ca/(p.188)
body.translated_text: The line of body hair, the complexion, the color, the speech, and the gait —

body.text: u13.6cd/.matiṃ sattvaṃ samīkṣeta kanyānāṃ śāstra^kovidaḥ/
body.translated_text: one skilled in the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) should examine the intellect and character of maidens.

body.text: u13.6ef/.tatra pūrvaṃ parīkṣeta svayam eva vicakṣaṇaḥ//
body.translated_text: There, a discerning person should first examine these by himself.

body.text: u13.7ab/.kaṃsasvarā meghavarṇā nārī madhura^locanā/
body.translated_text: A woman whose voice is like bronze, whose complexion is like a cloud, and whose eyes are sweet,

body.text: u13.7cd/.aṣṭau putrān prasūyeta dāsīdāsaiḥ samāvṛtā//
body.translated_text: she will bear eight sons and be surrounded by male and female servants.

body.text: u13.8ab/.avyāvartāś catvāro yasyāḥ sarve ca^eva pradakṣiṇāḥ/
body.translated_text: A woman whose four hair-whorls all turn to the right,

body.text: u13.8cd/.samagātravibhaktāṅgī putrānaṣṭau prasūyate//
body.translated_text: with well-proportioned body and symmetrical limbs, bears eight sons.

body.text: u13.9ab/.maṇḍūkakukṣir yā nārī saiśvaryam adhigacchati/
body.translated_text: A woman with a belly like a frog's attains sovereignty;

body.text: u13.9cd/.dhanyān sā janayet putrāṃs teṣāṃ prītiṃ ca bhuñjate//
body.translated_text: she begets fortunate sons and enjoys their affection.

body.text: u13.10ab/.yasyāḥ pāṇitale vyaktaḥ kacchapaḥ svastiko dhavajaḥ/
body.translated_text: A woman on whose palms are clearly visible a tortoise, a <s>svastika</s>, a banner,

body.text: u13.10cd/.aṅkuśaṃ kuṇḍalaṃ mālā dṛśyante supratiṣṭhitāḥ/
body.translated_text: a goad, an earring, and a garland, well-established —

body.text: u13.10ef/.ekaṃ sā janayet putraṃ taṃ ca rājānam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: she will bear one son, and one should predict that he will be a king.

body.text: u13.11ab/.yasyāḥ pāṇau prakṛśyeta koṣṭha^āgāraṃ satoraṇaṃ/
body.translated_text: A woman on whose palm can be discerned a storehouse with a gateway,

body.text: u13.11cd/.api dāsakule jātā rāja^patnī bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: even if born in a family of servants, she will become a king's wife.

body.text: u13.12ab/.dvātriṃśad daśanā yasyāḥ sarve gokṣīrapāṇḍarāḥ/
body.translated_text: A woman who has thirty-two teeth, all white as cow's milk,

body.text: u13.12cd/.samaśikhari snigdhābhā rājānaṃ sā prasūyate//
body.translated_text: even, peaked, and lustrous — she gives birth to a king.

body.text: u13.13ab/.snigdhā kāraṇḍavaprekṣā hariṇākṣī tanutvacā/
body.translated_text: A woman with a smooth complexion, with the gaze of a <s>kāraṇḍava</s> (duck), with eyes like a doe's, with delicate skin,

body.text: u13.13cd/.rakta^uṣṭhajihvā sumukhī rājānam upatiṣṭhati//
body.translated_text: with red lips and tongue, with a beautiful face — she attends upon a king.

body.text: u13.14ab/.sūkṣmā ca tuṅganāsā ca muktam āraktimodarī/
body.translated_text: A woman with a fine, prominent nose, free, with a slightly red abdomen,

body.text: u13.14cd/.subhrūḥ suvarakeśāntā sā tu kanyā bahu^prajā//
body.translated_text: with beautiful eyebrows, with lovely hair-tips — such a maiden is very fertile.

body.text: u13.15ab/.aṅgulyaḥ saṃhitāḥ kāntā nakhāḥ kamalasannibhāḥ/
body.translated_text: Fingers that are compact and beautiful, nails resembling lotuses,

body.text: u13.15cd/.suṛjurakta^caraṇā sā kanyā sukha^medhate//
body.translated_text: with straight, red feet — such a maiden prospers in happiness.

body.text: u13.16ab/.yasyāvartau samau snighdau ubhau pārśvau susaṃsthitau/
body.translated_text: A woman whose two hair-whorls are even and smooth, both sides well-positioned,

body.text: u13.16cd/......................rāja^patnī tu sā bhavet//
body.translated_text: [lacuna] ... she shall become a king's wife.

body.text: u13.17ab/.pradakṣiṇaṃ prakrameta prekṣate ca pradakṣiṇaṃ/(p.189)
body.translated_text: She who walks to the right and looks to the right,

body.text: u13.17cd/.pradakṣiṇa^samācārāṃ kanyāṃ bhāryā^artham āvahet//
body.translated_text: a maiden of rightward conduct — one should take her as a wife.

body.text: u13.18ab/.ūrū jaṅghe ca pārśve ca tathā vikramaḥ saṃsthitaḥ/
body.translated_text: With thighs, shins, and sides well-proportioned, and with a steady gait,

body.text: u13.18cd/.rakta^ante vipule netre sā kanyā sukhamedhate//
body.translated_text: with wide eyes that are red at the corners — such a maiden prospers in happiness.

body.text: u13.19ab/.mṛga^akṣī mṛga^jaṅghā ca mṛga^grīvā mṛga^udarī/
body.translated_text: A woman with deer-like eyes, deer-like shins, a deer-like neck, and a deer-like belly,

body.text: u13.19cd/.yukta^nāmā tu yā nārī rājānam upatiṣṭhite//
body.translated_text: a woman with a fitting name — she attends upon a king.

body.text: u13.20ab/.yasya^agra^lalitāḥ keśā mukhaṃ ca parimaṇḍalaṃ/
body.translated_text: A woman whose hair-tips are gracefully curled, whose face is round,

body.text: u13.20cd/.nābhiḥ pradakṣiṇa^āvartā sā kanyā kula^vardhinī//
body.translated_text: whose navel-whorl turns to the right — such a maiden increases the family.

body.text: u13.21ab/.na^atidīrghā na^atihrasvā supratiṣṭha^tanu^tvacā/
body.translated_text: Neither too tall nor too short, with well-set and delicate skin,

body.text: u13.21cd/.sukha^saṃsparśa^keśa^agrā saubhāgyaṃ na^ativartate//
body.translated_text: with hair-tips soft to the touch — her good fortune never wanes.

body.text: u13.22ab/.kānta^jihvā tu yā nārī rakta^uṣṭhī priya^bhāṣiṇī/
body.translated_text: A woman with a lovely tongue, with red lips, who speaks pleasantly —

body.text: u13.22cd/.tādṛśīṃ varayet prājño gṛha^arthaṃ sukhamedhinīṃ//
body.translated_text: a wise man should choose such a woman for his household, one who promotes happiness.

body.text: u13.23ab/.nīla^utpala^suvarṇa^ābhā dīrgha^aṅguli talā tu yā/
body.translated_text: A woman whose fingers and palms have the luster of a blue lotus and gold,

body.text: u13.23cd/.sahasrāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ tu svāminī sā bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: she will become the mistress of many thousands.

body.text: u13.24ab/.dhana^dhānyaiḥ samāyuktāṃ āyuṣā yaśasā śriyā/
body.translated_text: Endowed with wealth and grain, with long life, fame, and prosperity —

body.text: u13.24cd/.kanyāṃ lakṣaṇa^sampannāṃ prāpya vardhati mānavaḥ//
body.translated_text: a man prospers upon obtaining a maiden endowed with auspicious marks.

body.text: u13.25ab/.kīrtitās tu mayā dhanyā maṅgalya^lakṣaṇāḥ striyaḥ/
body.translated_text: I have described the fortunate women with auspicious characteristics;

body.text: u13.25cd/.apraśastaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathā^uddeśena lakṣaṇaṃ//
body.translated_text: now I shall describe the inauspicious marks, in summary.

body.text: u13.26ab/.ūrdhva^prekṣī adhaḥprekṣī yā ca tiryak ca prekṣiṇī/
body.translated_text: A woman who looks upward, who looks downward, or who looks sideways,

body.text: u13.26cd/.udbhrāntā vipulākṣī ca varjanīyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ//
body.translated_text: who is wild-eyed or has excessively large eyes — she should be avoided by the discerning.

body.text: u13.27ab/.bhinna^agraśatikā rūkṣāḥ keśaā yasyāḥ pralambhikāḥ//
body.translated_text: A woman whose hair has split ends, is rough, and hangs loosely,

body.text: u13.27cd/.citra^avalī citra^gātrā bhavati kāma^cāriṇī//
body.translated_text: with mottled lines and mottled limbs — she becomes one who follows her desires.

body.text: u13.28ab/.kāmukā piṅgalā ca^eva gaurī caiva^atikālikā/
body.translated_text: A woman who is lustful, tawny-eyed, exceedingly fair, or exceedingly dark,

body.text: u13.28cd/.atidīrghā atihrasvā varjanīya vicakṣaṇaiḥ//
body.translated_text: excessively tall or excessively short — she should be avoided by the discerning.

body.text: u13.29ab/.yasya^astrīṇi pralambanti lalāṭam udaraṃ sphicau/(p.190)
body.translated_text: A woman whose three parts hang down — the forehead, the belly, and the buttocks —

body.text: u13.29cd/.trīṃś ca sā puruṣān hanti devaraṃ śvaśuraṃ patiṃ//
body.translated_text: she destroys three men: the brother-in-law, the father-in-law, and the husband.

body.text: u13.30ab/.pārśvato roma^rājī tu vinatā ca kaṭir bhavet/
body.translated_text: If the line of body hair runs along the sides and the waist is sunken,

body.text: u13.30cd/.dīrgham āyur avāpnoti dīrgha^kālaṃ ca duḥkhitā//
body.translated_text: she attains a long life but is unhappy for a long time.

body.text: u13.31ab/.kāka^jaṅghā ca yā nārī rakta^akṣī vardhasvarā/
body.translated_text: A woman with crow-like shins, red eyes, and a harsh voice,

body.text: u13.31cd/.niḥsukhā ca nirāśā ca varjitā naṣṭa^bāndhavā//
body.translated_text: she is without happiness and without hope, abandoned and bereft of kinsmen.

body.text: u13.32ab/.atisthūla^udaraṃ yasyāḥ pralambo nimra^sannibhaḥ/
body.translated_text: A woman whose belly is excessively thick and hangs down like a <s>nimba</s> (neem) fruit,

body.text: u13.32cd/.atyantam avaśā nārī bahu^putrā suduḥkhitā//
body.translated_text: such a woman is utterly helpless, with many children but very miserable.

body.text: u13.33ab/.yā tu sarva^samācārā mṛd^vaṅgī samatāṃ gatā/
body.translated_text: A woman who is even in all her conduct, soft-limbed, and of balanced disposition,

body.text: u13.33cd/.sarvaiḥ samair guṇair yuktā vijñeyā kāma^cāriṇī//
body.translated_text: endowed with all equal qualities — she should be known as one who follows her desires.

body.text: u13.34ab/.yasyā roma^cite jaṅghe mukhaṃ ca parimaṇḍalaṃ/
body.translated_text: A woman whose shins are covered with hair and whose face is round,

body.text: u13.34cd/.putraṃ vā bhrātaraṃ vā^api jāram icchati tādṛśī//
body.translated_text: such a one desires a son, or a brother, or even a lover.

body.text: u13.35ab/.yasyā bāhu^prakoṣṭhau dvau roma^rājī^samāvṛtau/
body.translated_text: A woman whose two arms and forearms are covered with lines of hair,

body.text: u13.35cd/.uttaroṣṭhe ca romāṇi sā tu bhakṣayate patiṃ//
body.translated_text: and who has hair on the upper lip — she devours her husband.

body.text: u13.36ab/.yasya hastau ca pādāu ca chidrau danta^antarāṇi ca/
body.translated_text: A woman whose hands and feet have gaps, and whose teeth have spaces between them,

body.text: u13.36cd/.patinā^upārjitaṃ dravyaṃ na tasyā ramate gṛhe//
body.translated_text: the wealth earned by her husband does not remain in that household.

body.text: u13.37ab/.tasyās tu vrajamānāyāḥ sphuṭante parva^sandhayaḥ/
body.translated_text: A woman whose joints crack as she walks,

body.text: u13.37cd/.sā jñeyā duḥkha^bahulā sukhaṃ naiva^adhigacchati//
body.translated_text: she should be known as one full of sorrow — she never attains happiness.

body.text: u13.38ab/.yasyāḥ kaniṣṭhikā pāde bhūmiṃ na spṛśate +aṅguliḥ/
body.translated_text: A woman whose little toe on the foot does not touch the ground,

body.text: u13.38cd/.kaumāraṃ sā patiṃ syaktvā ātmanaḥ kurute priyaṃ//
body.translated_text: she abandons her husband in youth and takes a lover of her own choosing.

body.text: u13.39ab/.anāmāṅguliḥ pādasya mahīṃ na spṛśate +aṅguliḥ/
body.translated_text: If the ring-finger toe of the foot does not touch the ground,

body.text: u13.39cd/.na sā ramati kaumāraṃ bandhakītvena jīvati//
body.translated_text: she does not enjoy her youth — she lives as a courtesan.

body.text: u13.40ab/.yasyāḥ pradeśinī pāde +aṅgulṣṭhaṃ samatikramet/
body.translated_text: A woman whose index toe on the foot exceeds the big toe,

body.text: u13.40cd/.kumārī kurute jāraṃ yauvanasthā viśeṣataḥ//
body.translated_text: as a maiden she takes a lover, especially when in the bloom of youth.

body.text: u13.41ab/.āvartaḥ pṛṣṭhato yasyā nābhī sā ca^anubandhati/(p.191)
body.translated_text: A woman whose hair-whorl is on the back and follows the navel,

body.text: u13.41cd/.na sā ramati kaumāraṃ dvitīyaṃ labhate patiṃ//
body.translated_text: she does not enjoy her youth — she obtains a second husband.

body.text: u13.42ab/.vikṛtā sthirajālā ca rūkṣa^gaṇḍa^śiroruhā/
body.translated_text: A woman who is deformed, with rigid veins, and rough hair on the cheeks and head,

body.text: u13.42cd/.api rāja^kule jātā dāsītvam adhigacchati//
body.translated_text: even if born in a royal family, she attains the condition of a servant.

body.text: u13.43ab/.yasyās tu hasamānāyā gaṇḍe jāyati kūpakaṃ/
body.translated_text: A woman on whose cheek a dimple appears when she laughs,

body.text: u13.43cd/.agnikārye +api sā gatvā kṣipraṃ doṣaṃ kariṣyati//
body.translated_text: even when going to a fire ritual, she will quickly commit a transgression.

body.text: u13.44ab/.sama^asama^gatā subhrūr gaṇḍa^āvartā ca ya bhavet/
body.translated_text: A woman with an uneven gait, beautiful eyebrows but whorls on the cheeks,

body.text: u13.44cd/.pralambhoṣṭhī tu yā nārī naikatra ramate ciraṃ//
body.translated_text: and drooping lips — such a woman does not remain long in one place.

body.text: u13.45ab/.lamba^udarī sthūlaśirā rakta^akṣī piṅgala^ānanā/
body.translated_text: A woman with a pendulous belly, thick veins, red eyes, and a tawny face,

body.text: u13.45cd/.aṣṭau bhakṣayate vīrān navame tiṣṭhate ciraṃ//
body.translated_text: she devours eight heroes and remains long with the ninth.

body.text: u13.46ab/.na devikā na nadikā na ca daivata^nāmikā/
body.translated_text: She should not be named after a goddess, nor after a river, nor after a deity;

body.text: u13.46cd/.vṛkṣa^gulma^sanāmā ca varjayīyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ//
body.translated_text: one named after a tree or a shrub should be avoided by the discerning.

body.text: u13.47ab/.nakṣatra^nāmā yā nārī yā ca gotra^sanāmikā/
body.translated_text: A woman who has a name identical to a <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), and one whose name is the same as the clan (<s>gotra</s>) —

body.text: u13.47cd/.suguptā rakṣitā vā^api manasā pāpām ācaret//
body.translated_text: even if well-guarded or protected, she will commit sin in her mind.

body.text: u13.48ab/.dārān vivarjayed etān yā mayā parikīrtitāḥ/
body.translated_text: One should avoid such wives as have been enumerated by me;

body.text: u13.48cd/.praśastā yās tu pūrvoktās tādṛśīyān naraḥ sadā//
body.translated_text: those that were praised earlier — a man should always [marry] one of such kind.

body.text: u13.49ab/.padma^aṅkuśa^svastika^vardhamānaiś cakra^dhvajābhyāṃ kalaśena pāṇau//
body.translated_text: With [marks of] a lotus, elephant-goad, <s>svastika</s>, <s>vardhamāna</s> (prosperity symbol), a discus and banner, a water-pot in the hand,

body.text: u13.49cd/.śaṅkha^ātapatra^uttama^lakṣaṇaiś ca sampattaye sādhu bhavanti kanyāḥ//
body.translated_text: a conch, a parasol, and supreme auspicious marks — such maidens bring prosperity.

body.text: u13.50/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin kanyā^lakṣaṇaṃ nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Characteristics of Maidens.'

body.text: u13.51/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vastra^adhyāyaṃ vyākhāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagavān triśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter on garments. Listen to it. Now what [does he say]? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text: u14 vastra^adhyāyaḥ (p.192)
body.translated_text: Chapter 14: The Chapter on Garments

body.text: u14.1ab/.kṛttikāsu dahaty agnir artha^lābhāya rohiṇī/
body.translated_text: In [the <s>nakṣatra</s>] <s>Kṛttikā</s>, fire burns [the garment]; <s>Rohiṇī</s> is for the gain of wealth;

body.text: u14.1cd/.mṛgaśirā mūṣīdaṃśā ārdrā prāṇa^vināśinī//
body.translated_text: <s>Mṛgaśirā</s> [brings] rat-bites; <s>Ārdrā</s> is destructive of life.

body.text: u14.2ab/.punarvasuś ca dhanyā syāt puṣye vai vastravān bhavet/
body.translated_text: <s>Punarvasu</s> would be auspicious; in <s>Puṣya</s>, one will become possessed of garments;

body.text: u14.2cd/.aśleṣāsu bhaven moṣaḥ śmaśānaṃ maghayā vrajet//
body.translated_text: in <s>Aśleṣā</s>, there will be theft; by <s>Maghā</s>, one will go to the cremation ground.

body.text: u14.3ab/.phālgunīsu bhaved vidyā uttarāsu ca vastravān/
body.translated_text: In <s>Phālgunī</s> (Pūrva), there will be learning; in <s>Uttarā</s> (Phālgunī), one will be possessed of garments;

body.text: u14.3cd/.hastāsu hasta^karmāṇi citrāyāṃ gamanaṃ dhruvaṃ//
body.translated_text: in <s>Hastā</s>, there will be handiwork; in <s>Citrā</s>, travel is certain.

body.text: u14.4ab/.svātyāṃ ca śobhanaṃ vastraṃ viśākhā priya^darśanaṃ/
body.translated_text: In <s>Svātī</s>, the garment will be beautiful; <s>Viśākhā</s> is pleasant to behold;

body.text: u14.4cd/.bahu^vastrā ca^anurādhā jyeṣṭhā vastra^vināśnī//
body.translated_text: <s>Anurādhā</s> [brings] many garments; <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> is destructive of garments.

body.text: u14.5ab/.mūlena kledayed vāsa āṣāḍhā roga^sambhavā/
body.translated_text: By <s>Mūla</s>, the garment will become damp; <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> [brings] the arising of disease;

body.text: u14.5cd/.uttarā mṛṣṭa^bhojī syāc chravaṇe cakṣuṣo rujaṃ//
body.translated_text: <s>Uttarā</s> (Āṣāḍhā) will bring refined food; in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, there is pain of the eyes.

body.text: u14.6ab/.dhaniṣṭhā dhānya^bahulā vidyāc chatabhiṣe bhayaṃ/
body.translated_text: <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> [brings] abundance of grain; one should know fear in <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>;

body.text: u14.6cd/.pūrvabhādrapade toyaṃ putra^lābhāya ca^uttarā//
body.translated_text: in <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, water [i.e. rain]; <s>Uttarā</s> (Bhādrapadā) is for the gain of a son.

body.text: u14.7ab/.revatī dhana^lābhāya aśvinī vastra^lābhadā/
body.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s> is for the gain of wealth; <s>Aśvinī</s> grants the gain of garments;

body.text: u14.7cd/.bharaṇī ca bhaya^ākīrṇā caura^gamyā ca sā bhavet//
body.translated_text: <s>Bharaṇī</s> is filled with fear, and frequented by thieves.

body.text: u14.8/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vastra^adhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter on garments.

body.text: u14.8/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin luṅgādhyāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/kathayatu bhagavān triśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall declare the chapter on <s>luṅgā</s> (sprout divination). Listen to it. Now what [does he say]? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text: u15 luṅgādhyāyaḥ (p.193)
body.translated_text: Chapter 15: The Chapter on <s>Luṅgā</s> (Sprout Divination)

body.text: u15.1ab/.kutra^utpannā ime bījāḥ (?) śasyānāṃ ca yavādayaḥ/
body.translated_text: Where did these seeds originate — barley and the other grains,

body.text: u15.1cd/.yair idaṃ dhriyate viśvaṃ kṛtsnaṃ sthāvara^jaṅgamaṃ//
body.translated_text: by which this entire universe is sustained, both the stationary and the moving?

body.text: u15.2ab/.vāpayet tu kathaṃ bījaṃ lāṅgalaṃ yojayet kathaṃ/
body.translated_text: How should one sow the seed? How should one yoke the plough?
