body.text: u15.2cd/.keṣu nakṣatra^yogeṣu tithi^yogeṣu keṣu ca//
body.translated_text: In which conjunctions of <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), and in which conjunctions of <s>tithis</s> (lunar days)?

body.text: u15.3ab/.śāradaṃ vā^atha graiṣmaṃ tu kasmin māse tu vāpayet/
body.translated_text: Whether autumn or summer [sowing], in which month should one sow?

body.text: u15.3cd/.nimittaṃ kati śasyante kāni vā parivarjayet/
body.translated_text: How many omens are recommended, and which should one avoid?

body.text: u15.3ef/.kasya vā dāpayed dhūpaṃ kena mantreṇa dāpayet//
body.translated_text: To whom should incense be offered, and with what <s>mantra</s> should it be offered?

body.text: u15.4ab/.pradakṣiṇa^samāvṛttā yadi luṅgā prajāyate/
body.translated_text: When a sprout arises turning clockwise,

body.text: u15.4cd/.tadā nāga^mukhī luṅgā dahati citra^mukhy api//
body.translated_text: then a snake-faced sprout burns, and so does a variegated-faced one.

body.text: u15.5ab/.darbha^sūcī^mukhī vā^api kāraṇaṃ tatra ko bhavet/
body.translated_text: If it is a <s>darbha</s>-grass-needle-faced [sprout], what would be the cause therein?

body.text: u15.5cd/.kati saubhikṣikā luṅgaḥ kati daurbhikṣikāḥ smṛtāḥ/
body.translated_text: How many [types of sprouts] indicate prosperity, and how many are reckoned as [indicating] famine?

body.text: u15.5ef/.kati varṇāḥ samākhyātāḥ kati varṇā nidarśitāḥ//
body.translated_text: How many colors are declared, and how many colors are demonstrated?

body.text: u15.6ab/.naṣṭa^apanaṣṭa^bījasya varṣati yadi vāsavaḥ/
body.translated_text: If <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) rains upon seed that is lost or scattered,

body.text: u15.6cd/.nirghāto vā bhavet tīvro +athavā^api medinī calet//
body.translated_text: or if there is a terrible thunderclap, or the earth trembles —

body.text: u15.7ab/.śasyaṃ phalasya kiṃ tatra nimittam upalakṣayet/
body.translated_text: what omen for the fruiting of the crop should one observe therein?

body.text: u15.7cd/.sarvam etat samāsena śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ//
body.translated_text: All this, in summary, I wish to hear truthfully.

body.text: u15.8ab/.puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya vacanaṃ śrūtvā triśaṅku^mātaṅga^adhipatir idaṃ vacanam abravīt/
body.translated_text: Having heard the words of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s> (elephants/outcasts), spoke these words:

body.text: u15.9ab/.purā deva^asurar nāgair yakṣa^rākṣasa^kinnaraiḥ/
body.translated_text: Long ago, by gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>,

body.text: u15.9cd/.sāgarād amṛtaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ manthite tu samudbhavaṃ//
body.translated_text: the immortal nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) was seen arising from the churning of the ocean.

body.text: u15.10ab/.amṛte bhakṣyamāṇe tu bhāgaṃ prārthitavān dvijaḥ/(p.194)
body.translated_text: While the <s>amṛta</s> was being consumed, a twice-born one (<s>dvija</s>) requested a share;

body.text: u15.10cd/.tato dattāḥ surair bhāgā amṛtād daśavindavaḥ//
body.translated_text: thereupon the gods gave portions from the <s>amṛta</s> — ten drops.

body.text: u15.11ab/.tata utpannā ime bījā bhuvi loka^sukha^āvahāḥ/
body.translated_text: From those arose these seeds on earth, bringing happiness to the world:

body.text: u15.11cd/.yava^brīhi^tilāś ca^eva godhūmā mudga^māṣakāḥ//
body.translated_text: barley, rice, sesame, wheat, green gram, and black gram.

body.text: u15.12ab/.śyāmakaṃ saptamaṃ vidyād ikṣuś ca^aṣṭamakaḥ smṛtaḥ/
body.translated_text: One should know <s>śyāmaka</s> (millet) as the seventh; sugarcane is reckoned as the eighth;

body.text: u15.12cd/.śeṣās tu saṅgatā jātā bahavaḥ śasya^jātayaḥ//
body.translated_text: the rest arose by combination — many varieties of crops.

body.text: u15.13ab/.haritakeṣu sarveṣu ye ca^anye sattva^jātayaḥ/
body.translated_text: In all green vegetables and in whatever other types of living beings —

body.text: u15.13cd/.parito navamo vinduḥ sarva^dehe +amṛto +abhavat/
body.translated_text: the ninth drop of <s>amṛta</s> spread around in every body,

body.text: u15.13ef/.mūleṣu ca^eva sarveṣu vindur ekaḥ prapātitaḥ//
body.translated_text: and a single drop was deposited in all roots.

body.text: u15.14ab/.āṣāḍhe śukla^pakṣe +asya vrīhi^dhānyāni vāpayet/
body.translated_text: In the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, in the bright fortnight, one should sow rice and paddy grains;

body.text: u15.14cd/.śārada^ādīni sarvāṇi māse bhādrapade tathā//
body.translated_text: all autumn [crops] and such, likewise in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>.

body.text: u15.15ab/.kārttike mārgaśīrṣe vā grīāma dhānyāni vāpayet/
body.translated_text: In <s>Kārttika</s> or <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, one should sow summer grains;

body.text: u15.15cd/.pañcabhyāṃ śukla^saptamyāṃ ṣaṣṭhyām ekādaśīṣu ca//
body.translated_text: on the fifth, the bright seventh, sixth, and the eleventh [<s>tithis</s>],

body.text: u15.16ab/.trayodaśyāṃ dvitīyāyāṃ tathā hi navamīṣu ca/
body.translated_text: on the thirteenth, the second, and likewise on the ninths;

body.text: u15.16cd/.viśeṣatas tu nimneṣu sarva^bījāni hy utsṛjet//
body.translated_text: especially in low-lying lands, one should sow all seeds.

body.text: u15.17ab/.bharaṇī puṣya^mūleṣu hasta^aśivanī^maghāsu ca/
body.translated_text: In <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, and <s>Maghā</s>,

body.text: u15.17cd/.kṛttikāsu viśākhāsu viśeṣeṇa tu śāradaṃ//
body.translated_text: in <s>Kṛttikā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s> — especially the autumn [crop].

body.text: u15.18ab/.saumye maitre +anurādhe ca dhaniṣṭhā^śravaṇāsu ca/
body.translated_text: In <s>Saumya</s> (Mṛgaśiras), <s>Maitra</s> (Anurādhā), and <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> and <s>Śravaṇa</s>,

body.text: u15.18cd/.utsargaḥ sarva^bījānām uttareṣu praśasyate/
body.translated_text: the sowing of all seeds is recommended in the <s>Uttara</s> [nakṣatras];

body.text: u15.18ef/.varjayej janma^nakṣatraṃ saṃgrahaṃ ca vivarhayet//
body.translated_text: one should avoid the birth-<s>nakṣatra</s> and avoid the ingathering [day].

body.text: u15.19ab/.grāma^kṣetre ca yad bījaṃ gṛhe ca gṛha^devatā/
body.translated_text: For seed [to be sown] in a village field or [stored] in the house — [one should honor] the household deity;

body.text: u15.19cd/.nimittam upalakṣeta maṅgalāni śubhāni ca//
body.translated_text: one should observe the omens and auspicious signs.

body.text: u15.20ab/.brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ kanyām arciṣmantaṃ ca pāvakaṃ/(p.195)
body.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a maiden, a blazing fire,

body.text: u15.20cd/.vāraṇa^indraṃ vṛṣaṃ ca^eva hayaṃ vā svabhyalaṃkṛtaṃ//
body.translated_text: a lordly elephant, a bull, or a well-adorned horse,

body.text: u15.21ab/.pūrṇa^kumbhaṃ dhvajaṃ chatram āmāmāṃsaṃ surāṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: a full water-pot, a banner, a parasol, raw meat, liquor,

body.text: u15.21cd/.uddhṛtāṃ dhāraṇīṃ ca^eva baddham eka^paśuṃ dadhi//
body.translated_text: upraised earth, and a single bound animal, yogurt,

body.text: u15.22ab/.cakra^ārūḍhaṃ ca śakaṭaṃ kāka^ārūḍhāṃ ca sūkarīṃ/
body.translated_text: a cart mounted with a wheel, and a sow mounted by a crow —

body.text: u15.22cd/.parasya^āropaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sasya^sampattim ādiśet//
body.translated_text: seeing [someone] mounting another's [vehicle], one should predict the prosperity of the crop.

body.text: u15.23ab/.sarve dakṣiṇato dhanyāḥ puraś ca mṛga^pakṣiṇaḥ/
body.translated_text: All [omens] from the south are auspicious, and animals and birds [seen] in front;

body.text: u15.23cd/.daśanaṃ śukha^puṣpāṇāṃ phalānaṃ ca^eva śasyate//
body.translated_text: the seeing of parrot-flowers and fruits is also commended.

body.text: u15.24ab/.ajo vā vāmataḥ śasyo jambukaś ca praśasyate/
body.translated_text: A goat on the left side is auspicious, and a jackal is commended;

body.text: u15.24cd/.vikṛtaṃ kubja^kuṣṭhiṃ ca mukhaṃ śmaśrudharaṃ tathā//
body.translated_text: deformed, hunchbacked, or leprous [persons], and a bearded face likewise,

body.text: u15.25ab/.naraṃ nirbhartsitaṃ dīnaṃ śokārtaṃ vyādhi^pīḍitaṃ/
body.translated_text: a man who is censured, wretched, grief-stricken, or afflicted by disease,

body.text: u15.25cd/.varāha^vṛndaṃ sarpaṃ ca gardabhaṃ bhāra^hīnakaṃ/
body.translated_text: a herd of boars, a serpent, and a donkey without a load —

body.text: u15.25ef/.dṛṣṭvā nivartayed bījaṃ punar grāmaṃ praveśayet//
body.translated_text: having seen [these], one should turn back the seed and re-enter the village.

body.text: u15.26ab/.tilasya bahu(?) pūrṇasya bhāṇḍe syād vapanam tathā/
body.translated_text: The sowing should be in a vessel full of sesame;

body.text: u15.26cd/.śrūtvā hy etāni vrajatāṃ sasya^sampattim ādiśet//
body.translated_text: having heard these [omens] for those who go forth, one should predict the crop's prosperity.

body.text: u15.27ab/.rāśisthaṃ grathitaṃ dhautaṃ svasthamaṃ kuritaṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: [If one hears sounds of grain being] heaped, bound, washed, placed well, or ground,

body.text: u15.27cd/.śrūtvā saṃmārjitaṃ ca^eva ity āśukṛtinaṃ viduḥ//
body.translated_text: and hearing [it being] swept — these are known as signs of swift success.

body.text: u15.28ab/.śrūtvā mlānaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca manda^vṛṣṭiṃ ca nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: Hearing [sounds of grain that is] wilted or dried, one should predict scanty rainfall;

body.text: u15.28cd/.śrūtvā nivartayed bījaṃ punar grāmaṃ praveśayet//
body.translated_text: having heard [this], one should turn back the seed and re-enter the village.

body.text: u15.29ab/.nīyamānaṃ ca yad bījaṃ varṣate yadi vāsavaḥ/
body.translated_text: If, while the seed is being carried, <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) rains,

body.text: u15.29cd/.svayam eva tu tac chasyaṃ kāmaṃ kālena bhujyate//
body.translated_text: that crop itself is enjoyed in due time at will.

body.text: u15.30ab/.nīyamānaṃ ca yad bījaṃ kampate yadi medinī/
body.translated_text: If, while the seed is being carried, the earth trembles,

body.text: u15.30cd/.bhramyate karṣakaḥ sthānān na tac chakyaṃ tu vāpituṃ//
body.translated_text: the farmer wanders from his place; that [seed] cannot be sown.

body.text: u15.31ab/.nīyamānasya bījasya nirghāto dāruṇo bhavet/(p.196)
body.translated_text: If, while the seed is being carried, there is a terrible thunderclap,

body.text: u15.31cd/.svāmino maraṇaṃ kṣipraṃ śasya^pālasya nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: one should predict the swift death of the owner and the guardian of the crop.

body.text: u15.32ab/.atha vā vyākulaṃ kuryād rāja^daṇḍa^nikṛntati/
body.translated_text: Or it will cause disturbance, [or] the king's punishment will cut [one] down;

body.text: u15.32cd/.dṛṣṭvā nivartayed bījaṃ punar grāmaṃ niveśayet//
body.translated_text: having seen [this], one should turn back the seed and re-enter the village.

body.text: u15.33ab/.brāhmaṇebhyo yathā^śakti datvā tu saṃprayojayet/
body.translated_text: Having given [offerings] to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> according to one's capacity, one should begin [the sowing];

body.text: u15.33cd/.kṛtvā suvipulāṃ vedīṃ darbhān āstīrya sarvataḥ/
body.translated_text: having prepared a large ritual altar (<s>vedī</s>) and having spread <s>darbha</s> grass all around,

body.text: u15.34ab/.samidbhir agniṃ prajvālya juhuyād ghṛta^sarṣapaṃ/
body.translated_text: having kindled the fire with fuel-sticks, one should offer oblations of ghee and mustard seeds;

body.text: u15.34cd/.veda^śāntiṃ japet pūrvaṃ śasyāśāntim ataḥ praṃ/
body.translated_text: first one should recite the Vedic <s>śānti</s> (peace) [hymn], then the crop <s>śānti</s> thereafter.

body.text: u15.35ab/.jayet pārāśaraṃ pūrvaṃ priyataṃ vācayed dvijaiḥ/
body.translated_text: First one should recite the [hymn of] <s>Parāśara</s> and have the <s>dvijas</s> (twice-born) recite what is pleasing;

body.text: u15.35cd/.prathamaṃ prāṅmukhaṃ bījaṃ prakṣiped uttare +atha vā//
body.translated_text: the first [seed] should be cast facing east, or alternatively to the north.

body.text: u15.36ab/.pipīlikā yadā kṣetre bījaṃ kurvanti saṅcayaṃ/
body.translated_text: When ants in the field make a collection of seeds,

body.text: u15.36cd/.suvṛṣṭiṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca sarva^sasyeṣu sampadā/
body.translated_text: [it portends] good rain, abundance, and prosperity in all crops.

body.text: u15.37ab/.haranti cet tṛṇād bījaṃ tṛṇe śasya^apahā api/
body.translated_text: If they carry the seeds from grass [to their holes], the crops on the grass will be destroyed too;

body.text: u15.37cd/.prasparaṃ ca hiṃsanti dhānyaṃ ca nidhanaṃ vrajet//
body.translated_text: and they attack each other — the grain will go to ruin.

body.text: u15.38ab/.sthaleṣu sañcayaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahā^vṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet/
body.translated_text: Seeing a collection [of ants] on high ground, one should predict heavy rain;

body.text: u15.38cd/.dṛṣṭvā tu sañcayaṃ nimne +anāvṛṣṭiṃ ca nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: but seeing a collection in low ground, one should predict drought.

body.text: u15.39ab/.yadā tu proṣitaṃ bījaṃ sapta^rātreṇa jāyate/
body.translated_text: When seed that has been sown sprouts within seven nights,

body.text: u15.39cd/.suvṛṣṭiṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca sarva^śasyeṣu sampadā//
body.translated_text: [it portends] good rain, abundance, and prosperity in all crops.

body.text: u15.40ab/.yadā tu proṣitaṃ bījam ardha^māsena jāyate/
body.translated_text: When seed that has been sown sprouts in half a month,

body.text: u15.40cd/.alpaṃ niṣpadyate śasyaṃ durbhikṣaṃ ca^atra jāyate//
body.translated_text: little crop is produced, and famine arises therein.

body.text: u15.41ab/.tri^rātrāc catūrātrād vā yadi luṅgaḥ prajāyate/
body.translated_text: If the sprout (<s>luṅga</s>) arises in three or four nights,

body.text: u15.41cd/.ativṛṣṭir bhavet tatra para^cakra^bhayaṃ viduḥ//
body.translated_text: there will be excessive rain there, and danger from an invading army is known.

body.text: u15.42ab/.luṅgasya tu ye pādāḥ pañca sapta navā tathā/
body.translated_text: If the legs of the sprout are five, seven, or nine,

body.text: u15.42cd/.suvṛṣṭiṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca sarva^sasyeṣu sampadā//
body.translated_text: [it portends] good rain, abundance, and prosperity in all crops.

body.text: u15.43ab/.syāl luṅgasya tu ye pādāś catvāroṣṭapadā^atha vā/(p.197)
body.translated_text: If the legs of the sprout are four, eight, or six,

body.text: u15.43cd/.alpaṃ niṣpadyate śasyaṃ durbhikṣaṃ ca^atra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: little crop is produced; one should predict famine therein.

body.text: u15.44ab/.luṅgasya yadi pādās tu dṛśyante dvādaśa kvacit/
body.translated_text: If anywhere the legs of the sprout are seen to be twelve,

body.text: u15.44cd/.kvacin niṣpadyate śasyaṃ drubhikṣaṃ kvacid ādiśet/
body.translated_text: the crop is produced in some places; one should predict famine in others;

body.text: u15.44ef/.vāma^āvartāḥ pradṛśyante durbhikṣaṃ tatra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: if they appear turning leftward, one should predict famine there.

body.text: u15.45ab/.yadā pūrva^mūkhī luṅgā kṣemaṃ vṛṣṭiṃ ca nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: When the sprout faces east, one should predict well-being and rain;

body.text: u15.45cd/.yadā paścān mukhī luṅgā ativṛṣṭiṃ ca nirdeśet//
body.translated_text: when the sprout faces west, one should predict excessive rain.

body.text: u15.46ab/.kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ caiva^atra yadā luṅga^uttarāmukhī
body.translated_text: Well-being and abundance [are predicted] when the sprout faces north,

body.text: u15.46cd/.haritāla^suvarṇa^ābhā bhadra^śocir iva^utthitā//
body.translated_text: gleaming like orpiment and gold, risen like an auspicious flame.

body.text: u15.47ab/.darbha^sūcī^mukhī ca^api dṛśyate yatra kutracit/
body.translated_text: If a <s>darbha</s>-grass-needle-faced [sprout] is seen anywhere,

body.text: u15.47cd/.kvacin niṣpadyate śasyaṃ durbhikṣaṃ tatra nirdiśet//
body.translated_text: the crop is produced in some places; one should predict famine there.

body.text: u15.48ab/.yadā nāga^mukhī luṅgā dṛśyate yatra vā kavcit/
body.translated_text: When a snake-faced sprout is seen anywhere,

body.text: u15.48cd/.kvacin niśyadyate śasyaṃ durbhikṣaṃ ca^atra nirdiśet/
body.translated_text: the crop is produced in some places; one should predict famine therein;

body.text: u15.48ef/.tatra^aśani^bhayaṃ ca^api bhayaṃ meghān na saṃśayaḥ//
body.translated_text: there is also fear of thunderbolts, and danger from clouds without doubt.

body.text: u15.49ab/.kṛṣi^mūlam idaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaraṃ/
body.translated_text: All this triple world with its moving and stationary [beings] is rooted in agriculture;

body.text: u15.49cd/.na^asti kṛṣi^samāvṛttiḥ svayam uktaṃ svayambhuvā//
body.translated_text: there is no livelihood equal to agriculture — so said <s>Svayambhū</s> (the Self-born) himself.

body.text: u15.50ab/.nākṛṣer dharmam āpnoti nākṛṣeḥ sukham āpnuyāt/
body.translated_text: Without agriculture, one does not attain <s>dharma</s>; without agriculture, one cannot attain happiness;

body.text: u15.50cd/.dharmam arthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ sarvaṃ prāpnoti karṣakaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, wealth, and likewise pleasure — the farmer obtains all.

body.text: u15.51ab/.iti luṅgādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the chapter on <s>luṅgā</s> (sprout divination).

body.text: u15.52ab/.punar api puṣkarasārī brāhmaṇas triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅga^adhipatim etad avocat/
body.translated_text: Again, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> spoke this to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>:

body.text: u15.53ab/.kathaṃ pṛthivyāṃ nāgāś ca kena vā vinivāritāḥ/(p.198)
body.translated_text: How are the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) [distributed] on the earth, and by whom are they restrained?

body.text: u15.53cd/.kuto mūla^samutthānaṃ nirghātaḥ kutra jāyate//
body.translated_text: Whence is the origin from the root [of the earth], and where does the thunderclap arise?

body.text:
u15.54ab/.kutaś ca^abhrāṇi jāyante nānā^varṇā diśo daśa/
u15.54cd/.kasya^eṣa mahataḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate dundubhis varaḥ//
body.translated_text: Whence do clouds arise, of various colors, in the ten directions? Whose is this great sound that is heard, this excellent drum?

body.text: u15.55ab/.ko hi sṛjati durbhikṣaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca^eva prāṇināṃ/
body.translated_text: Who indeed creates famine and also abundance for living beings?

body.text: u15.55cd/.kas tatra sa muni^śreṣṭho nāma gotraṃ bravīhi me//
body.translated_text: Who is that best of sages there? Tell me his name and lineage.

body.text: u15.56ab/.daivatāni ca me brūhi vidhānāni svayambhuvaḥ/
body.translated_text: Tell me the deities and the ordinances of the Self-born (<s>Svayambhu</s>),

body.text: u15.56cd/.yajñaṃ ca yajña^bhāgaṃ ca hotavyaś ca yathā baliḥ//
body.translated_text: the sacrifice and the share of the sacrifice, and how the offering should be made.

body.text: u15.57ab/.pṛthivyāṃ daivataṃ brūhi āśrame daivataṃ brūhi/
body.translated_text: Tell me the deity of the earth; tell me the deity of the hermitage;

body.text: u15.57cd/.deve tu daivataṃ brūhi kena devo sā kalpitā//
body.translated_text: tell me the deity in the sky — by whom was the sky fashioned?

body.text: u15.58ab/.pātrasya daivataṃ brūhi pūrṇa^kumbhasya daivataṃ/
body.translated_text: Tell me the deity of the vessel; the deity of the full water-pot;

body.text: u15.58cd/.karake daivataṃ brūhi tathā sthālyāṃ ca daivataṃ//
body.translated_text: tell me the deity of the water-jar; and likewise the deity of the cooking pot.

body.text: u15.59ab/.śasyasya daivataṃ brūhi śasya^pālasya daivataṃ/
body.translated_text: Tell me the deity of crops; tell me the deity of the crop-protector.

body.text: u15.59cd/.vāyu^skandhaiś ca katibhiḥ śukro vegaṃ pramuñcati//
body.translated_text: And with how many divisions of wind does <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) release its force?

body.text: u15.60ab/.atha triśaṅkur mātaṅga^adhipatir brāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇam etad avocat/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>, spoke thus to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>:

body.text: u15.61ab/.pṛthivī vā vāyur ākāśam apo jyotiś ca pañcamaṃ/
body.translated_text: Earth, wind, space, water, and fire as the fifth —

body.text: u15.61cd/.tatra saṃvartate piṇḍaṃ tato meghaḥ pravartate//
body.translated_text: therein the mass condenses, and thence the cloud arises.

body.text: u15.62ab/.eṣa vyāpnoti ca^ākāśaṃ vāyunā janyate ghanaḥ/
body.translated_text: It pervades space; the dense [cloud] is produced by wind.

body.text: u15.62cd/.āditya^raśmayo vāri samudrasya nabhas^tale//
body.translated_text: The rays of the sun [draw] water from the ocean to the sky.

body.text: u15.63ab/.tajjalaṃ nāga^saṃkṣiptaṃ tato varuṇa^saṃkṣayaḥ/
body.translated_text: That water is gathered by the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-deities); thence comes the diminution by <s>Varuṇa</s>.

body.text: u15.63cd/.vāyur nabho garjayate agnir vidyotate diśaḥ//
body.translated_text: The wind makes the sky rumble; fire illuminates the directions.

body.text: u15.64ab/.marutā kṣipyate piṇḍaṃ sannipātaś ca garjate/(p.199)
body.translated_text: The mass is hurled by <s>Maruta</s> (the wind), and the confluence thunders.

body.text: u15.64cd/.virodhanaṃ tu vāyoś ca agnaś ca anilasya ca//
body.translated_text: The opposition of wind, fire, and breeze —

body.text: u15.65ab/.ākāśe vartate piṇḍaṃ paścāt patati medinīṃ/
body.translated_text: the mass moves in space and afterwards falls to the earth.

body.text: u15.65cd/.yad grahāṇām adhipatir nakṣatra^jyotiṣām api/
body.translated_text: He who is lord of the planets and of the stellar luminaries,

body.text: u15.65ef/.tato māruta^saṃsargāt parjanyam api varṣati//
body.translated_text: from the conjunction with the wind, he also makes <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-cloud) rain.

body.text: u15.66ab/.varṣate śaila^śikhare yatra saṃprasthito janaḥ/
body.translated_text: It rains on the mountain peaks where people have set forth,

body.text: u15.66cd/.yatra satyaṃ ca dharmaś ca havirmeghaś ca vartate//
body.translated_text: where truth and <s>dharma</s> prevail, and where the oblation-cloud is present.

body.text: u15.67ab/.tatra bījāni rohanti anna^pānaṃ samṛdhyati/
body.translated_text: There seeds sprout and food and drink flourish.

body.text: u15.67cd/.evaṃ piṇḍāśanirādyā tato vātāśanī smṛtā/
body.translated_text: Thus the first [calamity] is the hailstone-thunderbolt; then the wind-thunderbolt is declared;

body.text: u15.67ef/.dantāśanī tṛtīyā tu aśanis tu caturthikā//
body.translated_text: the tooth-thunderbolt is the third, and the [ordinary] thunderbolt is the fourth.

body.text: u15.68ab/.pañcamī krimayaḥ proktāḥ ṣaṣṭhī tu śalabhās tathā/
body.translated_text: The fifth is declared to be worms (locusts); the sixth, grasshoppers;

body.text: u15.68cd/.saptamī syād anāvṛṣṭir ativṛṣṭhis tathāṣṭamī//
body.translated_text: the seventh would be drought; and the eighth, excessive rain.

body.text: u15.69/.navamī sambaraḥ proktā ity āha bhagavāms triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: The ninth is declared to be <s>Sambara</s> (a demon/obstruction) — thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text: u15.70ab/.etāstv aśanyo vyākhyātās tāsāṃ vai devatāḥ śṛṇu/
body.translated_text: These thunderbolts have been explained; now hear their deities.

body.text: u15.70cd/.piṇḍāśanī brahmasṛṣṭā eṣā jyeṣṭhādyadevatā//
body.translated_text: The hailstone-thunderbolt is created by <s>Brahmā</s>; this is the foremost deity.

body.text: u15.71ab/.dantāśanī tu sainyānāṃ grahā vātāśanī smṛtā/
body.translated_text: The tooth-thunderbolt [presides over] armies; the planets are [the deity of] the wind-thunderbolt.
In a place without [proper conditions] ... [the text is lacunose] ... deities.

body.text: u15.72ab/.śalabhāḥ ketudaivatyā ādityā ditidevatāḥ/
body.translated_text: Grasshoppers have the comets as their deity; the <s>Ādityas</s> have <s>Diti</s> as their deity.

body.text: u15.72cd/.saṃsakām ativarṣasya anāvṛṣṭes tu jyoti[ṣaḥ}/
body.translated_text: The desire for excessive rain, and of drought, the luminaries [are the deities];

body.text: u15.73ab/.[samba]rasya tu parjanyam ākhyātāḥ nava devatāḥ/
body.translated_text: and of <s>Sambara</s>, <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) — the nine deities have been declared.

body.text: u15.73cd/.aśanyā devatāḥ proktā ākāśa^gamana^arthaṃ bodhata//
body.translated_text: The deities of the thunderbolts have been declared. Understand [this] for the purpose of traversing the sky.

body.text: u15.74ab/.pūrvam adhīndra^daivatyaṃ dakṣiṇo yama^daivataṃ/
body.translated_text: In the east, <s>Indra</s> is the deity; in the south, <s>Yama</s> is the deity.

body.text: u15.74cd/.varuṇaṃ paścime vidyād uttare dhanadaḥ smṛtaḥ/(p.200)
body.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s> should be known in the west; in the north, <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) is declared.

body.text: u15.74ef/..... tyā daivataṃ viZṇur āśramaṃ viśva^daivataṃ//
body.translated_text: ... the deity is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the hermitage has the universal deities.

body.text: u15.75ab/.samihā^daivatā devās tebhyo devī prakalpitā/
body.translated_text: The gods are the deities of the ritual intention; for them the goddess was ordained.

body.text: u15.75cd/.samidhā^daivatā ..........to 'gni^hutāśanaṃ//
body.translated_text: The deities of the kindling-wood ... [lacuna] ... <s>Agni</s> the fire-god.

body.text: u15.76ab/.vedyāṃ tu daivataṃ ......... kārāditya^daivataṃ/
body.translated_text: On the altar, the deity ... [lacuna] ... the sun as deity.

body.text: u15.76cd/.pātrasya devatā dharmaḥ pūrṇa^kumbhe janārdanaḥ//
body.translated_text: The deity of the vessel is <s>Dharma</s>; of the full water-pot, <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).

body.text: u15.77ab/.caruṃ ceti ...........dhūpa^sthānasya jyotiṣaḥ/
body.translated_text: The oblation ... [lacuna] ... of the incense-stand, the luminaries.

body.text: u15.77cd/.śasya ....... śasya^pālo mahā^matiḥ/
body.translated_text: Of crops ... [lacuna] ... the crop-protector is of great wisdom.

body.text: u15.77ef/.vāyu^skandhaiś caturbhis tu śukro vegaṃ pramuñcati//
body.translated_text: With four divisions of wind, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) releases its force.

body.text: u15.78ab/.atra madhye pṛthivyāya āśramo viśva^daivataḥ/
body.translated_text: In the midst of this, of the earth, the hermitage has the universal deities.

body.text: u15.78cd/.tasmin deśe ...... yasmin prīto vṛṣa^dhvajaḥ//
body.translated_text: In that place ... [lacuna] ... where <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, the bull-bannered one) is pleased.

body.text: u15.79ab/.aty āha bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/ punar api puṣkarasārī brāhmaṇas triśaṅkum evam āha/
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s>. And again the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> spoke thus to <s>Triśaṅku</s>:

body.text: u15.80ab/.kim artham āśrame nityaṃ hūyate havya^vāhanaḥ/
body.translated_text: For what purpose is the fire-bearer (<s>Agni</s>) always offered oblations in the hermitage,

body.text: u15.80cd/.tṛṇa^kāṣṭhāni saṃhṛtya meghaṃ dṛṣṭvā samutthitaṃ//
body.translated_text: having gathered grass and wood, when a cloud is seen to have arisen?

body.text: u15.81ab/.ati .......... nyate agniṃ sudāruṇaṃ/
body.translated_text: ... [lacuna] ... the most terrible fire,

body.text: u15.81cd/.sarva^loka^hita^arthāya dhyātvā divyena cakṣuṣā/
body.translated_text: for the welfare of all the worlds, having meditated with divine vision,

body.text: u15.81ef/.praśamec ca samāsena tad bhava^arthaṃ tu ..... //
body.translated_text: one should pacify [it] in brief — that is for the purpose of [this] existence ... [lacuna].

body.text: u15.82/.evam ukte triśaṅkur mātaṅga^adhipatir brāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇam etad avocat/
body.translated_text: When thus addressed, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>, spoke thus to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>:

body.text: u16 dhūmikādhyāyaḥ (p.201)
body.translated_text: Chapter 16: The Chapter on Smoke

body.text: u16.1ab/.purā hi khāṇḍava^dvīpam arjunena mahā^ātmanā/
body.translated_text: Formerly, the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> forest was [burned] by the great-souled <s>Arjuna</s>,

body.text: u16.1cd/................ jvalitaṃ jāta^vedasā//
body.translated_text: ... [lacuna] ... set ablaze by <s>Jātavedas</s> (fire).

body.text: u16.2ab/................ prasanna^mānān nidhi^gataṃ/
body.translated_text: ... [lacuna] ... of pleased minds, gone to the treasure,

body.text: u16.2cd/.tatra dagdhā anekā hi nāgāḥ koṭī^sahasraśaḥ//
body.translated_text: there indeed many <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) were burned, in tens of millions.

body.text: u16.3ab/.purā mahā^uragagaṇā yakṣa^rākṣasa^pannagāḥ/
body.translated_text: Formerly the great serpent-hosts, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Pannagas</s> —

body.text: u16.3cd/.pāda^hīnāḥ kṛtāḥ kecid vāhu^hīnāḥ kṛtāpare//
body.translated_text: some were made footless, others were made armless.

body.text: u16.4ab/.vaikalyaṃ karṇa^nāsābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ caiva^akṣipātanaṃ/
body.translated_text: Mutilation of ears and noses was done, and also the gouging of eyes.

body.text: u16.4cd/.tadā^prabhṛti bhūtānāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vai trāsitaṃ manaḥ//
body.translated_text: From that time forth, the minds of beings were seen to be terrified.

body.text: u16.5ab/.agninā tāpitāḥ kecid vāṇair anye ca sūditāḥ/
body.translated_text: Some were scorched by fire, others were slain by arrows.

body.text: u16.5cd/.vācāṭakena^api purā kādraveyāḥ prapātitāḥ//
body.translated_text: And formerly, the sons of <s>Kadrū</s> (serpents) were felled by <s>Vācāṭaka</s> (a chattering bird/weapon).

body.text: u16.6ab/.ācaṣā havi^gandhena muhyamānā nabhontare/
body.translated_text: Bewildered by the scent of oblations, [the beings] in the sky,

body.text: u16.6cd/.tadvihīnāḥ patanty anye guhyakā dharaṇī^tale//
body.translated_text: deprived of that [scent], the <s>Guhyakas</s> (hidden beings) fall to the surface of the earth.

body.text: u16.7ab/.sahāmpatis tu nāmnā sa śasya^kāle tadāśrame/
body.translated_text: <s>Sahāmpati</s> is his name — in the crop season, at that hermitage,

body.text: u16.7cd/.śasya^pālais tu satatam hotavyo havya^vāhanaḥ//
body.translated_text: by the crop-protectors, the fire-bearer should always be given oblations.

body.text: u16.8ab/.gṛha^medhī jvālayed agniṃ nirmale +api nabhontare/
body.translated_text: The householder should kindle fire even when the sky is clear,

body.text: u16.8cd/.dig^bhāgeṣu ca bhūtānāṃ teṣām arthaṃ dine dine//
body.translated_text: in the directional quarters, for the sake of those beings, day after day.

body.text: u16.9ab/.jāgratam satataṃ vahnim āśramastho +api dhārayet/
body.translated_text: One dwelling in the hermitage should always keep the fire vigilantly burning.

body.text: u16.9cd/.meghaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśeṣeṇa jvālitavyo hutāśanaḥ//
body.translated_text: Especially when a cloud is seen, the fire should be kindled.

body.text: u16.10ab/.sadhūmlaṃ jvalitaṃ dṛṣṭvā dīpyamānaṃ tu pāvakaṃ/
body.translated_text: Seeing the fire burning with smoke, blazing and shining,

body.text: u16.10cd/.bhayam āpatate teṣāṃ nāga^sainyaṃ vimuhyate//
body.translated_text: fear falls upon them, and the army of <s>Nāgas</s> is bewildered.

body.text: u16.11ab/.agniṃ paricarato +asya śasya^pālasya ca^āśrame/
body.translated_text: For this crop-protector who tends the fire in the hermitage,

body.text: u16.11cd/.agninā hūyamānena sidhyate sarva^karma ca//
body.translated_text: by the fire being offered oblations, all actions are accomplished.

body.text: u16.12/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dhūmikādhyāyaḥ/
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the Chapter on Smoke.

body.text: u16.13/.atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin tithi^karma^nirdeśaṃ nāma^adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/ tac chrūyatāṃ/ atha kiṃ/ kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuḥ/
body.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'Instruction on Lunar Days and Actions.' Listen to it. Now what? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.

body.text: u17 tithi^karma^nirdeśaḥ (p.202)
body.translated_text: Chapter 17: Instruction on Lunar Days and Actions

body.text: u17.1ab/.nandāṃ pratipadām āhuḥ praśastāṃ sarva^kramasu/
body.translated_text: They call the first lunar day (<s>pratipad</s>) '<s>Nandā</s>' (joyful), auspicious in all undertakings,

body.text: u17.1cd/.vijñānasya samārambhe pravāse ca vigarhitā//
body.translated_text: but condemned for the commencement of learning and for travel.

body.text: u17.2ab/.dvitīyā kathitā bhadrā śastā bhūṣaṇa^karmasu/
body.translated_text: The second is called '<s>Bhadrā</s>' (blessed), praised for ornamentation and decorative works.

body.text: u17.2cd/.jayā tṛtīyā vyākhyātā praśastā jaya^karmasu//
body.translated_text: The third is declared '<s>Jayā</s>' (victorious), praised for actions aimed at victory.

body.text: u17.3ab/.caturthī kathitā riktā grāma^sainya^vadhe hitā/
body.translated_text: The fourth is called '<s>Riktā</s>' (empty), suited for the slaying of village [foes] and armies,

body.text: u17.3cd/.caurya^abhicāra^kūṭa^agnidāha^gorasa^sādhane//
body.translated_text: for theft, sorcery (<s>abhicāra</s>), fraud, arson, and the preparation of dairy products.

body.text: u17.4ab/.pūrṇā tu pañcamī jñeyā cikitsā^gamana^adhvasu/
body.translated_text: The fifth should be known as '<s>Pūrṇā</s>' (full), [auspicious] for medical treatment, travel, and journeys,

body.text: u17.4cd/.dāna^adhyayana^śilpeṣu vyāyāme ca praśasyate//
body.translated_text: and praised for charity, study, crafts, and exercise.

body.text: u17.5ab/.jyeti saṃjñitā ṣaṣṭhī garhitā +adhvasu śasyate/
body.translated_text: The sixth is designated '<s>Jyā</s>' (bowstring), condemned for journeys but praised [otherwise].

body.text: u17.5cd/.gṛhe kṣetre vivāhe vā +avāha^karmasu mitra^iti//
body.translated_text: For the house, fields, marriage, and rites of bringing [a bride] — [it is designated] '<s>Mitra</s>' (friend).

body.text: u17.6ab/.bhadrā ca saptamī khyātā śreṣṭhā sā saukṛte +adhvani/
body.translated_text: The seventh is known as '<s>Bhadrā</s>' (blessed), best for meritorious journeys,

body.text: u17.6cd/.nṛpāṇāṃ śāsane chatre śayyānāṃ karaṇeṣu ca//
body.translated_text: for the commands of kings, royal umbrellas, and the making of beds.

body.text: u17.7ab/.mahā^bala^aṣṭamī sā ca prayojyā parirakṣaṇe/
body.translated_text: The eighth is of great strength (<s>Mahābala</s>), and should be employed for protection,

body.text: u17.7cd/.bhaya^mandara^baddheṣu yogeṣu haraṇeṣu ca//
body.translated_text: in fearsome and bewildering [situations], in binding, in <s>yoga</s> practices, and in seizing.

body.text: u17.8ab/.agrasenā tu navamī tasyāṃ kuryād ripu^kṣayaṃ/
body.translated_text: The ninth is '<s>Agrasenā</s>' (leading the army) — on it one should effect the destruction of enemies,

body.text: u17.8cd/.tathā viṣaghna^avaskanda^vidyā^bandha^vadha^kriyāḥ//
body.translated_text: and also the arts of poison-curing, attack, knowledge, binding, and killing.

body.text: u17.9ab/.sudharmā daśamī śastā śāstra^ārambhe dhanodyate/
body.translated_text: The tenth, '<s>Sudharmā</s>' (good dharma), is praised for the commencement of treatises and the raising of wealth,

body.text: u17.9cd/.śānti^svastyayana^ārambhe dāna^yajña^udyateṣu ca//
body.translated_text: for the commencement of peace-rites and <s>svastyayana</s> (benedictions), and for those engaged in charity and sacrifice.

body.text: u17.10ab/.ekādaśī punarmānyā strīṣu ca māṃsa^madyayoḥ/
body.translated_text: The eleventh, '<s>Punarmānyā</s>' (re-honored), [is auspicious] for women, and for meat and liquor.

body.text: u17.10cd/.kārayen nagaraṃ guptaṃ vivāhaṃ śāstra^karma ca//
body.translated_text: One should build a protected city, [perform] marriage, and [undertake] scriptural activities.

body.text: u17.11ab/.yaśeti dvādaśīmm āhur vaire +adhvani ca garhitā/
body.translated_text: The twelfth is called '<s>Yaśa</s>' (fame), condemned for enmity and travel,

body.text: u17.11cd/.vivāhe ca girau kṣetre gṛha^kramasu pūjitā//
body.translated_text: but honored for marriage, on mountains, in fields, and in household undertakings.

body.text: u17.12ab/.jayā trayodaśī sādhvī maṇḍaleṣu ca yoṣitāṃ/(p.203)
body.translated_text: The thirteenth, '<s>Jayā</s>' (victorious), is virtuous — for <s>maṇḍalas</s> (ritual diagrams) and for women,

body.text: u17.12cd/.kanyā^varaṇa^vāṇijya^vivāha^ādiṣu ca^iṣyate//
body.translated_text: and desired for the selection of a bride, commerce, marriage, and the like.

body.text: u17.13ab/.ugrā caturdaśī tu syāt kārayed abhicārakaṃ/
body.translated_text: The fourteenth is '<s>Ugrā</s>' (fierce) — one should perform sorcery (<s>abhicāra</s>),

body.text: u17.13cd/.vadha^bandha^prayogāṃś ca pūrvaṃ ca prahared api//
body.translated_text: acts of killing, binding, and magical employment, and one should also strike first.

body.text: u17.14ab/.siddhā pañcadaśī sādhvī devatā^agni^vidhau hitā/
body.translated_text: The fifteenth, '<s>Siddhā</s>' (accomplished), is virtuous — suited for rites of deities and fire,

body.text: u17.14cd/.go^saṃgraha^vṛṣa^utsarga^bali^japya^vrateṣu ca//
body.translated_text: and for the gathering of cattle, the release of bulls, offerings, <s>japa</s> (recitation), and vows.

body.text: u17.15ab/.nanda^ādīnāṃ kriyā pūrve ṣaṣṭhy^ādīnāṃ tu madhyame/
body.translated_text: The activities of <s>Nandā</s> and the rest [are suited] to the earlier [part of the day]; those of the sixth and the rest, to the middle.

body.text: u17.15cd/.sunandāyāś ca saṃdhyābhir dinarātryoḥ prasidhyate//
body.translated_text: And of <s>Sunandā</s>, [the efficacy] is established at the twilight junctions, during day and night.

body.text:
u17.16/.ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin tithi^karma^nirdeśo nāma^adhyāyaḥ/
u17.17/.api ca mahā^brāhmaṇa idaṃ pūrva^nivāsa^anusmṛti^jñāna^sākṣāt kriyāyāṃ vidyāyāṃ cittam abhinirṇayāmi nivartayāmi/ aneka^vidha^pūrva^nivāsaṃ samanusmarami/
body.translated_text:
This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Instruction on Lunar Days and Actions.'
Moreover, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I direct my mind to, I apply [my mind] to the knowledge that is the direct realization of the recollection of past lives. I remember my manifold past lives.

body.text:
u17.18/.syāt te brāhmaṇa kākṣā vā vimatir vā anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena brahmā devānāṃ pravaro +abhūt/ na hy evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ/ aham eva sa tena kālena tena samayena brahmā devānāṃ pravaro +abhūvaṃ/ so +ahaṃ tataś cyutaḥ samāna indraḥ kauśiko +abhūvaṃ/ tataś cyutaḥ samāno +araṇemir gautamo +abhūvaṃ/ tataś cyutaḥ samānaḥ śvetaketur nāma maharṣir abhūvaṃ/
tataś cyutaḥ samānaḥ śuka^paṇḍito +abhūvaṃ/ mayā te tadā brāhmaṇa catvāro vedā vibhaktāḥ/
body.translated_text: You may have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [thinking] that someone else at that time, in that era, was <s>Brahmā</s>, the foremost of gods. It should not be viewed thus. I myself at that time, in that era, was <s>Brahmā</s>, the foremost of gods. Having fallen from there, I became <s>Indra Kauśika</s>. Having fallen from there, I became <s>Araṇemi Gautama</s>. Having fallen from there, I became a great sage named <s>Śvetaketu</s>. Having fallen from there, I became a learned parrot (<s>Śukapaṇḍita</s>). At that time, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I divided the four <s>Vedas</s>.

body.text:
u17.19/.(p.204)tad yathā puṣyo bahavṛcānāṃ paṃktiś chandogānāṃ/ eka^viṃśati^caraṇā adhvaryavaḥ/ kratur artha^vaṇikānāṃ/ syāt tava brāhmaṇa kāṅkṣā vā vimatir vā anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena vasur nāma maharṣir abhūt/ na hy evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ/ aham eva sa tena kālena tena samayena vasur nāma maharṣir abhūvaṃ/ mayā sā takṣakavadhūkāyāḥ kapilā nāma māṇivikā
duhitā +asāditā bhāryā^arthāya/ so +ahaṃ tatra saṃrakta^citta ṛddhyā bhraṣṭo dhyānebhyo vañcitaḥ parihīnaḥ/ so +aham ātmānaṃ jugupsamānas tasyāṃ velāyām imāṃ gāthāṃ babhāṣe/ oṃ bhubhuvaḥ svaḥ/ tatsavitur vareṇyaṃ bhargā devasya dhīmahi/ dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt/
body.translated_text: Namely: <s>Puṣya</s> for the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (Ṛgvedins), <s>Paṅkti</s> for the <s>Chandogas</s> (Sāmavedins), twenty-one branches for the <s>Adhvaryus</s> (Yajurvedins), and <s>Kratu</s> for the <s>Arthavaṇikas</s> (Atharvavedins). You may have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [thinking] that someone else at that time, in that era, was the great sage named <s>Vasu</s>. It should not be viewed thus. I myself at that time, in that era, was the great sage named <s>Vasu</s>. I obtained as my wife the daughter named <s>Kapilā</s>, a young gem-woman from the family of <s>Takṣakavadhūkā</s>. With my mind attached there, I fell from my supernatural powers, was cheated of my meditations, and declined. Self-reproaching, at that very moment I spoke this verse: '<s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>. We meditate upon the excellent splendor of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>; may he stimulate our thoughts.'

body.text:
u17.20/.so +ahaṃ brāhmaṇa tvāṃ bravīmi sāmānya^saṃjñā mātrakam idaṃ lokasya brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/ ekam eva^idaṃ sarvaṃ sarvam idam ekaṃ/ putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaram anuprayaccha bhāryā^arthāya/ yāvatakaṃ kula^śulkaṃ manyase tāvatakam anupradāsyāmi/ idaṃ ca vacanaṃ punaḥ śrūtvā triśaṅkor mātaṅga^rājasya
brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkrasārī idam avocat/
body.translated_text: I, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, tell you: these are merely conventional designations of the world — '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' or '<s>Kṣatriya</s>' or '<s>Vaiśya</s>' or '<s>Śūdra</s>.' All this is one; this one is all. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as his wife. Whatever bride-price you consider appropriate, I shall give that much. Having heard these words again, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> spoke thus to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s>-king:

body.text: u17.21ab/.bhagavān śrotriyaḥ śreṣṭhas tvatto bhūyān na vidyate/
body.translated_text: Blessed one, you are the foremost of Vedic scholars; none greater than you exists,

body.text: u17.21cd/.sa^devakeṣu lokeṣu mahā^brahmāsamo bhavān//
body.translated_text: in the worlds including the gods — you are the equal of great <s>Brahmā</s> himself, the lord. //

body.text: u17.22ab/.putrāya te bhoḥ prakṛtiṃ dadāmi (p.205) śīlena rūpeṇa guṇair upetaḥ/
body.translated_text: To your son, sir, I give <s>Prakṛti</s>, endowed with virtue, beauty, and good qualities;

body.text: u17.22cd/.śārdūlakarṇaḥ prakṛtis tu bhadrā ubhau rametāṃ rucitaṃ mama^idaṃ/
body.translated_text: <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s> the auspicious — may they both delight [in each other]; this is pleasing to me. //

body.text: u17.23/.tatra tāni pañca^mātrāṇi māṇavaka^śatāni uccaiḥ śabdāni procur mahā^śabdāni/ mā tvaṃ bho upādhyāya vidyamāneṣu brāhmaṇeṣu cāṇḍālena sārdhaṃ sambandhaṃ rocaya/ na^arhasi bho upādhyāya vidyamāneṣu brāhmaṇeṣu cāṇḍālena sārdhaṃ sambandhaṃ kartum/
body.translated_text: Thereupon, those five hundred young students cried out loudly with great voices: 'Do not, O teacher, while <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> exist, approve of a marriage alliance with a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>! You should not, O teacher, while <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> exist, enter into a marriage alliance with a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>!'

body.text: u17.24/.atha brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī teṣāṃ nidānaṃ nidāya śabdaṃ saṃsthāpya nipatya ślokena^etān arthān abhāṣata/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, having understood their cause, having silenced their clamor, standing up, spoke these words in verse:

body.text: u17.25ab/.evam etad yathā hy eṣa triśaṅkur bhāṣate giraṃ/
body.translated_text: It is indeed just as this <s>Triśaṅku</s> speaks his words —

body.text: u17.25cd/.tatvaṃ hy avitathaṃ bhūtaṃ satyam nityaṃ tathā dhruvaṃ//
body.translated_text: it is truth, unfailing, real, eternal, and fixed. //

body.text: u17.26/.atha brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī teṣāṃ māṇavakānāṃ taṃ mahāntaṃ śabdaṃ saṃsthāpya (p.206) triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅga^rājam idam avocat/ ayaṃ bhos triśaṅko brahmaṇā sahāpatinā cāturmahā^bhautiko mahā^puruṣaḥ prajñaptaḥ/ yasya/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, having silenced the great clamor of those young students, spoke thus to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s>-king: 'O <s>Triśaṅku</s>! This great being (<s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>), composed of the four great elements, was created by <s>Brahmā</s> together with the Lord. Of whom:' —

body.text: u17.27ab/.śiraḥ satāraṃ gaganam ākāśam udaraṃ tathā/
body.translated_text: The head is the sky together with stars; the belly is the ether (<s>ākāśa</s>) likewise;

body.text: u17.27cd/.parvatāś ca^apy ubhāv ūrū pādau ca dharaṇī^talaṃ//
body.translated_text: the mountains are his two thighs; and his feet are the surface of the earth. //

body.text: u17.28ab/.sūryā^candramasau netre roma tṛṇa^vanaspatī/
body.translated_text: The sun and moon are his eyes; his body-hair is the grass, trees, and plants;

body.text: u17.28cd/.sāgarāś ca^apy amedhyaṃ vai nadyo sūtra^sravo +asya tu//
body.translated_text: the oceans are indeed his impurity; the rivers are the flow of his threads. //

body.text: u17.29ab/.aśrūṇi varṣaṇaṃ cārasya eṣa brahmā sahāpatiḥ/
body.translated_text: His tears are the rainfall — this is <s>Brahmā</s> together with the Lord.

body.text: u17.29cd/.bhavāṃs tu parama^jño +asi tan me brūhi yathā tathā//
body.translated_text: You are indeed one of supreme knowledge; therefore tell me as it truly is. //

body.text: u17.30/.iha bhos triśaṅko kim āha svalakṣaṇaṃ brahmaṇaḥ pratyavekṣasva/ pitrā ca mātrā ca kṛtāni karmāṇi bhavanti/ aśvastanā stena vañcitāḥ/
body.translated_text: Here, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, what do you say? Examine the inherent nature of <s>Brahman</s>. The deeds done by father and mother come to pass. Those of uncertain tomorrow are deceived by thieves.

body.text: u17.31ab/.gacchanti sattvā bahu^garbha^yoniṃ na ca^eva kaścin manujo hy ayoniḥ/
body.translated_text: Beings go through many wombs and births, and no human being is indeed without a womb;

body.text: u17.31cd/.samasta jātau pracaranti sattvā na mārutāj jāyate kaścid eva//
body.translated_text: all beings of every birth move about — no one at all is born from mere wind. //

body.text: u17.32ab/.svabhāva^bhāvyaṃ hy avagaccha loke ke brāhmaṇa^kṣatriya^vaiśya^śūdrāḥ/
body.translated_text: Understand that [all] in the world is determined by inherent nature — who then are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, or <s>Śūdras</s>?

body.text: u17.32cd/.sarvatra kāṇāḥ kuṇinaś ca khañjāḥ kuṣṭhī kilāsī hy apasmāriṇo 'pi//
body.translated_text: Everywhere there are the one-eyed, the crippled, and the lame, the leper, the white-spotted, and the epileptic. //

body.text: u17.33ab/.kṛṣṇāś ca gaurāś ca tathā^eva śyāmāḥ sattvāḥ prajā hy anyatame viśiṣṭāḥ/(p.207)
body.translated_text: Dark-skinned and fair-skinned and likewise brown — beings and creatures are distinguished in various ways;

body.text: u17.33cd/.saha^asthi^carmāḥ sanakhāḥ samāṃsā duḥkhī sukhī mūtra^purīṣa^yuktāḥ/
body.translated_text: with bones, skin, nails, and flesh alike, subject to suffering and happiness, endowed with urine and excrement —

body.text: u17.33ef/.na ca^indriyāṇāṃ praviviktir asti tasmān na varṇāś caturo bhavanti//
body.translated_text: there is no distinction of the sense organs; therefore, there are not four <s>varṇas</s> (social orders). //

body.text: u17.34ab/.mantrair hi yadi labhyeta svargaṃ tu gamanaṃ dvijaḥ/
body.translated_text: If, by <s>mantras</s> (sacred chants) alone, a twice-born could obtain passage to heaven,

body.text: u17.34cd/.kṛṣṇa^śuklāni karmāṇi bhaveyur niṣphalāni hi/
body.translated_text: then dark and bright deeds would be fruitless indeed;

body.text: u17.34ef/.yasmāt kṛṣṇāni śuklāni karmāṇi saphalāni hi/
body.translated_text: since dark and bright deeds are indeed fruitful,

body.text: u17.34gh/.pacyamānāni dṛśyante gatiṣv etāni pañca^su//
body.translated_text: their ripening is seen in the five destinies. //

body.text: u17.35/.mānavaka^śateṣu sa tatra vinihato mahā^yaśasā triśaṅkunā puṣkarasārī brāhmaṇo +abravīt/ brāhmaṇo +asau mātaṅga^rājo hi triśaṅkur nāma/ bhavān hi brahmā indraś ca kauśikaḥ/ tvam araṇemiś ca gautamaḥ/ tvaṃ śvetaketuś ca śuka^paṇḍitaḥ/ vedaḥ samākhyātas tvayā caturdhā/ bhagavān vasūrāja^rṣir mahā^yaśā bhagavān/
body.translated_text: Being defeated there among the hundreds of students by the greatly renowned <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> said: 'That <s>Mātaṅga</s>-king named <s>Triśaṅku</s> is indeed a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! You, sir, are <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Indra</s> <s>Kauśika</s>! You are <s>Araṇemi</s> and <s>Gautama</s>! You are <s>Śvetaketu</s> and the wise <s>Śuka</s>! The <s>Veda</s> was declared by you in four parts! You are the blessed <s>Vasu</s>, the royal sage of great renown!'

body.text: u17.36ab/.jñānena hi tvaṃ parameṇa yuktaḥ svaṣu śāstreṣu bhavān kṛtārthaḥ/
body.translated_text: For you are endowed with supreme knowledge; you have accomplished your purpose in your own scriptures;

body.text: u17.36cd/.śreṣṭho viśiṣṭo paramo +asi loke bhavān hi vidyā^caraṇena yuktaḥ//
body.translated_text: you are the foremost, the most distinguished, the supreme in the world; you are endowed with learning and conduct. //

body.text: u17.37ab/.dadāmi te +ahaṃ prakṛtiṃ mamāmalāṃ śīlena rūpeṇa guṇair upetaḥ/
body.translated_text: I give to you my pure [daughter] <s>Prakṛti</s>, endowed with virtue, beauty, and good qualities;

body.text: u17.37cd/.śārdūlakarṇaḥ prakṛtiś ca bhadrā ubhau rametaṃ rucitaṃ mama^idaṃ//
body.translated_text: <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s> the auspicious — may they both delight [in each other]; this is pleasing to me. //

body.text: u17.38ab/.pragṛhya bhṛṅgāram udaka^prapūrṇam āvarjito brāhmaṇo hṛṣṭa^cittaḥ/(p.208)
body.translated_text: Having taken a water-vessel filled with water, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, glad of heart, poured it out;

body.text: u17.38cd/.anupradāsīd udakena kanyakāṃ śārdūlakarṇasya iyam astu bhāryā//
body.translated_text: he gave the maiden with water [as witness] — 'May she be the wife of <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>!' //

body.text: u17.39/.udagracitta āsīn mātaṅga^rājaḥ/
body.translated_text: The <s>Mātaṅga</s>-king was overjoyed in heart.

body.text: u17.40ab/.kṛtvā niveśaṃ sa tadātmajasya gatvā^āśrame +asau nagaraṃ yaśasvī/
body.translated_text: Having performed the wedding of his son, the renowned one went to the city from the hermitage;

body.text: u17.40cd/.dharmeṇa vai kārayati svarājyaṃ kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca sadā^utsava^ādyaṃ // iti/
body.translated_text: and he governed his own kingdom through <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), with security, abundance, and perpetual festivities. // Thus.

body.text:
u17.41/.syād bhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatir vā vicikitsā vā/ anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena triśaṅkur nāma mātaṅga^rājo +abhūvaṃ/ syād evaṃ ca bhikṣavo yusmākam anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena śārdūlakarṇā nāma mātaṅga^rāja^kumāro +abhūt/ naiva draṣṭavyaṃ/ eṣa sa ānando bhikṣuḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena śārdūlakarṇā nāma mātaṅga^rāja^kumāro
+abhūt/ syād evaṃ yuṣmākam anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena puṣkarasārī nāma brāhmaṇo +abhūt/ naiva draṣṭavyaṃ/ eṣa śāradvatīputro bhikṣuḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena puṣkarasārī nāma brāhmaṇo +abhūt/ na^anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya prakṛtir nāma māṇavikā duhitā^abhūt/ na^evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ/ eṣā sā prakṛtir bhikṣuṇī tena kālena
tena samayena puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya prakṛtir nāma māṇavikā duhitā^abhūt/ sā etarhi (p.209) tena^eva snehena tena^eva premṇā +anandaṃ bhikṣuṃ gacchantam anugacchati tiṣṭhantam anutiṣṭhati/ yad yad eva kulaṃ piṇḍāya praviśati tatra tatra^eva dvāre tūṣṇīṃ bhūtā +asthāt/
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), you may have doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation. 'Someone else was, at that time and on that occasion, the <s>Mātaṅga</s>-king named <s>Triśaṅku</s>.' It should not be regarded thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>. It was I who, at that time and on that occasion, was the <s>Mātaṅga</s>-king named <s>Triśaṅku</s>. You may think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'Someone else was, at that time and on that occasion, the <s>Mātaṅga</s>-prince named <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>.' It should not be regarded thus. It is this <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ānanda</s> who, at that time and on that occasion, was the <s>Mātaṅga</s>-prince named <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>. You may think: 'Someone else was, at that time and on that occasion, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>.' It should not be regarded thus. It is this <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>) who, at that time and on that occasion, was the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>. Nor was it another — the maiden <s>Prakṛti</s>, the daughter of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, at that time and on that occasion. It should not be regarded thus. It is this <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) <s>Prakṛti</s> who, at that time and on that occasion, was the maiden <s>Prakṛti</s>, the daughter of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>. She now, with that very affection, with that very love, follows the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ānanda</s> when he goes, stands when he stands. Whatever household he enters for alms, there at the door she stands silently.

body.text: u17.42/.atha khalu bhagavān etasmin nidāne etasmin prakaraṇe tasyāṃ velāyām imāṃ gāthām abhāṣata/
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, at that time, spoke this verse:

body.text: u17.43ab/.pūrvakeṇa nivāsena pratyutpannena tena ca/
body.translated_text: Through the habitation of former [lives], and through the present [connection],

body.text: u17.43cd/.etena jāyate prema candrasya kumude yathā//
body.translated_text: love is born — as of the moon for the water-lily. //

body.text:
u17.44/.tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavo +anabhisamitānāṃ caturṇām ārya^satyānām abhisamayāya, adhimātraṃ vīryaṃ tīvra^cchando vīryaṃ śabdāpayāmi/ utsāha unnatir aprativāṇiḥ smṛtyā saṃprajanyena apramādato yogaḥ caraṇīyaḥ/ drutam eṣāṃ caturṇā duḥkhasya^ārya^satyasya duḥkha^samudayanya nirodhasya nirodha^gāminyāḥ pratipada ārya^satyasya amīṣāṃ caturṇām ārya^satyānām
anabhisamitānām abhisamayāya^adhimātraṃ tīvra^cchando vīryaṃ vyāyāma utsāha unnatir aprativāṇiḥ smṛtyā saṃprajanyena^apramādato yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
body.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, for the realization of the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>) that have not yet been realized, I urge upon you supreme vigor, intense zeal, and effort — exertion, elevation, unrelenting [energy]; with mindfulness, clear comprehension, and diligence, the practice (<s>yoga</s>) should be undertaken. Swiftly — for the realization of these four noble truths: the noble truth of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), of the origin of suffering (<s>duḥkhasamudaya</s>), of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and of the path leading to cessation (<s>nirodhagāminī pratipat</s>) — for the realization of these four noble truths not yet realized, supreme intense zeal, effort, exertion, elevation, unrelenting [energy]; with mindfulness, clear comprehension, and diligence, the practice should be undertaken.

body.text: u17.45/.(p.210) asmiṃś ca khalu punar dharma^paryāye bhāṣyamāṇe bhikṣūṇāṃ ṣaṣṭi^mātrāṇām anupādāyāsravebhyaś cittāni vimuktāni/ saṃbahulānāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ brahmaṇāṃ gṛhapatīnaṃ ca virajaskaṃ vigata^malaṃ dharma^cakṣur udapādi viśuddhaṃ/
body.translated_text: And when this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, the minds of sixty <s>bhikṣus</s> were liberated from the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) without further clinging. And for a great number of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders, the pure, dust-free, stain-free <s>Dharma</s>-eye arose.

body.text: u17.46/.idam avocad bhagavān/ ātta^manasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan/ iti śrīdivyāvadāne śārdūlakarṇāvadānaṃ/
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Those <s>bhikṣus</s>, with uplifted hearts, rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One. Thus concludes the <s>Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna</s> in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>.

body.text: End
body.translated_text: End
